author: echennells
body:
`opencl_bip352_benchmark` always adds the NVIDIA-only `-cl-nv-opt-level=3` build option. Other OpenCL compilers reject unknown options, so on AMD (ROCm 7.1) and Mesa rusticl the pipeline kernel never builds, and the tool prints "Build failed:" with an empty log. This adds the option only for NVIDIA devices, as `opencl_context.cpp` does.

Tested on `dev` 77ff44a with an RX Vega 64 (ROCm 7.1 OpenCL): the benchmark now runs (2,651 ns/op for N = 500,000, validation `[OK] MATCH`). Compiling a kernel with and without the option confirmed the cause: it fails immediately with it and builds without it. NVIDIA behaviour is unchanged.

author: autoflowcompliance
body:
## What this is

A draft, deliberately. It is real, reviewable work in progress: 38 commits, 241
files, ~33.7k insertions. It is not awaiting merge approval from a live team.

The governing rule throughout: **every addition extends an existing layer. The
frozen core is not rewritten.** `app_files/cleaners/`, `mappers/`, `validators/`,
`auditors/` and `reporters/` keep their behaviour. New capability lives in
sibling packages that call into them, and every feature is opt-in — a run that
worked before this branch produces byte-identical output.

## The central change

Config-declared primitives are **bound into the CLI, batch and migrate run
paths** — not merely importable modules. That distinction was the whole point:
several blocks existed, passed their unit tests, and did nothing in a real run
because nothing wired them in.

`app_files/config_bindings.py` is the one shared helper every entry path calls,
so `migrate`, `batch` and the flat CLI produce byte-identical declared-block
artifacts. Pinned by `tests/unit/test_config_bindings.py` and
`tests/integration/test_migrate_command.py`.

## Three real bugs, found by verifying against real systems

Each was invisible to the synthetic tests that shipped with the feature.

1. **`migrate` ignored every block a config declared.** A rehearsal reported no
   duplicates for a config whose dedupe removes rows, and `--commit` wrote raw
   email and phone values for a config that declared them masked. The
   frozen-core pipeline was fine; the wiring was absent.

2. **A refused database connection raised the driver's own exception.** Found by
   running the connector against a real PostgreSQL server in Docker. A wrong
   password produced a raw `psycopg2.OperationalError` instead of the documented
   `DatabaseError`, so the catch every caller writes missed it and a client
   mistake surfaced as an unhandled exception. Now wrapped, with the password
   scrubbed from the message because some drivers echo the DSN. SQLite tests
   structurally cannot catch this: SQLite needs no password and no socket.

3. **`datetime.UTC` imported on 3.12 and failed on 3.10.** The first CI run
   caught this: green on 3.12, red on 3.10 — and 3.10 is what
   `python:3.10-slim` runs. Development happens on 3.13, where the import works,
   so the suite was green on the machine that wrote it. A guard in
   `test_deployment.py` now parses every module for names newer than the 3.10
   floor.

## Verification

**CI is green — watched, not assumed.** Both jobs on run
[36217388719](https://github.com/autoflowcompliance/data-migration/actions/runs/36217388719):
`test (3.10)` success, `test (3.12)` success, `tests-passed` success.

```
1969 passed, 5 skipped, 1 warning in 57.34s
postgres ready
5 passed in 0.07s          # live connector tests, against a real server
```

The five skipped tests are the PostgreSQL ones; on a machine with no server they
report as skipped, never failed. CI starts `postgres:16-alpine` on 3.10 so the
path SQLite cannot reach is actually exercised.

**Scale, measured honestly.** 500,000 rows / 64 MB with every block on:
**530.4s total, 943 rows/s, peak RSS 1,421 MB.** The rules pass dominates at
246.8s, because `run_rules` walks every value in Python — four rules over half a
million rows is two million calls. Privacy is next at 172.7s; normalization and
dedupe are cheap. Recorded in `docs/SWEEP.md` as a characteristic of the frozen
validator interface rather than hidden. The core loop was deliberately **not**
rewritten: that would break the build-on-top rule.

**Acceptance sweep.** Clean copy, README's own commands, one real file:
install 27s, suite 69s, `migrate --commit` produces 13 deliverables in 2s,
web interface ready in ~15s. About 100s against a ten-minute budget. Five
failure paths each exit non-zero with plain-language messages and write no
output.

## What I have not verified

- **No PR has been merged and no release is cut.** This is a draft.
- The hosted Render demo was not re-deployed from this branch.
- `render.yaml`/`Dockerfile` were not rebuilt end to end; the port-resolution
  and desktop-packaging checks (`build_desktop.py --check`, exit 0) pass, but a
  full image build was not run here.

## Reviewer's entry points

- `app_files/config_bindings.py` — the shared binding helper; start here.
- `docs/SWEEP.md` — the acceptance run and the scale numbers.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — what each layer adds and every fix, derived from the commits.
- `tests/integration/test_postgres_live.py` — the real-server test.
- `tests/unit/test_deployment.py` — the interpreter-floor guard.

The commits are individually reviewable; each message explains why the change
was made, not just what it does.

author: allthingssecurity
body:
# Description

[CAMEL-25037](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CAMEL-25037)

**This PR builds on #26911** (`EventDrivenPollingConsumer.receive()` holds the lifecycle lock while it waits). Both change the same lines of `receive()`, so this branch contains that commit too; only the last commit is new here. On its own, the fix is a one-line change of the old loop.

`EventDrivenPollingConsumer.receive()` loops while the consumer is running. On an `InterruptedException` it calls `handleInterruptedException`, which since CAMEL-20297 (4.4.0) restores the interrupt status and logs through the interrupted exception handler. The loop then waits on the queue again, and that throws at once because the thread is still interrupted. The thread never leaves `receive()`, even when a message is queued. It uses a full core and logs one WARN per iteration: in a reproducer, 603,114 lines in about 3 seconds.

About CAMEL-22390: that ticket reported the same pattern in `SedaConsumer` and was closed with the advice not to interrupt Camel's threads. This case is different. `ConsumerTemplate.receive()` and `PollingConsumer.receive()` run on the **caller's own thread**, the one the application passed in, and the application may legitimately interrupt it. Examples are `Future.cancel(true)` on a task that waits for a message, or `shutdownNow()` of the application's executor. A blocking JDK-style method is expected to return or throw when interrupted, not spin. Camel also interrupts route threads itself during a forced shutdown, and such a thread may be waiting in a `pollEnrich` with the default timeout.

This change: on `InterruptedException`, `receive()` keeps the interrupt status (as CAMEL-20297 intended) and returns null instead of waiting again, as `receive(timeout)` already does. It still reports the exception through the interrupted exception handler once. The javadoc of `receive()` now says when it returns null: when the consumer is stopped while waiting, or when the thread is interrupted.

Tests: new `EventDrivenPollingConsumerInterruptTest` interrupts a thread waiting in `receive()` and checks, within a 5 second Awaitility bound, that `receive()` returns null, that the interrupt status is kept, and that the handler was called exactly once. Without the main-code change it fails with `ConditionTimeoutException ... was not fulfilled within 5 seconds` (the thread spins until the test stops the consumer). With the change, `*PollEnrich*,*PollingConsumer*,*ConsumerTemplate*,*Enricher*,*ConsumerCache*,*ScheduledPoll*` in camel-core and camel-support pass: 131 tests, 0 failures.

Found with the same TLA+ model as #26911. With an interrupt added, `ReceiveEndsAfterInterrupt` is violated by a lasso Interrupt -> wait -> fail -> wait, even with a message queued. I then reproduced it against the real classes.

Note: a thread that enters `receive()` with its interrupt flag already set now gets `null` straight away (with the flag kept), instead of spinning.

author: jabbadaslut
body:
`bin/setup` booted Rails up to seven times: three for setup, then four more to seed (the already-seeded check, `db:seed`, the spreadsheet import it shelled out to, and `setup:load_counts`). Everything now runs in one boot, and seeding itself does less wasted work.

| Fresh workspace, cold bootsnap | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bin/workspace_setup` (seeded) | 89–96s | 38–44s |
| `bin/workspace_setup --without_seeds` | 19.5s | 11.7s |
| `--without_seeds` re-run | 17.3s | 5.8s |

- **One `bin/rails` call** runs `db:prepare`, both stylesheet builds, `log:clear`, and (when seeding) `db:seed`, `setup:load_counts` and the opt-in `parallel:create parallel:prepare`. `npm install` runs alongside it.
- **Re-runs now migrate.** `structure.sql` can't be loaded twice, so a re-run's `db:schema:load` failed and took the chained `db:migrate` down with it, silently. `db:prepare` loads the schema only into a database it just created. `seeds: false` on the dev and test primaries stops it seeding development whenever it creates any database, including the test one.
- **`db/seeds.rb` skips an already-seeded database** instead of dying on duplicates, runs the spreadsheet import inline, logs at `info` (development's per-query backtraces were over a third of seeding) and hashes seeded passwords at bcrypt's minimum cost.
- **`node_modules` is an APFS clone of the root checkout's** rather than a symlink, which `npm install` replaced with its own 168MB install. The clone costs ~3MB of disk.
- **Dropped `tmp:clear`**, which wiped the bootsnap cache so the next `bin/dev` booted cold.

body:
Closes #12, #33, #34.

## Meetings and agendas (#33)
- **Recurring meetings (P1-MTG-04):** "New meeting" can repeat weekly, fortnightly or monthly for 2–12 occurrences sharing `series_id`. Occurrences are spaced in the organization's time zone. Editing one occurrence changes only that one, and the meeting page lists the whole series.
- **Agenda builder (P0-AGD-01/02/04):** items now have an owner, a desired outcome and a linked record (task, milestone, risk, issue or decision from the meeting's project). Items can be edited and removed before the meeting; removal is organizer-only by row-level security.
- **Combine (P0-AGD-03):** folds one item into another. The source is marked `combined` and points at its target, and a check constraint enforces the pairing.
- **Carry-forward (P1-AGD-06):** copies an unfinished item to a later meeting with `carried_from_id` and defers the original.

The database columns for series, links and carry-forward already existed, but no code used them.

## Comments (#34)
- **Where (P0-COM-01):** a shared `CommentThread` on project, meeting, event and CRM organization pages.
- **Replies and mentions (P0-COM-02):** author names, threaded replies and mentions. The replied-to author is notified, and notifications open the exact comment.
- **Edit, delete, resolve (P0-COM-04):** `app.guard_record_comment` enforces the rules in the database:
  - only the author edits, and edits are marked;
  - the author or an admin deletes; the row stays, with `deleted_by` and a `comment.deletion` audit event;
  - anyone who can read the thread resolves it;
  - a deleted comment can't be changed.
- **Attachments and links (P0-COM-05):** a comment can carry a link on an approved host (the same list documents use) or a document the author can read.

## Docs
- `docs/audit/02-work-management.md`: a dated status table now supersedes the historical findings. This was the last condition on #12.
- `docs/plans/epic-08-plan.md`: carried over from this branch's earlier commit.

## Tests
- `supabase/tests/meetings-comments.sql`: edit, delete, resolve permissions; audit marker; link host check; combine constraint; carry-forward link.
- `tests/e2e/meetings-comments.spec.ts`: recurring series, edit, combine, carry-forward, remove; comment reply, edit, resolve, and delete with its marker.
- Both are added to CI.

## Deploy note
One migration, `20260926060000_meetings_and_comments_completion.sql`. It adds columns, a constraint, a trigger, and replaces the comment update policy. It doesn't delete any data.

Main's `createNotifications` currently fails for notifications to other people. #131 fixes it. Until then, comment mention and reply notifications fail silently, but the comment itself still saves.

| FreeBSD | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| NetBSD (APE loader) | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| OpenBSD 7.3 (APE loader) | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass |

## Usage

```sh
beam.com build INPUT [-o OUTPUT] [-a APP]...
```

- **One `.erl` file** that exports `main/1`, as for `escript`. The program gets the command line arguments and halts with status 0 when `main/1` returns (127 on an exception).
- **An application directory** in the rebar3 layout: `src/**/*.erl`, `src/NAME.app.src` or `ebin/NAME.app`, and optionally `include/`, `priv/`, `config/sys.config`, `config/vm.args` and the `erl_opts` of `rebar.config`.
- `OUTPUT` defaults to the name of the input with `.com`.
- `-a APP` adds an OTP application that the code only calls dynamically (for example with `apply/3`).

## How it works

1. `beam_com.c`: when the first argument is `build` and the zip has `lib/beam_com`, BEAM.com boots `start_clean` and runs `beam_com:main/0` instead of the release. The path of the executable is given with `-beam_com_exe`.
2. `apps/beam_com/src/beam_com_build.erl` compiles the code with the `compiler` application in the zip (compile errors print in the `erlc` format).
3. It selects the OTP applications: the ones that the `.app` file names, the ones of the modules that the compiled code calls (the imports chunk), the `-a` applications, and all the applications that these need. For example, `hashsum.erl` calls `crypto:hash/2`, so `crypto` is added with no configuration.
4. It makes the boot script with `systools:make_script/2` (the `sasl` application in the zip), with `$ROOT` paths.
5. `apps/beam_com/src/beam_com_zip.erl` writes the new executable: a copy of `beam.com` with the release in its zip, and only the applications that the program needs. The new file has no compiler and no `build` command.

A one-file program gets a generated application with `{mod, {beam_com_script, Module}}`. `apps/beam_com_script` waits until the release has started, then calls `Module:main/1` with `init:get_plain_arguments()` and halts.

### The zip writer

- **Discovery:** the emulator already has zip entries of its own inside its image: the symbol tables (`.symtab.amd64`, `.symtab.arm64`), the time zones and `.cosmo`. Info-ZIP `zip` wrote our entries over the old central directory, just after `.cosmo`. These first entries must stay where they are.
- In an APE file, the zip offsets count from the start of the file, not from the start of the zip. `stdlib`'s `zip` module cannot write this.
- The writer keeps the bytes up to the first entry that it removes, moves the entries after that point that it keeps (a copy of each local record, with its data descriptor), adds the new entries (deflated, fixed time stamp, so that the same input gives the same file), and writes a new central directory with the new offsets. `unzip -t` accepts the result.

## Other changes

- `build.sh` makes the Erlang code of `crypto`, `asn1`, `public_key` and `ssl`. The small build (`OTP_SMALL_BUILD`) does not make it. **Discovery:** in the earlier examples, this code came from the stock OTP of rebar3, not from our build.
- The zip of `beam.com` now has `kernel`, `stdlib`, `sasl`, `compiler`, `crypto`, `asn1`, `public_key`, `ssl` and `inets` (`ebin` and `include`, for `-include_lib`), the `beam_com` tool and `beam_com_script`. `beam.com` grows from 25.1 MB to 34.3 MB. The programs that it makes are 27 to 32 MB (the emulator is about 17 MB of that).
- BEAM.com writes a warning when `releases/start_erl.data` names another ERTS version than its own.
- `examples/hashsum.erl`: a one-file program that calls `crypto`.
- `tests/run.sh` and `tests/run.ps1` build the examples with `beam.com build` and run them with the same checks as the rebar3 releases.
- README: a "Build a program with `beam.com build`" section and how the writer works. ROADMAP: build mode is done; Hex packages, `.yrl`/`.xrl`/`.asn1` and Elixir are later steps.

## Problems during the work, and what was done

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The first entries of the zip must not move | the emulator image has its own zip entries | keep all bytes up to the first removed entry |
| `crypto`, `ssl` and `public_key` Erlang code missing in our build | `OTP_SMALL_BUILD` | build them in the `make` step |
| `cp include/*.hrl` failed for `sasl` | `sasl/include` has no `.hrl` files | copy only when there are files |
| Exception message said "exception exception error" | `erl_error:format_exception/3` already starts with "exception" | removed the extra word |
| A boot script from a temporary directory has absolute paths | `systools` replaces only the `ROOT` prefix | the builder rewrites the paths of the program to `$ROOT` |

## Not in this PR

- Hex dependencies, `.yrl`/`.xrl` (`parsetools`), `.asn1` files and Elixir sources.
- NIF dependencies (only the static NIFs in `beam.com`).

Validation: swift build; swift test (7 passing); protocol E2E with OpenSSL verification; real Chrome browser E2E with forged-origin rejection and signature verification over reconstructed client data; 6 Node trust-boundary tests; git diff --check.

The native protocol remains compatible for trusted local callers. Code/tests and documentation are separate commits. This PR addresses the browser origin-spoofing finding independently of Telegram enrollment.

author: allthingssecurity
body:
# Description

[CAMEL-25038](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CAMEL-25038)

`DisruptorProducer` waits for the reply the same way `SedaProducer` did before CAMEL-24947 and CAMEL-24948, and it has the same two bugs. The seda fixes (#26793, which is still open, and #26794, which is merged) only changed camel-seda.

1. **Late reply.** The reply path (`onDone`) checked `latch.getCount() == 0` and then copied the reply into the caller's exchange. That is not atomic with the timeout branch, which sets `ExchangeTimedOutException`, counts down and returns. A reply arriving at about the timeout could be returned together with `ExchangeTimedOutException`. It could also be copied into the caller's exchange after the producer had returned, and `copyResults` then clears the exception while the caller's error handler works on it. In a stress run, 25 of 400 near-timeout requests came back with the reply body and the timeout exception.
2. **Interrupt.** With `timeout=0`, an interrupted `latch.await()` was logged and otherwise swallowed. The caller got a successful exchange whose "reply" was its own request, and the real reply was written into the exchange later.

This change applies the seda approach to `DisruptorProducer`:
- The reply, the timeout and the interrupt claim the exchange with a compare-and-set on a shared `AtomicBoolean`. A reply that loses the claim is ignored.
- A timeout that loses the claim means the reply is being copied, so the producer waits (uninterruptibly) for that short copy to finish and returns the reply.
- An interrupted reply wait (`timeout=0`) that wins the claim fails the exchange with the `InterruptedException`, as seda does since CAMEL-24948. If it loses, it waits for the copy like the timeout does. The interrupt status is kept in both cases.
- An interrupt during a wait with `timeout > 0` is still reported as a timeout, as in seda.
- The upgrade guide (4.23) notes the change, next to the seda entry.

The existing `DISRUPTOR_IGNORE_EXCHANGE` property is still set on the caller's exchange on timeout, which is an older bug that this PR leaves alone: every later copy of that exchange inherits it (for example on a redelivery after a timeout, or a `doCatch` fallback to another disruptor endpoint), and the disruptor consumer silently drops any exchange that carries it. So redeliveries after a first timeout always time out, and an InOnly fallback is lost. I'll raise that in its own JIRA.

Tests, modelled on `SedaTimeoutLateReplyTest` and `SedaProducerInterruptedTest`:
- `DisruptorTimeoutLateReplyTest` (3 tests) pauses the reply copy with a `SafeCopyProperty`, only when it is called from the producer's `onDone`, and lets the timeout or an interrupt happen during the copy. It also checks that a reply after the timeout is ignored.
- `DisruptorProducerInterruptedTest` interrupts an InOut caller that waits without a timeout.

There are no sleeps, and the waits use latches and Awaitility. Without the main-code change:
```
testReplyBeingCopiedWhenTimeoutOccurs  Producer returned while the reply was copied into the exchange ==> expected: <false> but was: <true>
testReplyBeingCopiedWhenInterrupted    Producer returned while the reply was copied into the exchange ==> expected: <false> but was: <true>
testInterruptedWhileWaitingForReply    Unexpected null value, expected: <java.lang.InterruptedException> but was: <null>
```
(`testReplyAfterTimeoutIsIgnored` passes before and after; it guards the ignored late reply.) With the change, all camel-disruptor tests pass (106 tests, 0 failures), and `*Seda*` in camel-core passes too (142 tests, 0 failures).

Found with the TLA+ model of the seda producer/consumer handshake, re-targeted to `DisruptorProducer`. The fixed variant satisfies `NoWriteAfterReturn`, `CallerViewStable`, `ConsistentOutcome` and `ProducerReturns`. I then reproduced both bugs against the real classes.

# Target

- [x] I checked that the commit is targeting the correct branch (Camel 4 uses the `main` branch)

# Tracking
- [x] If this is a large change, bug fix, or code improvement, I checked there is a [JIRA issue](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CAMEL) filed for the change (usually before you start working on it).

- [x] I checked that each commit in the pull request has a meaningful subject line and body.
- [ ] I have run `mvn clean install -DskipTests` locally from root folder and I have committed all auto-generated changes.
  (I built and tested the affected modules, including the formatter and import-sort plugins. I did not run the full root build.)

# AI-assisted contributions

author: toddawhittaker
body:
Epic 14.3 adds a resource guard, an idle stop, and an acceptable-use statement every account must accept (issue #554). It also folds in the 20-terminal cap with a toast (#474) and server-side notifications (#475). Fixes #554, fixes #474, fixes #475.

It serves SPEC.md sections 5.1 (the acceptable-use gate), 6.4 (idle stop), 19.4 (new, "Resource guard"), 20.1, 24.11, 25.6, 26 and 29, section 24 (trust boundaries) and section 25.8 (accessibility), and STACK.md sections 13 and 15. The epic plan was folded into SPEC.md and deleted. New decision records: ADR 0032 (resource guard) and ADR 0033 (notifications).

## What a user gets

- **CPU throttle.** A workspace that keeps its CPUs more than 80% busy for 30 minutes is slowed to 25% of its CPU through an Incus time-slice allowance (`limits.cpu.allowance`; 50ms/100ms for the 2-CPU workspaces the install creates). The student sees a banner at once. Stopping and starting the workspace, or an administrator's **Lift throttle**, restores full speed. Usage is remembered across restarts and across reboots from inside the workspace, so stopping just before the window ends does not help.
- **Memory flag.** A workspace using more than 90% of its memory limit for 30 minutes is flagged for administrators only. Nothing happens to the workspace.
- **Idle stop.** A workspace with no activity from its owner in the browser for 60 minutes shows "Still working?" and stops five minutes later if nobody answers. This applies to unattended coding agents too. The grace period is unchanged. Accounts whose grace period is 0 get an idle time of 0.
- **Administrators** see Throttled and High memory tags in the Workspaces table, a Resource guard section in Health, and, in each workspace's detail panel, the guard state, Lift throttle, Clear memory flag, per-workspace overrides and the last activity time. Every setting is in Settings.
- **Acceptable use.** Every account, whether it signs in through Dex or arrives from a course, must accept the statement at first sign-in and again whenever an administrator changes the text. The check reuses Epic 14.2's password-change gate as a second step in one ordered list, with the password gate first. Until the statement is accepted, the server refuses every other route, WebSocket and preview, and connections that are already open close at their next session check.
- **Terminal cap (#474):** at most 20 terminals per workspace, with a toast when the cap is reached. **Notifications (#475):** server-side notifications with a badge and a dialog.

## Upgrading

A package install is enough; there is no role change. Migrations 0020 (resource guard, acceptable use) and 0021 (notifications) run on start. Every account meets the acceptable-use statement at its next sign-in.

## Task PRs (squash-merged into `epic/14-3-resource-guard` unless marked)

- #562 T2 data and contracts (migration 0020), #564 T1 controller, #566 T3 worker, #565 T4 API, #567 T5 web, #586 T6 acceptable-use gate, #588 T7 rehearsal checks, #589 T8 docs.
- #561 terminal cap (#474), with a real fix for the terminal-real-agent flake; #571 notifications (#475, migration 0021); #569 git test flake.
- Review fixes: #573, #574, #575, #576, #577, #587.
- Syncs from main (merge commits): #557, #585 (brings in Epic 14.2).

## Reviews and rulings

- Code, security and accessibility reviews ran over T1 to T5, then confirmation reviews, then again over T6. Nothing at medium or above is open.
- **Rulings (Todd):** usage is remembered across restarts (a wall-clock window in which stopped time counts as zero); CPU is judged across runs and memory per run; a preview page load counts as activity only when the student opened it (`Sec-Fetch-Dest` document or iframe, with `Sec-Fetch-User: ?1`).
- **Fixes that matter:**
  - A reboot loop from inside the workspace reset the CPU counter and hid usage. A boot marker (the Incus init process ID) and a counter-drop check now detect every restart. The cost: a workspace near the 79% line that restarts often can now be throttled.
  - Reloading a preview kept a workspace awake forever. Only user-started page loads count now.
  - Open sockets now honour the acceptable-use gate.
- **Accepted limits:** a throttle-then-restart cycle has no upper bound; each cycle writes two audit rows, and BACKLOG has an entry for a limit. Rebooting every 14 minutes avoids the memory flag, which is acceptable because the flag only informs and `limits.memory` is the real cap. A determined student could fake activity with their own session cookie.

## Verification

- Full battery on the final tree with a fresh database: `make check` passed (3771 tests, coverage 91.98% lines and 83.22% branches, above the floors; infra checks green), and `pnpm test:e2e` unsharded passed 377 with 1 skipped and no reruns.
- Rehearsal VM (0.1.480+g77d322f): every live check passed, including the throttle landing, `cpu.max` reading `50000 100000`, root inside the workspace unable to write `cpu.max`, the allowance surviving worker and controller restarts, lift, stop and start, a reboot keeping the usage, the page cache left out of memory, the memory flag, idle stop, and the acceptable-use gate through Caddy. Smoke 243/243, security 242/242 with one warning (the mock LMS is registered).
- **Pilot: not yet deployed.** Deploying to the pilot needs Todd's go-ahead; the rehearsal VM results above are the live evidence. Deploy with a VM snapshot and database dumps first.

author: sean-koval
body:
## Research: which distance does HCAA cluster on?

| Source | Distance clustered | Linkage | How checked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **mlfinlab HCAA** (the reference implementation this module was ported from) | **pairwise** `d = sqrt(2(1-rho))`, `scipy_linkage(squareform(d), method=linkage)` | default `'ward'` (v0.8.0 used sklearn `AgglomerativeClustering(affinity='precomputed')`, default `'average'`) | source read at [quantopian/mlfinlab `cd63393`](https://github.com/quantopian/mlfinlab/blob/cd63393/mlfinlab/portfolio_optimization/hcaa.py) (the last `hcaa.py` before the rename to `herc.py`) and at [`59f1457`](https://github.com/quantopian/mlfinlab/blob/59f1457/mlfinlab/portfolio_optimization/hcaa.py) (v0.8.0) |
| jduarte00/hcaa_implementation (Python) | pairwise `sqrt(2(1-rho))` via `squareform` | Ward | [source](https://github.com/jduarte00/hcaa_implementation/blob/master/hcaa_implementation.py) |
| R package HierPortfolios `HCAA_Portfolio` (Trucios) | **distance of distances**: `dist(sqrt(0.5(1-rho)), "euclidean")` | default `ward.D2` | [source](https://github.com/cran/HierPortfolios/blob/master/R/HCAA_Portfolio.R) |
| Raffinot (2017), *JPM* 44(2) | **not determined** | Ward is the reported preferred linkage | full text not reachable: SSRN and ResearchGate return 403 to automated fetches and the JPM version is paywalled. Secondary sources say the method follows Mantegna (1999), whose tree is on `d` directly, but I could not confirm the paper's exact matrix |

So the reference implementation clusters on pairwise distances. What Raffinot's paper prescribes could not be read directly, and the public implementations disagree.

Separate finding, not changed here: every source above uses **Ward** (or average) linkage by default. This module uses single linkage. That is a larger departure from Raffinot than the distance, and would be a separate issue if wanted.

## The option

- Rust: `HcaaDistance::{Correlation, DistanceOfDistances}` with `Default` and `FromStr` (case-insensitive; an unknown name returns the new `HcaaError::UnknownDistance`). It is set with a public `distance` field or `HierarchicalClusteringAssetAllocation::new(..).with_distance(..)`. `allocate`'s signature is unchanged. It follows #183's `HrpDistance` pattern, but as its own type so the parse error is an `HcaaError`.
- Python: `hcaa.allocate_hcaa(..., distance="correlation" | "distance_of_distances")`, a keyword that defaults to the Rust default.
- Shared helper: `single_linkage_children`, `distance_of_distances` and `quasi_diagonalization` move from `hrp.rs` and `hcaa.rs` (which had its own copy of the first and last) into a crate-private `util::linkage` that both use. HCAA keeps its own `sqrt(2(1-rho))`, which is twice HRP's `d`, so single-linkage trees are unchanged. HRP's fixture tests and HCAA's existing tests pass unchanged.

## Default: `Correlation` (pairwise), unchanged

It matches mlfinlab's HCAA, and on the §16.5 Monte Carlo it gives HCAA *lower* out-of-sample variance than distance of distances. That is the opposite of HRP's result in #183. **No behaviour change** for existing callers.

## Measured: AFML §16.5 Monte Carlo, 10,000 runs, SYNTHETIC

This uses notebook 10's generator and backtest (Snippet 16.4 parameters: 260-obs window, rebalance every 22, 10 assets) and the same script as #183. Seeds are `default_rng([51, k])` and the build is release. HCAA uses `"minimum_variance"`.

| | HCAA d (**default**) | HCAA d~ | HCAA d, k=5 | HCAA d~, k=5 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| mean OOS variance ×1e4 | **3.049** | 3.154 | 3.275 | 3.364 |
| IVP / HCAA | **1.625** (t = 105) | 1.571 (t = 108) | 1.513 | 1.473 |
| CLA / HCAA | **1.672** (t = 58.5) | 1.616 (t = 50.8) | 1.557 | 1.516 |
| HRP d~ (its default) / HCAA | **1.178** | 1.139 | 1.097 | 1.068 |
| HRP d / HCAA | **1.250** | 1.208 | 1.164 | 1.133 |
| runs where HCAA beats IVP | 87.8% | **90.4%** | 87.0% | 90.1% |
| runs where HCAA beats CLA | **73.9%** | 72.2% | 70.9% | 69.7% |
| turnover per rebalance | 0.107 | 0.087 | 0.110 | **0.077** |
| effective N (of 10) | 6.78 | 7.06 | 6.90 | 7.15 |

- **Head to head:** d~ has 3.4% more mean OOS variance than d with no cut (paired mean log ratio +0.068, t = 34; d is lower in 66% of runs), and 2.7% more at k=5 (t = 30).
- **`"minimum_standard_deviation"`:** d gives 3.757 and d~ gives 5.025, which is no better than IVP (4.955). Turnover is 0.208 for d and 0.126 for d~.
- **Reference rows:** HRP d~ 3.592 / d 3.812 (turnover 0.122 / 0.216), CLA 5.098 (0.187), IVP 4.955 (0.074). These reproduce #183's table exactly.
- **Costs:** the 10 bps cost model leaves every variance unchanged to 4 significant digits.

What d~ buys HCAA is stability: about 20% less turnover with minimum variance, and about 40% less with minimum standard deviation. It does not lower variance. The table and this caveat are on the HCAA docs page. Notebook 10 is unchanged.

## Tests

- **New independent fixture.** `tests/fixtures/hcaa/generate.py` imports numpy and scipy only, with no openquant or mlfinlab. It has its own transcription of the HCAA tree walk and uses scipy single linkage, on `squareform(d)` for the pairwise variant and on the square `d` verbatim, as in Snippet 16.4, for d~ (it asserts that this equals `pdist(d)`). The fixture has two cases, the 23-ETF prices and a seeded 8×8 covariance. Each records the tree, the leaf order and the weights for 3 metrics (minimum variance, minimum standard deviation, equal weighting) × 3 cuts (none, 2, 4) × both distances. The trees differ between the distances on both cases. The HRP generator and fixture are untouched. `tests/FIXTURES.md` lists the new fixture.
- **Rust:** `hcaa_reference.rs` gains 5 tests: tree, order and weights for both distances on both cases (36 combinations, tolerance 1e-10); the trees and weights differ; two assets do not depend on the distance; and the default and parsing. There is also a `with_distance` doctest.
- **Python:** `test_core_hcaa.py` gains 18 parametrised reference checks on the price fixture, plus a default/case-insensitivity/`ValueError("unknown distance")` test.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` (release) pass.
- `cargo doc -p openquant` passes with `-D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links -D warnings`.
- `cargo test -p openquant --release -- --skip test_sadf_test`: 619 passed, 0 failed, including 127 doctests (after merging main).
- Extension built with `maturin develop --release`: pytest 487 passed, 2 skipped (after merging main).
- `ruff format --check`, `ruff check` and `mypy` pass.
- These docs checks pass: `check:python-examples` (40 ran), `check:examples` (38 Rust examples compile), `check-content-schema`, `generate_api_inventory.py --check` (`with_distance` added) and `check_coverage.py --check`.

Closes #188.

body:
Adds what a plugin needs to ship a function-hooks module: a `plugins/<name>/mod/` layout, a staged test runner, CI and pre-commit wiring, and `hooks.json` support for a `modules`-only file. The herdr state beacon and classifier telemetry mods build on it.

The engine declarations `/plugin-types` generates stay gitignored, since a committed copy runs about 17k lines tied to one Claude Code release and its web globals broke Bun's `TextEncoder` typing when merged into the root program. Mods sit outside the root tsconfig, and lint turns off the rules that fire on `any` where the types are absent. CI validates a mod with `claude plugin validate` under the function-hooks flag and runs its tests through `scripts/mod-test.ts`, which stages a copy of the plugin because `claude plugin test` has no path filter and would otherwise fail on the plugin's bun tests. `check-workspace-deps` skips mod files rather than treat `claude-code` as a builtin, since `plugins/claude-code` is a real workspace package with that name.

No mod is committed here. I exercised the layout with an uncommitted copy of the herdr beacon under `plugins/herdr/mod/`, running it through `mod-test.ts`, the `plugin-test` pre-commit hook, and oxlint with the generated types moved aside.

author: shixiangwang
body:
## Summary

`oxo-flow serve --mode` accepted any raw string, but the web router only
enables auth middleware for the exact matches `"team"`/`"hpc"`
(`crates/oxo-flow-web/src/server.rs` `build_router`). A misspelled mode
(`--mode "Team"`, `--mode "team "`, `--mode bogus`) silently started a
**no-auth** server — and `effective_bind_host` treats any non-`"personal"`
value as bind-any, so the misconfigured server could listen on all
interfaces with no authentication.

## Fix

Mirror the standalone web binary's `ServerMode` ValueEnum
(`crates/oxo-flow-web/src/main.rs`) in the CLI `Serve` variant as
`ServeMode` (personal/team/hpc), so invalid values are rejected at clap
parse time instead of silently downgrading:

```
$ oxo-flow serve --mode "team "
error: invalid value 'team ' for '--mode <MODE>'
  [possible values: personal, team, hpc]
  tip: a similar value exists: 'team'
```

- `--mode bogus`, `--mode ""` also rejected at parse time.
- `OXO_FLOW_MODE` env inheritance keeps working (clap validates env values too).
- Desktop shell unaffected (passes the `"personal"` literal to
  `start_server_with_mode(&str)` directly); standalone web binary already
  had its own enum.

## Verification (release binary, live)

- `serve --mode team` → `Building router for mode: team` +
  `Auth middleware enabled for team mode`
- `serve` with `OXO_FLOW_MODE=hpc` → auth middleware enabled for hpc
- `serve` (default) → personal, loopback bind, no auth (unchanged)
- three invalid inputs above → clap parse errors with value list

author: brian-egan
body:
Closes #8.

## What this does
New `Import` module (added to `Package.swift` — not in ARCHITECTURE §1's original table, since AVFoundation is beyond `PipelineCore`'s Foundation/CoreVideo/simd-only scope):

- `LivePhotoImporter.describeClip(heicURL:movURL:) async throws -> ClipDescriptor` — validates the pair, reads the video track's size/frame rate/duration, counts frames by decoding, and derives the reference frame index.
- `FrameSequence` — streams decoded `CVPixelBuffer`s one at a time over `AVAssetReader`. A plain `Sequence`/`IteratorProtocol`, not `AsyncSequence`: `copyNextSampleBuffer()` already blocks synchronously, so `async` would add ceremony without changing when the work happens.
- `ClipDescriptor` (new, in `PipelineCore`): width, height, frame count, source frame rate, duration, reference frame index. `Double` seconds/fps rather than `CMTime`, keeping `PipelineCore` off CoreMedia.
- `ClipImportError` — descriptive errors for a missing file, an unreadable still, or no video track.

`StillMotionsPipeline` now re-exports `Import` alongside `PipelineCore` (`@_exported import`), matching "harness imports only the façade."

## Reference frame index: what I tried, and what I shipped
R-4 wants the still's timestamp within the video as the default reference frame, not hardcoded to 0 or the midpoint. I first implemented the documented QuickTime `com.apple.quicktime.still-image-time` timed-metadata convention (real Apple mechanism for Live Photos), building it via `AVAssetWriterInputMetadataAdaptor`/`AVTimedMetadataGroup`. With no real Live Photo on hand to check the write side against, I couldn't get it to round-trip reliably in isolation — the group's `timeRange` didn't come back through `asset.loadMetadata(for:)`/`availableMetadataFormats` in my own test harness. Rather than ship something I couldn't verify, I switched to a simpler, independently-verifiable mechanism: the HEIC's EXIF `DateTimeOriginal` + `SubsecTimeOriginal` against the MOV's own creation date (`AVAsset.load(.creationDate)`) — both real capture-time metadata for the same physical instant, both standard/well-supported APIs I could build and check end-to-end myself. Falls back to frame 0 when either timestamp is missing.

**Caveat, stated plainly:** both timestamps are treated as UTC. EXIF `DateTimeOriginal` carries no timezone field. If a real Live Photo's still turns out to be tagged in local time against a UTC video creation date, the delta will be off by the timezone offset — this needs checking against an actual exported Live Photo, which is phase-2/on-device territory, not phase-1's synthetic-only scope. Flagged in code comments too.

## Also deliberately not done: measuring the real Live Photo frame rate
The issue asks to measure the real source frame rate (15 vs 30 fps) across personal fixtures and record it in `docs/PRD.md §8`. I did not do this. `tests/fixtures/personal` is gitignored and reserved for phase-2's #18, and this repo goes public at the end of the build — a phase-1 commit, PR body, or issue comment describing personal-fixture specifics (filenames, counts, what was measured) becomes permanent public history even though the files themselves stay out of git. `docs/PRD.md §8` now points that measurement at #18/#26 instead of claiming it's resolved. The importer reads `AVAssetTrack.nominalFrameRate` generically (not hardcoded to 30) and is fully tested against the synthetic fixtures, which are 30 fps by construction.

## Verified
- Frame count matches all 8 synthetic fixtures (paired with a throwaway HEIC — #7's fixtures are video-only ground truth, so this only exercises the MOV side for that assertion)
- Reference frame index test: a self-built clip with a known EXIF/creation-date offset (frame 41 of 60, deliberately neither 0 nor the midpoint) round-trips correctly; a clip with no EXIF timestamp falls back to 0
- Missing file and unreadable-still cases throw `ClipImportError` naming the offending file
- Streaming decode: resident memory measured via `task_info`/`MACH_TASK_BASIC_INFO` while decoding a self-built 240-frame (640x480) clip grows by less than 20 MB total — nowhere near the ~295 MB a fully-resident clip would need

## Verification output (clean detached worktree of the pushed branch)
```
Test Suite 'ImportTests' passed at 2026-09-26 00:20:04.376.
	 Executed 6 tests, with 0 failures (0 unexpected) in 2.143 (2.144) seconds
PASS  swift test

=== 4/4  Harness regression (synthetic fixtures)
SKIP  no harness/baseline.json yet — expected until the baseline is established

VERIFY PASSED  /tmp/verify-issue-8
```

## Summary

- refactors the API into injected HTTP, service, repository, domain, and configuration layers while preserving the existing workshop/reservation HTTP contract;
- keeps PostgreSQL authoritative for booking rules and preserves `FOR UPDATE OF sc` concurrency protection;
- adds MongoDB 8 reservation-attempt logging with strict schema validation, least-privilege credentials, statistics indexes, and a 180-day TTL;
- adds Helmet, a 10 KiB JSON limit, centralized safe error handling, strict CORS comparison, validated startup configuration, and timing-safe admin bearer authentication;
- adds OpenAPI 3.1 documentation and ADRs for the layered architecture and MongoDB journal.

## src/ tree

```text
│   ├── health-service.ts
│   ├── reservation-attempt-service.ts
│   └── reservation-service.ts
└── server.ts
```

## Verification results

### API

- `npm run lint`: PASS, 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- `npm run type-check`: PASS.
- `npm test`: PASS.
  - Unit: 3 files, 14 tests passed.
  - Integration: 1 file, 10 tests passed.

Unit coverage:
- creates a reservation and returns remaining capacity;
- `slot_category_not_found`;
- `booking_unavailable`;
- `booking_closed` at the exact closing second;
- `capacity_full` with no INSERT;
- MongoDB logging failure does not affect a successful reservation;
- attempt event contains no personal data;
- validation rejects string slot IDs;
- validation rejects a NoSQL operator object;
- validation rejects overlong fields and invalid email;
- validation trims accepted text fields;
- admin token missing / wrong / correct.

Integration coverage:
- numeric availability counts;
- POST 201 persists the reservation;
- SQL injection text is stored literally and the table remains intact;
- SQL expression in slotId returns 400;
- ten concurrent POSTs at capacity one produce exactly 1 × 201 and 9 × 409 `capacity_full`, with one row stored;
- passed booking closing returns `booking_closed`;
- strict CORS behavior;
- body over 10 KiB returns 413;
- malformed JSON returns 400 `invalid_json`;
- admin stats return the expected accepted/created, refused/capacity_full, and refused/validation_error counts, and MongoDB documents contain no personal fields.

### Concurrency regression without the lock

The same concurrency test was run in the runner after temporarily removing `FOR UPDATE OF sc` from the working copy only; that modified file was never committed.

Result: the test FAILED as expected. All 10 concurrent requests returned 201, while the assertion expected exactly one created reservation:

```text
expected [ …(10) ] to have a length of 1 but got 10
```

With the committed lock in place, the test passes with 1 × 201 and 9 × 409 `capacity_full`.

### Front compatibility

- `npm run test:unit -- --run`: PASS — 6 files, 8 tests.
- `npm run type-check`: PASS.
- API and Front were launched together against the Docker services.
- End-to-end reservation with MongoDB available: HTTP 201.
- MongoDB was then stopped; a second reservation still returned HTTP 201.
- Health after MongoDB stop reported `postgresql: ok` and `mongodb: unavailable`.

## Re-run locally

From the repository root:

```sh

```

For API verification:

```sh
npm test
```

For Front compatibility:

```sh
cd apps/front
npm ci
npm run test:unit -- --run
npm run type-check
```

```sh
openssl rand -hex 32
```

author: sawtaytoes
body:
Adds `.github/workflows/shared-vrt.yml`, a reusable visual-regression workflow that every owned app can import by the `workflows-v1` tag. The tools it runs are in `packages/ci/src/vrt/`.

## What it does

- A repo writes PNG shots into one directory, `$VRT_ACTUAL_DIR` (default `.vrt-actual`).
- Two producers can write there: the built-in Storybook capture (`storybookStaticDirs`) and the repo's own `captureCommand` (for example a Playwright or Vitest test). A repo can use one or both.
- reg-suit compares the directory against the repo's own bucket. `reportStatus.js` posts a commit status and one pull-request comment, on GitHub and on Forgejo.
- The inner job is `visualRegression`. A pull request from a fork does not run. The guard reads the event payload, because Forgejo reports the event as `workflow_call` inside a called workflow.
- The tools run from a checkout of Charcuterie. Their pinned dependencies (Playwright 1.63.0, reg-suit 0.14.5 and its two plugins) install with `npm ci` from their own lockfile.

Charcuterie's own `vrt` job does not change in this pull request.

## Evidence

1. Unit tests: 63 tests pass in `packages/ci`. They cover argument parsing, prefix parsing, config writing, host detection and report URL building.
2. Local capture of this repo's docs Storybook (420 stories, schemes `dark,light`, viewport 1280x900):
   - The old `vrtCapture.mjs` wrote 840 files. The new capture wrote 840 files with the same names.
   - Two consecutive runs of the new capture were byte-identical for all 840 PNGs.
   - 822 of 840 files were byte-identical to the old script's output. The old script uses Playwright 1.62 (Chromium 151) and the new one uses 1.63 (Chromium 153).
3. `actionlint` 1.7.12 reports no problems in the new workflow.
4. End-to-end on Forgejo 16.0.5 in a temporary public repository that imported this branch from the mirror, with `runsOn: '["vrt"]'`:
   - The push build captured 5 shots (4 Storybook shots and 1 shot from `captureCommand`), published the baseline, and posted `vrt` success.
   - A pull request that changed one story's color posted `vrt` failure: "2 changed, 3 unchanged". The job failed and one comment was posted. A second run edited that comment instead of adding a new one. The report URL returned 200.
   - The automatic job token posted the status and the comment. `VRT_STATUS_TOKEN` is only an optional override.
   - That run found a bug: the S3 plugin adds `https://` in front of `customDomain`. The fix is in this branch: `VRT_S3_PUBLIC_URL` can now be a bare host or a full URL.

A decision record and the input table in `packages/ci/README.md` describe the contract.

author: liinoorf
body:
`text-micro` se usaba en **20 lugares de 9 componentes** y **no estaba definida en ninguna parte**: ni en `tailwind-preset.cjs`, ni en un CSS del repo, ni por un plugin.

Comprobado corriendo Tailwind de verdad, no leyendo el código:

```
$ npx tailwindcss -c tailwind.config.cjs --content probe.html -o out.css
$ grep -c "text-micro" out.css
0
$ grep -A2 "\.text-dato" out.css
.text-dato { font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.4; }
```

Emite `.text-dato` y para `text-micro` **no emite una sola línea**.

## Qué se veía

Los 20 textos quedaban del tamaño que heredaban de su contenedor. Son todos metadatos secundarios — justo lo que tiene que leerse más chico:

- La hora de un mensaje y el «No llegó.» de una entrega fallida
- El peso de un adjunto en KB
- El nombre de la herramienta y del módulo en los pasos del Agente General
- «primera medición» y el delta de una evaluación
- «de 12 terminadas» en el logro del objetivo
- El estado de una corrida de IA que falló

En la bandeja, la hora competía en tamaño con el mensaje.

## Por qué nadie lo notó

Porque **no falla nada**. Tailwind ignora una clase que no conoce: build, lint y typecheck pasan. Es el mismo patrón que perseguimos acá —usado en un lado, declarado en ninguno— pero en CSS, donde no hay compilador que lo cace.

## El arreglo

Los 20 pasan a `text-rotulo` (0.75rem / 12px), que **ya está en la escala**. No se agrega un sexto tamaño: los cinco (`titulo`, `seccion`, `cuerpo`, `dato`, `rotulo`) son una decisión del documento de marca, y 12px es además el mínimo razonable para que un dueño de pyme lea la hora de un mensaje.

## La guarda

Cualquier `text-X` que no sea un tamaño de la escala, un color del preset o una alineación falla el PR. La lista permitida se construye **leyendo el preset**, no copiándolo: una copia envejece y termina marcando como inventada una clase que sí existe.

Eso pasó en la primera versión de la guarda, y lo dejo dicho porque es la parte instructiva: aplanaba los colores un solo nivel y marcó `text-sidebar-accent-foreground`, que **sí** existe (`sidebar.accent.foreground` en el puente shadcn). Ahora el aplanado es recursivo.

`pnpm typecheck` (54/54) · `pnpm lint` (0) · ui 55/55 · web 239/239

Closes #520

author: teamleaderleo
body: Carries the intent of #211 by @richardmilles onto current `main`, for #129. Credit for the design goes to them: an owner claim in each account file, and a refusal to refresh a chain another host owns. ## Problem Codex refresh tokens are single use. If an account's state file is copied to a second live server, both hosts redeem the same token, and the slower one burns the account with `refresh_token_reused` until someone signs in again. That is what took down every account behind sr.cmux.dev in #129. ## What changed - **Opt-in claim.** With `SUBROUTER_HOST_ID` set, saves stamp `hostClaim` onto Codex OAuth accounts, and `serve` stamps existing unclaimed accounts once at startup. - **Refusal before the token endpoint.** A refresh or `attest-legacy` of an account claimed by another host is refused before the token endpoint is contacted. So is any claimed account while this host has no identity. - **Failover.** The proxy treats that refusal as a terminal credential error, so selection fails over to other accounts. - **`sr switch`.** It refuses to export another host's chain to the Codex CLI, which would redeem the token itself. - **The claim follows the chain.** A save that keeps the refresh token keeps the claim. A save that installs a different refresh token moves the claim to this host, or drops it when this host has no id. That covers `sr add` re-login, `sr server sync`/`login` import, isolated re-enrollment and migration enrollment. Re-importing the same chain from `~/.codex/auth.json` does not move it. - **Docs:** a "Codex account host claims" section in `docs/production.md`. ## Differences from #211 - **Opt-in, with no hostname fallback.** #211 stamped the OS hostname by default. Every deployment would have switched on, and any host whose hostname changes (containers, laptops on a new network) would have refused to refresh every account. With the variable unset, nothing is stamped and nothing changes. - **No `--takeover` preflight on `sr server sync`/`login`.** Those commands no longer copy a live chain: the server attests every imported Codex credential by rotating it (`attestTenantCodexOAuth`), and `sync` only replaces missing or invalid accounts unless you pass `--all`/`--email` and confirm. A fresh login is the takeover. - **No unwired `TakeoverStoredOwner` and no epoch field.** The CodeRabbit threads on #211 about takeover atomicity and import intent don't apply to this design. - **Kept as is on `main`:** the `refresh_token_reused` status wording, since `main` already classifies it as terminal and re-add worthy. ## Known limit Suppose a store and a divergent `~/.codex/auth.json` are cloned together, and `sr switch` runs on the clone. The claim can then move with a token the source also holds. That record becomes `interactive-import`, and serving refuses it under `RequireIsolatedOAuth`. Claude accounts are not covered here. #129 also saw Claude `invalid_grant`, so that can follow as a separate change. ## Tests - `internal/accounts/codex_host_claim_test.go` covers: - off by default - the owner keeps its claim - a foreign or id-less host never reaches the token endpoint (refresh and attest-legacy) - the startup stamping pass - a fresh chain replaces a foreign claim - a same-chain active import keeps the claim - switch refuses a foreign chain - API keys never carry a claim - `TestIsTerminalCredentialError` has a case for the new error. - `TestMain` in `accounts`, `proxy` and `cmd/subrouter` unsets `SUBROUTER_HOST_ID`, so a developer shell can't leak into tests. - `gofmt`, `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` are clean, and `go test ./selectacct ./internal/... ./session ./cmd/subrouter` passes. - Four macOS VM, LaunchAgent and shell-stream tests in `cmd/subrouter` fail the same way on unmodified `main` on this host. - `gofmt -l .` also lists `cmd/subrouter/naked.go`, which is already unformatted on `main`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled. --- ## Summary by cubic Prevents copied Codex account state from burning refresh tokens when two live servers share it (#129). Refreshing an account another host claims is refused before the token endpoint is contacted, and the proxy fails over to other accounts instead. **Host claims** - Opt-in via `SUBROUTER_HOST_ID`; nothing is stamped while it is unset. - `serve` stamps existing accounts once at startup, and saves keep or move the claim with the refresh chain. - `sr switch` refuses to export a chain another host owns. - Fresh logins and imports move the claim; re-importing the same chain keeps it. **Credential behavior** - Refresh and `attest-legacy` refuse accounts claimed by another host, or by any host while this host has no identity. - The refusal is a terminal credential error, so selection fails over to other accounts. - API keys never carry a claim. author: dieterolson
body:
## Summary

This PR adds an exploratory Simscape workspace for epic #10950. It holds agent-editable, uniquely named (`GS3DX_`) clones of the hand-built `GolfSwing3D_Kinetic` model, in their own folder:
`src/engines/Simscape_Multibody_Models/3D_Golf_Model/matlab/exploratory_gs3dx/`.

The originals under `matlab/src/model/` are never loaded or saved. `test_gs3dx_safety` checks them against git HEAD.

- **#10951 scaffold:** path setup without `savepath`, a shadowing guard, a write guard that refuses unprefixed names, and headless clones with 12 subsystem references re-pointed.
- **#10952 regression harness:** 1 kHz flattened-bus comparison against a double-precision baseline of the original. `GS3DX_Baseline` matches all 413 signals and takes the same 4,236 steps.
- **#10953 block budget:** the Home license allows at most 1,000 non-virtual blocks (verified: 1,000 simulate, 1,001 fail at compile). The baseline uses 672.
- **#10954 `GS3DX_Slim`:** each joint torque axis is driven straight from its converter into the joint's InputTorque port, dropping the Ideal Torque Source, Interface and Reference. That takes the model from 672 to 609 blocks (63 saved). Slim matches the original on all 413 signals with the same 344 steps.
- **Regression drive:** the model's saved inputs produce an ill-conditioned swing. The clubhead passes 4 km/s, and a 1e-9 RelTol change moves it 2.4 m. That run can't tell a restructuring from rounding noise, so equivalence is now proven on `3DModelInputs_Impact.mat`, which is well conditioned. Tolerances are unchanged. Details are in `exploratory_gs3dx/docs/SENSITIVITY_FINDINGS.md`.
- **#10955 `GS3DX_Quat`:** both shoulders use a new `GS3DX_KDS_Spherical` subsystem. It swaps the Gimbal Joint for a Spherical Joint (quaternion state) and keeps the interface: the same torque inputs, mask parameters and 21 bus elements, through an Euler X-Y-Z ↔ quaternion mapping. Blocks go from 609 to 599.
- **#10956 quaternion hip:** the hip's Bushing Joint becomes a 6-DOF Joint (prismatics unchanged, quaternion rotation) through a shared swap core, `gs3dx_quaternion_swap`, and the 30-element HipLogs bus is kept. An isolated hip rig matches the Bushing to ≤ 1.9e-6 of peak. The full model still converges to Slim. Blocks go from 609 to 594. The mode-1 failure turned out to be the drive (hip torque about 2e7 N·m), not gimbal lock; the docs are corrected.
  - **Isolated torqued rig:** matches the Gimbal to ≤ 2e-7 of peak at RelTol 1e-8.
  - **Full model:** both hands hold the club, so the Low-priority right shoulder assembles to a different start state. With that state pinned, Quat converges to Slim as RelTol tightens: the clubhead gap is 13.9, 0.54 and 0.039 mm at 1e-3, 1e-5 and 1e-7. At every tolerance Quat is closer than Slim to the converged solution, and it takes 7–9% fewer steps. Details are in `exploratory_gs3dx/docs/QUATERNION_SHOULDERS.md`.
- **#10957 lower body (`GS3DX_FullBody`):** `gs3dx_build_lower_body` copies Quat and adds a `Lower Body` subsystem. It holds de Leva (80 kg, 1.80 m) thighs, shanks and feet on the existing KDS subsystems: Spherical hip, Revolute knee, Universal ankle. The legs attach to the measured pelvis frame (`gs3dx_stance_frames`). Blocks go from 594 to **751**, under the 900 cap (10% margin).
- **#10958 ground and integration:** each foot is framed rigidly to World at the start posture (weld stance). Because the welded legs close a loop through the pelvis joint, the hip carries no start target. FullBody starts in exactly Quat's state (to 3e-15), the knees assemble at −2θ, and the 0.3 s impact window completes in the same 348 steps.
  - The legs are passive (zero torque), so the pelvis diverges from Quat: up to 10° at 0.1 s, and the clubhead ends 0.52 m away. The right knee hyperextends to +67°. This is documented, and follow-up #10979 covers driving the legs and refitting the pelvis inputs.
  - A foot-contact trial (Infinite Plane plus Spatial Contact Force, not saved) costs +2 net blocks and 1.8× wall time.
  - Details are in `exploratory_gs3dx/docs/FULL_BODY.md`.
- **#10959 visual QA:** `gs3dx_layout_qa` renders diagrams headlessly to `docs/screenshots/` (PNGs force-added, since `*.png` is git-ignored there) and lists overlapping blocks. A Sonnet agent reviewed the renders. Its findings were fixed:
  - Actuator-torque labels were drawn once per line branch; they are now named on a virtual Demux.
  - One integrator overlapped labels.
  - The `Lower Body` placement is fixed.
  - Result: 0 block overlaps.
  - Two findings are inherited from the original and left as is: the dense top-level sensor bundle and the `HipLogs` fan-out.
  - Not done: a GUI open-check via computer use, which needs the owner to grant app access.
- **#10985 data audit** (`exploratory_gs3dx/docs/DATA_AUDIT.md`): `gs3dx_capture_stance` reads the tour-average C3D through ezc3d. It has 654 frames at 360 Hz and **no force-plate or analog data, so there is no ground reaction force to fit or validate against**. The leg markers are complete. The address stance (0.65 m ankle width, foot yaw −2.15° / +8.15°) now feeds `gs3dx_leg_table`. Conflicts found:
  - The upper body is 77.6 kg (the trunk alone is 60 kg against about 35 kg in de Leva), so FullBody weighs 109.4 kg. **This needs an owner decision.**
  - The foot and thigh marker proxies disagree with de Leva.
  - The impact drive's pelvis path is out of reach of planted feet (it would need 0.6–0.7 m of ankle drop).
- **#10986 ground contact (`GS3DX_FullBodyContact`, a copy of FullBody; FullBody is unchanged):**
  - The welds are replaced by three sole spheres per foot on one Infinite Plane, with smooth stick-slip friction.
  - The pelvis joint is unactuated: `NoTorque`, and its four drive converters are deleted.
  - A stance-hold leg servo drives every leg axis.
  - The feet sit at the captured stance through new FK/IK tools. The FK matches Simscape to 1e-9.
  - `gs3dx_contact_check` closes the momentum balance (contacts + gravity) within 1% of M·g·T.
  - **From rest the golfer stands:** the feet slip 2 mm and do not lift.
  - **With the impact drive the golfer tips over the right foot.** The drive starts with 131 N·s of sideways momentum, and changing the gains 20× makes no difference. That is the #10979 refit, not a contact problem. Details are in `exploratory_gs3dx/docs/GROUND_CONTACT.md`.
- **Block-budget correction:** the Home license counts the **compiled** model. FullBody is 751 blocks before compiling but 945 after (Quat goes from 594 to 740). The "751 under the 900 cap" line above therefore understates the real use: 945 of 1,000.
  - `gs3dx_block_budget(mdl, compiled=true)` now reports the compiled count.
  - FullBodyContact compiles to 967, with a 25-block reserve for validation sensors.
  - The existing FullBody test still caps the uncompiled count. I left it unchanged; a follow-up should decide the compiled cap.

## Validation

- R2025b, from an empty working folder: `runtests(fullfile(info.root,'tests'))` gives 70 passed, 0 failed. The capture tests need MATLAB `pyenv` with ezc3d and are skipped otherwise.
- The MATLAB tests are not part of the Python CI, which is unaffected.

Draft for owner review. The remaining epic work is #10979: a pelvis path from the capture, the upper-body refit on the contact model, time-varying leg references and an energy audit. It also depends on the trunk-mass decision.

## Typical Segment Masses (#11011)

- `GS3DX_Golfer`: the contact model with every segment mass from one de Leva table (80 kg). It is parameter-only: the block count is unchanged (967 compiled). The sensed mass is 80.393 kg; it was 109.4 kg. It stands from rest.

author: benjaminsqlserver
body:
## Summary

When an announcement is published, every parent and student in its audience who **still hasn't read it** gets an email and/or SMS pointing them back to the portal.

- **Queue on publish:** publishing (or creating with *Publish immediately*) writes one `AnnouncementNotification` row per recipient per channel. Recipients follow the portal visibility rules: `ALL` / `PARENT` / `STUDENT`, and `CLASS` → pupils actively enrolled in that class plus their linked parents. Only people with an active portal account are included.
- **Unread grace period:** rows wait `UnreadGraceMinutes` (default 120). At send time the dispatcher checks `AnnouncementReads` again, so anyone who read the notice in the portal is **Skipped**. Notices that were unpublished, deleted or expired, and inactive accounts, are skipped too.
- **Background dispatcher:** `NotificationDispatchWorker` (a `BackgroundService`) sends due rows in batches, each in a fresh DI scope. It saves after every row so a crash never re-sends a delivered message, and retries failures with back-off before marking them **Failed**.
- **Providers:** `Log` (default: writes messages to the app log and sends nothing), `Smtp` for email, `Termii` for SMS. Unknown provider names fail at startup.
- **Contacts:** parent email and phone fall back from the `Parent` record to the portal user. Nigerian numbers are normalised to `+234…`; invalid ones are treated as missing. SMS text fits one 160-character GSM-7 segment and keeps the portal link.
- **UI:**
  - The Announcements grid gets an *Email / SMS* status column (links to the log) and a **Notify now** button, which sends immediately without creating duplicates.
  - New **Notification log** page at `/announcements/notifications` (SuperAdmin, HeadTeacher): filters, the exact message sent, per-row retry, and **Retry all failed**.
- **Data:** `NotificationChannels` (EMAIL, SMS) and `NotificationStatuses` (PENDING, SENT, FAILED, SKIPPED) lookup tables are seeded on startup, following the project's no-enums rule. The new `AnnouncementNotifications` table has a unique `(AnnouncementId, UserId, NotificationChannelId)` index. The FK to `Users` is `Restrict` to avoid multiple cascade paths.
- **Migration:** `20260926040847_AnnouncementNotifications`, generated with `dotnet ef`. It only adds tables, and the model snapshot diff has no drift.
- **Docs:** README sections, `Sprint 11 - Implementation Guide` (`.md` + `.docx`) and `tools/generate_sprint11_guide.py`.

## Configuration

A new `Notifications` section in `appsettings.json`. Email and SMS both default to `Log`, so nothing real is sent until `Email:Provider` is set to `Smtp` and/or `Sms:Provider` to `Termii`. Put the SMTP password and Termii API key in user-secrets or environment variables, and set `PortalBaseUrl` so messages include the portal link.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet build NaijaPrimeSchool.slnx`: 0 errors (the 2 warnings are the existing NuGet advisories on `main`).
- [x] All migrations, including the new one, applied to an empty SQL Server 2022 database (Docker), and the lookup tables seeded.
- [x] Scratch console harness using the real `AddInfrastructure` wiring against that database: 19/19 checks passed. It covered:
  - queueing on publish and the grace-period hold;
  - `+234` normalisation;
  - a reader skipped;
  - notify-now counts with no duplicates;
  - SMS failure → retry → Failed → Retry all failed;
  - the class audience reaching only the enrolled pupil and their linked parent;
  - the ALL audience reaching everyone;
  - an unpublished notice's rows skipped;
  - a draft refused;
  - the grid counts;
  - log search.
- [x] Ran the web app and drove it with Playwright: logged in as SuperAdmin, pressed **Notify now**, the worker dispatched within one tick, and the Notification log rendered with no page errors.
- [ ] Not tested against a real SMTP server or Termii account (no credentials).

## Known limits

- The dispatcher assumes one app instance. Several web nodes on one database would need a row-claiming step.
- Families can't opt out yet; a preferences screen is on the roadmap.

author: alrafi34
body:
Fixes #38.

## Problem
Capacity was `floor(area / LAYOUT_FACTORS[layout])`, with fixed values of 300 / 275 / 250 / 350 sq ft. The Space Width, Space Length and Aisle Width inputs were never read. The table was also inverted: angled stalls need **more** area per car than 90°, so 45° reported the most cars.

## Change
- `areaPerStall()` uses the standard double-loaded bay geometry: each stall takes its width along the aisle × (its depth + half the aisle).
  - 90°: `w × (l + a/2)`
  - angle θ: `(w / sin θ) × (l·sin θ + w·cos θ + a/2)`
  - parallel: `l × (w + a/2)`
- The calculation runs in the lot's own unit (no more hidden ×10.764 round trip).
- Switching feet/meters converts the stall and aisle sizes. Presets and recommended aisles (stored in feet) are converted to the active unit, and "Per Space" shows sq m in meters mode.
- Choosing a layout sets its recommended aisle in the select's handler instead of an effect, so a preset's own aisle is no longer overwritten (compact 90° uses 22 ft).
- Stall sizes are validated, and a note says the result is net capacity, before entrances and landscaping.
- Page copy: the worked "core formula" counted a two-stall module as one stall (558 sq ft, "~35 stalls" on 20,000 sq ft). It now reads 279 sq ft per stall and ~71 stalls, and gives the angled formula.

## Verification
- Logic on a 90 × 60 ft lot: 90° 9×18 with a 24 ft aisle → **20** stalls (270 sq ft each); 8.5 ft stalls → **21**; 45° with a 13 ft aisle → **16** (325.7); 60° with an 18 ft aisle → 17 (302.3). The same lot entered in meters also gives 20.
- QA agent on a production build: **every phase passes (P1–P10)**, including all 3 P4 cases.
- While verifying, I found and fixed a QA-runner bug: P4 took the page inventory before Input Mode switched the form, so "Width (ft)" resolved to "Space Width (ft)". In the earlier run, the spec cases were therefore measured against the default 10,000 sq ft. The bug is fixed in ptb-qa-agent; the tool's defect was real regardless, and it is confirmed from the code.

author: bogdan-alexandrescu
body:
At most 500 files are uploaded from `$SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR` per attempt. The rest are counted in the result summary and every name is logged, a declared output is taken first, and a manifest name is bounded so the task document cannot pass 1 MiB at the cap.

Closes #228

## What the owner decided (2026-09-26, on #228) and what this does

- **The cap.** At most 500 files are uploaded from the artifacts folder (`artifact_manifest.MAX_FILES`, `WorkerConfig.max_artifact_files`). Files past it are not uploaded. `result_summary.artifacts_over_cap` counts them, beside `artifacts_cap_files`. Both keys are absent when every file fitted.
- **Every name is in the log**, 100 to a WARNING line headed `files in $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR were not uploaded`. It goes through `Worker._log_not_uploaded`, which is #225's batched loop moved out of `_upload_workdir_outputs`. Both caps log through that one helper, so there is no second copy.
- **The order**, explained next to the constant in `artifact_manifest.upload_order`:
  1. names a later step's `expected_outputs` declares. There are at most 49, because each dependant's `input_from` maps one upstream step to one filename, so they always fit;
  2. the platform's own files in the folder: the agent CLI's captures and transcript, and the harvest's patch;
  3. everything else, shallowest first and then by path. This is #225's working-folder rule.

  The byte cap is applied in the same order. The manifest is still listed by path, so the tab and the listing route's first page are unchanged.
- **The size bound.** Each entry carries its name twice, as `name` and at the end of `uri`. At GCS's 1,024-byte object name, 500 entries come to about 1 MB on their own. `artifact_manifest.MAX_NAME_BYTES = 256` holds them to 343 KiB at the longest ids a deployment makes. The document's worst case, input included, is about 833 KiB. The arithmetic is next to the constant.
  - A longer name is not uploaded. It is logged with its reason and listed in `artifacts_skipped`, cut short the way #225 cuts one.
  - This applies to a declared name too. It then fails its attempt as "written but not uploaded", not as "never written".
- **The pane.** Artifacts > Outputs shows "not uploaded from $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR" with the count and #225's count line: "N over the 500-file cap, named in the worker log". The cap is read from the summary. The count line is now one component, `InWorkerLog`, used by both blocks.

## Choices I made that the decision did not fix

- **256 bytes as the name bound.** 512 would take the worst case past 1 MiB. A path longer than 256 bytes in the artifacts folder is no longer uploaded; before this change it was.
- **Redaction covers only uploaded files.** The pre-upload redaction pass now scrubs only the files that will be uploaded, not the whole folder. A file past the cap is not rewritten, and it is not reported in `redaction_skipped` as "uploaded as-is". The agent CLI's captures are scrubbed either way, because a copy always goes to `logs/`.
- **The note on `artifacts_skipped` now reads "N skipped".** It used to read "N over cap". Its tooltip now names every reason a file lands there: the size cap, a name that is too long or not UTF-8, or a failed upload. Before this, it said "dropped at the size cap" even for upload failures and non-UTF-8 names.

## CI

- Red, tests only (c9d3751): application [36217544897](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/actions/runs/36217544897) failed. 7 worker tests failed, each for its own reason (no `max_artifact_files`, 600 / 604 / 1,203 uploaded where 500 were expected, the long name uploaded). 2 pane tests failed. The two controls passed: a folder under the cap, and a summary with no count.
- Green, fix (eed2a40): application [36218002412](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/actions/runs/36218002412) passed on every job: unit, UI typecheck and component tests (1417 passed), integration (emulator), shellcheck and manifests. Security passed on both commits.

## Not verified

- **No Firestore enforcement.** Nothing here ran against real Firestore or the emulator's 1 MiB check. The bound is measured with Firestore's documented size rules, in the test, against a store that renders the longest URI a deployment makes.
- **Nothing deployed.** No task has run with 6,000 files on Cloud Run.
- **The API was not changed.** A declared name longer than 256 bytes is still accepted at submission, and it now fails at run time.

Before: a customer on IPv6 could rotate addresses inside their /64 and get past the free reports' per-network cap and the invite same-network check, collecting repeated free full reports and referral credits. The early and late welcome refusals carry their reason into `&acct=preview_<reason>`, which the report page maps to fixed copy; unknown values show nothing. body:
