_Requested by **Nick** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_012M3UsTTV9HyJnE5GBt2MSN?thread=cmsg_012M3UsTTV9HyJnE5GBt2MSNSuLkwcCSFtnSfPHJuRtSwv)_

Batch D item 28, PLAYOFF-WEEK VALUE, **shadow**. Ready for batch D: head `340c6a52`, 6596 pass, 0 fail (49 skipped).

## Goal

Item 28: "weeks 15-17 matchup strength (from our 2026 data, research R6 as a tiebreaker) in the title sim's player value."

Before: nothing reads playoff-week opponents. `matchups.js` holds every matchup multiplier at 1 (MATCHUP_EVIDENCE, tested 2026-09-17: DvP did not beat no adjustment on held-out 2025; an early-season DvP read correlates r ~ 0.01 with weeks 15-17), and ONE-PLAN kills forward schedule strength (TM-12) and the playoff-week specialist (TM-19) on R6.

After: with `GRIDIRON_PLAYOFF_WEEK_VALUE=shadow`, plans.json gets `_run.inputs.playoff_week`: for Nick's roster and the entry's targets, each of the league's own playoff weeks with the opponent, the title sim's expected points that week, a same-season defense-vs-position multiplier and the points delta; plus the tiebreak it WOULD make among served targets tied within 1 SE (`applied: false`). A grader answers the one open question (does a same-season read taken at the deadline predict that season's playoff weeks?) against a bar fixed before any result.

How: `defenseRatios` reuses matchups.js's DvP method and its fitted K 200 on one season's lines strictly before this week; the points come from the base world's `weekData.expected` (season-sim, the one producer of weekly player points); one reader of `player_week_usage` serves both the block and the grader. No multiplier enters `season-sim.js#weekPool`; no target is reordered.

## Pre-registration

Committed in the RED commit `8dfee397` before any implementation: `docs/tdd/PLAYOFF-WEEK-VALUE-PREREG.md`.

- Metric: MAE change of (baseline x mult) vs baseline on weeks 15-17, baseline = the player's mean over weeks < 13 of the same season (at least 4 games), mult from that season's weeks < 13 only; paired bootstrap clustered by player, 2,000 iterations, seed 1, 90% CI. PPR.
- Pass bar: **P1** 2025 CI entirely below 0; **P2** 2023 and 2024 mean change <= 0; **P3** at least 300 graded player-weeks per season.
- What fails it: any of P1-P3. Prior evidence says it will fail; if so the flag stays shadow, the tiebreak stays logged-only, and item 28 closes as tested-not-supported.
- A pass would license only a follow-up that uses the delta as a tiebreaker on the served target order (R6), with its own bar, never a multiplier inside the title sim.

## Measured

Tree `b5d2ae85` (head `340c6a52`), base `origin/main` `b369c6bf`. Before -> after:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| served numbers, flag off | n/a | byte-identical (T5: no hook, no `playoff_week` key) |
| served numbers, flag on | n/a | identical outside `_run` (T5: `strip(on) == strip(off)`, and `_run` differs only by `inputs.playoff_week`) |
| grader power, synthetic real effect (0.35) | no grader | PASS: MAE change 2023 -0.151 [-0.167, -0.135], 2024 -0.136 [-0.151, -0.121], 2025 -0.141 [-0.154, -0.128] |
| grader, synthetic no effect | no grader | FAIL: P1 2025 CI [-0.0072, +0.0011]; P2 2023 +0.0028 |
| real-data grade | none | **not measured here** (no league database in the cloud), see below |

Checks (on `340c6a52`):
- `npm ci`: ok
- `node --test test/playoff-week-value.test.js`: 15 pass, 0 fail
- `npm test`: 6646 tests, **6596 pass, 0 fail, 49 skipped**, 0 cancelled (one pre-existing TODO, U1b bar 3)
- `npm run check:wiring`: exit 0, no missing-feed findings
- `npm run typecheck`: clean
- `npm run lint`: clean (1596 files)
- `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`: 8 files, only this unit's

## Flag

`GRIDIRON_PLAYOFF_WEEK_VALUE`: unset / `0` = off (plans.json byte-identical); `shadow` or `1` = the block is computed after planning and written to `_run.inputs.playoff_week`. Preview mode never turns it on. No served mode exists in this PR.

## Not confirmed

- Whether a same-season read beats no adjustment on real seasons: the real grade needs the local nflverse tables.
- The baseline in the grade is the player's same-season mean, not the live weekly blend MATCHUP_EVIDENCE used; it isolates the matchup read but is a simpler forecast.
- "Research R6" is read here as "schedule strength as a tiebreaker only" (ONE-PLAN's R6 kills); I could not open R6 itself.
- League 4's playoff weeks come from the world (`prep.bracketWeeks`), so a two-week-round league reads its own weeks; only fixture leagues were run.

## Needs local measurement

```
SCHEDULER_DISABLED=1 node scripts/rnd/playoff-week-grade.mjs --seasons 2023,2024,2025 --as-of 13
SCHEDULER_DISABLED=1 GRIDIRON_PLAYOFF_WEEK_VALUE=shadow node scripts/campaign/produce-plans.mjs --leagues 4
```
The first prints `verdict` and each season's MAE change with its CI (counts only, no ids). The second writes `_run.inputs.playoff_week`; check `status: ok`, `ratios.lines` > 0 (2026 weeks 1-2 today) and `tie_break.applied: false`.

## Benchmarks

Flag off: zero cost. Flag on: one `player_week_usage` read for this season (weeks before now) plus a pass over ~20-40 players x 3 weeks after planning. Not timed here (fixture adapter only); the local producer run above shows it in its total.

## Self-check

- Rule 5 (one producer): points are the world's `weekData.expected`; DvP method and K are matchups.js's; one reader for block and grader. Tests T3 and the reader test.
- Unproven pieces move no served number: tiebreak `applied: false`, served targets untouched (T4); entry outside `_run` identical with the flag on (T5).
- Rule 1 / privacy: block carries ids only, no `name` fields (T6); the grader prints counts and MAEs only.
- Rule 6 (Nick's rules): this unit adds no candidate, give or get and reorders nothing, so never-give.js, the 83+ floor, 277/160/80 and the overpay cap are untouched; it only reads `entry.targets`, which are already rule-filtered.
- Errors handled: missing table is `no_read` with a reason (T6); a throwing read is `status: error`, logged, and the league still plans (T5). No bare catch.

author: adsharma
body:
Commit 6cd21a2b1 switched `Int128_t::addInPlace`/`subInPlace` to an `__int128` intermediate so cases like `INT64_MIN + -1 + 1` don't overflow `int64` before the carry is applied (UBSan).

MSVC has no `__int128`, so the Windows build fails:

```
src/common/types/int128_t.cpp(104): error C4235: nonstandard extension used: '__int128' keyword not supported on this architecture
```

This broke ladybug-nodejs CI: https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug-nodejs/actions/runs/36214551510/job/108327816243?pr=25 (PR #25, windows-latest fails at `[413/1130] ... int128_t.cpp.obj`, other platforms green).

This PR replaces the `__int128` intermediate with small portable helpers (`addInt64WithCarry`/`subInt64WithBorrow`) using only well-defined unsigned wrapping arithmetic plus sign analysis. No behavior change on GCC/Clang.

Verification:
- Exhaustive edge values x carry/borrow plus 2M random pairs checked against the `__int128` reference: 4,000,676 cases, 0 mismatches.
- `ninja -C build/release test/common/types_test` passes (14/14 Int128/Uint128 tests).

author: jonsmithtlt
body:
## Summary

M1 of the Agent Engineering Workflow is a deterministic state engine and CLI (`aew`). It proves **one complete serial Ticket lifecycle** under the frozen spec set `aew-frozen-2026-09-25` (Workflow Contract v0.7, Knowledge Contract v0.4):

```text
init → Ticket + accepted plan → bounded implementer pack → implement + local checks
→ independent (R1) review → verification against the evaluated snapshot → COMMIT_READY
→ controlled integration → post-integration verification → DONE
→ destroy the Lead session → reconstruct from durable state → continue
```

It also covers the three required failure cases: an **unintegrated dependency** stays BLOCKED, **stale evidence** stops satisfying its gate while the history is kept, and a **crash or superseded Lead** cannot corrupt state.

The approved plan is in `docs/implementation/m1-implementation-plan.md`. Spec gaps and their operator-approved resolutions are in `docs/implementation/ambiguity-report.md`.

## What's in it

| Area | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Frozen spec pin | `docs/`, `docs/spec-pin.yaml`, `tests/test_spec_pin.py` | The spec docs are unchanged; hashes are pinned. The local tag `aew-spec-frozen-2026-09-25` is **not pushed** yet. |
| Crash-safe control state | `engine/store.py`, ADR-0001 | A single atomic commit point with a checksum trailer, staged multi-file writes, an OS advisory lock, and compare-and-swap on the revision |
| Lead authority + credentials | `engine/authority.py`, `engine/lead_ops.py`, `operator.py`, ADR-0005 | Only verifier hashes are stored; a generation guard; handoff; **takeover requires operator confirmation at an interactive terminal** (no flag or env var can authorize it) |
| Work graph + state machine | `engine/work_ops.py`, `engine/transitions.py`, ADR-0003 | Every transition names the only operation allowed to perform it; readiness is recomputed on every Lead commit |
| Evaluated snapshots + workspaces | `snapshot/fingerprint.py`, `workspace/`, ADR-0002 | A git tree fingerprint built in a temporary index, excluding `.aew/`; a worktree per mutating Ticket; a strict serial cap |
| Evidence, gates, review/verify, classification | `engine/evidence_ops.py`, `engine/gates.py`, `policy/` | The engine binds each result to a snapshot and applies review/verify results mechanically; the Lead alone classifies verification failures |
| Context packs / launch contracts | `knowledge/context.py`, `engine/context_ops.py` | Deterministic packs; the reviewer pack excludes implementer reasoning |
| Controlled integration | `engine/integration_ops.py`, `workspace/integration.py`, ADR-0004 | Validate, then publish with `git update-ref <branch> M H` (atomic compare-and-swap) under the control lock; interrupted publishes can be reconciled |
| Role archetypes + role cards | `roles/`, `engine/role_ops.py`, ADR-0006 | Operator clarification: a catalog ("deck") of cards, each extending one archetype and unable to widen its authority; per-Ticket role plans; per-card gates; each invocation pins the card version it used |
| Resume / next actions / checkpoint | `engine/resume_ops.py` | The Lead resume pack in KC §15.1 order, plus a list of detected contradictions |

## How to review

The commits are ordered by plan step, so reviewing **commit by commit** is easiest: 0 spec pin → 1 skeleton → 2 schemas → 3 store → 4 authority → 5 work graph → 6 snapshots/workspaces → 7 evidence/gates → 8 context packs → UTF-8 fix → 9 integration → 8b role cards → 10–12 resume/AT-1/docs.

Suggested focus, highest risk first:
1. `engine/store.py`: the commit/recovery ordering and roll-forward rules.
2. `engine/integration_ops.py`: the compare-and-swap happens under the lock with authority re-verified; the worktree sync touches only changed paths.
3. `engine/authority.py` + `operator.py`: stale-writer ordering (the authority check comes before any state-dependent answer) and the operator channel.
4. `engine/gates.py` + `evidence_ops.py`: CURRENT vs STALE semantics, and which fields the engine owns.
5. `roles/__init__.py` + `engine/role_ops.py`: escalation rejection and the role-selection precedence.

## Tests

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]"
python -m pytest -q                  # 477 tests
python -m pytest -m acceptance -q    # 37 acceptance scenarios (AT-1…AT-7, KC §26), mapped in docs/implementation/acceptance.md
```

- **Linux** (WSL Ubuntu 22.04, Python 3.11, ext4): 477 passed, including operator takeover through a real pseudo-terminal.
- **Windows** (Python 3.13): 476 passed, 1 skipped (the POSIX pseudo-terminal test). AT-1's takeover step substitutes the terminal channel in-process on Windows, so no console appears on the desktop.
- Persistence is tested with real `os._exit` crashes at every fault point, 200 randomized crashes, 2 processes × 50 racing writers, and crashes at 4 publish points followed by reconcile.
- Every scenario drives the real CLI in separate processes against real git repos. Roles are scripted drivers that use only the launch contract, their credential and the CLI.
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs ubuntu/py3.11 and windows/py3.13.

## Known limits (intentional for M1)

- **Credentials are not an OS security boundary.** All roles run as the same OS user. A same-user agent that deliberately fakes a terminal or patches the process is outside the M1 threat model (ADR-0005).
- **Operator role-plan pins** recorded through the Lead are attribution, not proof (ADR-0006).
- **Mutating concurrency is hard-capped at 1.** Isolation and CAS publishing exist, but concurrent integration is M5.
- **Story/Epic handling and non-mutating Tickets are Staged.** They come in M2, which is also required before the SPT backlog can be imported. Investigator/researcher/planner cards validate now but are dispatched in M2.
- **No live-harness run yet.** Roles are scripted; the OpenCode adapter is M3.
- Full status is in `docs/implementation/implementation-status.md`.

## Commit notes

`5f1c806` (step 8) was committed while a Windows-only test was failing. That was a real bug: piped CLI output crashed on the Windows code page. It is fixed in the next commit, `c8aab08`. Later commits are gated on pytest's own exit code.

author: alij021
body:
Web refunds now wait for an independent, authorized human decision before changing accounting or stock. API keys and PIN sessions cannot approve them; terminal decisions are checked before parsing legacy amounts, preserving conflict semantics on replay. The connector tracks pending/rejected decisions. New draft lines snapshot the price at addition while existing line prices remain unchanged; purchase receipt posting rejects one SKU at inconsistent rates.

The reconciled security fixes also cover permission changes, PIN restrictions, camera/WASM lifecycle, webhook/SSRF handling, sensitive logs, restore failure propagation, session lock acknowledgement, treasury replay identity, and the existing barcode-label limit. PR #93 behavior is preserved. Migrations 075, 077, and 078 were rehearsed against a restored database that already had 076, including repeated migration and historical-data fingerprints.

Validation on head `8e375e1e4234bde679ade0ffc4d14443fd39a1c9` (tree `903b97d337edca0755f3539b7068763bf78650ba`): [CI run 36217547933](https://github.com/AliJ021/labelmod-core/actions/runs/36217547933), all four jobs successful. API 780/780 with owner and 780/780 with restricted role; web unit 237/237; Chromium/WebKit 864/864; PHP suites 122/68/46/63 assertions; SQL, lint, typecheck, production dependency audit, builds and image checks passed. An independent isolated run on the identical tree also passed both API roles, SQL, web and PHP suites. A real-data isolated clone passed migration/repeat checks and internal-network HTTP API password/TOTP/session/refund-inbox smoke using a temporary clone-only account.

Earlier failed executions are retained as failures. The full-day receipt fixture now explicitly verifies rejection of the disallowed receipt and uses two valid receipts without dropping its accounting assertions. Two environment failures (missing PHP mbstring and PostgreSQL client/server mismatch) were corrected before the complete rerun. No assertions were relaxed or tests skipped.

This PR does not close the entire imported security backlog. Gift-fee account/tax policy, other reported permission/history/offline-queue issues, physical equipment acceptance and real SMS/bank delivery remain outside this change. Production deployment and connector installation are separate pending operations; no real payment or SMS was performed.

## RFC v26.9.26 implementation lane

Semantic root: https://github.com/seanchatmangpt/chatman-ecosystem/pull/296

Own deterministic qualification/architecture receipts, exact-subject standing, replay, supersession and independent evidence without granting DO authority.

This seed PR intentionally starts with a repo-local machine-oriented implementation charter at `docs/rfc/v26.9.26/abb-sbb-implementation.md`. Follow-on agents should implement the charter against this exact branch/head rather than inventing a parallel EA model.

### Cross-repo invariants
- Strategy != OperatingModel != Capability != Requirement != ABB != ArchitectureContract != SBB != Pack != Artifact.
- Candidate != truth != authority != DO != standing.
- Reuse -> compose -> extend -> invent.
- UNKNOWN stays first-class.
- Exact subject/provenance is mandatory for qualification.
- Qualification never grants consequential authority.
- Consume the canonical EA semantics from chatman-ecosystem PR #296; do not fork semantic ownership.

### Definition of done
The repository-specific DoD is committed in the implementation charter. The next agent should expand executable code/TTL/tests until that DoD is satisfied, then provide exact-head falsifiers, receipts/replay, downstream witness, and scoped standing.

This is an implementation seed, not a claim of RFC completion.

author: caomyer
body:
## Intent Two improvements to the UI, to be built as one PR: 1. When I answer a call from Bearings, the call rendered in our chat is plain text. I think we can reuse some of the rendering card solution we built for the answered call and comments when the artifact is reviewed. 2. When a new call needs my review, you usually just say what needs me in plain text, but the UI selector is not present. You can present a similar typed choice in the message so that the decision can be made directly in our chat. I reviewed the design and approved it with no comments, and answered `two-cards`: build as mocked, so the call card stays where it was raised, shrunk to one line, and a full answer card replaces my plain-text answer where I gave it. ## What Changed - A call from the snapshot's `calls[]` now appears in the chat as a card where it was raised, placed by `raised_at` through `pagePlaces`. Only calls raised in the last day show there. While a call is open, its card offers Bearings' own answer form (options, words, or a dated Not now) and answers through the same intake. Once the call is recorded, held, closed, or answered in a page's review, the card shrinks to one line, and the question and options stay one click away. If the options change after the call was raised, or a pick is no longer offered, the card says so. If the call was answered somewhere else while the captain was typing in the card, the unsent draft is kept and can be moved to the composer. - The captain's plain-text answer messages are now drawn as answer cards where the answer was given, and the text the first mate was sent stays one click away. The chat reads these messages back through the new `answerOfMessage`, which parses the app's own answer and reply lines. How far an answer has got (recorded, still with the first mate, held, or asked again) comes from `callStanding`, now shared by Bearings and the chat. The card logic is in `src/callviews.ts`, the cards are drawn by `src/CallCards.tsx`, and both have styles in `src/styles.css`. - `src/fixtures/call-messages.json` pins the answer-line format against `review.rs`. The mock moves a call's times only as `fm-captain-hold.sh` does. `AGENTS.md` now documents all of this. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The round-1 fix (sameWords) normalizes whitespace like review.rs shorten() and matches a cut message by prefix. body:
Queue tests built solely with candidate code can miss upgrade regressions. These tests extract pinned Codex 0.6.0, 0.6.1, 0.7.0 and 0.8.0 code, create their actual durable queue state, and pass it to the candidate. Acknowledged and pending cases check byte-identical retries, unstaged history, repeated messages, sequence/generation preservation, interrupted legacy migration, queue-copy reopen and authorized baseline recovery.

The new cases also exposed recovery accepting unsupported cursor metadata, including from a published transaction without cursor.json. Recovery now validates all durable cursor candidates before publishing, observing consent, cleaning staging state or draining. Unsupported formats hold without changing queue content or sending data; diagnostics remain writable.

Stacked on #76. CI fetches full history and runs the released-state matrix in its existing Node 20/22 jobs. Missing pins fail rather than skip tests. This is queue-format coverage, not a guarantee about arbitrary releases, installed hooks, consent/shared-auth migration or deployed backends. The proposed shared compatibility policy lives in the Claude ADR change.

Validation: 601 Node tests plus version/manifests pass on the feature; four unsupported-format cases were reproduced before the fix (three accepted incompatible state; one already refused with a generic error). Final test-only adjustment permits capture-status diagnostics when composed with #71; focused cases pass again. Combined with #70/#71, all 617 Node tests and the pinned collector #44 / reader #168 contract pass through stored-record equality and normalization. The existing harness also passes its scripted-analysis/schema checks; it does not certify live reporting. The merge resolution retains capture-phase health recording for unsupported-cursor-format.

author: ahoo-wang
body:
**Stacked on #3597 (R5).** This PR's own change is the top commit `120a44452`. After #3597 squash-merges I will rebase with `git rebase --onto origin/main 338971ecc`.

R7: performance and polish, invisible to TS. The descriptor JSON, REST shapes, error codes and statuses are unchanged: the REST error golden, the route inventory and the OpenAPI snapshots all pass without updates. Each review finding was re-checked against the post-R5 code before acting on it.

## What changed

### Performance
1. **Schema GET.** The descriptor and its `sha256` version are described once per schema instance, keyed by budget, `defaultListSize` and zone. A new schema version is a new instance, so a 304 no longer rebuilds or rehashes the descriptor. The cache is bounded at 16 keys, and the hex encoding uses `HexFormat`.
2. **Dynamic-key fields** (ABAC `tags.<key>`, map keys). These were re-resolved on every lookup, so the finding held. They are now cached per schema with their compiled capability record. Keys come from callers, so the cache is bounded at 1024; beyond that a field is resolved per lookup.
3. **`SchemaMasker`.** The mask values of an array's items (`withMask` plus a UNION of the allowed items) were rebuilt for every masked array node. They are now a lazy property of `QueryMaskValue`, computed once per mask value.
4. **ES grouped aggregation.** A `First(limit)` window whose limit fits in one composite page is now a single search, with no point in time opened or closed. Multi-page windows keep the PIT.
5. **`QueryLogObserver`.** Rejections the caller can fix are logged at DEBUG, message only: catalog violations and the missing authenticated scope. Server faults stay at ERROR, message only. Any other failure is logged at ERROR with its stack trace.
6. **Relative time.** Zone ids and date patterns are parsed once each, in bounded caches of 256 per kind in wow-api. The normalizer uses the new `RelativeTimeFilter.resolvedZoneId()`. POJO operands are converted with `valueToTree` once per value; before, it ran once per domain and type.
7. **`HttpQueryGuard`.** With `maxListSize = 0` (cap off), JSON lists were buffered with `collectList` and no bound. They now stream. The cost is that a late failure then truncates the response instead of turning it into an error body; with the cap on, buffering is unchanged and holds at most the cap.
9. **`QueryMetricsObserver`.** Timers and summaries are cached per tag set, since tags are bounded, instead of being built and registered for every query.
10. **Small ones.**
    - An empty ES projection reuses one `SourceFilter`.
    - `simplifyAnd` and `simplifyOr` skip the flattening copy when there is nothing to flatten.

### Polish
11. **Exhaustive `when`s** replace silent `else` branches in:
    - the resolver's `domainValues`;
    - `QueryFieldAliases.filter`;
    - the ES page `bucketWidth`, now a per-metric `subBuckets`.
12. **Policy order.** `QueryPolicy`s now run in `sortedByOrder` order, like `QueryFilter`, and the KDoc says so. Unordered policies keep their registration order.
14. **Narrower public API.** These are now `internal`, after checking every module, the benchmarks, the TCK, `example/` and the docs: `DenseFill`, `DateHistogramFill`, `DatePartFill`, `BoundedTopRows`, `matchesHaving`, `EmptyAggregationValues` and `FilterExpression.withCanonicalFields`.
15. **Docs.** The design doc's decision log gains the R5 row: server faults answer 500 as a defect fix.

## Didn't hold / dropped
- **#8, `QueryBodyExtractor` decoding twice.** Reading the body as an `ObjectNode` first is what yields `EMPTY_BODY`, `BODY_NOT_OBJECT` and `INVALID_JSON` with their current texts, which the REST golden freezes. Decoding straight into the POJO would turn those into `INVALID_VALUE`/`UNKNOWN_*`, a visible change, so it was not done.
- **#13, `QueryValueSchema` hand-copied in three places.** Only one full copy is left (`withMask`); R3 and R4 removed the others. No `copy()` was needed.
- **#15, the stale "compatibility contract" KDoc in `QueryViolation`.** R5 already rewrote it.

## Gates
Local, one gradle run at a time via heavy.sh; everything below exited 0.
- `check`: `:wow-api`, `:wow-query`, `:wow-webflux`, `:wow-spring`, `:wow-spring-boot-starter`, `:wow-tck`, `:wow-schema`, `:wow-mongo`, `:wow-elasticsearch`, `:wow-openapi`.
- Benchmarks: `:wow-benchmarks:jmhClasses` and `:wow-benchmarks:detekt`.
- Java test compiles: `:wow-query:compileTestJava` and `:wow-core:compileTestJava`.
- Integration test compiles: `:wow-mongo` and `:wow-elasticsearch`.
- Query integration tests:
  - Mongo: 194 passed.
  - ES: 209 run, 8 skipped, 0 failed.

JMH was not run because the machine is shared. The relevant benchmarks (schema/descriptor, SchemaProtection, aggregation compiler) compile.

## Release notes
- The JSON list response of an HTTP query route streams when `wow.query.http.max-list-size=0`. It no longer buffers without bound.
- Client-caused query rejections now log at DEBUG instead of ERROR.
- `QueryPolicy` beans are ordered by `@Order`.
- `DenseFill`, `BoundedTopRows`, `matchesHaving`, `EmptyAggregationValues` and `withCanonicalFields` are now internal. They had no users outside wow-query.

author: hansfbaier
body:
The lazily-built-chipdb rule derives the die from `PART` with the same device
class nextpnr's parser uses, so it has to know the Zynq-7000S die names, whose
trailing `s` is part of the die name. Without them `xc7z007sclg400-1` resolved
to the nonexistent die `xc7z007` and the generator was invoked with
`--device xc7z007`, which has no `tilegrid.json`:

```
$ PART=xc7z007sclg400-1
$ echo ${PART} | sed -E 's/^(xc7(s[0-9]+t?|a[0-9]+t|k[0-9]+t|z[0-9]+t?|v[xh]?[0-9]+t)).*/\1/'
xc7z007
$ ... xilinx_gen.py --xray .../zynq7 --device xc7z007 --bba xc7z007sclg400.bba
FileNotFoundError: .../zynq7/xc7z007/tilegrid.json
```

## The fix

Add the dies ahead of the generic class and alias `xc7z007s` to the `xc7z010`
database, as `toolchain-nix/nix/nextpnr-chipdb.nix` and
`himbaechel/uarch/xilinx/xilinx.cc` now do. `\d+[st]?` is deliberately not
used: it would break `xc7z030sbg485-1`, whose `s` belongs to the package
`sbg485`.

## Verification

- Recipe body run with `make` for each part name:

  | PART | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | `xc7z007sclg400-1` | `xc7z007` | `xc7z010` |
  | `xc7z007sclg225-2` | `xc7z007` | `xc7z010` |
  | `xc7a35tcsg324-1` | `xc7a35t` → `xc7a50t` | unchanged |
  | `xc7z030sbg485-1` | `xc7z030` | unchanged |
  | `xc7vx485tffg1761-2` | `xc7vx485t` | unchanged |
  | `xc7s50csga324-1` | `xc7s50` | unchanged |

- Sweep over every part name in prjxray-db: nothing but the four `xc7z007s`
  parts changes.

## Dependencies

Only the *lazily built* path is affected — CI pre-builds the chipdbs and sets
`CHIPDB`, so this rule never fires there. It needs the `xc7z007s` part
directories from openXC7/prjxray-db#29 to be reachable, and the chipdb it
builds comes from openXC7/toolchain-nix's derivation, which needs its matching
change. The device-parser change is in openXC7/nextpnr.

## Summary by Sourcery

Fix lazy chip database generation for Zynq-7000S parts by recognizing their complete die names and applying the xc7z007s database alias.

Bug Fixes:
- Resolve Zynq-7000S part names to the correct die when lazily generating chip databases, including mapping xc7z007s to the xc7z010 database.

Enhancements:
- Align openXC7.mk device matching with supported parser die names while preserving package-specific part handling.

Tests:
- Verify die resolution across representative Xilinx parts and sweep all prjxray-db part names to confirm only the intended xc7z007s mappings change.

author: tomaasz
body:
## CI is red on `main`, and has been for a week

The `Build & Security Scan` job fails at `Run pre-commit hooks on all files`. The hook is `end-of-file-fixer`, and eight files end with a blank line instead of a single newline:

```
.agents/skills/nextjs-app-router/SKILL.md
.agents/skills/tailwind-hermes-ui/SKILL.md
.agents/skills/vercel-deploy/SKILL.md
.claude/agents/architect.md
.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md
.claude/agents/debugger.md
.claude/agents/security-reviewer.md
.claude/agents/test-writer.md
```

All eight came in with [`5b3fdc0`](https://github.com/tomaasz/gotovalues-site/commit/5b3fdc0db9afcecd87ad7b48c04161d084aadd84) ("feat: add Vibe Coding hero and benefits section and configure AI agent harness"). `end-of-file-fixer` rewrites files in place and then exits non-zero, so the job dies on the *first* run and stays dead until the files are committed in their fixed form.

`main` runs **649 through 654 all fail this way**. The last green `main` run was at `1b39144` ([#316](https://github.com/tomaasz/gotovalues-site/pull/316)). Every PR opened or brought up to date since has inherited it — [#312](https://github.com/tomaasz/gotovalues-site/pull/312) is where I hit it.

## Change

Exactly what the hook does itself: drop the trailing blank line. Eight files, eight deleted lines, no content touched.

## Verification

`pre-commit` run locally against the real `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

**Before** — reproduces CI exactly, naming the same eight files:

```
check for merge conflicts................................................Passed
check for added large files..............................................Passed
fix end of files.........................................................Failed
- hook id: end-of-file-fixer
- exit code: 1
- files were modified by this hook
```

**After:**

```
check for merge conflicts................................................Passed
check for added large files..............................................Passed
fix end of files.........................................................Passed
trim trailing whitespace.................................................Passed
Reject backup / temp / cache files.......................................Passed
```

`end-of-file-fixer` is the only violation in the tree. `trailing-whitespace` flags nothing — the only files with trailing whitespace are binaries (`favicon/*`, `public/images/og.png`), which the hook skips.

## Why this is a separate PR

It is `main`'s breakage, not any one PR's, and it unblocks all of them at once. Folding eight whitespace-only lines into a dependency PR would have hidden a week-old base-branch failure inside an unrelated diff.

## Follow-up worth considering

The hooks only run in CI. Nothing installs them locally, so `pre-commit install` never happened for whoever committed `5b3fdc0` — which is why a hook that exists specifically to prevent this did not. A line in `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` under the verification commands, or a `prepare` script running `pre-commit install`, would close that gap. Say the word and I'll add it.

author: iamwhatever
body:
## Problem / Motivation

A one-time dashboard login link could be used as a session cookie. The link is printed, posted to chat and kept in logs, and it carries a 20-hour `session_exp`. Anyone who read it could put it in `Cookie: mc_token_<port>` and get a full 20-hour session, without ever clicking it. The same link sent as `?token=` on an internal path was also checked by the 20-hour session rule instead of the short link rule.

## Why it matters

Login links leak by design: into chat history, terminal scrollback and the journal. Today each leaked link is a 20-hour session for whoever finds it, and a link never clicked is never used up.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

| Token | Cookie before | Cookie after |
|---|---|---|
| Login link | accepted, 20 h | refused |
| Session from a link exchange | accepted | accepted |
| Session from refresh | accepted | accepted |
| App token | accepted | accepted |

Only a real session is now accepted as a session. `generate_token` in `src/kiro_crew/dashboard/token_auth.py` takes `session=True`, which stamps a signed `kind=session` claim. The two session mints pass it: the middleware's link exchange and the refresh rotation in `handlers/auth_refresh.py`. `validate_token_with_app` refuses, on the session path, any token without that claim unless it is an app token. The rule is an allow-list, so links signed before this upgrade, which carry no claim at all, are refused too. `kind` is reserved, so `extra` cannot set it.

On internal paths, a `?token=` link that is not a session gets the normal link rules: its short click window and a live nonce.

Remote instances used to send the minted link straight as the peer's cookie. `src/kiro_crew/instances/ssh_tunnel_manager.py` now trades the link for the peer's session cookie with `GET /api/status?token=`, as a browser does. The trade runs as soon as a link is stored (connect, re-mint, self-heal), while the link is inside its click window, and the session is cached against that link. A request that finds no cached session trades lazily; a trade the peer refuses (401 or 403) sends no cookie, so the existing single re-mint runs. A trade that cannot reach the peer, gets any other status, or gets no session back, fails as "could not exchange the credential with the peer" and does not spend the re-mint. The cache is cleared on teardown. `docs/system-specs/modules/dashboard-token-auth.md`, `docs/system-specs/modules/instances.md` and the `src/kiro_crew/security/redaction.py` comment name the new transport and claim.

This covers the bug in #12503 as well: after the link is exchanged, the connection kept resending a link that no longer worked. Here the exchanged session cookie is kept and reused.

## Backwards compatibility

Breaking: every cookie issued before the upgrade carries no `kind=session` claim and is refused once. Browsers with a refresh cookie recover by themselves: the 403 carries `X-Auth-Required`, the SPA calls `/api/auth/refresh`, and that endpoint does not need the old cookie. Tailnet QR phone sessions have no refresh cookie and must scan the QR again. An old local instance talking to a new remote fails its multi-instance requests until the local side is upgraded; a new local with an old remote works.

Writer sweep on origin/main @ 47594b8390: the only session mints are `token_auth.py` (link exchange) and `handlers/auth_refresh.py` (refresh rotation); both pass `session=True`. Every other `generate_token` caller (mobile, tailnet, core, Slack, Teams, Telegram, Webex) mints links. Electron, Mochi, `pod api` and the E2E helpers obtain links and exchange them through the same middleware. App tokens are unchanged.

## Tests

- `test/test_token_auth.py`: an unclicked link is refused as a cookie; a token with no claim is refused on the session path; skipping nonce registration does not make a session; the exchange mints a session the cookie path accepts; `extra` cannot set or strip `kind`; app tokens are not treated as links; an internal-path `?token=` link gets link rules.
- `test/test_instances.py`: the link is traded at connect while fresh; a session obtained at mint time survives a blocked re-mint (reconfiguring, mint failure); a re-mint trades its new link at once; an exchange raced by a re-mint does not displace it; the link is exchanged once per minted link; a refused exchange sends no link and re-mints once; an unreachable exchange or a peer error (500, 302) reports its own error and does not re-mint.
- `test/test_session_transfer.py`, `test/test_security.py`, `test/test_remote_crew_capabilities.py`, `test/test_instances_search_federation.py`: fixtures updated to mint sessions or stub the exchange.

`prove.py` fails the new tests with the production change reverted.

## Manual verification

Upgrade recovery, run against real code on both sides with one shared signing secret: `main`'s middleware exchanged a login link and set an access cookie plus a refresh cookie. This branch's middleware then refused that access cookie (403, `X-Auth-Required`). `POST /api/auth/refresh` with the old refresh cookie returned 200 and a new access cookie carrying `kind=session`, which this branch then accepted (200). The browser-side step is the existing `checkSessionExpired` → `attemptSilentRefresh` path in `website/src/api/client.ts`; it was read, not driven in a browser.

## Related Issues

no linked issue: reported privately as a security finding. Supersedes the fix in #12503.

## Pattern harvest

Rule candidate: review-prompt
Pattern: a credential printed for humans must not be accepted on the path that checks long-lived sessions; long-lived acceptance needs a positive claim, not the absence of a negative one.

## Checklist

- [x] At most two commits (one is the norm), with a Conventional Commits title (`feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore|ci|build|revert: ...`)
- [x] Existing tests pass and new tests added for new functionality
- [x] Self-review completed; code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or internal references in the diff

(utah-packages#269). They were the missing dependencies of:

- printing: cups, cups-client, cups-ipptool (cups needs cups-filters ->
  libppd -> ghostscript). cups.socket and cups.path are enabled, as Fedora's
  preset does for Bluefin, and the desktop contract asserts cups.socket.
- cameras in Files: gvfs-gphoto2 (libgphoto2 -> libexif). libgphoto2 is
  built without lockdev, which has no upstream source any more; only
  RS-232 serial cameras lose port locking.

The image build is the test: it runs `check-repos` against the new image, installs all of this, and runs both contract checks.

## 목적

대표 지시(2026-09-26 "가장 빠르게 개발속도를 낼수있는 방안으로 하라")에 따라 **레인 D(고객 보고)** 를 신설하고, 레인 A 대기열의 **A8**을 레인 D로 옮깁니다. 이 세션은 지금까지 대표 현황 보고만 했고 제품 코드·게시 이력이 없어 `docs/LANES.ko.md`(#140)의 세 레인 어디에도 해당하지 않았습니다.

- 기준 SHA: `63f8873` (origin/main)
- 배포: 하지 않음. 게시는 **레인 A 단독** 원칙을 그대로 둡니다.

## 왜 A8인가

레인 A 대기열 5개 중 **A8만 막힘이 없습니다.**

| 항목 | 상태 |
|---|---|
| A3·A6 종료 조건 | 사실 확정·스위치 켜기가 **대표 확인 대기** |
| **A8** | **선행 A4·B2·F2 전부 `merged`, 막힘 없음** |
| B4 2부 | 결정 16(첫 실게시) 확인 대기 |
| B3 | 레인 R의 R3b 병합 대기(공유 파일 순서) |
| 조건부 A5·B5 GEPA·B4 3부 | W24 발동 조건 확인 전 |

A8은 `LLM 0`(결정론 집계)이라 현재 소진된 HERMES 쿼터와 경쟁하지 않고, 레인 Q가 쿼터 복구를 기다리는 동안에도 진행됩니다. 새 모듈 중심이라 공유 코드 파일 충돌도 최소입니다.

## 변경 파일

| 파일 | 내용 |
|---|---|
| `docs/LANES.ko.md` | 레인 표에 `D` 행 추가, 레인 A 범위에서 A8 제외(`A8은 레인 D`), 레인 A 순서 2번을 포인터로 교체, `### 레인 D` 개발 순서 추가 |
| `docs/STATUS.md` | `## 레인 D` 칸 신설 |

## 공유 문서 규칙 준수

- `docs/STATUS.md`는 **레인 D 칸만** 추가했습니다. 공용 `마지막 갱신`·`현재 운영 상태` 표·`게시 대기열`·다른 레인 칸은 건드리지 않았습니다.
- `docs/LANES.ko.md`는 "레인을 바꾸려면 대표 확인을 받고 이 문서를 고친다" 규칙에 따라 대표 지시를 근거로 수정했습니다. 레인 A 담당자께서 배정에 이견이 있으면 이 PR에서 조정해 주십시오.
- `docs/releases/`, `docs/HANDOFF.ko.md`는 변경하지 않았습니다.

## 레인 D 범위

1. **A8** 고객 보고서·사실 지식 팩(LLM 0) — 브랜드·지점·기간 보고서와 확정 사실 팩을 결정론 집계로 출력. 지표 정의는 `data-truth-9`와 공유, **화면은 PR 5(레인 A) 범위로 남김**.
2. 대표 현황 보고(저장소 밖 산출물).
- 게시하지 않음. 필요하면 게시 대기열에 한 줄만 적습니다.
- 새 records kind는 `lib/record-kinds.ts` 끝 고정 묶음 앞에 레인 D 항목만 붙입니다.

## 검증

문서만 변경했습니다. 코드·테스트·게시 영향이 없어 별도 테스트를 돌리지 않았습니다(`not_run`). A8 구현은 별도 PR에서 전체 검증과 함께 올립니다.

## 남은 위험

- 레인 A가 이미 A8에 착수했다면 중복이 됩니다. 착수 이력은 STATUS 레인 A 칸에서 "진행 중: 없음"으로 확인했으나, 레인 A 담당자의 확인이 필요합니다.
- A8 화면은 PR 5(레인 A)에 남으므로, API·집계까지가 레인 D 몫이라는 경계를 유지해야 합니다.

## Summary Finding **A11Y-O2** (task 034, `findings/a11y-key-flows-2026-09-24.md`): in the task overlay the heading order jumped from the page `h1` straight to the task title `h4` (axe `heading-order`, moderate, WCAG 1.3.1), and every field label on the right (Status, Assignee, Priority, …) was also an `h4`. What changes: - The task title is an `h2` (`TaskDetailTitle.vue`: tag only). - The section headings in the overlay are `h3`: Details (`TaskDetailRightSide`), Custom fields (`customFieldRender`), Checklist (`CheckList`) and Attachments (`Attachments`). They have to move with the title, otherwise the next heading after the `h2` would be an `h4` and the skip would just move down. - The field labels are plain text (`
`), not headings. The "Suggest checklists" (`h5`) and "+ Custom field" (`h4`) actions are ``s. Leaving the `h5` would give a new h3 → h5 skip. - The styles that targeted these by tag (`.task-detail-right-side-label h4`, `.ah-detail__props … > h4`, `h4.details-heading`) now target classes. Where an element got its spacing from the browser's heading defaults (Checklist, Suggest checklists, both custom-field lines), the same margins/size are set on a class, so no `h2`/`h3` defaults leak through. Visual check: a harness page loaded the real CSS (global utilities, title, right side, overlay, checklist, custom field; old from `origin/beta`, new from this branch) with the old and new markup, at 1280, 1100 and 700 px. author: iamvihanga
body:
Implements the final phase of the app: editing book metadata, changing cover photos, crash reporting, and the release process.

## Summary

This PR completes Phase 8 of the build plan with three major components:

1. **Edit book details** – new screen to modify titles, authors, language, page count and format
2. **Change cover photo** – camera/gallery picker with upload and old cover cleanup
3. **Release infrastructure** – Sentry crash reporting, public pages (privacy, terms, account deletion), and a comprehensive release runbook

## Key changes

**Book editing**
- New route `app/(app)/book/edit/[id].tsx` with form validation (pages cannot drop below current page)
- `updateBook()` RPC in Supabase (only changed fields are updated, safe for offline replay)
- `useUpdateBook()` hook with optimistic updates and cache invalidation
- Edit schema validation in `src/features/books/schema.ts`
- Tests in `src/features/books/__tests__/edit.test.tsx`

**Cover photo management**
- `src/features/books/cover.ts` – `pickCover()` (camera or gallery with 2:3 aspect ratio), `uploadReplacementCover()`, `removeOldCover()`
- New sheet `ChangeCoverSheetBody` in `BookSheets.tsx` with camera permission handling
- Replacement covers get timestamped filenames to bypass cache
- Tests verify upload and cleanup flow

**Crash reporting**
- `src/lib/sentry.ts` – Sentry initialization (off in dev/test, requires DSN)
- `src/lib/sentryScrub.ts` – privacy scrubbing: strips query strings, drops console breadcrumbs, removes PII before sending
- `src/components/ds/CrashScreen.tsx` – error boundary that reports crashes and keeps the app usable
- Tests for scrubbing logic in `src/lib/__tests__/sentryScrub.test.ts`
- Metro config updated to include Sentry's Debug ID plugin for source map symbolication

**Release runbook and public pages**
- `docs/release.md` – 15-step runbook covering package name, EAS environment variables, service setup (Supabase, Google Cloud, TMDB, Sentry), Play Console submission, and staged rollout
- `site/` – static HTML pages (privacy policy, account deletion, terms) with templated contact email and update date
- `scripts/build-site.mjs` – build script to inject contact email and policy date
- `site/vercel.json` – Vercel deployment config
- `eas.json` updated with `EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV` per profile (development/preview/production)

**Supporting changes**
- `app.config.ts` – validates Android package name from `ANDROID_PACKAGE` env var, refuses placeholder in production
- `app/_layout.tsx` – Sentry navigation integration for screen transaction tracking
- `CrashScreen` error boundary added to app layout
- Copy updates: removed "not yet" error, added crash screen messages
- Environment validation: `EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` optional, `EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV` defaults to "development"
- Icon additions: `photo_library` for gallery picker

## Implementation notes

- Crash reporting is **off by default** (requires DSN and non-dev build); privacy scrubbing ensures only stack traces, device info, screen paths and anonymous user IDs leave the phone
- Cover uploads use timestamped paths (`front-{timestamp}.jpg`) so cached old photos don't persist
- Edit form validation prevents setting total pages below current page (enforced both client and server)
- Release runbook is comprehensive and prescriptive, covering all external services and Play Console steps needed for a production launch
- Public pages are built with environment variables (contact email, policy date) and can be deployed to any static host (Vercel example included)

author: ahoo-wang
body:
Reads the descriptor's numeric semantics (#3552: `DECIMAL {scale}`, `MONEY {scale, currency | currencyField}`) and formats values by them across the engine. Decision record: D50 in `docs/design/decisions.md`; landing notes: `capabilities.md` §21.

## What changes
- **Model**: `FieldDefinition.numeric` (`FieldNumeric`: `decimal` | fixed-currency `money` | row-currency `money`). Narrowing writes it from `FieldDescriptor.semantic` (`numericOf`) unless the definition declares one; admission checks it (`definition.field.numeric-invalid`).
- **One reading**: `numberFormatOf(field)`. The author's `numberFormat` wins; otherwise `scale` digits, plus a fixed ISO 4217 currency, in the surface locale (`Intl.NumberFormat`). Record cells, cards, detail, summaries, filter bar, analysis groups/metrics, chart axes and tooltips, and metric cards all read through it.
- **Row-level currency** (`currencyField`): record queries ask for the currency field along with the amount, and each cell reads in its row's currency (`inRowCurrency`). The code is never guessed: an unreadable code gives digits only.
- **Mixed currencies**: aggregates over row-currency money ask for two companion metrics, a `DISTINCT_COUNT` and an `ANY` of the currency field, carrying the metric's own condition.
  - A group with several currencies gets its value nulled, so no table cell, bar or card draws a meaningless sum. Its cell reads 「多种货币」 / "Mixed currencies".
  - A warning over the result (`analysis.result.mixed-currency`) offers 「按「币种」分组」, which adds the dimension and runs.
  - If the source can't answer the companions, the query still runs and `analysis.metric.currency-unchecked` says the totals may mix currencies.
  - When all rows are in one currency, the column format carries it, so the axis and card show it.
  - Record totals do the same (page totals from the rows; full-range totals via companions).
  - Derived metrics read their operands' currencies. A derived amount over row-currency money is now admitted without a currency of its own.
- **Files**: numbers whose format comes from the descriptor are written raw, and money gets a 「{列名}（币种）」 column next to it (record and analysis exports). This revises D25 Q28 for these fields only. Author-declared formats are unchanged, and so is D37.
- **`semanticText`** names DECIMAL/MONEY (`decimal scale 2`, `money CNY scale 2`, `money by currency scale 2`) instead of "date".
- **Public surface** (root +12): `FieldNumeric`, `DecimalNumeric`, `FixedMoneyNumeric`, `RowMoneyNumeric`, `NUMERIC_TYPES`, `MAX_NUMERIC_SCALE`, `CURRENCY_CODE_PATTERN`, `numberFormatOf`, `currencyPathOf`, `CurrencyReading`, `ColumnCurrency`, `rowCurrency`.
- **Size**: root 126,288 B of 140,000 B; ./ui 611,188 B of 616,000 B. The ./ui entry is now under 1% from its ceiling. No ceiling was raised.

## Checklist
Done
- [x] Model, narrowing, admission, `numberFormatOf`, `semanticText`
- [x] Row-level currency in cells, cards, detail, and projection
- [x] Companions, 「多种货币」, the warning plus group-by-currency offer, record totals
- [x] CSV raw values plus currency column (record and analysis)
- [x] Unit tests `test/money.test.tsx` (JPY 0 decimals, CNY 2, row-level currency, mixed totals, companions, files, workbench offer)
- [x] Story 「能力/金额与小数」 and its regression twin (axe runs as an error)
- [x] Docs: D50, capabilities §21, model.md, kernels.md, ui/record.md, ui/analysis.md, AGENTS tree
- [x] Gates, rebased on #3600: lint:check, test:type, build (size), full vitest with coverage (298 files), publicSurface, docs tests, story files (MoneyFields, AnalysisWorkbench, RecordWorkbench, CapabilityNarrowing), storybook typecheck/lint, prettier, scope

Left (recorded in capabilities §21 「没做的」)
- Row-currency amounts inside array elements; formula metrics (no companions); chart tooltips when rows differ in currency (the table and file read row by row).

## How to resume
Branch `feat/view-engine-money-decimal`. Entry points:
- `src/model/field.ts` (`FieldNumeric`, `numberFormatOf`, `currencyPathOf`)
- `src/analysis/currency.ts` (companions and issues)
- `src/ui/currency.ts`

body:
## Summary

Agent-created scheduled tasks persist `execution.toolMode`, but the Runtime Host ScheduledTask decoder rejected that field. Catalog queries could therefore return `internal_failure`, leaving Maka's Scheduled tasks page empty or stale even though the task had been stored.

Preserve and validate optional `toolMode` across task mutations and catalog reads, including legacy records that omit it. Advance the compatibility epoch from 189 to 190 because older peers reject the field. Preserve the latest upstream time and time-zone formatting.

The ScheduledTask tool now checks the same Host catalog for the newly created ID before reporting success. If verification fails, it reports the task ID and advises querying before retrying to avoid duplicates. Agent task creation rejects only missing or whitespace-only working directories, while valid Host paths including filesystem root remain supported. Successful creation reports the stored Agent execution directory.

## Verification

- Before rebasing, verified the actual Dev UI with an isolated test profile: the weekly report appeared as an Agent scheduled task with cron `0 9 * * 5` and next run `2026-10-02 09:00` in Asia/Shanghai. The same Runtime Host query returned `toolMode: direct` and the expected project working directory. This verifies creation and catalog visibility; it does not verify a future scheduled firing.
- After rebasing onto current upstream main, built `@maka/core`, `@maka/storage`, `@maka/runtime`, and `@maka/runtime-host` successfully.
- All 35 affected tests passed:
  ```sh
  node --test packages/runtime-host/dist/__tests__/scheduled-task-protocol.test.js packages/runtime/dist/__tests__/scheduled-task-tools.test.js packages/core/dist/__tests__/scheduled-task.test.js
  ```
- Added a regression test confirming a filesystem-root workspace can create an Agent scheduled task.
- Biome checks on the changed files, `git diff --check`, and the protocol epoch check against upstream main passed.
- The full repository test suite was not run.

## AI use

- [ ] No generative tool made a substantive contribution
- [x] Generative tooling made a substantive contribution

Tool(s) and scope: Codex assisted with diagnosis, implementation, regression tests, Dev UI verification, review response, and conflict resolution. The commit includes a `Generated-by: Codex` trailer.

- [x] Lint, format, typecheck and the affected suites pass locally

Does this PR entail a change in behavior?

author: shizukutanaka
body:
## Summary

`docs/improvement-research-2026.md` §1（Proof-of-Compute, arXiv:2501.05374 / 2408.07177）の残件「**ルート配線・実ジョブ収集は未**」を実装。検証基盤（work-verifier の ternary consensus / ゼロ負荷検出、verification-service、VerificationRepository）は実装済みだったが API から到達不能だったため、注文スコープのエンドポイントとして配線した（jobId = orderId）。（PR #14 と同一内容 — #14 はブランチ操作ミスで自動 close されたため再作成）

### 追加エンドポイント（`POST /api/v1/orders/:id/...`）
| パス | 権限 | 役割 |
|---|---|---|
| `verify/output` | 借り手 / admin | 借り手が観測したジョブ結果（出力ハッシュ/ベクトル）を primary output として記録。プロバイダは不可 — 自己申告だと検証が空転する |
| `verify/replica` | 第三者プロバイダ / admin | 監査再実行結果を replicaOutputs へ追加。本実行プロバイダは拒否（自己監査にならない） |
| `verify/finalize` | admin | verdict を確定。verified/failed は `recordAudit` で reputation へ反映。`verificationCtx` は escrow.evaluate にそのまま渡せる形で返却 |
| GET `/:id/verification` | 当事者 + admin | 検証レコード/verdict の参照 |

### 実ジョブ収集（§1 アクション2）
- lender heartbeat が `utilizationPct`（0-100、省略可）を受理 → `recordUtilSample()` がレコードを遅延開設して追記（上限 1000 サンプルで暴走防止）。finalize 時に `detectZeroLoad` で「課金されるのに実質無稼働」を検出 → `suspectedZeroLoad → failed`。
- `POST /orders/:id/stop` 完了時、pending の検証レコードがあれば自動 finalize し `verification` verdict を応答に同梱（best-effort、完了を妨げない）。

### 設計上の注意
- **楽観的検証**: `open` 時に `auditRate`（既定 0.1、jobId ハッシュで決定論的サンプリング）で監査要否を決める。非監査ジョブは再実行不要で `verified`、監査ジョブは replica ≥2 で ternary consensus、=1 で二者照合、=0 で inconclusive。`auditRate` は両 submit ルートで 0-1 上書き可能（厳しくしたい借り手/運用者向け）。
- ゼロ負荷疑いは監査対象・非対象に関わらず `failed` にする（cheap な完全性シグナル）。

### テスト（8件, tests/api/order-verification.test.js）

author: codegod100
body:
### Motivation
- Buck was failing to load generated Rust targets because the vendored `third-party/rust/vendor` tree is ignored and not materialized on fresh clones.
- The intent is to ensure the vendored sources exist before Buck evaluates generated targets so `just buck` works reliably without manual pre-vendoring.

### Description
- Add a private `ensure-vendor` recipe to `justfile` that runs `cd third-party/rust && cargo vendor --locked --versioned-dirs vendor` when `third-party/rust/vendor/.vidya-complete` is missing and writes the completion marker only after vendoring succeeds.
- Make the existing `buck *args` recipe depend on `ensure-vendor` by changing it to `buck *args: ensure-vendor` so every `just buck` invocation runs the vendor preflight.
- Update the `vendor` recipe in `justfile` to `touch third-party/rust/vendor/.vidya-complete` after a successful `cargo vendor` to keep the marker in sync with explicit refreshes.

### Testing
- Ran `git diff --check` which succeeded with no whitespace errors.
- Verified the `justfile` diff and committed the change (commit created locally).
- Attempted `cargo vendor --locked --versioned-dirs vendor` from a clean vendor directory but dependency downloads were blocked by the environment's crates.io proxy returning HTTP 403, so full vendoring could not be completed in this environment.
- Attempted the pinned `just` launcher (`PATH="$PWD/scripts:$PATH" ./scripts/just --list`) but it failed because the project’s `dotslash` launcher is unavailable outside the Nix development environment.

author: portare-ch
body:
#345 landed on the tool-descriptions branch after #341 had already been merged, so it never reached next. This is that change, the one squash commit, rebased onto next. Tracked in #333.

ScummVM was standalone because ROCKNIX had it so; the tree had no core package. Now it is the libretro core from libretro's ScummVM fork, and fluidsynth is gone.

## The core

- New package `scummvm-lr`. Its Makefile fetches libretro-deps and libretro-common at the commits it names and compiles in what it needs, FluidLite among them, so MIDI is synthesized inside the core, per game. No fluidsynth on the image: the package, its service and its place in SDL2_mixer go. The GeneralUser soundfont stays and the shipped ini names it.
- Built in the core's lite mode with our own engine list: the 96 engines the standalone's release build had, each with its default sub-engines named, since the list does not imply them (without that SCUMM v7/8, HE, SCI32 and others were silently left out). Ten of those are left out as no use on a handheld: glk, ultima and mm want a keyboard; director, bagel, crab, ngi, hypno, gamos and plumbers are multimedia CD-ROMs and one-title engines. Every engine in the tree came to 120 MB, the standalone's whole set to 99, this to 77. Built without a GL renderer, the standalone's `--opengl-mode=none`: with one, the core asks RetroArch for a GL context and RetroArch switches to the GL driver, off Vulkan and the timed presents.
- The core keeps its themes and engine data under RetroArch's system directory, `/storage/roms/bios/scummvm`, and they must match its version, so post-update copies them from `/usr/share/scummvm` after every update. The starting ini goes next to them only when there is none: it is where added games live.

## Games

Games are folders under `/storage/roms/scummvm` with a `.scummvm` hook file inside, holding the game's ScummVM id or target name. The core's own launcher writes those (Tools, Playlist Generator) after a game is added there; "Start ScummVM" opens that launcher through RetroArch with no content. The scan tool, which ran the standalone binary, is gone. runemu no longer has a case of its own for the core: the hook file is the content, like any other system.

## Tested on the Nova

Native build of the core at this configuration, bound into `/tmp/cores`, data unpacked under the BIOS folder, Lure of the Temptress (freeware) in a folder with a hook file `lure`, launched through the new runemu as the launcher would: the game runs, RetroArch stays on Vulkan. The core's own launcher comes up from the tool script too.

Not built by the build system. Two things to watch: the core's Makefile clones its two deps during the build (the runner has network, as ARMSX2's patch download does), and `zip`/`unzip` on the host, which the build already requires.

body:
Piece 2 of the Nebo Link employees PRD (`docs/prd/2026-09-26-nebo-link-employees.md` §6.3), PR (i), on top of #360.

## What

- **Hire.** `POST /agents` gains a `linked: {botId, agentId}` option (one function with parameters). The row is `kind = "linked"`, name and description come from the linked bot's contract roster (fetched through the hub with the Nebo bot's token, which the hub admits for a same-owner bot — neboloop #327), `name_locked`, and `entity_config.model_preference = linked/<bot>/<agent>` so the `LinkedProvider` drives it. The blank hire and the linked hire converge on one `activate_hire` routine (Rule 8.1). No introduction ceremony: the name is the linked agent's.
- **Soul and rules are the runtime's.** `PUT /agents/{id}` refuses a write that would change a linked employee's soul or rules ("<name>'s soul and rules are set on the linked bot."); the settings modal is read-only for them.
- **Workforce.** The hire modal offers **Hire from <linked bot>** for every same-owner linked bot with `chat: true` (neboloop #328) and lists its agents; `GET /agents/linked` serves that to the generated client. The hub calls are on the ONE hub client: `NeboAIApi::list_managed_bots()` and `linked_bot_agents(bot_id)`.
- **Offline.** The employee card reads **Offline** (the plain word, in place of the status line) when the hub's presence for the linked bot is offline, when the hub does not list the bot, or when the hub cannot be asked. One `manage/bots` call per roster load, only when a linked employee exists. `AgentListEntry` gains `kind` and `offline`.
- Copy per house rules: hire/employee, no wobble words. Styles: Tailwind/DaisyUI classes only. i18n keys added to `en.json` (other locales fall back to `en`).

## Tests
`crates/server/src/handlers/agents.rs` `linked_hire_tests`: the hire body parsing, the offline rule (bot offline / not listed / hub unreachable), the persona refusal (a change refused, an unchanged value passes, other employees untouched). `cargo test -p nebo-server linked` green; `make gen` (diff = the new endpoint + the two interfaces + two fields), `pnpm check` (0 errors; the one warning in the modal is the pre-existing `autofocus`), `pnpm build` green.

## For the live proof (§9.5)
Needs a harness Nebo bot signed in to the harness owner account, with the two test bots linked and announcing `chat`. Never the owner's token or bot id.

author: cholmes
body:
## Outcome

On a phone the map now fills the screen and one bottom sheet holds the
controls. Before this change the sidebar took 46 vh at the top, the image
panel took up to 45 vh at the bottom, and the map was the 9 vh strip between
them.

## What changed

At the existing `max-width: 760px` breakpoint:

- `#map` covers the viewport.
- The sidebar becomes a bottom sheet with a grab handle and three snap
  heights: peek (handle plus the status line), half (the default on load) and
  full. The handle answers a drag and a tap.
- The image controls render inside that same sheet, so a phone never shows two
  panels over the map.
- Showing a scene snaps the sheet to peek, so the user sees the image just
  asked for, with the "Showing … Clear" line still in view.
- The sheet uses `dvh` units, because the iOS address bar changes `vh`, and
  pads for `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`.

Desktop is untouched: `#sheet` computes to `display: contents`, the handle to
`display: none`, and the snap state is never written.

## Verification

Headless Chrome at 390x844, 428x926 and 1440x900:

1. The map is 50 % of the viewport on load and the page does not scroll.
2. Search, then show on map: the sheet is at peek, the "Showing …" line is
   hit-testable, and the scene is drawn at full resolution.
3. At full the band preset and the stretch handles work; a handle drag does
   not move the sheet.
4. The zoom buttons are hit-testable at every snap, and a map drag still pans.
5. Desktop keeps the 360 px sidebar and the lower-right image card.

`node --check` on all five explorer modules. `tests/run_all.py` and 217 unit
tests pass. `docs/mobile-layout-report.md` holds the detail and the
screenshots.

body:
## Ticket

DT-19

## What changed

- **Gradle build** (written by hand instead of copying Android Studio's template, with current versions): AGP 9.4.1, Gradle 9.8.0 wrapper with its checksum pinned, Kotlin 2.4.20 (AGP 9 bundles Kotlin 2.2, which cannot read libraries built with newer Kotlin, so the root build puts 2.4.20 on the classpath), Compose BOM 2026.09.00, compileSdk 37 (the libraries require it), targetSdk 36, minSdk 29. Release builds use R8 with resource shrinking: the release APK is 1.9 MB. `gradlew` is executable in git, which switches on the CI `android` build.
- **`AndroidManifest.xml`**: usage access, `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES`, notifications, calendar and Health Connect read permissions (sleep, steps, nutrition), the Health Connect rationale entry points (Android 13 and older, and the Android 14+ activity alias), and **no cloud backup** (`allowBackup=false`, backup and data-extraction rules exclude everything, device-protected storage included) so the event store and the hub token stay on the phone.
- **`ui/OnboardingScreen.kt`**: the permission model (one place that checks and requests each permission, refreshed when the app comes back from Settings) and the onboarding screen. Runtime permissions and Health Connect ask with their dialog; when Android answers without showing it (the user blocked it), the tap opens the right settings page instead, while a dialog closed with Back simply asks again. Health Connect errors never crash the app, overlapping refreshes cannot show stale states, and every settings screen opens on Daytrace's own task so Back returns here.
- **`ui/StatusScreen.kt`**: the home screen after onboarding, with each permission and a one-tap fix, a banner when usage access is off, and a hub card (pairing comes in DT-22).
- **Look and feel**: brand colors shared with the dashboard (indigo, pink, sunrise orange, mint, sky), light and dark themes, a gradient header with an animated progress ring, animated status pills, a pulsing "looking for your hub" dot, and an adaptive launcher icon (vector, so no PNGs). The whole screen scrolls, so landscape and large text work, and side insets are respected.
- `MainActivity.kt`, `DaytraceApp.kt`, `res/xml/network_security_config.xml` (plain HTTP to your own hub until DT-47), `android/README.md` (build and install steps, permissions).
- `app/src/test/.../OnboardingRulesTest.kt`: 4 unit tests for the onboarding rule.
- `.github/workflows/android.yml`: CI now also runs the unit tests and lint.

## How I tested it

- [x] `gradlew assembleDebug testDebugUnitTest lintDebug`: builds, 4 unit tests pass, lint clean; `assembleRelease` builds (1.9 MB)
- [x] **On a real device**: Galaxy S25 Ultra (SM-S938W), Android 16, installed over USB with adb. Onboarding shows all four steps; the owner granted each one from the buttons (usage access through Settings, notifications and calendar through the system dialog, Health Connect through its own screen) and every pill turned green. `adb` confirmed `GET_USAGE_STATS: allow` and all five runtime permissions `granted=true`. "Let's go" opened the status screen (4 of 4 on). No crashes in logcat. After the review fixes: the R8-shrunk release build (signed with the local debug key for the test only) runs with every permission read correctly, and Back from the re-shown welcome screen returns to the status screen.
- [ ] Hub tests: not touched

## Checklist

- [x] Only touched the files listed in the ticket (the layout is fixed by DT-1); the template-style additions are the ones the ticket allows (`ui/theme/*`, `res/mipmap-anydpi`, `res/drawable`, `values/themes.xml`, `values/colors.xml`, `xml/backup_rules.xml`, `xml/data_extraction_rules.xml`), plus the unit test, `ui/theme/Icons.kt` (one icon) and the CI step
- [x] No secrets, keys, databases or personal activity data (exported Shortcuts use Import Questions)
- [x] Bug review done: findings posted, and each one fixed or answered on the PR (tick before merging)

author: dwfreegethub
body:
From v0.91.3, jsDelivr went on serving v0.91.2. Its own `@main` resolver was answering 502, then `"version": null`, even though every purge was accepted and not throttled. A stale copy isn't an error, so the loader's GitHub fallback never ran.

- **New order:** the loader now fetches GitHub's raw bundle first (about 5 minutes of caching), falls back to jsDelivr only if that fails, and shows the on-screen notice if both fail. It never loads both.
- **Tests:** `test/loader.mjs` is rewritten for the new order. Putting jsDelivr first again fails 11 checks.
- **Also fixed:** the literal purge URL is restored. `decf02b` had changed it to `${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}`, and an existing loader check caught it.
- This change is in the installed loader, so it reaches players when their userscript manager updates it.
- `npm test` passes, apart from the 3 known CRLF loader header checks. `npm run release` has been run, and both install files are at 0.92.1.

author: dipakkr
body:
## Summary
Adds `fixtures/effects-golden.json`, the single source of truth for the effects format: the row deltas and schema changes a migration produces. pgwarden (TypeScript) and the skill's Python `effects.py` must both reproduce every case in it.

## Problem
The core safety check is "commit only if the real effects equal what the human approved". That only works if the effects computed during rehearsal in the sandbox and the effects computed by pgwarden on prod are byte-for-byte comparable. Two implementations in two languages will drift unless they share a fixed, testable definition.

## What changed
- `fixtures/effects-golden.json`:
  - `rules`: facts cover schema `public` only and exclude `schema_migrations`; `row_deltas` has one key per table in before or after (missing table counts as 0, zero deltas included); `+table`/`-table` suppress column/index/constraint entries; `+column`, `-column`, `~column:<t>.<c>:<old>-><new>`, `~nullable:...`; indexes and constraints compared by name; `schema_changes` sorted by code-point order and compared as a set.
  - `base`: the shopkart prod facts (`users` 5,014 rows, `orders` 20,000 rows, their columns, indexes and constraints).
  - `cases` (7): no-op, add unique index, add column, rename column (shows as `+column:users.mobile` and `-column:users.phone`), dedupe + index + add column, drop table `orders`, and type/nullability change.
  - `patch_ops`: definitions for `set_rows`, `add_index`, `add_column`, `rename_column`, `drop_table`, `alter_column`, used to derive each case's `after` from `base`.

## How to test
Data only. Check it parses: `python3 -m json.tool fixtures/effects-golden.json`. The TypeScript and Python implementations and their tests against these cases land in follow-up PRs.

## Notes
Cases are expressed as patches on one `base` rather than full before/after snapshots to keep the fixture small and readable.

author: kirillsachkov
body:
## Отчёт о реализации

### Результат

Код Platform оформлен одним форматтером: Prettier 3.9.9 с конфигом по умолчанию, как в inside-telegram. `pnpm format:check` входит в `check:static`, поэтому CI отклоняет неотформатированный код. Исправляет его `pnpm format`.

### Связанная задача

Часть #693 — PR 4 из 4 (Prettier). Задачу не закрывает: squash-коммит этого PR будет внесён в `.git-blame-ignore-revs` маленьким PR сразу следом. Его SHA появится только после merge через merge queue, и тот PR закроет #693.

### Затронутые части системы

| Часть системы | Изменена | Что изменилось |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Продукт и интерфейс | Нет | Только форматирование исходников web; поведение то же. |
| Серверная часть и API | Нет | Только форматирование; OpenAPI и MCP-поверхность не изменились. |
| Бизнес-правила | Нет | — |
| Данные и база | Нет | — |
| Доступ и безопасность | Нет | — |
| Эксплуатация и инфраструктура | Нет | Форматирование YAML Compose; образы и конфигурация те же. |
| Работа агентов и инструменты | Да | Prettier, `format`/`format:check`, проверка формата в `check:static` и CI, `.prettierignore`, runbook. |

### Как это работает

1. `prettier` 3.9.9 закреплён в корневом `package.json`. Скрипты: `format` (`prettier --write .`) и `format:check` (`prettier --check .`).
2. `check:static` начинается с `docs:check`, как требует документационный контракт, и сразу за ним запускает `format:check`. Job CI `Static checks` выполняет `pnpm check:static`.
3. Prettier читает `.gitignore`, а `.prettierignore` добавляет файлы, чьи байты принадлежат другому владельцу:
   - Markdown (свои переносы и таблицы) и lockfile;
   - файлы harness и три managed workflow;
   - сгенерированные и побайтно сверяемые файлы: OpenAPI, клиент web, `*.generated.ts`, `tool-surface.json`, `local-definitions.json`;
   - закреплённые корпуса контрактов;
   - зафиксированные evidence;
   - форк Logto на закреплённой ревизии upstream;
   - фикстуры guardrail, которые проверяют диагностику по номерам строк.
4. Перед форматированием три директивы (`oxlint-disable-next-line` и `@ts-expect-error`) поставлены над однострочными выражениями. Иначе после переноса длинных строк они оказались бы не над тем кодом.
5. Коммит `style: форматирование Prettier 3.9.9` чисто механический: повторный `prettier --write .` на его родителе в чистом worktree даёт идентичное дерево.

### Изменения бизнес-правил и предметной области

Нет.

### Архитектура и дальнейшее развитие

- Конфига `.prettierrc` нет: ширина 80 и остальные настройки по умолчанию совпадают с inside-telegram, это одно правило для всех repositories. Раньше код писали шире, отсюда большой механический diff.
- Из-за squash merge в `main` войдёт один коммит: конфиг, перенос директив и форматирование. Именно его следующий PR внесёт в `.git-blame-ignore-revs`. Вместе с форматированием `git blame` пропустит и небольшие немеханические правки этого PR: скрипты, `.prettierignore`, runbook и три директивы.
- Живые ветки после merge делают rebase и `pnpm format` на своём diff. Координатор предупредил сессию #742.

### Ключевые файлы и порядок проверки

1. `package.json` — Prettier, `format`, `format:check`, порядок `check:static`.
2. `.prettierignore` — что и почему не форматируется.
3. `apps/backend/src/infrastructure/http/problem-details.ts`, `apps/backend/test/unit/profile-avatar-http.test.ts`, `apps/backend/test/integration/source-guide-import.test.ts` — директивы над однострочными выражениями.
4. `docs/runbooks/continuous-integration.md`, `docs/runbooks/local-development.md` — проверка формата и `pnpm format`.

Механически изменено: коммит `style: форматирование Prettier 3.9.9` (1361 файл) и `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

### Проверки

Локально на Node 24.21.0 и pnpm 11.27.1:

body:
Closes #7050

## What the issue described vs. what ships

- **Verified:** `applyEntryMetadata` (`agent/internal/backup/restore.go` ~897–917, the lines named in the issue) has **no production caller**. Its only call site was removed in #5519 (SEC-121, commit 29e9445f3): file restore now applies mode/owner/mtime/Windows attributes on the pinned handle inside `securefs.InstallFileWithSecurity`, and the live loop wraps every install warning as `restored <displayPath> with reduced fidelity: …`, where `displayPath = restoreSourcePath(file)` (OriginalPath under VSS). So the shadow-path wording in those lines could not reach a job log today.
- **Fix:** remove the dead `applyEntryMetadata` (and its one test, which only exercised the dead function) instead of rewording it. Leaving it invites someone to re-wire it and bring the shadow path back.
- **Live path:** `RestoreContentlessEntry`'s content-entry error still printed `entry.SourcePath`. It now uses `restoreSourcePath(entry)`, like every other restore message.

- **BMR (review finding):** `bmr.go` printed the shadow path in the per-file `restore failed for …` warning (user-visible in `RecoveryResult.Warnings`) and in `restoreContentlessEntry`'s content-entry error. Both now use the original path.

## Tests

- New `bmr/vsspath_test.go` (2 tests): both **failed** before the bmr fix and pass after it.

- New `TestRestoreContentlessEntry_ErrorNamesOriginalPathNotShadowPath`: written first and **failed** on main (the error printed `\\?\GLOBALROOT\Device\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy7\…`), passes with the fix.
- `go test -race ./internal/backup/` ok; `go test -race ./internal/backup/bmr/` ok.
- `GOOS=windows go build ./...` ok; `GOOS=windows go test -c ./internal/backup/` compiles.

Does not touch `agent/internal/backup/systemstate/` (#7000 / #7021).

author: astrovm
body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"astrovm"} -->
_Requested by **astro** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_011ViXndtnnFSKSoSQ3Pph94?thread=cmsg_011ViXndtnnFSKSoSQ3Pph94LZPMyCtiEuRBVAcPqFgNqF)_

Before: several steps made replies slower than they needed to be:
- Every message took global database locks.
- Model pricing downloads blocked replies.
- Each worker kept a cold Telegram connection.
- The prompt re-sent the current message and changed its prefix on every turn.
- Streamed answers for all chats went through one thread.
- Failed updates waited for the next long poll.
- Tool calls ran one at a time.

There were also some feature bugs: mentioning the bot with an x.com or Instagram link got only the link fix, the AI never saw link previews, and "thinking" flashed on turns that ended silently.

After: on the common path, those steps are gone or run in parallel. The bugs above are fixed.

## How

**Per-message overhead** (72180bc)
- The chat-config schema is checked once, not on every message.
- The onboarding grant uses a lock-free fast path.
- Pricing is refreshed in the background.
- One Telegram client with keepalive is shared across workers.
- Link-preview probes have tighter timeouts and a 64 KiB body cap. This also fixes a UTF-8 slice panic.
- Redis and Postgres get connect timeouts.
- Regexes and fonts are compiled or loaded once.

**Prompt** (7a0ee04)
- The current message is removed from history (it was sent twice).
- Retrieved messages now come after the history, so the provider's prompt cache stays valid.
- History is capped to `max_history_messages`.
- Reasoning effort is `low` on rounds after a tool result.

**Dispatcher** (9de833a)
- A message addressed to the bot that contains a social link gets the link fix and an AI answer.
- Link-preview titles and descriptions are added to the AI context: at most 3 links, with a 4 s deadline.
- The "thinking" message is shown only after the turn passes the credit check.
- LRANGE and both GETs for memory now go in one Redis pipeline.

**Tools and data** (e7b34c0)
- Several `web_fetch` calls in one round run concurrently. Result order is preserved, and tools with side effects stay sequential.
- CriptoYa responses are cached for 45 s, and `/rulo` fetches its data in parallel.
- The Polymarket cache TTL goes from 5 s to 60 s.
- Pooled connections idle for more than 60 s are discarded instead of reused after the server may have closed them.

**Delivery and runtime** (8d7699a)
- Streamed edits go through 4 delivery threads, sharded by chat, so edits in one chat keep their order.
- A chat that is rate-limited no longer blocks other chats.
- Failed updates are requeued immediately, without waiting for the long poll to return.
- Confirmed updates are removed with a single `HDEL`, after the next batch is dispatched.
- Admin error reports are sent from a background thread.

**Dependencies:** already on the latest crates.io versions, Rust 1.98.1, cargo-chef 0.1.78 and cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1, so nothing needed bumping. I couldn't check GitHub Actions pins from this environment.

**Local checks:** `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`, and the full workspace test suite pass against Postgres 16 and Redis 7 with ffmpeg. Line coverage from `cargo llvm-cov`:

| crate | line coverage |
|---|---|
| bot-core | 95.17% |
| bot-adapters | 95.06% |
| botd | 95.15% |

body:
Release `v0.23.7-dev` (previous: `v0.23.6-dev`).

## In this release

- **#370** `setup` and `plane enable|disable` exit **3** (operator action pending), not 2, when an enrolled operator has no interactive terminal. Exit 2 now means only usage and unsupported platform, so an installer, CI or a dotfiles apply can treat every "waiting on a human" outcome the same way. `setup` validates its arguments before the terminal check, so a usage error stays exit 2. `operator`, `recover`, `web-research` and `approvals` keep exit 2.

## This PR

Renames `## Unreleased` to `## v0.23.7-dev (2026-09-26)` and bumps the README install examples. Nothing else changes. The tag goes on the squashed release commit.

## Behaviour change to know about

Callers that matched exit 2 for "no terminal" from `setup` or `plane enable|disable` must match 3. Documented in the installer headers and `docs/OPERATIONS.md`.

## Verification

#370 was verified on Windows and Linux (21 packages each), on both installer harnesses (`install_sh_test.sh` in WSL, `install_ps1_test.ps1` in pwsh), and with 19 of 19 CI checks. This PR touches only `CHANGELOG.md` and `README.md`.
