author: wavespestcontrolfl
body:
A delayed SendGrid callback could overwrite a newer Email attempt or start address recovery after that attempt took ownership. Webhook updates now compare the resolved attempt token, including legacy NULL tokens. Callbacks that need no row update verify ownership too, so a repeated delivery event can retry recovery only for its own attempt.

Old callbacks still record address-level opt-outs, complaints and hard bounces. When a newer attempt has rebound the provider ID or recipient, the signed callback's custom message ID supplies suppression context only; its original email remains the suppression target. Compatible precise marketing groups are retained, and a no-ASM `transactional_required` snapshot cannot override a signed service group.

This is the webhook-only slice of the approved billing Email delivery split. Retry ownership and crash recovery will follow separately. `GATE_BILLING_NOTIFICATION_CHANNELS` remains off.

**Review tier: Full** (shared customer Email webhook and recovery).

## Review map

| Requirement | Files | Invariant | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fence mutations and recovery to the resolved attempt | `webhooks-sendgrid.js`; newsletter and PostgreSQL suites | A newer token, including one replacing NULL, prevents old callbacks from mutating the row or initiating recovery; matching no-op delivery retains recovery | `npm exec --workspace=server -- jest --runInBand --coverage=false tests/newsletter.test.js` and PostgreSQL command below |
| Retain provider-evidenced address suppression | Same route and suites | Losing the attempt does not drop an opt-out, complaint or hard bounce, and never suppresses a rewritten destination instead | Same commands |
| Preserve precise compatible group scope | Same route and suites | A stale snapshot cannot turn signed service ASM into no-ASM transactional scope or broaden a compatible precise marketing scope | Same commands |
| Execute real interleavings in CI | `.github/workflows/tests.yml`; `sendgrid-webhook-attempt-fence-postgres.test.js` | Claims between resolution and transaction are tested against PostgreSQL | `APP_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<verified-private-QA-url> npm exec --workspace=server -- jest --runInBand --coverage=false tests/sendgrid-webhook-attempt-fence-postgres.test.js` |

## Validation

- Node 20 newsletter suite: 305 passed.
- Real PostgreSQL suite: 11 passed in the task-private database on verified Railway `codex-dev`. Tests remove their synthetic schema. Provider and customer communications are mocked.
- Targeted ESLint: zero errors, five structural warnings in the existing webhook dispatcher and helpers. Syntax and diff checks pass. Domain checks pass (2,313 files scanned).
- Main merged without conflicts; the four tested files were unchanged by integration. Final head `ea0e7b3a633ac097041e096062538e38b569a72d` passed the normal pre-push Codex audit with 0 P0 / 0 P1 and no actionable findings. Remote SHA matched immediately and again after two minutes; `verify-pr-checks.sh` confirmed fresh final-head test run `36229003280`.
- Independent review found a no-op callback ownership gap. The fix and regressions cover stale bounce, stale delivery and matching delivery recovery.

## Review history and split

- First GitHub finding [4110471645](https://github.com/wavespestcontrolfl/waves-customer-portal/pull/4900#discussion_r4110471645): a late callback could overwrite a new attempt. Token-scoped updates and recovery address it.
- Subsequent finding [4110568126](https://github.com/wavespestcontrolfl/waves-customer-portal/pull/4900#discussion_r4110568126): resolving an old attempt could discard its opt-out. The suppression-only custom-ID fallback addresses it, including rewritten recipients and ASM compatibility.
- Finding [4110568125](https://github.com/wavespestcontrolfl/waves-customer-portal/pull/4900#discussion_r4110568125) concerned the proposed ordinary retry ownership guard. That entire guard and its claim-lifecycle changes have been removed from this PR. The final template library and provider retry service match main. A later slice must establish positive pre-send evidence; missing uncertainty metadata is not proof that a send never happened.
- The broader work is preserved on local archive `backup/email-retry-claim-history-20260926` at `21acf758f3bdee4cb4046c0781f445561343077b`. The final PR is limited to webhook behavior and its tests.

## Deferred P2s

- `server/routes/webhooks-sendgrid.js:193`: the existing multi-owner dispatcher remains over the complexity threshold after adding stale-event suppression routing. Decomposing that dispatcher is outside this focused correctness fix.

## Release verification — 2026-09-26

- Exact reviewed head `ea0e7b3a633ac097041e096062538e38b569a72d` merged at 09:54:48 UTC as `ba82e7d7026debb02ddc6477da829002638cd35c`.
- Final-head CI run `36229003280` succeeded. Clean matching Codex comment `5845123259` and the complete stable delivery window were verified before merge; all historical findings were reconciled.
- Exact Railway production deployment `03b82015-2bc2-4325-ba18-4de11158cd4b` observed `SUCCESS` at 10:02 UTC for that merge commit.
- Public `/api/health` returned HTTP 200 at 10:03:30 UTC: status `ok`, database `ok`, staff maintenance disabled.

author: landco-debug
speak-agent
body:
0.14.0 removes the manual steps a project still needed after building with 0.13 (Sunrisepeak/GalTranslPP#2: unzip an embedded Python, run `Release.py`) and cuts the Qt download to a third. Engine floor unchanged: mcpp 2026.9.26.2. No engine change is needed.

**Files a program reads at run time, placed by the build.** A deployed file must be one the build graph knows how to produce. So each file is first produced by an action that names it as an output (SPEC-007 R3.2), and the output is deployed: `mcpp run` finds it beside the program and `mcpp pack` carries it. The following was measured:
- a library package's deployed outputs reach the `bin/` and the packed tree of every program that links it;
- a dependency's `artifact` actions run with the consumer's build.

- **`deps-archive`** (`mcpp.deps.archive`, new): `unpack({archive, to})` reads a zip's central directory while the build program runs, so every member is named before anything is extracted.
  - One `artifact` action, `mcpp-deps unpack` (`cmake -E tar xf --touch`), extracts it and names each file as an output; each file is then deployed under `to`.
  - ZIP64 archives and members whose path would leave the extraction directory are refused by name.
  - A missing `cmake` is a warning (R1.2).
  - `result::files` lists the copies for a project's own layout.
- **`deps-vcpkg` / `deps-cmake` `options::deploy`**: files of the installed prefix (`{"share/opencc/t2s.json", "BaseConfig/opencc"}`), copied by a `${mcpp.self} stage` action whose input is the installation's stamp, then deployed. `prefix::deployed` lists the copies.
- **`rules-qt` `translations::qt_languages`**: `lconvert` combines the catalogs of the linked modules into `qt_<language>.qm` under `deploy_to`. This is the file windeployqt writes, and it has no dependency left to resolve.

**`rules-qt-xim-base`** declares `xim:qt-base` (openxlings/xim-pkgindex#881, merged): qtbase, qttools, qttranslations and the QtQml library lupdate loads. The download is 56–73 MB against 187–245 MB for `xim:qt`. `roots()` uses `xim:qt` when a project declares both.

Criteria (`.github/scripts/check-deps-and-qt.sh`):

| fixture | criteria |
|---|---|
| `tests/archive-consumer` (new) | emit extracts nothing; the program reads two members from beside itself; a C++ member that `#error`s is deployed as data, not compiled; a second build does not extract again; a changed archive does; the packed tree carries the files and the packed program reads them |
| `tests/vcpkg-consumer` | `share/fmt/copyright` deployed beside the program, and in the packed tree on Windows |
| `tests/qt-consumer` | now on `rules-qt-xim-base`; loads the combined `qt_de.qm` and prints Qt's own `QProgressDialog` "Cancel" as "Abbrechen" |

All three were run locally against the released 2026.9.26.2, with `xim:qt-base` installed from the index.

Also:
- The deps modules use index loops over strings (GCC 16 fails to inline a string iterator in a module interface).
- `deps-cmake` lists the `cmake` executable among its action's inputs (R3.1).
- The README documents the Linux ABI constraint between a libc++ toolchain and vcpkg ports built against libstdc++.

author: shady20-tech
body:
Reworks the primary navigation and adds the three routes it links to.

## Header

`Home · About us · Departments (dropdown) · Services · Gallery · Contact · Blog`

The three departments move out of the top-level bar and into a dropdown, so the bar no longer competes with the departments for the same job. Order is deliberate: Departments sits between "who we are" and "what we do".

On desktop the department anchors stay real links inside the panel. The panel is hidden with CSS `visibility` rather than unmounted, so all three departments remain in the DOM — crawlable, and usable if JavaScript fails to load. It opens on click, on hover (pointer devices only), and on `:focus-within`, so keyboard users never depend on the toggle handler. Escape and outside-click close it.

On mobile the drawer lists departments under a labelled group instead of nesting a dropdown, which would add a tap for no benefit on a small screen.

## Three new routes

`/services`, `/gallery` and `/blog` **had no routes at all**. Linking to them would have shipped three 404s: the `[locale]/[department]` dynamic segment swallows those URLs and calls `notFound()`. The pages are added here. Static segments win over dynamic ones, so they resolve correctly — verified 200 in both locales.

## Content honesty

`/services` is an index, not a catalogue. The brief supplies no itemised service names, prices or durations, so it routes to the three departments rather than inventing a list.

`/gallery` and `/blog` render **explicit empty states**. No project photography or articles were ever supplied, and the brief rules out fabricated content. Stock imagery, invented captions, or lorem-ipsum posts published under the company name would misrepresent real work. Both pages say plainly that nothing is published yet and route the visitor to a department.

`BlogPosting`/author/`datePublished` structured data is deliberately **not** emitted — there is no content behind it, and emitting it against empty pages is structured-data spam. It must accompany real posts when they arrive.

## Structural change

Nav is now built from one shared model, `buildPrimaryNav` (`src/lib/config/navigation.ts`), consumed by the desktop header, the mobile drawer **and** the sitemap. It was previously assembled inline in the locale layout, which made it impossible to unit-test and let the header and sitemap drift apart. `NAV_PATHS` is wired into `sitemap.ts`, so a route cannot be added to the header and forgotten in the sitemap.

## Verification

- `tsc` clean, `eslint` clean
- **106 tests pass** (13 new: nav model + dropdown behaviour, incl. that links stay in the DOM while closed)
- Build prerenders **31 routes**
- All routes 200 in both locales; no `[department]` collision
- Nav order confirmed in rendered HTML, EN and FR
- Titles correct, no duplicated brand name
- Reciprocal `hreflang` alternates present on all new pages
- New dropdown contrast pairs measured: link text **10.76:1**, hover **9.92:1**, chevron **11.19:1** — 0 failures

## Notes

Two pre-existing issues remain open and are **not** addressed here: the `manifest.webmanifest` 307 redirect, and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` still defaulting to `localhost:3000`, which would emit wrong canonicals in production.

This PR was created by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of the repository owner.

body:
Implements operator ruling A on todo GUI-D3: for CommNet, a ghost replaying a committed recording counts as the real vessel. It relays signal for live vessels, and it is a probe control point when its recorded crew qualifies (stock parity). Only the real run counts, never loop replays. The binding scenarios are in `docs/parsek-flight-recorder-design.md` section 15.6.

## What changed
- **`GhostCommNet.cs` (pure core):**
  - Antenna combination copied from stock `CommNetVessel.UpdateComm`, including the no-direct-antenna raw-sum quirk, the relay-enabler promotion and `rangeModifier`.
  - The control-point rule (`ModuleProbeControlPoint` + `minimumCrew` pilots).
  - The deploy-event timeline, the ghost-window check, the mod guard and the registration diff.
- **`GhostCommNetManager.cs` (live side):**
  - A free `CommNode` subclass with a `position` override and range curves that are never null.
  - Antenna specs derived from the vessel snapshot plus part prefabs (`CanCommUnloaded` / `CommPowerUnloaded` / `CanControlUnloaded`).
  - Position and power are set in the node's pre-update hook; a node goes dark rather than keeping a stale position, and nodes are re-added after a network reset.
  - Held ghosts keep their end-state antennas but sit where the spawning vessel is now: the spawn path's terminal orbit, or the terminal surface position.
- **Hosts:** `ParsekFlight` (flight view + map view) and `ParsekTrackingStation`. The ghost node is removed on the frame the real vessel spawns.
- **Removed:** the dead draft (`GhostCommNetRelay`, `AntennaSpec`) and the `Recording.AntennaSpecs` field, which was never written or serialized. No schema change.
- **New lanes:** `CN-1-ghost-commnet-relay` (FLIGHT) and `CN-1T-ghost-commnet-relay-ts` (TRACKSTATION) over a new `ghost-commnet-relay` injection preset:
  - relay A is crewed with a pilot;
  - relay B has playback disabled;
  - relay C is looped;
  - all three sit on a Kerbin-synchronous orbit over the KSC.
- **In-game category `GhostCommNet`:** the rulings, per-node state, and routing through the REAL registered node with a negative control.
- **Coverage:** D6 `commnet-relay` claimed; coverage goes from 243 to 244 of 247.
- **Docs:** design 15.6 (scenarios), CHANGELOG, todo (GUI-D3 closed, two follow-ups filed), autotest status and roadmap.

## Validation
- `dotnet test`: 25436 passed, 0 failed.
- Harness suites, all OK: `lib` (3353 tests), `provision` (260), `missions/lib` (2561).
- Clean-context review found one blocker: a held node drifted during warp. It was fixed in `8a52b83d2` and re-reviewed. Six mutations of the core were each caught by a test.
- **Flights** (automation DLL sha256 `fcbe2979...`):
  - First flights `2026-09-26_1121` / `_1122` were PARSEK-FAIL on the synthetic routing cell only. Its endpoint reached a preset relay directly, which is a test-geometry defect, fixed in `9eee0e80e`.
  - Reading runs `_1130` / `_1131` PASS, and armed re-flights `_1149` / `_1151` PASS on the exact pins. Each batch was `total=9 passed=4 failed=0 skipped=5`, with 0 GhostCommNet warnings.
  - `H28-map-presence` `_1123` PASS confirms its re-derived pin.
  - An offline negative control over 22 seeded faults turned red on all 22.
- **Known gaps (filed in todo):**
  - A chain-ghosted real vessel has no node between its first claim and its reappearance.
  - The Tracking Station never latches a playback-disabled recording's playhead when entered first.

author: andrew-agents[bot]
body:
## Problem
Family Assistant was periodically querying connected MCP servers (such as `ha-mcp` / Home Assistant MCP) with `list_tools` calls approximately every 30 to 34 seconds as part of `MCPToolsProvider._run_health_checks`.

Over 24 hours, `ha-mcp` logged 2,526 `ListToolsRequest` calls versus only 13 `CallToolRequest` calls. Repeatedly fetching full tool definitions and serializing extensive JSON schemas caused severe memory accumulation and leaks in upstream servers (e.g. `ha-mcp` memory climbing from 100 MiB to ~950 MiB).

## Changes
1. **Lightweight Liveness Check**:
   - `MCPToolsProvider._run_health_checks` now checks connection liveness using `session.send_ping()` (with fallback to `list_tools()` if `send_ping` is not implemented on the session).
   - `McpError` (e.g., `MethodNotFound` from servers without explicit ping support) is treated as a passing health check since receiving a valid JSON-RPC error response confirms the server transport and process are active.
   - Transport loss (`BrokenPipeError`, `ConnectionError`, etc.) marks the server as `failed` and triggers the existing scheduled reconnect and backoff logic.

2. **Decoupled Tool Refresh Interval**:
   - Tool discovery now occurs on initial connection (`initialize`), on reconnect (`_reconnect_server`), on-demand via a new public method `refresh_server_tools(server_id)`, or periodically based on `tool_refresh_interval_seconds`.
   - `tool_refresh_interval_seconds` defaults to 30 minutes (`1800.0`s), significantly relaxing the frequency from 30s to 30m. Setting it to `None` disables periodic tool polling.
   - Added `mcp_health_check_interval_seconds` (default: 30) and `mcp_tool_refresh_interval_seconds` (default: 1800) to `ToolsConfig` and `defaults.yaml`, wired through `Assistant` when constructing `MCPToolsProvider`.

3. **Testing**:
   - Updated existing tool refresh tests to set `tool_refresh_interval_seconds=0` so tool reconciliation is explicitly validated.
   - Updated reconnect backoff tests to verify ping health checking.
   - Added unit tests in `tests/unit/tools/test_mcp_health_check.py` covering:
     - Health checks preferring `send_ping` over `list_tools`
     - Fallback to `list_tools` when `send_ping` is absent
     - `McpError` handling during ping
     - Transport failure detection and teardown
     - Skipping tool refresh when interval has not elapsed
     - Refreshing tools when interval has elapsed
     - Disabling periodic refresh when interval is `None`
     - On-demand `refresh_server_tools`
     - Default configuration settings in `ToolsConfig`

author: samuel-ku
body:
## Що знайшлось

Коли я заводив #1022, я описав це як **конфлікт вимог #553 і #991** і чекав рішення власника, який варіант обрати. Розібравшись із ним як слід, бачу: **це не конфлікт вимог і не привід щось міняти у вигляді сторінки книги.** Тест просто перевіряв не ту властивість.

## Що насправді відбувається

Hero малює обкладинку на всю ширину, прикріплену до **гори**, і кладе зверху два скрими: верхній 140 dp (чорний 55 % → прозорий) — щоб іконки тулбара читалися, і нижній 360 dp, що переходить у фон сторінки — щоб було на чому сидіти заголовку. Обидва — свідомий дизайн.

Виміряв на емуляторі API 35 (фікстура 400×600, вузол 1080×1727), стовпчик по центру:

```
y=0     r=0.45   ← верхня смуга джерела, затемнена верхнім скримом
y=100   b=0.60   ← тіло обкладинки
y=1000  b=0.75   ← ще обкладинка
y=1500  фон      ← нижній скрим уже перейшов у фон сторінки
```

Звідси видно, що старе твердження «обидві смуги вижили» **не може** виконуватися: верхня затемнена нижче будь-якого строгого порогу червоного, а нижня лежить під непрозорим градієнтом.

І обрізання тут узагалі ні до чого. Для **всіх** реальних пропорцій обкладинка коротша за hero (2:3 → 616 dp < 642 dp), тож `height(maxOf(natural, hero))` виводить її на висоту hero, а `Crop` показує зображення **цілком**, зрізаючи ≈8 dp з кожного боку. Тобто те, чого хотів #553 («повна обкладинка»), фактично працює.

## Що зроблено

Тест переписано на контракт, який дизайн справді дає:

1. верхній край обкладинки видно в горі hero (із поправкою на скрим — «червонуватий», а не `red > 0.8`);
2. обкладинка займає **всю ширину** (не в рамці);
3. квадрат лишається квадратом (центровий зонд у `waitUntil`).

Фікстуру зсунуто з 1:2 (200×400 — пропорція, якої не має жодна обкладинка) на реальні 2:3 і 1:1.

## Перевірка

Позитивний прогін і **два негативні контролі**, щоб тест не був порожнім:

| Стан | Результат |
|---|---|
| як є | ✅ 2 тести |
| обкладинку звузити (`fillMaxWidth(0.5f)`) | ❌ «must span the full width» |
| прибрати верхній маркер із фікстури | ❌ таймаут завантаження |

Плюс `scripts/run-instrumented-suites.sh` — усі 5 сюїт зелені.

Тобто #1022 закривається **без зміни вигляду сторінки книги**: показувати обкладинку цілком уже працює для реальних пропорцій, а тест тепер це фіксує замість протилежного.

Closes #1022.

author: sutharanshul
body:
Three commits that have been sitting off `main` since September. Merging this is what puts them on the domain — it currently serves the Sep 11 build.

## What's in it

**`78642e0` — More from the project, on a board, and the frames stand still**
Seven more Incentiwise screens on a board. Drops `Interlace.tsx` and `Tube.tsx`, and stops the frames moving.

**`cf40b37` — Stand the crosshair aside over the name**
`CustomCursor` and `NameMark`: the crosshair steps aside rather than sitting on the letters.

**`6a355e6` — Strip the site back to one mark, and give Incentiwise its own scroll**
The large one, and the reason this is worth a look before it goes live.

*The chrome is gone.* Four layers of it — `LayoutShell`, `SideNav`, `MobileChrome`, `BreadcrumbNav` — replaced by a single fixed name-mark that is also the way home. The work index stops being a route (`app/work/page.tsx` deleted) and becomes the second half of the home page, because with no rail there is nothing to navigate to.

*Things that hung off the rail went with it.* The chat cat and its endpoint (`app/api/chat/route.ts`, `ChatDrawer`, `OrionCat`, `lib/profile.ts`, `lib/meow.ts`), all audio (`lib/audio.ts`, `SoundControl`), plus `Presenter`, `AboutStage`, `PhoneOnly`. The About portrait is gone too.

*What replaces them.* `Shell` holds the mark. `Veil` puts glass under it — `backdrop-filter` for blur, since a canvas cannot sample the document behind it, and a shader for the colour on top. `CaseIndex` runs a tape of frame titles in a record's margin, read from what each frame is already called. `Lightbox` opens any picture at its own size and zooms at the pointer. `lib/frame-size.ts` reads real image dimensions from file headers at build time, so a record's height is known before anything loads — without it the index reported frame 15 to a reader at the top of the page.

*Incentiwise becomes a long scroll.* Ten acts, its own markup and stylesheet scoped under `.story`. Images written out as files rather than inline, which took a 7MB document to 88KB that fetches what it reaches. `StoryFit` scales the whole 1440px piece with `zoom` rather than a transform, so the page is as tall as the scaled record. `StoryBackground` gives each act's colour to the page instead of painting it behind the content.

## Verified

- `pnpm build` clean — 7 static pages, no type errors
- Dev server driven in Chromium at 1440×900 and 390×844
- All routes 200: `/`, `/work/aris`, `/work/incentiwise`, `/work/superhealth`, `/work/solic-arc`
- No console errors, no page errors on any route

## Worth knowing before merging

This removes user-facing features on purpose — the chat cat, all sound, the old navigation. That is the intent of the change, not a side effect, but it is the thing to be sure about, since merging deploys it.

author: ogsamrat
body:
## What

The project archive never includes gitignored content any more: `node_modules/`, `dist/`, build output, venvs and caches can be rebuilt, and they made single projects many gigabytes (one production session was 13 GB). This applies to base, delta and final archives, in whole-folder mode (git, `git_parent` and all-folders) and in touched-files mode. The workspace snapshots already worked this way.

## How

New `apps/server/src/session-archive/ignore.ts`. Git decides, using all of its rules: every `.gitignore`, `.git/info/exclude` and `core.excludesFile`.

- **Root in a repository**: one `git ls-files -z --others --ignored --exclude-standard --directory` in the root, with `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` at home like every archive git run. An ignored directory comes back as a single `dir/` line, so pass 1 drops it before any `lstat`, and nothing inside it is walked. Tracked files are never ignored (a force-added `dist/vendor.js` stays).
- **Folder in no repository** (all-folders policy): the same command, with a private, empty, bare `GIT_DIR` (`git init --bare --template=` in a fresh `mkdtemp` dir, removed after the scan) and the root as `GIT_WORK_TREE`. The folder's `.gitignore` files apply exactly as git would apply them, and nothing is written into the folder.
- **Nested repository** (submodule or cloned dependency): the outer git never looks inside one, so when the scan enters it, that repository is asked for its own answer.
- **Without git** (missing, over the 2 min timeout, or more than 2M ignored paths): the collector's walkFallback `.gitignore` rules (`scopedIgnoreRules` / `ignoredByRules`, now exported).
- **Always kept**: `.git/` (history) and every `.gitignore` file.
- **Touched files**: `git check-ignore -z --stdin` runs over the touched files only, so the folder is never walked. An ignored touched file is skipped and counts as gone, so a delta deletes the chain's copy.
- **Deltas**: an ignored path is not in the scan. A path that becomes ignored shows up in `deleted` (descendants included), and one that stops being ignored is added again. A rename into an ignored folder is a deletion.

## Unchanged

Credentials denylist, size caps, ORSEAL01 format and seal vectors, consent/policy, and the upload protocol are all unchanged. The manifest keeps exactly the same keys and the same six `excluded` counters. The ignored count goes only to the "OmniRush project archive queued" log line (`gitignored`).

## Backend doc change needed (not edited here)

author: smaug123
body:
Moves the definition-level half of the interpreter's vtable layout (`VirtualSlotLayout`) into `WoofWare.PawPrint.Loader`, as a new module, `MethodTableLayout`. It computes three things for a type definition:
- which slot each declaration owns;
- what each vtable slot holds once MethodImpls are applied;
- the slots beyond the vtable.

## Why

This is a prerequisite for the `MemberRef` resolver the exception-escape analyser needs. CoreCLR's `MemberLoader::FindMethod` searches a type's *method table*, including every inherited vtable slot, from the end. Codex found a case where walking the ancestry instead gives the wrong method: generic substitution makes two distinct slots' signatures coincide, and only slot order decides between them. The resolver lives in Loader, so it needs the real slot layout there. Keeping one implementation of that layout, rather than a second copy in the resolver, is the point of this PR.

## Two commits

1. **In place, no behaviour change.** The definition-level code touched `IlMachineState` only as a carrier of loaded assemblies and concrete types, plus three wrappers over Loader functions (`resolveTypeFromRef`, `signaturesEquivalent`, `methodConstraintsMatch`). It now takes a `TypeConcretization.ConcretizationContext`, in a module placed before `IlMachineStateModel.fs` in compile order, so the compiler confirms it cannot reach the state.
   - The edits to the moved code are mechanical: `state` becomes `ctx`; the `BaseClassTypes` parameter becomes `dotnetRuntimeDirs`, since the context carries `BaseTypes`; the wrappers become direct Loader calls.
   - `VirtualSlotLayout` keeps the closed-type walks and the dispatch memo. It gains one adapter, `inContext`, and its state-taking functions keep their names and signatures as wrappers over it.
   - The pure helpers (`declaredMethodsOf`, `slotIndexInTable` and similar, and the `MethodSlotTable` type) are now called as `MethodTableLayout.*` directly.
2. **A pure move into Loader.** `scripts/check-move-is-rename-only.sh HEAD~1` reports the file differing only in its namespace and `open` lines, and it built in Loader without an edit.

**Breaking:** the helpers listed above leave the published `WoofWare.PawPrint` surface for `WoofWare.PawPrint.Loader`'s. WoofWare.PawPrint is already at 0.10 on `main` from #1558, and that bump is unreleased.

## Testing

No behaviour change is intended.
- Default suite: 3,939 passed, 1 skipped (after each commit).
- Guest suite: 1,248 passed (after each commit).
- Docstring-attachment check: clean.
- Codex review: nothing to act on. Its one Guest failure was a socket operation its own sandbox denied.

author: mickaelrebeau
body:
Closes #6

## Problème
1. Pas de paramètre `state` OAuth → risque CSRF (login forcé sur le compte d'un attaquant).
2. Le JWT était passé dans l'URL de callback (`/auth/callback?token=...`) → fuite possible via historique, logs, referrer, analytics.

## Changements
**State anti-CSRF**
- `GET /api/auth/google` génère un `state` aléatoire, envoyé à Google et stocké dans un cookie `oauth_state` (httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, 10 min, Secure si l'URI de redirection est en https, path `/api/auth/google`).
- Le callback compare le cookie et le `state` (`compare_digest`). En cas d'écart → `/login?error=google_oauth&reason=invalid_state`. Le cookie est supprimé après usage.
- Le cookie reste sur le domaine du backend, du départ vers Google jusqu'au retour : ça fonctionne même si le front est sur un autre domaine.

**Plus de JWT dans l'URL**
- Le callback redirige vers `/auth/callback?code=…` : code aléatoire à usage unique, valable 60 s (Redis `oauth_code:*`, ou en mémoire si Redis est indisponible). Voir `app/services/oauth_service.py`.
- Nouvel endpoint `POST /api/auth/google/exchange` `{code}` → `AuthResponse`. Un code rejoué ou inconnu → `400`.
- Front : `AuthCallbackView.vue` retire le code de l'URL dès lecture, puis `completeGoogleCallback(code)` fait l'échange. `initializeAuth` n'accepte plus `?token=`. Nouveau message d'erreur `invalid_state` dans `LoginView.vue`.

## Tests
- `tests/test_auth_google.py` (6 tests) : cookie de `state` posé, `state` absent ou falsifié rejeté, redirection avec un code et non un JWT, échange qui marche une seule fois, code inconnu rejeté.
- Suite backend complète : 20 tests verts (PostgreSQL 16 dans Docker).
- Stockage des codes vérifié sur un Redis 7 jetable : TTL 60 s, code consommé une seule fois.
- `npm run build` (front) OK.

## Déploiement
⚠️ Déployer le front et le backend ensemble : l'ancien front attend `?token=` et le nouveau backend ne l'envoie plus.

- [ ] Connexion Google de bout en bout en prod après déploiement

author: jleni
body:
#397 shipped a selector that matches nothing. Found while explaining why that
PR needed conformance before a release — the concern turned out to be concrete.

## The bug

Warm members are labelled with a hash of the **upstream WarmPool's** name,
which is `kobe-<pool>` (`management_object_name`,
`sandbox_pool_certification.rs:90`). The selector hashed the **SandboxPool's
own** name.

For a pool `agents`: the label is `hash("kobe-agents")`, the selector asked for
`hash("agents")`.

## Why this is worse than destructive

It is not destructive — `delete_collection` removes zero objects and returns
`Ok`. So:

1. no warm member is deleted
2. the new `resourceVersion` is recorded anyway
3. the rotation is marked handled
4. every warm member keeps serving the old credential

Silent, and indistinguishable from working. The exact failure #374 reports,
now with a status field claiming it was fixed.

## The fix

`warm_member_selector` lives beside `management_object_name`, so the selector
and the name it depends on cannot drift. The call site in `sandbox.rs` asks for
the selector rather than rebuilding it.

`the_warm_selector_hashes_the_upstream_name_not_the_pool_name` pins both the
name and, explicitly, that hashing the pool's own name is **not** it.

## Why #397's tests could not catch it

They cover `secret_rotated` — the pure decision, "did this version move". That
is correct and still passes. Nothing exercised the selector, the Secret read,
or the delete, which are the parts that talk to a cluster.

A conformance run would have shown it. Unit tests over a hash comparison never
could, and I said as much when arguing this change needed one before a release
rather than after.

## Verification

1707 tests (one new), `clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` clean.

Still unvalidated against a cluster: no CI run has executed on `main` since
`b694e43`.

author: smartpbx
body:
Fixes the intermittent `StashScanWorkspaceViewModelTests.A_snapshot_saved_while_the_page_is_open_appears_without_navigating` failure, "The calling thread cannot access this object because a different thread owns it" from `DefaultRenderLoop.Add`. It failed on main Windows run 36228754571 and on #940's Linux run 36225649223 (attempt 1). No issue.

**Root cause.** #869 made `HeadlessSessions` single-owner, which keeps two sessions apart. It does not keep the rest of the suite apart. Avalonia 12.1.2's `HeadlessUnitTestSession.EnsureIsolatedApplication` calls `Dispatcher.ResetBeforeUnitTests()`, which sets the UI-thread dispatcher to null, and then `SetupUnsafe()`. In that window, the first thread in the process that touches `Dispatcher.UIThread` gets a new dispatcher, and that dispatcher becomes the UI thread (`s_uiThread ??= this`). The headless platform then builds its `DefaultRenderLoop`, whose `Add` calls `Dispatcher.UIThread.VerifyAccess()`, and the check fails on the session's own thread. The Stash scan class was the only class that starts a session without `[Collection(AvaloniaHeadlessCollection.Name)]`, so it ran in parallel with view-model tests. About 35 App files call `Dispatcher.UIThread`, and these tests call it from pool threads. So did this class's own other tests.

**Fix (tests only).** `StashScanWorkspaceViewModelTests` joins the headless collection (`DisableParallelization = true`), so nothing runs beside its session. The `HeadlessSessions` remark now says the semaphore alone is not enough. Every other class that starts a session was already in the collection (grep over `tests/`). The product is correct: the view model's `SnapshotSaved`, guided-scan and capture-status handlers all marshal through `Dispatcher.UIThread.Post`, so there is no product race.

**Repeats** on `dev`, one build slot, 4-core busy-loop stressor bounded with `timeout`. Each round runs StashScan + V2Shell + V2MapRenderer + V2Raid + V2DesignSystem + Personalization (1312 tests), which includes every headless class:

| | Thread-owner failures | Other failures |
|---|---|---|
| Before (main b97e7cf4) | **3/20** (plus 1/1 in an unstressed first run) | 0 |
| After | **0/20** | 2/20, see below |

The 2 other failures are a separate flake: `MapLabelPlacementTests.Placing_again_at_a_new_zoom_allocates_nothing` (from #931) measured 2784 and 5800 bytes against an expected 0. It is a synchronous single-thread allocation count under CPU load, and this change only affects which classes run in parallel. Not fixed here; reported to the coordinator.

Whole UnitTests project on `dev`: 5908/5908 passed.

## Contexto verificado antes de este PR

- `max_positions_open` existía solo en texto de estado, sin ningún chequeo real.

## Cambios
1. **Registro de aperturas LIVE** — `record_live_trade_open()`/`get_live_trades()`, escrito al abrir una posición real (`~/.vectrax/etoro_live_trades.jsonl`).
2. **Detección de cierres LIVE** — `check_live_positions_closed()`, en el mismo ciclo que `check_open_positions()`. Compara contra `get_portfolio()`; si el bróker no da el PnL realizado, marca `closed_pnl_pending` y avisa por Telegram — **nunca inventa un PnL**.
3. **Registro único** — `trade_id` ahora obligatorio y deduplicado también en LIVE (mismo `_locked_config()` que ya protegía PAPER).
4. **Máximo de posiciones** — `check_risk_before_trade()` ahora sí aplica `max_positions_open`; en LIVE cuenta contra el bróker real, y si la consulta falla, bloquea (fail closed).
5. **Validación de límites** — `validate_risk_limit()` con techos duros (constantes de módulo, no configurables por Telegram): `max_position_usd` ≤ $200, `max_daily_loss_usd` ≤ $50 (techos confirmados por el creador), rangos para el resto.
6. **Cortacircuitos → pausa de 24h, no reversión a PAPER** (cambio adicional pedido en el mismo PR): pérdidas consecutivas y límite de pérdida diaria activan una pausa de 24h; el modo se queda en LIVE todo el tiempo. `check_risk_before_trade()` bloquea entradas nuevas durante la pausa; se levanta sola al vencer (reinicia contadores, avisa por Telegram en ambos extremos). El HALT manual es completamente independiente. La pausa persiste en la misma config JSON — un reinicio no la acorta.
7. **Documentación** — encabezado de `auto_executor.py` corregido para describir el comportamiento real.

## Tests
`tests/test_live_trading_safety.py` (nuevo): cierre único/duplicado, `max_positions_open` en ambos modos, fallo del bróker (fail closed), `closed_pnl_pending`, activación/bloqueo/reanudación automática de la pausa, independencia del HALT, persistencia tras reinicio.

Se actualizó un test preexistente en `test_etoro_auto_live_promotion.py` cuya premisa (el cortacircuito revierte a PAPER) el creador reemplazó explícitamente por la pausa.

**Suite completa (equivalente a `make check`) verificada contra `origin/main` limpio**: mismas 4 fallas preexistentes y no relacionadas en ambos casos, cero regresiones nuevas (4849 vs 4803 passed — la diferencia son los 46 tests nuevos de este PR).

## Explícitamente fuera de alcance
No se tocó aprendizaje, patrones, estrellas, convergencias, TA-Lib, las condiciones de `entry_validator`, el modo, `ETORO_ENVIRONMENT` ni credenciales. No se desplegó ni se reinició ningún proceso.

author: marshallofsound
body:
#### Description of Change

Follow-up to #53664.

- `requestPointerLock()` reaches the browser over the requesting frame's local-root widget, so an iframe that shares its parent's renderer process (for example a same-site, cross-origin child) was reported to `setPermissionRequestHandler` with the parent's `requestingUrl` and `isMainFrame`. A new patch carries the requesting frame with the request and `WebContentsImpl` records it; the permission helper reports that frame.
- `keyboard.lock()` is main-frame only, so the keyboard lock request is attributed to the primary main frame directly, and refused if the lock widget is ever not the main frame's.
- The pointer lock spec now covers a cross-site child and a same-site cross-origin child.

author: iskhakovt
body:
## What

This is the part of step 2 in `design/prompt-caching.md` that ships ahead of the turn context. A `freeze-turn-inputs` step freezes:
- in chat turns: the voice decision and the batch-delivery decision;
- in chat and pipeline stage turns: the tool table.

## Why

These were resolved in the bare function body, which Inngest re-runs at every step boundary. They come from reads that can change or fail between invocations of the same turn: the profile, the voice config, the delivery handle's sessions, and the image, skill, sub-agent and MCP catalogs. So a later iteration could:
- send a different `tools` param, which breaks the prompt cache mid-turn;
- skip a voice reply its prompt was assembled for;
- add or drop the `batch-delivery` step. After a parallel tool group, steps are requested by name, so a missing one fails the turn with `step-not-found`.

Tests reproduced each before the change.

## How

- **The tool table:** the step returns each tool's data half, its definition plus the policy the loop dispatches on (`durable`, `parallelSafe`, `sideEffectful`, `invocationBudget`). Every invocation binds live handlers to it (`bindFrozenTools`). A frozen tool with no live handler gets an `is_error` result, or its replayed result if its durable step already ran.
- **Returned as JSON text:** the Inngest server hands memoized objects back with their keys sorted at every depth (measured on the dev server). Returned as an object, the table would change the `tools` bytes after the first invocation. `.claude/rules/inngest.md` now says so.
- **Delivery steps:** `voice-delivery` and `batch-delivery` are gated on the frozen decisions. Their live capability checks run inside the steps, which skip if the capability is gone.
- **No cassette changes:** request bytes on a normal turn are unchanged.

## Tests

Replay tests, each red before its change:
- a skill that stops loading mid-turn;
- voice switched off mid-turn;
- batch targets that disappear or appear between invocations;
- a cached table replayed from the server's key-sorted copy, for chat and stage turns.

## Residuals

Recorded in `design/crash-recovery.md`:
- **Profile reads:** the frozen table and the base prompt can come from profile reads in different invocations, if a settings change lands between them. `# Tools` and `tools` always match.
- **A tool edited mid-turn:** it keeps its frozen definition while the live handler serves the call.
- **Deploy:** a run in flight whose next step is requested by name (after a parallel tool group) fails with `step-not-found`, because the new build stops at the unrun `freeze-turn-inputs`. Other in-flight runs execute it once.

## Also

- **Retention:** the design now states when the 1-hour cache pays for itself: once the share of replies between five minutes and an hour passes a bar that falls as a conversation grows. Early production gaps sit near that bar for mid-sized conversations and above it for long ones, so step 2 keeps its switch of chat and pipeline runs to `"long"`.
- **Other early measurements** (tool-calling share, core-memory edit rate) are recorded as inconclusive rather than sized, since they come from little use and low counts may reflect bugs.
- **New p3:** a `tool_use` named after a `generate_image` parameter.

Supersedes #2 (a plain bump to TS 7 breaks `npm run check` and `npm run lint`).

author: hmbown
body:
Stacked on #6618. The base is that branch, so this diff shows only this slice. GitHub retargets it to `main` once #6618 merges.

## What was wrong

Codewhale's deliberate catalog holds existed only as hand edits to the offline seed (`models_dev.bundled.json`). They covered prices left out where a flat rate would mislead, and DeepSeek's output limit kept at its published 384K. A live Models.dev refresh replaces seed rows wholesale, so the holds disappeared on every networked install. Upstream today:
- **MiMo and DeepSeek:** priced.
- **Alibaba Token and Coding Plan rows:** listed at `$0`, which reads as free.
- **DeepSeek output limit:** `393216`.

The "honesty" rule in the seed's `_meta` was prose that the runtime never read.

## The fix

The holds now live in `crates/config/assets/catalog_corrections.json` as field patches in the cloud-facts `ModelFact` shape. The signed layer's patch code applies them to every Models.dev row as it is hydrated, whether it comes from the bundled seed (`bundled_catalog_offerings`) or a live refresh (`live_offerings_from_models_dev`). A correction therefore ranks above both Models.dev layers and below signed cloud facts and provider rosters. The same correction holds online and offline.

- **`ModelFact.pricing_withheld: Option<String>`** (a reason) clears the price, so the route reports `PricingSku::UnknownOrStale`. The field is optional, and payloads without it parse unchanged. Per-provider rules expand to one withheld-price patch per row.
- **One patch path.** `catalog_patch::apply_patches` is shared. Signed facts may create rows; corrections may not. The loader refuses:
  - hide, deprecate and `allow_unlisted`;
  - labels;
  - a patch that changes nothing;
  - a limit patch without a reason.
- **A corrected row keeps its own `source`.** The price a correction owns reports `CatalogSource::CodewhaleBundled` through `cost_source`. See the deviations section for why.
- **Dead field removed.** `CatalogCompiler.codewhale_bundled` was declared, but nothing had ever set it. The layer docs in `catalog.rs`, `CATALOG_REFRESH.md` and `CLOUD_FACTS.md` now describe the rank where corrections actually apply.

## Reasoning controls (second commit)

Regenerating the seed in #6612 turned up a second kind of hold that works only offline: reasoning controls. Before this change, a live refresh replaced all of these, and the picker, `/effort` and the effort clamp all read them:
- **Grok:** default effort `high` (xAI docs, #6501).
- **MiniMax M2.7:** thinking always on.
- **MiniMax M3:** thinking is adaptive or disabled, with a different default per dialect.
- **qwen3.8-max:** thinking-only.
- **Muse Spark:** also takes the `none` and `ultra` efforts.
- **Step 3.5:** reasoning is adaptive.

`ModelFact.reasoning_options` (optional) replaces a row's controls and keeps any signed annotation already on the row. These 18 rows get corrections, each with the source it cites.

Two groups were left out:
- **GLM-5.3's high/max ladder.** It was only a placeholder inherited from GLM-5.2, and upstream now publishes low/high/max.
- **The Coding Plan qwen `budget_tokens` entries.** They were copies of Token Plan rows, not a Codewhale decision.

## Each hold, checked again on its merits

| Hold | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek native pricing | kept (provider rule) | billed by time of day; `crates/tui/src/pricing.rs` has the time-aware table |
| xAI pricing | kept (provider rule) | upstream's own `tiers` field shows rates doubling past 200K |
| Xiaomi MiMo pricing | kept (provider rule) | PAYG and Token Plan keys cannot be told apart |
| Model Studio Token/Coding Plan pricing (4 providers) | kept (provider rules) | plan quota, not per-token; upstream `0` would read as free |
| StepFun pricing | kept (provider rule) | the same ids serve Step Plan and PAYG; `pricing.rs` has endpoint-scoped rates |
| DeepSeek native `max_output` 384000 | kept, marked unverified | DeepSeek publishes 384K; upstream 393216 = 384×1024. Which value the API accepts is unverified, and the lower bound is always accepted. Settling it takes one real provider call (provider spend, so a human runs it) |
| MiniMax-M3 pricing | **added** | upstream tiers the price at 512K, the same rule as Grok. The seed already listed it unpriced without saying why |
| aggregator-hosted DeepSeek pricing (9 rows) | kept (restored in the third commit) | I dropped this first, then #6612's generated seed broke `hosted_flash_and_pro_routes_price_from_bundled_docs_rates`. `crates/tui/src/pricing.rs` prices these routes from a reviewed provider-docs table (Fireworks V4 Pro: 1.74 vs Models.dev 1.20), and a catalog rate outranks it |
| Novita DeepSeek `max_output` 384000 | **added** | same published-384K question as native DeepSeek (upstream 393216) |
| grok-4.3 `reasoning_options: []` | **added** | xAI documents no effort control for 4.3 (#6501); upstream lists a ladder |
| OpenRouter `dots-3-note-preview:free` pricing | **dropped** | a free model's price is `0` |
| zai `GLM-5.3` pricing | kept (restored in the fourth commit) | I first dropped it, reasoning that `zai` was the pay-as-you-go API. That was wrong: `DEFAULT_ZAI_BASE_URL` is the Coding Plan (`api/coding/paas/v4`), which bills credits |
| MiMo 2.6 text-only image input | **dropped** | #6618 made a stale text-only row harmless; holding it down would strip images |
| MiMo 1,000,000 context | **dropped** | the only citation was our own rows; upstream says 1,048,576 |

## Deviations from the approved design

- **Where corrections apply.** The design put corrections inside `CatalogCompiler::compile`. But `CatalogCompiler` is only used in tests; the runtime merge is `crates/tui/src/provider_lake.rs::compute_merged_snapshot`. Applying corrections at hydration, the single funnel both Models.dev layers pass through, reaches the resolver, the provider lake, pricing fallbacks and the export path without adding a second merge.
- **Row source.** The design relabelled corrected rows `CodewhaleBundled`. That moved a live Models.dev row across a layer boundary: `CatalogCompiler::with_live` sorts rows by source, so a relabelled row ranked above signed facts, and `signed_facts_correct_a_live_models_dev_row_but_never_the_provider_roster` failed. Rows now keep their source, and only the owned price is attributed to `CodewhaleBundled`.

## Not in this PR

- **Tiered pricing is inconsistent.** Upstream tiers 569 rows by prompt length. The seed prices the OpenAI gpt-5.5/5.6 rows (tier at 272K) and three OpenRouter Qwen rows (256K) at their base rate while withholding Grok and MiniMax-M3. The real fix is tier-aware pricing, not more holds, and it needs its own issue.
- **A third offline store still overlaps.** The legacy `crates/models/assets/model_catalog.bundled.json` duplicates some of these facts. Its module doc already schedules removal once the `models`/`pricing` compat callers migrate.
- **Upstream providers are matched by id.** A new upstream MiMo or Model Studio id is covered by the provider rules, but a new upstream provider id is not.

## Verification

body:
Replaces #2040. That branch's history diverged and a force-push is blocked, so this is the same work rebased onto `origin/master` 17274b3a44.

Makes the Windows OS-matrix jobs green at the root for the failures found in [run 36105161718](https://github.com/ScriptedAlchemy/tracedecay/actions/runs/36105161718).

Root causes fixed:
- **Verbatim `\\?\` vs plain root identity (production):** the daemon compared registered roots, runtime-registry keys, LSP owners, and multi-root locators against raw `canonicalize()`, which on Windows never equals the stored plain identity. The HTTP cold resolver answered 503 `http.project_router_unavailable`, LSP admission was `Denied`, and multi-root was `unavailable`. These now use `canonical_existing_identity`.
- **Verbatim fixture roots (tests):** shared fixtures (`tests/common`, dashboard, mcp_suite, CLI scope, global-db, profile registry) built roots with raw `canonicalize()`. They now use the same identity authority production emits.
- **Private-fs ACL:** `set_private_dir_permissions` was a no-op on Windows, so hook spool readers refused inherited-ACE dirs as unsafe. It now installs the protected current-user DACL through `tracedecay_private_fs::make_private_directory`.
- **Read-only flush:** feedback permission restore now flushes through a writable handle. `FlushFileBuffers` needs write access.
- **Process spawning:** PATH lookup skips extensionless npm shims that CreateProcess cannot launch. ast-grep resolves npm's native `.exe`.
- **Host binary spelling:** host lifecycle expectations now use the installed forward-slash `.exe` path that production writes.
- **Handle sharing:** the quarantine recovery test drops the pre-restart handle, and the rebind test asserts that Windows refuses renaming a held capability.
- **Init admission:** repository discovery reports the verbatim worktree root on Windows, so exact equality refused every fixture and host init as `project_not_enrolled`. It now uses `same_canonical_path`, and so does the core-admission graph match.
- **Skill lifecycle exports:** `uses_default_user_profile` compared `profile_root == home/.tracedecay` exactly. A verbatim home never matched a plain profile, so no host received the change. It is now one shared helper using `same_canonical_path`. Hermes pending paths now join by component, so separators stay native.
- **Fixture JSON:** a raw Windows path pasted into a JSON string literal is an invalid escape. The Cursor composer fixture now builds its params with `serde_json`.
- **Misc:** a missing daemon authority record now reports "TraceDecay daemon is not available". Removed a debug `/tmp` proof write from `lcm_load_session`.

author: lfventura
body:
Adds a `pritunl_administrator` resource managing the logins of the web console and of the API — the accounts that operate Pritunl itself, as opposed to `pritunl_user`'s VPN profiles. Like the settings resource, it has been running in production for a while as part of the `lfventura/pritunl` fork and this ports it back.

**Stacked on #129** (they share the API client plumbing): the review surface is the last commit.

## What it manages

`username` (with Pritunl's own normalisation mirrored, so the configured value keeps matching what the API reports), the write-only `password` (required to create an account, never read back, kept as-is when left out), `super_user`, `auth_api` with the generated `token`/`secret` exposed read-only, `otp_auth`/`local_otp_auth` (mutually exclusive, enforced at plan time), `yubikey_id` (whole OTPs accepted and truncated to the public id, like the console) and `disabled`. The read-only `default` flag tells the seeded account apart.

## Design notes

- **Every write is a read-modify-write of the complete administrator object**: `PUT /admin/<id>` is a full replace, and a request that leaves a field out has it reset rather than kept — a rename alone would otherwise strip the super user flag and rotate the API credentials.
- **The seeded account is adoptable**: the importer takes the object id or the username and resolves it through the API, so `terraform import pritunl_administrator.default pritunl` works without looking ids up first.
- **Pritunl's own guards are surfaced with their meaning**: last super user (`no_super_users`), last enabled admin (`no_admins_enabled`), duplicate username (`admin_username_exists`).
- **Requires the provider's account to be a super user** — `/admin` refuses everybody else with `requires_super_user` — and the docs warn about the account managing itself: `auth_api = false` or `disabled = true` on it revokes the credentials Terraform is holding mid-run.

## Testing

Acceptance tests (lifecycle, adoption, credential generation, the mutual exclusions and Pritunl's guards) plus unit tests for the username/yubikey normalisation. Docs and examples included.

author: harshitnub077
body:
### Summary

Fix two conformance and lifecycle issues in the POSIX spinlock implementation:
1. Convert negative return codes from `k_spin_trylock()` in `pthread_spin_trylock()` so that contention returns `EBUSY` instead of `-EBUSY`.
2. Invalidate the descriptor handle upon destruction in `pthread_spin_destroy()` by setting `*lock = (pthread_spinlock_t)-1`, aligning with the behavior of `pthread_mutex_destroy()`, `pthread_cond_destroy()`, `pthread_rwlock_destroy()`, and `pthread_barrier_destroy()`.

### Motivation

- Under POSIX (IEEE Std 1003.1), `pthread_*` synchronization functions return zero on success and a positive error number on failure. `pthread_spin_trylock()` forwarded the return value of `k_spin_trylock()`, returning `-EBUSY` on contention and causing callers checking `ret == EBUSY` to fail.
- `pthread_spin_destroy()` released the bit in `posix_spinlock_bitarray` but left `*lock` marked initialized. Stale references to destroyed spinlocks could subsequently access or mutate newly allocated spinlocks that reallocated the same pool slot.

### Testing

Added regression assertions in `tests/subsys/portability/posix/spinlocks`:
- Verified that calling `pthread_spin_destroy()` marks the handle as invalid (`-1`).
- Verified that calling `pthread_spin_lock()`, `pthread_spin_trylock()`, `pthread_spin_unlock()`, or `pthread_spin_destroy()` on a destroyed handle returns `EINVAL`.
- Verified that reallocating the recycled pool slot with a new spinlock does not revive access through the stale destroyed handle.

Fixes #120412

author: thefrederiksen
body:
Part A of the plan on #3311 (comment "Audit of the macOS install path"): every error the macOS install script and the setup wizard show, or die of, reaches the Gateway's public, no-sign-in `POST /install-reports`, and lands in a local log.

## What changes
- **`install-mac.sh`**
  - An ERR trap now reports any command that fails without its own check (mkdir, mv, open, shasum...). Before, those stopped the script with no report and no ERROR line of ours.
  - Each report names the real step (`preconditions`, `download`, `verify`, `unpack`, `place`, `open`) instead of always `download`.
  - Every line is also written to `~/Library/Application Support/cc-director/logs/setup/install-mac-<time>.log`, and a failure prints that path.
  - The failure path runs with `set +e`, so a command failing inside the reporting cannot stop the script before it has said where the log is. A test run showed exactly that: `uuidgen` missing made it exit 127.
- **Wizard (`tools/cc-director-setup-avalonia`)**
  - Crash handlers: unhandled, unobserved task, UI thread, and start failure. Each logs and reports; the UI-thread one shows the error on screen with Retry.
  - An exception out of an install or repair run is caught, shown with Retry, logged and reported. It used to leave a disabled "Installing..." button with nothing said.
  - A failed release fetch, including a GitHub rate limit, is reported, not only shown.
  - A failed "Launch Director" says why on screen and is reported.
  - Every step report carries the tail of the setup log; `director/place` used to carry nothing.

## Proof
- `bash -n` passes. Run on Windows with `HOME` in a scratch folder and the Gateway at a dead address: it fails at the macOS check, writes `ERROR (step preconditions)` to the log, prints the log path, and exits 1. A separate harness shows the ERR trap turning an unchecked `mv` failure into a report labelled with its step.
- The wizard builds (`dotnet build tools/cc-director-setup-avalonia`).

## What this does NOT prove
- The Avalonia wizard has no test project (`cc-director-setup.Tests` covers the Windows WPF wizard), so these paths have no automated test. They need a run on a Mac.
- Nothing here covers the launcher or the Director before sign-in: that is Part B, in its own pull request.

author: cedricziel
body:
## Summary

Third PR of layer 3 (type authority) of `openspec/changes/otel-native-schema`. It is stacked on #1751.

It adds the semconv tier of the type precedence on top of the existing `SchemaResolver`, without a second semconv store.

- `SchemaResolver::type_hints(tenant)` returns `SemconvTypeHints`, a synchronous snapshot of the registries the tenant can see. It implements `TypeHints` with one map lookup per call and no allocation.
- How a `schema_url` picks a registry:
  - any `https://opentelemetry.io/schemas/*` URL selects the pinned bundled `otel` snapshot (1.43.0), whatever the version in the URL, because cross-version renaming is out of scope;
  - any other URL selects the registry that declares exactly that `schema_url` (tenant custom registries, or the bundled `signaldb` one);
  - an unknown URL gives no hint and never an error.
- How Weaver types map: `string`, `int`, `double` and `boolean` map to the four canonical types. An enum takes its members' type when they all agree. Arrays, `template[...]`, `any`, `map` and unknown types give no hint, since those values go to the residue.
- `OTEL_NAMESPACE` replaces the `"otel"` string literal.

Nothing calls this yet. PR 4 wires it into the cached per-(tenant, dataset) resolution.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p common --test type_hints`: 4 tests pass. They use real keys from the vendored snapshot, check that another OTel version's URL still gets hints, that an unknown URL and array types give none, and that a custom registry is selected by its exact URL without falling back to `otel`.
- `cargo test -p common --lib schema` (138 tests) and `--test schema_registry` pass. `clippy -D warnings` and `fmt` are clean.

The docs check flags `docs/users/schema-registry.md`. Nothing users can see changes until registry types drive storage, so that doc gets its section in a later PR.

author: abysmalbiscuit
body:
## TL;DR (human written)


---

Closes #135

---

## Agent summary

`issue dashboard` lost its worktree triage table once the PR tables below it rendered. At 100x40 the whole `ISSUE WORKTREES` table disappeared, scrollback included.

While `issue prs` fetches, it draws last run's tables as a dimmed live block on stderr. Those rows carry OSC 8 hyperlinks, and console 0.15 (what indicatif measures width with) counts a link target as visible text. indicatif therefore reckoned each linked row as two terminal rows and moved the cursor up too far on every 80ms spinner tick, so the block climbed over whatever was printed above it. The same miscount caused the `MERGE (unrevi` truncation in the stale rows.

The fix is in `LiveLines::set_lines`:
- OSC escapes are stripped before lines reach indicatif. Colour stays, and the final stdout render keeps its links.
- The line template is `{msg}` instead of `{wide_msg}`. `{wide_msg}` truncates by bytes and can cut an escape sequence in half; an overwide line now wraps, and indicatif counts the wrapped rows.

`ui::visible` reuses the new `ui::strip_hyperlinks` instead of its own OSC loop. The `issue status` live table goes through the same code and had the same creep on its PR column.

Tested with a regression test that draws linked lines into an emulated 40-column terminal and asserts the line above survives (red before, green after), and by running `issue dashboard --no-plots` in tmux at 100x40 and 80x15 before and after.

body:
## 1. TILT rebalance — «трохи прибирає, багато дає»
The matched ±12 dB pair from #28 removed as much as it gave. Now the tilt is deliberately **asymmetric**:

| Band | Warm extreme | Bright extreme |
|---|---|---|
| Band that yields | −3.75 dB max | **+15 dB max** |
| Band that opens | **+15 dB max** | −3.75 dB max |

- removal capped at ~3.75 dB, the opposite band opens up to +15 dB — the knob takes away a little and gives a lot;
- **50 % stays exactly neutral by construction** (gains from the raw control, both unity at the pivot);
- record pole still travels 3 → 30 kHz with the same curve.

## 2. Libraries — from "linked" to actually used
Honest audit: CMake fetched and linked both packages, but **nothing referenced them**. Fixed:

- **chowdsp_utils** → `chowdsp::DecibelsApprox::gainToDecibels` now runs the auto-gain level-ratio maths (per-block, hot path) instead of libm's exp2/log2 chain. Conditional include (`__has_include`) keeps the DSP harness — which cuts structs out of the headers verbatim and compiles them without chowdsp — unaffected, with a JUCE fallback that keeps behaviour identical.
- **melatonin_inspector** → the component inspector is **embedded in the editor under `JUCE_DEBUG`**: created at the end of the constructor (walks the finished panel), released first in the destructor before the watched components die. Release builds never compile it.

## CI
New **build-linux-debug** job: full Debug configure+compile (also exercises CPM from a cold cache in a second config) so the inspector code path cannot silently rot, and uploads the Debug VST3 as an artifact for debugging sessions. Release jobs untouched.

## Verification
- `bash tests/dsp/run.sh` — **ALL CHECKS PASSED (0 failures)** after every stage

author: abubakarshahid16
body:
## What
A review no longer runs inside the HTTP request. It runs on the **existing B11 job queue**: the same `jobs` table, the same atomic claim, retries, poison state, audit and `job_max_running`. This PR adds no second queue.

| Requirement | How |
|---|---|
| Request returns a job/run id | `POST /api/reviews/run` creates the run (`queued`) and its `review_run` job under one write lock, then returns the queued run with `job` |
| No duplicate active review | Refused (409) while a review of the same submittal is queued or running; decided inside the lock |
| Progress | Three named steps: reading the datasheet, selecting the applicable standards, comparing. Shown as "step N of 3", never as a percentage |
| Cancellation | A queued job is cancelled at once. A running job gets `cancel_requested` and stops at its next step, deletes the unconfirmed findings it had written, and marks the run `cancelled` |
| Retries | `job_queue.fail`: back off and retry, with the run set back to `queued`; after the last retry the job is poisoned and the run marked `failed` with the reason |
| Crash recovery | A stale running review job is re-queued with its run, both at startup and on each worker pass. The orphaned-run sweep no longer fails a run whose job is still active |
| Permissions | The worker runs the review under the **requester's** grants, rebuilt from the grant tables when it runs (unrestricted only when sign-in is disabled). Starting stays admin-gated; the job API is scoped to readable documents |
| Provenance | `created_by`, `code_version` (comparison, applicability, datasheets) and `config_version` are recorded on the job |
| Audit | `job.queued`, `job.cancel_requested`, `job.cancelled`, `job.done`, `job.poisoned` and `job.recovered` |

**UI:** each queued or running run shows its step. The list polls every 3 s while any review is active and stops by itself. A "Cancel this review" control sits beside the card, since the card is itself a button. A pending cancellation is shown as pending, and the server's refusal is shown as given.

## Tests
- `backend/tests/test_p3_review_jobs.py` (10) covers:
  - the request does no review work;
  - the worker reaches a verdict and records progress;
  - a duplicate request is refused;
  - cancel while queued, and cancel while running (the earlier attempt's finding is removed);
  - retry, then poison, with the reason on the run;
  - the requester's revoked grant stops the review;
  - a crashed run is re-queued rather than failed;
  - provenance and audit;
  - the job API is readers-only.
- `frontend/src/views/ReviewRunsView.jobs.test.tsx` (5).
- The B5 live-route tests now drain the queue exactly as the worker does.
- Mutations M880–M889: 10/10 detected.
- Every existing mutation anchored in the files touched was re-run. M208, M209 and M740 were stale after this change; all three are re-anchored and detected.
- Local backend suite: 3861 passed, with only the 4 local-only OCR failures. Frontend: 736/738, with the 2 local-only failures that are green in CI.
- Privacy scan of the diff: 0 client terms.

## Not changed
The model-assisted datasheet read and recheck routes (`claude_api.py`) still run inline. They are opt-in and gated behind the Claude lane.

author: duketopceo
body:
## Why this exists

[DUK-103](https://github.com/duketopceo/orchestral/pull/48) is closed as superseded by [#39](https://github.com/duketopceo/orchestral/pull/39), which fixed `StatusBar` at the root. That part is done and this PR does not touch it.

What did **not** reach `main` is why the defect cost six days. `17f6c54` removed the `set_message` writer and its `self._message = ""` initialiser but left the reader in `_render_text`. Nothing tested `StatusBar`'s rendered text, so:

- mypy was the first signal, and only after the fact;
- the only runtime signal was 8 pilot tests failing with a raw `AttributeError: 'StatusBar' object has no attribute '_message'`;
- every PR in the repo inherited the redness while the actual cause sat in one untested method.

`main` today still has no `StatusBar` test. `grep StatusBar tests/` returns nothing.

This is the surviving half of DUK-103: the guard, not the fix.

## What it adds

A `TestStatusBar` class in `tests/test_tui.py` — 51 lines, one file, no production code.

| Test | Guards |
|---|---|
| `test_counts_render_without_a_note` | counts and cost render with no note set — the direct regression |
| `test_note_renders_after_counts` | the note reaches the rendered strip |
| `test_active_jobs_are_listed_and_terminal_ones_are_not` | active jobs shown, terminal ones dropped |
| `test_active_jobs_are_capped_at_three_with_a_count` | the 3-job cap and its `+N more` suffix |

## Verified by mutation, not by inspection

Reintroducing the exact `17f6c54` defect — drop the `_note` initialiser, drop `set_note`, and point the read back at `self._message`:

```
clean main          -> Ran 4 tests, OK
defect reintroduced -> Ran 4 tests, FAILED (errors=4)
    AttributeError: 'StatusBar' object has no attribute '_message'
```

All four fail with the original error. That is the proof they would catch this class of bug again.

## Full suite on this branch

Python 3.11.15, `pip install -e .[dev,tui]`, ruff 0.16.9, mypy 2.3.1, textual 8.2.8.

```
ruff check .                            All checks passed!
mypy orchestral harness.py               Success: no issues found in 30 source files
python -m unittest discover -s tests    Ran 374 tests -> OK (skipped=1)
```

374 = `main`'s 370 + these 4.

## Notes

- `StatusBar` owns its state as `_note` and never touches Textual privates. `Static._message` was removed upstream in textual 8.x, which is why a stale read raised instead of returning a value.
- The tests use the same `skipUnless(HAS_TEXTUAL, ...)` guard as the pilot suite, so a venv without the `[tui]` extra skips rather than fails. [DUK-142](/DUK/issues/DUK-142) tracked that measurement gap; CI installs `.[dev,tui]`, so these run there.
- No `# type: ignore`, no skip markers, no `noqa` added.
- #48 is left closed. This is a separate branch off `main`, not a reopen.

author: iskhakovt
body:
## What

Step 4 of `design/prompt-caching.md`: OpenAI-compatible providers map the cache intent through `llm_providers.attrs.cacheDialect`, which replaces the `promptCaching` boolean.

| Dialect | Sent |
|-|-|
| `openrouter` | With a cache intent, `session_id` on every model. A system-message `cache_control` marker for `anthropic/` models (at the intent's TTL, plus the top-level field), and for `google/` and `qwen/` models (no TTL). |
| `openai` | `prompt_cache_key`, with an intent |
| `xai` | the `x-grok-conv-id` header, with an intent |
| `none` | nothing |

Without an intent (one-shot calls, structured output, `countTokens`), only OpenRouter's system marker on `anthropic/`, `google/` and `qwen/` models goes out, as `promptCaching: true` sent it.

One narrowing from `main`: `main` marked every model on an OpenRouter row. Models outside those three families now get no marker. OpenRouter documents explicit markers only for those families, apart from `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2` when it's routed to Alibaba.

## Design change: Gemini

The design planned a marker on the last message for Gemini. Measured through OpenRouter:
- **On the last message:** on Vertex it wrote a fresh cache on every request and read none, about 40% dearer than no marker. AI Studio ignored it.
- **The top-level field:** did nothing on either.
- **A system-prompt marker:** wrote once, and every later request read it, on both.

The adapter sends the system marker, and the design doc records the measurements.

## Configuration and migration

- **New rows:** an OpenAI-compatible row takes, in order:
  1. an explicit dialect (`--cache-dialect`, `COGMO_LLM_CACHE_DIALECT`; rejected for `anthropic`);
  2. its provider type's (`openrouter` at any URL);
  3. its base-URL host's.

  Known hosts are `openrouter.ai`, `api.openai.com` and `api.x.ai`, each with its regional subdomains; anything else gets `none`.
- **Non-interactive setup** now goes through `addProvider`, so the secret and the provider row are written in one transaction.
- **Migration `0057`** (`db:generate --custom`) sets each existing row to what it sent before:
  - an explicit `promptCaching: false` becomes `none`;
  - otherwise the host's dialect;
  - otherwise `openrouter` if the row had `true`, else `none`.

  A test holds the SQL to `cacheDialectForBaseUrl` over regional and look-alike URLs.

## Tests

- Unit tests cover:
  - each dialect and model family;
  - the no-intent guards;
  - the writers and their defaults;
  - the migration against PGlite.

  Each failed before its change.
- Live scenario D measured these cache reads on requests 1–3:

| Route | Cache reads |
|-|-|
| OpenRouter → Claude Sonnet 5 | 0 / 4,701 / 4,723 |
| OpenRouter → Grok 4.3 | 128 / 3,136 / 3,136 |
| OpenRouter → Gemini 2.5 Flash | 3,543 on all three |
| OpenAI `gpt-4.1-nano` | 0 / 2,816 / 2,816 |

- xAI direct is unit-tested only, since there's no key.

## `todo.md`

- **New p2:** OpenAI's GPT-5-family models reject `max_tokens`, which predates this PR.
- **New p3:** show and change a provider's dialect (`provider list`, `provider set --cache-dialect`).
- **Removed:** a stale p3 about an `as any` that no longer exists.

author: rtkelly13
body:
## 📝 Description

Stacked on #520. This adds a `protected-paths` check that fails a PR from a fork if it changes any path listed in `.github/protected-paths.txt`, which #519 adds: `.github/`, `.config/`, `scripts/`, `tools/`, the `Directory.Build.*` and `Directory.Packages.props` files, `global.json`, the NuGet config and the solution file.

**How a fork is prevented from bypassing it:**
- It runs on `pull_request_target`, so it always uses the base branch's copy of both the workflow and the list. A fork can't edit its way past the check.
- `pull_request_target` is safe here because nothing from the PR is checked out or run. The list comes from a sparse checkout of the base branch, and the changed files come from the API. The workflow header warns never to add a checkout of the PR head.
- A rename counts on both sides, so moving a protected file out also fails.
- PRs from branches of this repo pass straight away, since they're already reviewed and gated.

**Making it required:** the ruleset is managed by `REPO_REQUIRED_CHECKS_MAP` in shared-utilities, so `protected-paths` goes into that map in a separate PR there, then gets applied to the live ruleset. It can only become required once this workflow is on main: `pull_request_target` only ever runs the default branch's copy, so it won't report on this PR itself.

**Known gap:** entries are exact paths or folder prefixes. A nested `test/Directory.Build.props` isn't covered. Glob entries can be added if you want that covered.

## 🧪 Verification Checklist
- [x] `actionlint` is clean.
- [x] Matching tested locally against sample paths: prefixes, exact files, look-alikes like `docs/global.json` and `toolsX/`.
- [ ] After merging, it reports on an open PR; then it's added to the ruleset.

author: dyoshyy
body:
## 背景

補助の割り振り（#185・`docs/specs/2026-09-26-accessory-allocation-design.md`）の計測で、`five_way`（5分割）は週2回だと各日が4週目標を100%のスロット効率でも満たせないことが分かった（胸0.88 背中0.52 肩1.04 腕0.63 脚0.37）。週4回からは帯域内に収まる。

選べる設定を残したまま本人に「これで足りているか」を判断させるのは、CLAUDE.md の「答えるべき問いと、答えるべきでない問いを分ける」に反する。選べる選択肢から外すことにした。

## 決めたこと（ユーザー指定）

1. `five_way` を頻度が週4回未満のときに選ぼうとすると拒否する（サーバー側の検証）。画面はそもそも選べないボタンとして出す。
2. `five_way` が設定済みの状態で頻度を週4回未満へ下げようとすると拒否する（自動でプリセットを外すフォールバックはしない）。既存の400経路（`respondError`）で理由付きのメッセージを返す。

## 設計 — 下限はどこに置いたか

`Program.cycle` は展開済みの `[]Split` しか持たず、選んだプリセットの「キー」は保存されない（`SplitPreset` のコメント通り）。`PUT /api/program/split` もクライアントからキーではなく展開済みの周期を送ってくるため、**サーバーはプリセットキーを知らない**。

そこで:

- `seed.SplitPreset` に `MinFrequencyPerWeek int` を追加（0 は下限なし）。いま値を持つのは `five_way`（4）だけで、他は0。1つのプリセットにしか要らないので、頻度や区分数から導く一般式は作らず、プリセットごとの値のまま持たせた（必要になるまで作らない）。
- `seed.MatchPreset(cycle []program.Split) (SplitPreset, bool, error)` を新設。周期の中身（名前と区分）でプリセットを引き当てる。基準は `web/src/features/settings/split.ts` の `matchingPresetKey`（既存・フロント側で同じ問題を同じ方法で解いている）と揃えた。
- `internal/application/usecase/set_split_cycle.go`（`SetSplitCycle`）: 選ぼうとした周期が下限付きプリセットと一致し、いまの頻度がそれ未満なら拒否。
- `internal/application/usecase/set_frequency.go`（`SetFrequency`）: いまの分割が下限付きプリセットと一致し、変更後の頻度がそれ未満なら拒否。

ドメイン集約 `Program` 自体には手を入れていない。頻度と分割の組み合わせ自体は依然として自由に構築できる（後述の既存データ互換のため）。検証は「新しく選ぶ／変える」操作を受け付けるユースケース層だけに置いた。

エラーは既存の `apperror.ErrInvalidInput` → 400 の経路にそのまま乗る（`respondError`）。`GET /api/split-presets` の応答に `min_frequency_per_week` を足して、画面が押す前に選べない理由を出せるようにした。

## 既存データへの影響

- 集約 `Program` に検証を足していないので、`five_way` + 週3回のように今日すでにあり得る保存済みプログラムは、読み出し（`GET /api/program`）も計画（`GET /api/sessions`）もこれまで通り動く。
- 弾かれるのは新しく `SetSplitCycle` / `SetFrequency` を呼んだときだけ。既存の組み合わせを直す方法は「分割を先に変える」か「頻度を週4回以上へ上げる」の2つ。
- 開発用シミュレーション（`internal/application/devsim`）は `program.NewProgram` / `WithCycle` で集約を直接組んでおり、この2つのユースケースを経由しない。5分割を週2回で測るという計測用途としては、下限の影響を受けないのが正しい挙動。

## 画面側

- `min_frequency_per_week` を `SplitPreset` 型に追加。
- `split.ts` に `isSplitSelectable` / `splitUnselectableReason` を追加（純粋関数、`split.test.ts` で検査）。`"five_way"` というキーを画面側に書かないので、下限を持つプリセットが増えても直さずに済む。
- `ProgramSettings.tsx` は選べないプリセットのボタンを `disabled` にし、理由を `title` と直下の `Note` に出す（判断はフックと `split.ts` 側、`.tsx` は描画のみ）。
- `useProgramSettings.ts` の `put()` は、失敗した PUT の応答本文（`{error}`）を読んで画面にそのまま出す（`describePutFailure`。`web/src/dev/simulate.ts` の `describeFailure` と同じ考え方）。これは `put()` を経由する全フィールドに効く変更で、以前は「変えられませんでした（400）」だけだった `declared` / `selected` / `focus` / `volume` の失敗も、サーバーが書いた理由をそのまま出すようになる。共有関数を最小修正した結果としての副次効果であり、フィールドごとに特別扱いはしていない。

## テストと変異

- `internal/domain/training/seed/split_presets_test.go`: `MinFrequencyPerWeek` を持つのが `five_way` だけであること、`MatchPreset` が名前・区分の両方で一致を見ること（名前だけ違う周期は一致しない）を検査。
- `internal/application/usecase/set_split_cycle_test.go`: 週3回で `five_way` を選ぼうとすると拒否・週4回なら通る・`upper_lower` には下限が無いので週2回でも通る。
- `internal/application/usecase/set_frequency_test.go`（新規）: `five_way` のまま週3回へ下げると拒否・週4回はそのまま通る・`PPL`/分割なしには下限が無い。

author: mchwang
kingsleydon
body:
## What

`PUT /v1/admin/products/{slug} {public_key, webhook_url, reason}` replaces an issued product's request-verification key and webhook URL. Until now `POST /v1/admin/products` refused any change with `409`, so a leaked product key could not be replaced.

## Design

- **The key id does not change.** It lives in the attested route (`destination.product_kid`). Every loaded route of a product must name the same key id (`product_destination`, checked at startup), and older route versions stay loaded for historical deposits. So a new key id cannot be introduced with a new route version.
- **The cut is immediate, with no overlap window.** Authentication reads the product's one stored key on every request, under the route's key id. The old key stops verifying as soon as the `PUT` commits. An overlap window would need several keys per product, which the architecture does not have (one key id per product, and the database stores one public key).
- **Audited, with semantics that match `POST`.** The audit row `product.update` records the reason and the replaced key and webhook URL, in the same transaction. A repeat with the stored values changes nothing and writes no audit row. An unknown slug returns `404`. An unrouted slug, invalid key, invalid webhook URL, or empty reason returns `400`. Only the admin key is accepted.

## Also in this PR

- Architecture §12 (admin actions, endpoint list) and §15 (Rotation: product key).
- `openapi.json`, the regenerated Python client (`update_product`, `UpdateProductRequest`), and both changelogs.
- `deploy/README.md` (Product credentials) and integration guide §3.4 "Rotate the product key". Existing section numbers are unchanged, since the Phala Cloud checklist refers to them.
- New runbook `deploy/runbooks/product-key-compromise.md`, linked from the runbook index.

The reference-slug and staging-route work was dropped from this PR, because the settlement design is changing.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check`; clippy `-D warnings` with all features and with default features; `cargo deny`.
- `cargo test --workspace` on a throwaway PostgreSQL 18 with `CI=true`: 345 tests passed with all features, 331 with default features. The new test `admin_product_key_replacement` covers admin-only access, `400`/`404`, the hard cut from the old key to the new one, and a single audit row.
- `cargo sqlx prepare --check`, `make sdk-check`, `make runbook-check`, `make product-conformance` (15 passed, 0 warnings), `deploy/validate-compose.sh`, `deploy/tests/*`, and `make cvm-rehearsal` (all checks passed, no leftovers).
