body:
Closes #128

CI only ran the Go job, so EmberKit decode breakage (incl. the Go golden
files the Swift tests decode, added in #125) and app compile errors were
only caught locally.

## What changed
- New `changes` job (`dorny/paths-filter`) computes whether `macos/**`,
  `cmd/ember/testdata/**`, or the workflow file itself changed.
- New `macos` job, gated on that filter, `runs-on: macos-latest` (currently
  macOS 26/Xcode 26 — matches `project.yml`'s `deploymentTarget.macOS: "26.0"`
  and `Package.swift`'s `swift-tools-version: 6.0`):
  - `brew install xcodegen`
  - `swift test --package-path macos`
  - `xcodegen generate --spec macos/project.yml --project macos`
  - unsigned `xcodebuild -project macos/Ember.xcodeproj -scheme Ember
    -configuration Debug CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build`
  - SPM build cache keyed on `Package.swift`'s hash (EmberKit has no external
    SPM dependencies, so this mostly saves recompiling stdlib-ish output on
    reruns of the same branch).
- `scripts/build-producers.sh`'s "Bundle & sign producer helpers" phase now
  skips itself under `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` instead of running `go build` +
  `codesign` (there's no Developer ID on the runner, and `go` isn't
  guaranteed to be there either). Local dev/release builds are unaffected —
  that env var is unset outside GitHub Actions.
- Documented the new job in `docs/RUNBOOK.md`.

## Test evidence
- `swift test --package-path macos` — 239 tests pass locally.
- `xcodegen generate --spec macos/project.yml --project macos` +
  `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true xcodebuild -project macos/Ember.xcodeproj -scheme Ember
  -configuration Debug CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build` — **BUILD SUCCEEDED**,
  with the sign phase printing its skip message instead of failing codesign.
- `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.0 go fmt ./...` clean, `go vet ./...`,
  `go test ./... -race` all green.
- `yamllint -d relaxed .github/workflows/ci.yml` — only a pre-existing
  line-length warning on line 5, unrelated to this change.

author: sntran
body:
## Summary

SQLite 3.53.4 (with the esqlite NIF) is now part of the default `beam.com`. It was a probe behind `SQLITE=1`, built in CI as a separate `beam-sqlite.com`. `SQLITE=0` leaves it out.

```
$ beam.com version
  ...
  Applications: asn1-5.5.2 beam_com-0.1.0 beam_com_script-0.1.0 compiler-10.0.6 crypto-5.10 esqlite-0.8.9 inets-9.8 kernel-11.0.4 public_key-1.21.7 sasl-4.4 ssl-11.7.7 stdlib-8.1 wasm-0.1.0
$ beam.com build examples/sqlite_check.erl
$ ./sqlite_check.com
sqlite: version 3.53.4
sqlite: rows [[1,<<"alpha">>],[2,<<"beta">>],[3,<<"gamma">>]]
sqlite: json ["alpha","beta","gamma"]
sqlite: 3 rows in :memory:
```

## Why esqlite, and not SQLite alone

The question was: do we need the esqlite NIF, or can we compile SQLite directly with cosmocc?

- SQLite **is** compiled directly with `cosmocc`: `build.sh` uses the amalgamation of sqlite.org (3.53.4), not the older copy in esqlite.
- Erlang code cannot call C functions directly. Something must convert Erlang terms to SQLite values and back, and hold the database and statement handles as resources that the garbage collector can free. That is a NIF. esqlite does this in one C file (about 1300 lines, Apache-2.0).
- An own NIF (as we did for `wasm`) is possible later, if esqlite does not fit. This is in `docs/ROADMAP.md`.

## Cost

SQLite and the NIF add about **1.8 MB** (two CPUs, compiled with `-Os`) to `beam.com` and to each program that `beam.com build` makes, also when the program does not use SQLite: the NIF is in the emulator, and all programs share the emulator. In this run, `hashsum.com` (a one-file program with `crypto`) is 30.1 MB.

## Changes

- `build.sh`: `SQLITE` is 1 by default.
- CI: the "Build with SQLite" job and `beam-sqlite.com` are removed (one build job less).
- Tests (`tests/run.sh`, `tests/run.ps1`): the SQLite program (an in-memory database and a database file) is built with `beam.com` and runs on every platform. It always runs: a check that is skipped when a tool (`unzip`) is missing on a BSD machine would hide a problem. `beam.com version` must list `esqlite-` and `wasm-`.
- README and `docs/ROADMAP.md`: SQLite is a normal feature now, with the cost and the reason for esqlite.

## Local test

sqlite.org is not reachable from the development container (HTTP 403), so the local build used the SQLite 3.50.4 files of an older build (`SQLITE_VERSION=3.50.4`). CI downloads and tests 3.53.4.

## Test plan

- [x] CI green on all 11 jobs (Linux x86_64 and aarch64, macOS arm64 and x86_64, Windows, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD 7.3).
- [x] `build.sh test` in CI: SQLite 3.53.4 from a program built with `beam.com`.
- [x] Locally on Linux x86_64: 63 behavior checks pass.

author: peiyuanqi
body:
## Why

The owner can ask SCV from WeChat or Feishu to change, publish, and deploy SCV itself; a delegated agent (claude/codex) then runs the feature flow. Publishing to crates.io cannot be undone, so the owner now says yes or no in chat before it happens.

## What

- **CLI** `scv confirm [--timeout SECS] QUESTION` asks the owner and waits. Exit **0** yes; **1** no, or no answer before the timeout; **2** could not ask or the answer was not learned (no daemon, a daemon too old for the command (`invalid_json`), no reachable owner chat, a question already waiting there, the daemon restarted/stopped while waiting). Default timeout 1800 s, capped at 14400 s (4 h), the default `tools.max_timeout_seconds` ceiling, the longest a delegated agent's own call can wait. Allowed through `refuse_nested_daemon_control` like `restart --when-idle`.
- **Protocol** (stays v3, additive): `daemon.control` actions `confirm_ask {question, parent?, timeout_seconds?}` and `confirm_status {id}`; optional `daemon.status.confirm {id, state, chat, deadline_unix_seconds}` with `ConfirmState` = `pending|yes|no|expired|withdrawn|failed` (unknown values parse as `unknown`); new error code `confirm_error`.
- **Where it goes**: the chat that started the work, resolved from the caller's `SCV_PARENT` chain exactly as `restart --when-idle` does. The chain parsing is now one helper, `DelegationRegistry::own_run` (scv-tools), used by both. Work that did not start in a chat falls back to `Notifier::owner_chat` (first connected `[notify].owner` account, else the owner's last chat). It must be an account owner's direct chat, or nothing is asked.
- **Chat side**: the question waits in the channel hub next to the notices (`Hub::ask/open/withdraw`, `Registration::asking/take_question`). `intake::classify` returns a new `Verdict::Answer` for the owner's explicit yes/no in that direct chat. The bridge stores the acknowledgement as the message's reply, hands the answer over, and starts no turn. Any other message runs as a normal turn and the question keeps waiting. Other senders, group messages (the owner's included), and messages with files never answer.
- **publish.sh**: when `SCV_PARENT` is set, it asks through `host.sh scv confirm` before its first `cargo publish`, naming the version, the crates, and the origin/main commit, and stops unless the answer is yes. `--check` and terminal runs never ask. SKILL.md stages 0 and 6 are updated.
- Pending questions are in memory only. CONFIG_LAYOUT stays 1, and no on-disk formats change.

### Exact chat texts

- Question: `<question>\n\nReply yes or no. No answer in <N> minutes counts as no.` (`1 minute` when N is 1)
- Answers: yes = `yes y ok okay 是 是的 好 好的 确认 可以 同意`; no = `no n 否 不 不要 取消 算了 stop` (after trim, lowercase, and stripping trailing `. ! 。 ！`)
- Acknowledgements: `OK, going ahead.` / `OK, stopped.`
- Timeout: `No answer, so stopped.`
- Withdrawn (see deviations): `The question was withdrawn, so stopped.`

## Deviations from the brief, and why

1. **Ask-then-poll** (not a per-command timeout): `confirm_ask` returns an ID at once and the CLI follows it with `confirm_status` every 2 s. One control request is capped at 20 s, and polling also lets the CLI notice a restarted daemon (unknown ID, or no socket), which then exits 2. I chose 2 s rather than 1 s because each status reply scans the process table for delegations.
2. **Lease / withdrawal (added)**: a question nobody follows for 60 s is withdrawn, and the chat is told `The question was withdrawn, so stopped.` An agent's shell tool can kill `scv confirm` (Claude Code caps foreground commands at 10 minutes). Without the lease, a later yes would be acknowledged "OK, going ahead." while nothing proceeds, and a retry would be refused because a question is already pending.
3. **Answers count only once the question is queued in the outbox** (`Hub::open`), so a "yes" typed before the question was queued cannot answer it.
4. **Messages with files are not answers** (for example an image captioned "ok").
5. **`SCV_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT`** (default 1800) lets publish.sh shorten the wait for agents whose tools cap command time.
6. **Extra test**: `tests/it/feature_flow.rs` runs the real `publish.sh` against a local git remote with fake `curl`/`scv`/`cargo`. It checks that the question is asked first, that publishing happens only on yes, and that `--check` and terminal runs never ask.

## Tests (no network, no live chat)

- `intake` answer normalization, owner-only answering (other senders, groups, and files never answer; owner-only accounts drop strangers), an answer needing no room and never being taken twice; `hub` one question per chat, open/take/withdraw, lost answers.
- Bridge-level (fake transport + fake daemon): the question is delivered unprompted to the owner's chat; other words, another sender's yes, and the owner's group yes run turns; the owner's `Yes!` / `不` are acknowledged without a turn and resolve the question.
- Server: `confirm_ask`/`confirm_status` through `daemon_control`, the starting chat winning over the notify target, the notify fallback, the timeout telling the chat, withdrawal of an unfollowed question, refusals (no chat, non-owner chat, repeat question, empty or oversized question, unknown ID), and shutdown withdrawing the question.
- `tests/it/confirm.rs`: exit codes against a scripted daemon (yes 0, no 1, expired 1, failed/withdrawn/unknown ID 2, daemon gone 2), no daemon 2, a too-old daemon 2, `--timeout` bounds, and an **isolated real daemon with no reachable chat → 2** (at delegation depth 1, not refused).

Gates run locally: `cargo fmt --check`, workspace clippy plus the three scv-channels feature variants, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo build --release --locked`, `git diff --check`, and `bash -n publish.sh`. cargo-deny is not installed locally (CI runs it), and this PR adds no dependencies.

body:
The setup-backbone battery constructs systemd units and a stub systemctl, but inherited the test host's kernel. On macOS this selected launchd paths and failed 26 tests before they could exercise the intended Linux contracts. Make the existing model explicitly Linux on every host, preserve all prior safety assertions, and add private Darwin backend-routing and Linux-installer-refusal controls.

Refs #1810. Fixture-only prerequisite for #1859; #1810 stays open for its CI/native acceptance and other blockers. Only `tests/test_setup_backbone.py` changes. No production script, shared fixture, workflow or service behavior changes. Native launchd acceptance stays with the phase03 lane.

Verification at `c08768dde8197ba355bd0218f6f4049d8a44fe92` (parent `28bbab1`):

- Parent native Darwin: 26 failures / 12 valid controls. Same unchanged parent with explicit modeled Linux: 38 passed.
- Candidate: all 40 scoped tests pass, including the two Darwin controls. Exact candidate archive independently of the working directory also passes all 40.
- Meaningful private mutations fail the Darwin routing test (1 fail / 1 control), Darwin installer-refusal test (1 fail / 1 control), and existing legacy keepalive active-before-retirement guard (1 fail / 5 controls).
- Constructed environments and private HOME/root/tmp/socket/channel state; closed utility PATH with rejecting service/outbound stubs. Native Bash 3.2 and BSD utilities run. The parent attempted two launchctl reads, both caught by the private stub. No real manager, model, credential or production operation.
- Independent review of this exact commit found no blocking findings and reproduced the 40 candidate passes, both unchanged-parent controls, and all three targeted mutation failures. All 925 tracked archive files remained byte-identical; all 114 original assertions were preserved (133 total after the added controls). No full-suite or hosted native-lane success claim.

Risk is test modeling: these fixtures do not prove native systemd/launchd registration. Keep hosted default checks and the integrated phase03 minimum-Python/macOS lane required before declaring the prerequisite complete. The file is read at pytest collection; no generation, fleet restart or production activation is involved. Explicit approval is required before merge. Backout is a test-only revert with the restored macOS coverage gap disclosed.

author: hide-1925
body:
#19 のあとの2版分です。

## v1.49.25 / 拡張 1.4.36 — Web Speech（日本語）の句読点と、判断層の空回り

### 句読点が付かなかった件
Chrome の Web Speech は、日本語に句読点を付けません。代わりに、息継ぎの位置に半角スペースを入れて返します。これまでは、その空白をそのまま流していました。そのため文末が一つも無く、区切りは 120字の長さ打切り（`semantic-length-fallback`）まで入りませんでした。実測ではカードが1枚 110〜120字になり、「。」は最後の一文にしか付いていませんでした。

- 空白を、直前の語尾だけを見て置き換えます（`jaSpacePunct` / `webSpeechPunct`）。
  - です・ます・ですよね など → 「。」
  - ですか・ませんか など → 「？」
  - それ以外 → 「、」
- 「〜みる」「〜違う」のような言い切りは、語尾だけでは文末と決められないので「、」にとどめます。「まだ」「何か」「静かな」も文末扱いにしません。
- 英数字に接する空白は単語の区切りなので、文末でなければ残します。
- 途中結果にもかけます。Web Speech の呼び出し5か所（逐次・マイク・共有音声Track）すべてに入れました。後ろの文字は見ないので、確定済みの前半が後から書き換わることはありません。
- 外部API（gpt-4o 系・gpt-live）は句読点付きで返すので、その経路には手を入れていません。

### 判断層（Jev）が一度も効いていなかった件（INV-12）
同じログで、Jev（active）は約130秒に525回呼ばれ、採用は0件でした。答えは質問した revision にしか使えません。一方で Web Speech の途中結果は、約0.1秒ごとに版が進みます（ログでは427まで）。そのため、話している最中の質問は、答えが返る前に必ず版が変わって捨てられていました。

- 対策として、テキストが `turnDecisionSettleMs`（既定200ms、0 で従来どおり、上限1000）止まってから聞くようにしました。
- STT final は待たないので、録音分割RESTは遅れません。
- 設定は ⚙→判断層「話が止まってから聞くまで ms」です。

## v1.49.24 / 拡張 1.4.35 — キーボード入力が読み上げられなかった件
- 読み上げ対象が B2A のところへ入力文が自分(A)扱いで入り、無言で外れていました。外れた理由を `tts-target-B2A`／`A2B`・`empty`・`tts-off`・`conference-original-only`・`self-recognition-guard` に分けて記録します。入力文が外れたときは、1回目から画面に案内を出します。
- 入力文には判断層をかけないようにしました。以前は1件ごとに3往復し、2秒止めてから確定していました。

## 確認
- `node extension/tests/run-all.cjs --with-e2e`：540件、全通過。
  - `test-webspeech-punct`：新設15件
  - `test-tts-skip`：新設11件
  - `test-turn-providers`：80→84件
  - `test-turn-decision`：84→86件
- headless Chromium での確認：報告の発話に一文足した79字を、途中結果として1文字ずつ流しました。
  - 旧版：最後まで確定せず、1部分79字のまま。
  - 新版：1文目が話し終わる前に `semantic-sentence` で確定。
- 未確認：

author: bajor
body:
## Problem

After #34, the GCP site's low-resolution lettering that the tracer can still represent rendered **bolder and blockier** than the PDF. Example: *INFORMATION_SCHEMA / JOBS / RESERVATIONS …* in the 45 ppi `Im31`, where the trace carried 1.21× the reference ink. There are two causes:

- **Bold:** the pixel tracer puts edges at alpha 95.5, about 37% coverage, instead of the 50% edge of opaque ink. On a 1–3 px stroke that dilation is large.
- **Blocky:** marching squares on the coarse source grid gives straight segments between pixel-edge crossings.

## Change

The traceable-component partition now has three outcomes:

| Component | Representation |
| --- | --- |
| >25% of ink below alpha 88 | raster residual (unchanged from #34) |
| thin (`2·covered < 3·boundary`, ≈ ≤3 px wide) **and** single-colour | **new smooth trace** |
| everything else (thick or multicolour) | pixel trace, byte-identical |

The smooth trace, in `Factory.Vectorize.traceSmoothImage`:

1. Keys bicubic field of the component's own alpha, supersampled 4× per axis. Only 16 px tiles near the stroke are evaluated, so long connector lines cost in proportion to their footprint.
2. Per-component contour level from a histogram, chosen so enclosed area = ink area. Weight is correct by construction, and dim diagonals aren't cut by a global level.
3. Existing edge walker and simplification tolerance, then closed cubic `C` curves. Tangents follow the neighbours, but **each handle is capped at ⅓ of its own segment**, and turns sharper than 120° stay corners.

The handle cap fixes a regression I hit with uniform Catmull-Rom. A handle sized by a long neighbouring segment looped around small features, turning the solid dots at connector ends into hollow hooks under even-odd fill. A unit test now covers it.

The scene schema, runtime, workflow and thresholds are unchanged. Path data now contains `C` segments, which the runtime passes straight to `d`.

## Not changed, deliberately

I tried to also make the **raster residual** (sub-pixel handwriting) crisp, and it isn't viable:

- At its ink-area level the handwriting fragments again.
- At a level that keeps it connected, it becomes wide, faint, illegible strokes.

The soft raster stays; it's the faithful rendering of 45 ppi samples. Real crispness there needs a higher-resolution Freeform export. Evidence is in Issue 0016.

## Verification

- `make test`: 102 tests pass. 7 new tests cover smooth/multicolour classification, the closed cubic shape, sampled-curve area within 20% of ink, the handle bound, corner ends and determinism. Partition fixtures moved from 2×2 blocks (now correctly "thin") to a thick block.
- Factory `make evaluate`: zero error at 18 and 72 DPI.
- **GCP** `make evaluate` passes, and every metric improves on the deployed version:

  | Scale | Mean error | Within tolerance | Ink ratio |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 18 DPI | 0.002232 (was 0.002250) | 0.99212 (was 0.99208) | **1.0069** (was 1.0176) |
  | 72 DPI | 0.001406 (was 0.001417) | 0.99495 (was 0.99494) | **1.0347** (was 1.0458) |

  `validate-dist` passes, and I inspected the zoom-detail crops. The JOBS crop is now smooth and legible.
- **Algos** `make evaluate` passes and improves. Its 72 DPI ink ratio goes from 1.1403 to 1.1351, widening the thin margin against the 1.15 max.
- **Cost:** the GCP scene grows 1.6% and the build takes about 15 s longer. 874 components switch to smooth tracing: about 89% of traceable components below 100 ppi, and under 1% at ≥180 ppi.
- Spot checks at 105–155 ppi show equal or smoother strokes and no new artifacts.

## Docs

- Added ADR 0013, BDR 0020 (supersedes BDR 0019) and Issue 0016.
- Updated the indexes, architecture data flow and module table, support profile, glossary and CHANGELOG.
- `visual-explanations/0020-smooth-thin-strokes.svg` is PR-only and gets deleted after merge.

author: sjf-oa
body:
## Why

Transient HTTP 5xx responses currently fail Agents API message, steering, tool-result, and cancellation submissions immediately. Retrying the existing submission can recover without restarting the turn or rerunning a tool.

## What Problem This Solves

Message, steering, tool-result, and cancellation inputs can be lost to a transient server error even when replaying the same submission is safe. The SDK retry mechanism is disabled here because its backoff does not honor the operation abort signal.

## Changes

Use the shared `retryAsync` owner at the SDK event-submission boundary for at most three attempts with bounded backoff. Each logical submission retains its payload and idempotency key; a subsequent submission gets a new key. HTTP 4xx responses and `x-should-retry: false` preserve the existing no-retry behavior. Abort-aware backoff and current-session ownership checks prevent invalid resends.

This does not repair a session whose backend startup remains unresolved. Follow-up commit `064b9d3b3936bcf077e8355190fe7028152da09b` formats the two changed TypeScript files. Final commit `b41c849a1577616866d063fd5a56cefd09ff40ed` replaces a test lookup with equivalent `findLast` to satisfy lint; production code is unchanged from the transport-proven revision.

## Evidence

- Final-head retry suite: `pnpm test extensions/agentsapi/agentsapi-client.retry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, **11 passed**, **2.29 seconds wall**, Vitest 1.01 seconds.
- Published head `064b9d3b3936bcf077e8355190fe7028152da09b`: retry, existing client, and file-client suites together, **37 passed**, **3.04 seconds wall**, Vitest 1.17 seconds.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent full-diff review: no actionable P0-P2 findings. The formatting-only follow-up was inspected separately.
- Targeted type-aware lint could not run in the native nested PR checkout: declaration preparation rejected dependency lookup in its parent checkout. No dependency isolation guard was bypassed. Final-head syntax lint and isolated GitHub extension lint, production types, and test types passed.
- [Final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36232700985): all checks passed. The 11 retry tests total **0.034 seconds** of reported test execution; the enclosing 8-file, 82-test shard passed in **42.17 seconds wall** (Vitest 40.71 seconds).
- [ClawSweeper final review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158775#issuecomment-5844855506): no actionable findings and no remaining pre-merge requests on `b41c849a1577616866d063fd5a56cefd09ff40ed`.

### Production-client fault injection

**PASS on the published head.** A one-shot, secretless harness used the unchanged `AgentsApiClient`, OpenAI SDK 7.17.0, production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` managed-proxy path, and real loopback CONNECT/HTTPS sockets. It did not mock the SDK, guarded fetch, retries, or clock.

The HTTPS fixture admitted an event, then returned 503. The retry returned 202 using the exact same HTTP idempotency header and serialized body, and retained one logical fixture admission. A subsequent submission used a distinct key and produced a second admission. This passed for messages, tool results, and cancellation; cancellation retained its idle-session settlement GETs. Aborting after observing the production backoff timer produced `AbortError: aborted` with exactly one POST and no resend.

| Operation | First submission statuses | Replayed key and body | Fixture admissions for first submission | Next submission |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Message | 503, 202 | Identical | 1 | New key, admission 2 |
| Tool result | 503, 202 | Identical | 1 | New key, admission 2 |
| Cancel | 503, 202, then idle GET | Identical | 1 | New key, admission 2, then idle GET |
| Abort during backoff | 503, then abort | No resend | 1 | Not submitted |

The installed SDK contract documents the idempotency header for submitted messages and maps it into the HTTP header. **Scope:** the fixture owns admission/deduplication, so this proves production client wire behavior against that contract, not the live Agents API server's deduplication implementation. Direct DNS pinning and a live Gateway were not exercised. No live credentials or Gateway state were used.

body:
## What

Implement user enumeration for staked/locked positions and add validation to
prevent min_lock_period violations, while clarifying transfer_admin event format.

## Issues Resolved
Closes #300
Closes #301
Closes #302
Closes #303

## Changes

### #300 - set_min_lock_period doesn't validate against unlock_ledger
Added validation to set_min_lock_period that prevents increasing the minimum
lock period if existing locked positions would be violated by the change.

### #301 - transfer_admin doesn't emit event with old_admin address
Updated transfer_admin event documentation to explicitly clarify that the event
emits (old_admin, new_admin) tuple, making the format unambiguous for indexers.

### #302 - No way to view all staked users or their positions
Added get_staked_users() and get_locked_users() functions that provide paginated
enumeration of all users with active stakes or locked positions.

### #303 - No way to view total staked amount across all users
Added StakedUsers and LockedUsers tracking DataKeys to support enumeration of
users, improving off-chain indexing capability and enabling TVL queries.

author: jsboige
body:
## Grain 4 (pool v17, [#458 c.5843387663](https://github.com/ArgumentumGames/Argumentum/issues/458#issuecomment-5843387663)) — `overflowCss` imprimé dans les deux tables

### Le constat

Depuis #1567, chaque constat capture `overflowCss` (`cs.overflow`) dans son payload JSON — mais `FormatMarkdown` ne l'imprimait nulle part. Un lecteur du rapport ne pouvait pas distinguer :

- un texte **coupé** (`hidden` → texte perdu, clippé par sa boîte) ;
- un texte **peint hors boîte** (`visible` → chevauchement, rien n'est perdu mais ça déborde).

C'est la reco (a) de po-2023 sur le rapport du 25/09.

### La correction (option « print » du grain)

Colonne **`Overflow`** ajoutée aux deux tables :

| Table | Contenu |
|---|---|
| Synthèse (`## Cards with overflow`) | ensemble **distinct** des valeurs de la carte, à côté des sélecteurs — ex. `hidden` ou `hidden, visible` |
| Détaillée (`### par carte`) | valeur propre à chaque constat, juste après `Kind` |

`hidden` se lit « le constat est une perte de texte » ; `visible` se lit « peint hors boîte » — la classification coupé/peint-hors-boîte devient lisible ligne à ligne sans logique d'interprétation embarquée (les combinaisons kind×overflow que le détecteur ne peut pas trancher restent à l'œil du lecteur).

### Organe

`FormatMarkdown_OverflowCss_AppearsInBothTables` : une carte portant un constat `self`/`hidden` et un `container`/`visible` doit rendre `| \`.texte\` | self | hidden |` et `| \`.title\` | container | visible |` dans le tableau détaillé, et la ligne de synthèse doit porter les deux valeurs distinctes.

- 6/6 vert sur `OverflowDetectorReportTests` (les 5 tests existants, à base de `Contain`, sont inchangés) ;
- seul autre consommateur de `FormatMarkdown` : `HarvestManager.WriteMarkdownReport` (écriture fichier, aucun golden snapshot) ;
- `overflowCss` vide (constats construits à la main en tests unitaires) rend une cellule vide, sans `Distinct` parasite en synthèse (filtrage `IsNullOrEmpty`).

author: kalekoi
dhh1128
body:
Fixes tick ~7onn: Codex found three ways around the Registrar's cap on concurrent callback resolutions (on #19 at 129f2fd). Each is pinned by a new test that fails on `main`.

1. **The slot was released before its thread started.** `_admit` released its reservation when `_within` tracked the worker, but the worker started only afterwards. A concurrent admission could therefore prune the unstarted thread as dead and resolve past `MAX_ADMISSIONS`. The test injects exactly that race and saw two resolutions against a cap of one. Slots are now a counter. A slot is taken at reservation and given back by the resolving thread when it finishes, or by the request itself if the thread never started.
2. **Replays were resolved before they were refused.** Admission ran before the replay check, so re-sending an accepted signed subscription made the Registrar resolve an attacker-chosen host again each time. A request already acted on, or identical to one still in admission, is now refused (409 replay) before anything is resolved. The replay record still commits with the subscription, so a request refused for any other reason can still be retried unchanged, and a test pins that.
3. **A resolution that never returned held its slot until restart.** `getaddrinfo` cannot be interrupted from Python, so sixteen stalled resolutions closed admission for good. The default resolver now runs `getaddrinfo` in a child interpreter (`sys.executable -I -S`) that is killed at `RESOLVE_TIMEOUT` (5 s). It is still the system resolver, so `/etc/hosts` and nsswitch behave as before. Delivery shares the resolver, so its abandoned threads are bounded the same way.

The decision is recorded first, in its own commit, as a child of @qgacju62 in `this.i`. `docs/registrar.md` describes the new behaviour, and the door census gains an exemption for the resolver child's stdout. That output is a JSON list of address strings or it is refused, and every address is still checked by `CallbackPolicy`.

**Cost.** Each resolution starts an interpreter, about 35 ms measured here. That happens once per subscription and once per subscriber per window. I also checked that the child runs inside the built image, where `sys.executable` is `/opt/venv/bin/python`.

The unit suite passes at 100% branch coverage, and the new tests passed three repeated runs.

## Contexte
La branche contenait du code non fonctionnel qui empêchait l'API de démarrer
et exposait le hash des mots de passe. Le Frontend ne vérifiait pas réellement
la session et dépendait de `localStorage` pour l'authentification.

## Modifications

### Backend
- **app.js** : branche `notFound` + `errorHandler`, le handler inline masquait toutes les 404.
- **config/db.js / server.js** : passage à `module.exports = { connectDatabase, pool }` — le
  destructuring dans `server.js` ne resolvait pas la fonction, le serveur ne démarrait pas.
- **config/db.js** : suppression de l'`ALTER TABLE clients` redondant.
- **models/user.model.js** : introduction de `PUBLIC_FIELDS`, plus de `SELECT *` / `RETURNING *`
  qui renvoyait le hash `password` dans chaque réponse.
- **controllers/user.controller.js** :
  - validation email / mot de passe (8 caractères min) / rôle, `bcrypt.hash(..., 12)`
  - création automatique de la ligne `client` lors de la création d'un utilisateur
  - `409` sur doublon d'email (`23505`), erreurs déléguées à `next(error)`
  - correctifs : `require("react")` parasite, `user.body`, `error` hors scope dans
    `deleteUsers`, `massage` → `message`, statuts `201` → `200` sur les GET
  - renommages cohérents : `updateRole`, `activateUser`, `deactivateUser`
- **routes/user.route.js** : la route dupliquait `/register`, `/login`, `/me` avec `auth.route`
  et exposait `/fullname` sans authentification. Remplacée par le CRUD complet protégé par
  `authenticate` + `isAdmin`.
- **auth.controller.js** : `publicUser()` expose `fullname`.
- **Suppression** de `product.controller.js`, `product.models.js`, `product.route.js`,
  `isOwner.middleware.js`, `validate.middleware.js` (vides ou obsolètes).

### Frontend
- **user.services.js** : `API_URL` exportée, suppression du fallback `"CRM-Commerce-Backend"`,
  envoi automatique du header `Authorization: Bearer`, ajout de `getCurrentUser()` et `logout()`,
  `getFullName()` sécurisé.
- **ProtectedRoute.jsx** : ne se fie plus à `localStorage.role` — appelle `/auth/me`, affiche un
  état de chargement, purge la session si le token est invalide.
- **Navbar.jsx** : déconnexion déléguée au service.
- **admin/dashboard.jsx** : compteur utilisateurs réel via `/users/count` au lieu de `0` en dur.
- **user/dashboard.jsx** : cartes « modules à venir », icônes Font Awesome.
- **user/catalog.jsx** : suppression du `fetch` vers `localhost:3000` (mauvais port).
- **Home.jsx** : JSON-LD injecté via `useEffect` au lieu de `<script>` dans le JSX.
- **Nettoyage** : `<title>` dupliqué, `@types/react`, commentaires morts, CSS admin ajouté,
  nouveau `src/styles/global.css`.

### Documentation
- `README.md` : variables d'env corrigées (`DB_DATABASE`, `DB_SSL`, `CLIENT_URL`, `JWT_EXPIRES_IN`).
- `Technologie.md` : Axios / TypeScript retirés (non utilisés), `fetch` documenté.
- Ajout de `regles-vibe-coding-eviter.md`.

## Impact
- Aucun changement de schéma BDD (le `ALTER TABLE` retiré était un no-op).
- Le contrat de l'API `/api/users` change : réponse sans `password`, et toutes les routes
  exigent un token admin.
- Aucune fonctionnalité métier perdue : les compteurs non reliés à l'API sont affichés « — ».

## Vérification
- [ ] `npm start` (Backend) démarre et `/api/auth/login` répond
- [ ] `npm run dev` (Frontend) : login admin → dashboard affiche le nombre réel d'utilisateurs
- [ ] Un utilisateur non-admin ne peut plus accéder aux routes `/api/users`
- [ ] Inscription avec un email déjà utilisé → `409`

author: benoitc
body:
Every hornbeam Python request restores a CPython image, and a restore writes the whole 42 MB memory: about 12 ms of CPU even with `restore_ahead` taking it off the request's path. A request itself writes 44 of the image's 640 chunks of 64 KiB.

A restore with `recycle => true` now takes the memory of the last instance of the same image the process destroyed, swaps in zeroed chunks for the ones it wrote, and lays only the image runs that land in those. A memory restored this way marks the chunk each write lands in: every write path in `wasm_memory` goes through one accessor that does it, and the store the compiled tier inlines does the same, so generated code moves to ABI 5. Memories restored this way use 64 KiB chunks, which measured best against 256 KiB and 1 MiB. A restore also stops evaluating the element segments the image overwrites. The `restore_ahead` runner recycles on its own.

I did not build copy-on-write. Generated code reads the chunk tuple from `#mut{}` on every access and never rebinds it on a store, so copying on first write would mean threading a new `#mut{}` through every store in the generator, the interpreter and host writes. It would also copy the same 44 chunks during the request instead of at the restore. `test/audit/ATTEMPTS.md` has the reasoning and the numbers.

A recycled CPython restore is 3.9 ms against 12.0, which is short of the prompt's 1 ms: what is left is rewriting those 44 chunks at one `atomics:put/3` a word. The mark costs a store in generated code 16.7 ns against 12.3 in a recycled memory, and 12.6 in any other. On a CPython request that is about 4 ms of `handle()` (a store-heavy compile of the source) and 0.15 ms of `call()`. Throughput with `restore_ahead`, 14 workers, 64 callers, three builds interleaved twice on a loaded machine: 0.5.0 128 to 156 requests a second, main 201 to 275, this branch 368 to 466.

A test restores, writes through every path (stores, fill, copy, init, atomics, vector stores, growth, host writes) on both tiers, and checks the next recycling restore is the image byte for byte; it fails with the mark removed from the compiled store, from fill, or from host writes. The language suites' `restore_ahead` groups now run on recycled memory and still find no marker from one request in the next instance.

author: samjmc
body:
Closes the gaps listed at the end of PR #17.

## What changed

- **Tasks get an owner.** `TaskManager.create_task` records the signed-in user whose request created the task. `require_owner` now also checks `task_id`: the recorded user, or else the owner of the run, project or report in the task's metadata. The bundle tasks are created outside a request, and they carry `simulation_id`/`project_id`. Another user's task now gets a 404 on:
  - `/api/graph/task/<id>`;
  - `/api/simulation/prepare/status` and `/api/report/generate/status`;
  - `/api/source/deep-research/status|result/<id>`. These returned anyone's research dossier by task id.
- **The check runs on three more blueprints: session, bundle and source.** That closes two holes:
  - `PATCH /api/session/<id>` accepted any `project_id`/`simulation_id`.
  - `POST /api/bundle/<id>/complete-scenario` accepted any `simulation_id`/`report_id`, and the bundle comparison view would then show that run.
- **Dashboard shows real data.** `/api/dashboard/overview` read the Supabase `projects`/`simulations` tables, which nothing writes, so its lists were always empty. It now lists the caller's projects and runs from disk, with the fields `DashboardView.vue` uses (`id`, `title`, `status`, `created_at`).
- **Deleted `simulation_entities.py`, `graph_project_routes.py`, `report_tools_routes.py`.** No code imported them since #7 created them (`api/__init__.py` never listed them). An AST check shows every function in them also exists in the registered modules. The Graphiti plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-22-zep-to-graphiti-migration.md`) lists two of them as Zep call sites to migrate; they need no migration.

## Kept on purpose: `simulation_run_routes.py`

It is also never imported, but its `/start` has billing logic the live `/start` (`simulation.py`) lacks:
- A session's first run is covered by the credit that creating the session already took.
- The session's `simulation_id`, `status` and `simulation_count` are updated, and `_mark_session_completed_for_sim` marks the session done.

As shipped, creating a session takes 1 credit, and the live `/start` takes 1 more on every start, restarts too. Step 3 also sends no `session_id`. Moving that rule into the live `/start` is a pricing decision, so it is not in this PR. No backend is live, so nobody has been charged.

## Checks

- `tests/test_simulation_access.py`: **33 tests** (10 new: task stamping and owner rule, 5 task routes, session `PATCH`, bundle, dashboard).
  - With the three new blueprints left out of the registration, 4 tests fail.
  - With `task_id` left out of the checked fields, 5 tests fail.
- Backend suite: **569 passed, 0 failed**. `ruff check app/` and `ruff format --check app/` pass.

## Summary
A command palette: every grid action by name, with a one-line description and the key the user bound to it. Before this, someone with no `keymap` (the default) could reach an action only with the mouse, and nothing listed which keys were bound.

- **Opening it:** a new **Commands** button in the toolbar, plus a new `command-palette` keymap action with **no default binding**.
- **The list:** every action except `copy` / `paste` (which are decided inside the terminal) and the palette itself. The matching is the file finder's, over the name and the action id, so typing `find` finds `files-find`.
- **Actions that can't run now:** an action the current view can't run is greyed out with the reason. Enter on it does nothing and keeps the palette open.
- **Running an action:** a pick runs through the same gate a key goes through.

Closes #2266

## Items to Confirm / Review
- **The maintainer chose "button + unbound action" over binding `Cmd+Shift+P` by default**, so the "no default bindings" policy still holds. The docs suggest `"Cmd+Shift+p"` (lowercase on a Mac) for anyone who wants VS Code's key.
- **The `mulmoterminal-keys` skill used to suggest VS Code's palette key for `files-find`.** That advice now points at `command-palette`. A user who already has `Cmd+Shift+p` on `files-find` is told they can keep it.
- **`FileFinder.vue`'s template was NOT extracted into a shared component.** Only its pure matcher (`rankPaths` / `highlightParts`) is reused, so the finder is untouched and there is no refactor to prove.
- **A pick needs the grid to be in front** (found by cross review round 1). The toolbar keeps the palette reachable over another view and over the launch panel, and a pick used to act on the hidden grid. The host now says whether the grid has the keyboard — the same condition that makes the grid leave a key alone — and every row is disabled with a reason while it does not. The host also refuses a pick as a backstop.
- **Text fields and IME (moved):** those key-level checks moved from GridView into `useGridKeys.onKey`, in the same order: grid, then target, then IME. The existing GridView specs for the launch panel's Escape (#1890), text fields and IME confirmation still pass.
- **Scroll and IME in the palette (fixed in round 1):** the palette scrolls the active row into view, as the file finder does. It also leaves Enter and the arrows to an IME that is composing; that one was my own finding, not Codex's.
- **`GridView.vue` is at its file-length limit.** The palette's host (running a pick, and the `command-palette` action) lives in the new `useGridKeys`, which wraps `usePrefixKeys`. GridView only swapped one composable for the other.
- The palette is teleported to `body`, so it sets `font-sans` itself; without it the rows fell back to the browser's serif, which I found on the real screen.
- The strings are new in all five locales: the action label, the palette UI, and 13 descriptions.

## User Prompt
- #2266: how does it look, and do we decide the UI? → Open with a toolbar button + a keymap action with no default (A). For the rest, follow the recommendations: the finder's look, disabled rows with a reason, `KEYMAP_ACTIONS` only, a one-line description per row.
- Same flow as the other #2257 children: implement, cross review, merge once CI passes, update the issue and the umbrella.

## Verification
- **Real app, real Chrome**, on a server built from this branch with `{"command-palette": "F1", "files-find": "Ctrl+k p"}`:
  - the toolbar button opens the palette listing the palette actions;
  - `find` puts `files-find` first, greyed with "Needs an enlarged terminal" and showing `Ctrl+k p`;
  - Esc closes it, and F1 opens it;
  - "launch panel" then Enter opens the launch panel;
  - no page errors.
- **Mutation.** I removed twelve decisions one at a time, and each turned a spec red. Six are from the first version: `command-palette` opening the palette, the gate on a pick, the disabled-row guard, excluding the palette from its own list, the disabled reason, and host withdrawal only clearing its own registration. Six are from round 1: rows disabled while the grid is hidden, the host's backstop, the key-level yield, scroll into view, the IME guard, and GridView passing its real condition.
- `yarn format`, `yarn lint`, `yarn typecheck`, `yarn build` and the full `yarn test` pass locally.

ClickUp: https://app.clickup.com/t/86akptqg5

## Entrega
- `atualizarPorDeploy` aceita snapshots e prova opcional, reaproveita `calculateGuideImpact` e abre até 5 PRs draft, uma por guia impactado, via `submitContentPackage` e `assertPublicSubmit`.
- Branch derivada de `guideId` e SHAs implantados; consulta PR aberta antes de escrever e reaproveita a mesma em eventos repetidos. Execução local serializada; colisão remota não abre segunda PR.
- MCP `atualizar_por_deploy` com `mutates: true` e CLI `pilot/scripts/update-by-deploy.mjs`. Sem workflow ou leitura dos repositórios do produto (M5.41).
- A proposta acrescenta apenas um comentário editorial não renderizado ao MDX. O conteúdo canônico fica aguardando revisão humana; gate público segue rejeitando qualquer texto visível não aprovado. PRs geradas ficam draft e nunca são aprovadas ou mergeadas automaticamente.

## Testes
- Primeiro commit contém somente testes; RED: `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` para `update-by-deploy.mjs` antes da implementação.
- `npm run mcp:test`: passou (71 arquivos); `npm run content:validate`, `npm run types:check`, `npm run lint` e `npm run build`: passaram.
- Integração GitHub simulada: segundo evento reutiliza PR pela branch, sem novo POST `/pulls` nem PUT de conteúdo. Execução paralela, zero writes sem impacto, SHA da prova divergente, gate rejeitado e teto de 5 cobertos.
- Mutações verificadas e restauradas: remover busca de PR existente → exit 1 (`busca a PR pela branch determinística`); trocar teto 5 por 7 → exit 1; aceitar `appSha` diferente → exit 1.

Os testes após o primeiro commit foram ajustados para registrar a nova ferramenta nos inventários MCP e no fixture HTTP, e o mock de GitHub passou a contar apenas writes reais após a busca de PR. Acrescentei também o contraexemplo que confirma que o comentário editorial não permite alterar texto visível do guia.

Pendência operacional: a M5.41 fará o disparo pelo workflow e fornecerá snapshots e prova da versão implantada. Esta PR não aciona deploy.


## Correção r1 (9c948ff)
- `proofOutcome` no runner avalia os `stepId` do guia compilado por perfil, exige staging e SHA implantado, e devolve motivos explícitos. O runner grava `outcome` e encerra com código 1 em staging quando a prova fica pendente. O update-by-deploy usa esse mesmo resultado.
- Cada passo emitido informa `role`; `blocked` no perfil denied é sucesso esperado, enquanto `passed` nesse perfil é acesso indevido.
- Teste primeiro: commit `93fb5b7` falhou por falta de export `proofOutcome`. Após esse commit, a fixture foi ajustada para desabilitar Salvar Alterações no perfil denied, permitindo um relatório positivo real com `blocked` e negativos derivados dele por uma alteração cada.
- Gate final: `content:validate`, `mcp:test` (71 arquivos), `types:check`, `lint` e `build` passaram.
- Mutações verificadas e restauradas, todas vermelhas: aceitar `steps: []` (exit 1), tratar `blocked` no denied como falha (exit 1), ignorar os `stepId` exigidos (exit 1).


## Correção r2 (a47b6cc)
- `proofOutcome` valida o formato completo do relatório por uma lista única de campos conhecidos: staging, SHA, perfis, QR, guias, passos, screenshots, cleanup e listas de problemas. Campo desconhecido, warning, cleanup pendente ou status de cleanup sem sucesso geram pendência explícita.
- Todos os resultados authorized para cada stepId precisam passar. Um `manual_required` ou `blocked` permanece pendente mesmo ao lado de outro `passed`.
- Teste primeiro: commit `3f90511` usa relatório emitido pelo runner em fixture, cria cada negativo com uma alteração e falhou por asserção em `cleanupPending`. Implementação no commit `a47b6cc`.
- Mutações verificadas e restauradas, todas vermelhas por asserção: ignorar `cleanupPending` (exit 1), aceitar campo desconhecido (exit 1), remover regra explícita de `manual_required` (exit 1).
- Gate local: `content:validate`, `mcp:test` (71 arquivos), `types:check`, `lint` e `build` passaram. `origin/integration/claricia-v2` foi trazida por merge antes do push; base já estava atualizada.

## Summary

**`.env` loading.** `hybrid/config.py` is now the only loader.

- Previously `pipeline.py` and `llm_agent.py` loaded `TradingAgents/.env` first, so the project-root `.env` (the one `.env.template` tells you to create) never took effect outside Docker.

- `HybridConfig` no longer re-applies `TRADINGAGENTS_*` on top of explicit settings. TradingAgents' `DEFAULT_CONFIG` already applies them with type coercion. The duplicate made **env beat CLI flags** and turned ints such as `max_debate_rounds` into strings.

**Tests.** The source-grep P0 tests are replaced with behaviour tests:
- learned-weight scaling, using a temp weights file
- a SQLite storage round trip
- the Jupiter quote request going to `lite-api.jup.ag`
- the Uniswap swap deadline being epoch now+300s

The funding test is dropped because `test_btc_funding_units.py` now covers it. A new `test_config_env.py` covers `.env` and LLM precedence. CI now installs `aiosqlite`, so the storage test runs instead of skipping.

### Motivation
- Recipients of external one-time shares had no public page to enter a separately-delivered verification code and reveal a credential once, which prevented the full recipient journey.
- Current links could leak secrets into request paths, logs, referrers, or browser history and did not provide a deliberate one-time reveal UX.
- The implementation must avoid disclosing whether a credential exists and must resist token leakage, indexing, and caching.

### Description
- Add a minimal public landing page at `GET /credential-share` with template `app/templates/credential_share.html`, accessible markup, non-indexing headers, and no plaintext embedded in HTML. 
- Implement client-side flow in `app/static/js/credential_share.js` that reads the opaque token from the URL fragment, immediately removes it from history, sends verification and reveal requests with `credentials: 'omit'` and `referrerPolicy: 'no-referrer'`, and only writes the plaintext into the DOM after a successful reveal; styling in `app/static/css/credential_share.css`.
- Place external share tokens in the URL fragment by changing generated links to use a fragment (`#token`) in `app/services/workflow_credential_shares.py` so tokens never reach server request paths or referrers.
- Add per-client rate limiting for external share verification via a new `SimpleRateLimiter` instance `_external_share_limiter` in `app/api/routes/vault.py` and preserve the generic "Share unavailable" response for failed/expired/revoked/consumed/invalid states to prevent enumeration.
- Exempt the public share APIs from session CSRF and from IP-whitelist blocking by adding `/api/vault/shares/verify` and `/api/vault/shares/reveal` to the middleware exemption lists configured in `app/main.py`.
- Add a regression test `tests/test_external_credential_share_page.py` verifying no embedded token/plaintext, history/referrer protections, accessible markup, and fragment-only generated URLs; record a change log file under `changes/`.

### Testing
- Ran targeted pytest: `python -m pytest -q tests/test_external_credential_share_page.py tests/test_credential_grants.py tests/test_workflow_credential_share_step.py`, which completed successfully (tests passed).

## Summary

Patch the reported anyhow, crossbeam-epoch, quick-xml and rustls dependency issues, including rustls-webpki. Adapt the two XML consumers to quick-xml 0.41 so encoded MTP settings, TRX references and surrounding spaces survive parsing. Make the security job fail when `cargo audit` fails.

Include the rewrite registry and both Claude rewrite hooks in the critical-file alert. Anchor the matcher so similarly named documentation and backup files do not trigger the alert, and cover both workflow extensions.

## Evidence

- Before: the successful security job logged four dependency vulnerabilities and an anyhow warning. A direct XML API migration lost references and spaces, and stopped recognising `true` as true.
- After: both focused XML regressions pass. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test --all` pass locally: 3,845 tests passed and eight were ignored across 27 suites.
- A fabricated audit command verifies both exit paths. GitHub's implicit `bash -e` shell hid a failing audit behind `tee`; explicit `shell: bash` enables `pipefail`, so the step now returns one for a failing audit and zero for a clean audit.
- Five locked crates change; quick-xml is the only manifest range change. Cargo resolved versions compatible with the existing Rust 1.91 minimum.
- Hosted Linux, macOS and Windows tests, formatting, Clippy, benchmarks, Security Scan and Semgrep pass on commit `44d23b07ca3409bcb78fb3e9d16d29703ffe1586`.
- The critical-file matcher passes 12 positive and four negative path fixtures. Before the fix, it missed the registry, both rewrite hooks and `.yaml` workflows, and falsely matched two ordinary paths.

## Merge danger

**Door:** two-way. **Blast radius:** XML parsing, TLS dependencies and CI.

Dependency audit failures now block CI. The XML tests cover encoded values, named and numeric references, CDATA and adjacent spaces.

## Unverified

`cargo audit` was not installed locally; the hosted security job ran it successfully. The eight existing ignored Rust tests were not enabled. An additional actionlint check confirms valid workflow structure but reports 90 pre-existing ShellCheck information/style messages, unchanged by this patch. author: samuelelijah585
body:
## Overview

Adds end-to-end coverage for the colour-blind operation flow on the treasury overview. The flow is the path a designer or QA engineer walks before signing off status colours, and it was the only part of the feature without e2e coverage — `ColorBlindSimulationProvider`, `ColorBlindToggle` and `contrastUtils.ts` each had unit tests, so a break in the wiring between them stayed green.

The new spec drives the real UI (`page.goto` plus clicks on the visible preset chips and the banner's disable button), never imports from `src/`, and asserts the whole chain as DOM state: selected preset -> `data-colorblind-simulation` on the wrapper -> the wrapper's inline `filter` reference -> the referenced `<filter>` element -> its `feColorMatrix[type=matrix]` matrix -> the sticky banner and preview description. A dropped or mismatched filter definition now fails the suite instead of silently previewing unfiltered colours.

## Related Issue

Tracks the missing e2e coverage reported for the colour-blind operation flow. Test-and-docs only; no application source, styles, or CI configuration is modified.

## Changes

### Colour-blind operation flow suite

* **[ADD]** `e2e/colorblind-simulation-flow.spec.ts`
  * `openColorBlindControls()` walks to `/app/treasurypage` and waits for the settled (data-loaded) overview before driving the preview.
  * `selectPreset()` clicks the visible preset chip (the visually hidden radio follows its label) and asserts the radio reports checked by its accessible name.
  * `colorBlindChainIsIntact()` reads the preset -> filter-definition chain out of the live DOM and returns `false` the moment any single link is broken, including a malformed (not 20-value) colour matrix.
  * `storedArtifacts()` reports any leftover simulation keys in `localStorage` / `sessionStorage`.
  * Success path: every preset (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia) is selected from `Off`, verified through the chain plus the banner/preview text, and disabled again from the banner, with the overview still rendered underneath the filter (the chips are only ever clicked while the page is unfiltered, matching the order a designer works in).
  * Success path: preset selection by keyboard alone — focus moves and the selection follows native radio-group arrow navigation.
  * Failure path: all four documented storage keys seeded in both `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` before load cannot enable the preview, and the leftovers are cleaned up on mount.
  * Failure path: a reload returns the preview to `Off` and persists nothing.
  * Canary: with the flow intact the chain assertion passes, then removing the SVG filter definitions — the way a regression would break it — turns the same assertion red, so the success path cannot pass vacuously.

* **[MODIFY]** `e2e/README.md`
  * New "Colour-blind simulation flow" section: run command, what is covered, and the failure paths.

## Verification Results

```
Executed through the GitHub Playwright suite. Intended exact-head commands:

  npx playwright test e2e/colorblind-simulation-flow.spec.ts
  npm run test:e2e            # what CI runs (chromium + firefox)

This environment produced the change through the GitHub REST API only (no local
clone), so the run itself was not executed here and pass/fail is reported by CI on
this head rather than claimed here. The selectors and behaviours the spec relies
on were read from the application source at this head:

  - src/pages/TreasuryPage.tsx: the provider wraps the page and
    `IS_DEV && <ColorBlindToggle />` renders the controls on /app/treasurypage
  - src/components/colorBlindSimulation/ColorBlindToggle.tsx: radio accessible
    names from SIMULATION_LABELS, chip text from modeShortLabel, and the
    `active-filter-description` preview text
  - src/components/colorBlindSimulation/ColorBlindSimulationProvider.tsx:
    `[data-colorblind-simulation]` wrapper + `filter: url(#cb-filter-<mode>)`,
    the `cb-filter-<mode>` feColorMatrix definitions, the active banner, and
    COLORBLIND_STORAGE_KEYS / COLORBLIND_PERSISTENCE_POLICY
  - .github/workflows/ci.yml: the `Build & test` job runs `npm run test:e2e`
    (whole e2e directory, chromium + firefox) on every pull request to main
```

| Acceptance Criteria | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Test follows the flow as a user would, without reaching into internals | ✅ Navigates by URL and drives the visible chips and the banner's disable button; the spec imports nothing from `src/` |
| Covers the success path and the primary failure | ✅ Success: all three presets applied and disabled, plus a keyboard-only selection. Failure: spoofed storage cannot enable the preview, and a reload resets to `Off` |
| Runs in CI on every pull request | ✅ Picked up automatically by `npm run test:e2e` in the `Build & test` job of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which triggers on `pull_request` to `main` |
| Fails when any step of the flow breaks | ✅ The chain assertion covers preset -> filter reference -> live `feColorMatrix` definition -> banner; the canary test breaks one step and shows the assertion goes red |
| Validation: break one step of the flow and confirm the end-to-end test fails | ✅ Canary test removes the SVG filter definitions and asserts the chain assertion reports the break (`false`) after first proving it reports `true` when intact |
| Existing lint, typecheck, build, and e2e checks stay green | Pending CI on this head — `tsconfig.json` includes only `src`, so the new spec is not part of `tsc -b` |

Closes #1782

body:
- [x] I have read the contributing guidelines.
- [x] I have registered the PR changes.

### Ⅰ. Describe what this PR did
The fastjson2 JSONB concurrent-reference tests still fail intermittently after reader warmup, returning null `$ref` fields in RPC messages and UndoLog images. Issue #8277 contains the actual failing JDK 8/17/21 CI stacks.

Route both decoders through a shared `Fastjson2JsonbParser` monitor covering the complete parse, including deferred reference resolution. This prevents overlapping Seata RPC/UndoLog parses from accessing fastjson2's shared runtime reference state concurrently. Preserve the existing JSONB format, reader features and RPC auto-type filter.

Strengthen the cold-JVM regressions to use two parser instances and check shared-object identity, not just non-null fields. Forward the configurable worker count into child JVMs. Add tests that mix the filtered/unfiltered entry points and verify that malformed input does not block a later decode on another thread.

### Ⅱ. Does this pull request fix one issue?
Fixes #8277.

This follows the incomplete mitigation in #8160 / #8159.

### Ⅲ. Test cases
- Java 17: 13 focused tests passed: common parser/warmup (4), UndoLog (6), RPC serializer (3).
- Both cold-JVM regressions ran 20 rounds with 200 threads on Java 17.
- Executed the same compiled regression `main` entry points in fresh Java 8u181 and Java 21.0.7 JVMs: 10 rounds per path per JDK, 200 threads per JVM. All passed.
- Total fixed-code stress coverage: 80 fresh JVMs / 16,000 decoding tasks, plus the common parser's mixed-entry-point test.
- Changed-file Checkstyle and all three affected modules' Spotless checks passed.

The local Java 17 pre-fix control also passed 20 rounds per path. The linked CI failures are the observed reproduction evidence; local passing stress tests are not presented as a deterministic before/after reproduction.

### Ⅳ. Describe how to verify it
Using Java 17 and the repository's baseline dependencies installed:

```sh
mvn -pl json-common/json-common-core install \
  -Dtest=Fastjson2JsonbParserTest,Fastjson2ObjectReaderWarmupTest
mvn -pl serializer/seata-serializer-fastjson2,rm-datasource test \
  -Dtest=Fastjson2ConcurrentRefDeserializationTest,Fastjson2SerializerTest,Fastjson2UndoLogParserTest \
  -Dseata.fastjson2.concurrentRef.rounds=20
```

On a clean checkout, add `-am -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false` to build prerequisite modules.

### Ⅴ. Special notes for reviews
This is a conservative correctness mitigation: fastjson2 RPC and UndoLog decoding share one monitor per classloader, so these decode calls no longer execute in parallel. Encoding remains concurrent. The throughput cost has not been benchmarked; removing this guard requires a separately verified upstream fix rather than relying only on ObjectReader warmup. Tests are neither skipped nor retried after assertion failures.

author: its-applekid
body:
Closes #380

## Problem

`recoverConnectorStorage` only looked in the `receipts` table for dispatch evidence. The KHA-121 dispatcher keeps its state and receipts in `dispatch_records` and never writes `receipts`. So in the composed connector, a release that reached the session and then lost its reply was `outcome_unknown` in the dispatch ledger, but the recovery lifecycle reported it as `undispatchedReleases: 1, unknownReleaseIds: []` and never reconciled it.

## Change

Recovery now also reads the `dispatch_records.state` column:

| Dispatcher state | Recovery view |
| --- | --- |
| `dispatching`, `accepted`, `outcome_unknown` | dispatch evidence: `outcomeUnknownReleases` (held and reconciled, never resubmitted) |
| `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `abandoned` | settled: no longer open |
| `queued`, `claimed`, `quarantined`, `rejected` | no effect ran: stays `undispatchedReleases` |

`claimed` stays undispatched on purpose. The dispatcher documents it as "no effect has run", and `Dispatcher.reconcile` requeues it. The settled row fixes a second problem the same gap caused: a release the dispatcher had completed was reported as undispatched, and `resumeReleases` handed it over again, where it was refused as a duplicate.

The receipt-table path is unchanged. The storage README invariant row is updated.

## Verification

- Test that fails on the wrong implementation: `pnpm -C packages/connector exec vitest run src/storage/dispatch.test.ts -t "recovery view"`. It writes every dispatcher state through the real `createConnectorDispatchStorage` and nothing to `receipts`. It passes with this change and fails with only `recovery.ts` reverted.
- `packages/connector` vitest: 546 passed. `apps/connector` vitest: 117 passed. Typecheck, eslint and `check:boundaries` pass.
- #381 has merged, and this branch merges main (`05aca59`). This PR flips its `tests/e2e/security/recovery.test.ts` case from `it.fails('KNOWN DEFECT: …')` to a plain `it` and updates `docs/evidence/security-acceptance.md`: the delivery-ambiguity row is now **pass**, and the security suite shows 48 passed and 3 live cases skipped. `pnpm test:e2e` after the merge: 133 passed, 4 skipped.

author: tannevaled
body:
## What this changes

The `386` lane stops using `qemu-i386` and runs the test binary directly on the
x86-64 runner. Every other lane is unchanged.

## Why — measured, not assumed

The 386 lane panicked in `go-gfx/gfx` at a line the arithmetic makes impossible.
Two instrumented runs passed, which looked like the instrumentation mattering —
until the lane was sampled properly. **Eight identical lanes on one commit**,
repeated for each condition:

| condition | failures |
|---|---|
| under `qemu-i386` | **5 of 8** |
| under `qemu-i386`, `GODEBUG=asyncpreemptoff=1` | 0 of 8 |
| **native** on the same runner, preemption on | 0 of 8 |
| under `qemu-arm` | 0 of 8 |

If the true rate under emulation were 5/8, seeing 0/8 has probability
`0.375^8 ≈ 4e-4`, so asynchronous preemption is the mechanism and the emulator is
the variable. Each failure landed on a *different* input although the seed is
fixed, and the wrong value was a sign flip rather than a rounding difference:
`qemu-i386` loses the guest's floating-point state across the signal Go delivers
to preempt a goroutine.

The control for "did it really run without the emulator": `qemu-user-static`
registers `binfmt_misc` handlers, so the riscv64 lane ran under qemu in both
conditions and took 71 s in both. The 386 lane went from ~85 s to ~40 s. Same job
shape, one lane moved.

## Why this is the right fix rather than a retry

A lane that goes red at random teaches people to ignore red. Emulating 386 buys
nothing here — a 386 ELF is a native binary on this runner — so the lane is
faster *and* it only fails for reasons that belong to us.

`arm` stays under `qemu-arm`: there is no native option, and it was clean in
8 of 8.

author: mano8
body:
## B34 — lock integrity guard (`G34`(b))

`npm ci` checks a package's bytes only against the `integrity` its lock entry records, and installs an entry that has none without saying anything. `fa-ui-m8`'s lock carried 909 such entries through three regenerations (`G33`), and no npm repository in the fleet had a gate that would have caught it. This PR adds that gate.

- **Guard:** `scripts/verify-lock-integrity.mjs` (`npm run verify:lock-integrity`). It has no dependencies and is byte-identical in all six npm repositories. It exits 1 and names every offending key when the lock is below `lockfileVersion` 3, or when an entry has no `integrity` or no `resolved`, has a non-`sha512` hash, resolves outside `https://registry.npmjs.org/`, or is a link, a `file:` source, or a key outside `node_modules/`. The root entry is exempt.
- **CI:** `CI.yaml` runs it before `npm ci` in every job that installs.
- **Tests:** `tests/lock-integrity.test.ts` has one fixture lock per rule, each refused with its key named. A clean fixture passes, the CLI's exit codes are checked, and the repository's **real** lock is asserted to pass.


**No version bump.** The script and the test are not in `files`, and `npm pack --dry-run` lists neither. `package.json` gains one non-lifecycle `scripts` entry, which changes nothing a consumer runs.

This lock already passes (0 offending entries), so the fixtures prove the red path. `CHANGELOG.md` has an `### Added` bullet under `[Unreleased]`.

### Local gates
- `typecheck`, `lint`, `npm test` (100 %), `verify:fleet-gates`, `npm pack --dry-run`

### Codacy follow-up
Codacy (Lizard) rated the first `entryReasons` at cyclomatic complexity 15, above its limit of 10. A follow-up commit moves the `resolved` and `integrity` checks into `resolvedReason` / `integrityReason`, and the highest function is now 8. Behaviour is unchanged, `tests/lock-integrity.test.ts` is unmodified, and the script is still byte-identical in all six repositories.

author: bjnabs
body:
# Pull Request

## Summary

Trivy now reports **CVE-2026-84939** (CRITICAL: path traversal through a malformed locale identifier) in the Apache FreeMarker 2.3.32 jar bundled in Keycloak 26.7.4. FreeMarker renders every login, account and email template. The Foundation container gate now fails on every PR because of it; #40 hit it first.

This PR swaps in FreeMarker **2.3.35**, the fixed release, using the same verified jar-override pattern this Dockerfile already uses for Bouncy Castle.

## Related Issues

This unblocks baobab-platform/baobab-iam#40, which carries this same change as a merge.

## Business Value

It removes a critical vulnerability from the component that renders every identity-facing page.

## Type of Change

- [x] Security fix

## Implementation Summary

- A new `freemarker` build stage fetches `freemarker-2.3.35.jar` from Maven Central and checks it against a pinned SHA-256. I confirmed the jar's SHA-1 matches the one Maven Central publishes (`dd1d9737c3e8b8a5bf0d44981eb308df4822e241`).
- The builder stage replaces `lib/lib/main/org.freemarker.freemarker-2.3.32.jar` in place and keeps the filename, because Quarkus' fast-jar classpath refers to the jar by name.
- A guard fails the build if Keycloak stops shipping that exact jar, so the override gets revisited instead of silently misapplied.
- Remove the stage once `upstream.lock.yaml` pins a Keycloak release that bundles FreeMarker 2.3.35 or later.

## Database Changes

- [x] No database changes

## API Changes

- [x] No API changes

## User Interface Changes

- [x] No UI changes (same templates, patched engine)

## Multi-Tenant Impact

- [x] No tenant impact

## Security Review

- Fixes CVE-2026-84939 (CRITICAL).
- The jar comes from Maven Central over HTTPS and its checksum is pinned, as the Bouncy Castle override already does.

## Performance Impact

- [x] No measurable impact

## Testing Performed

I tested against a real **Keycloak 26.7.4**, run locally from the release tarball with the 2.3.35 jar swapped in:
- Keycloak starts and reports healthy.
- A fresh realm bootstraps, and the integration suite passes **97 of 97**. That run includes #40's section, so it covers both changes together.
- FreeMarker renders the `baobab` realm's login page ("Sign in to Baobab Platform").

I couldn't build the image in my environment because the image registries are blocked, so this PR's CI (build, Trivy container scan and integration test) provides that proof.

## Documentation

- [x] Dockerfile comments explain the override and when to remove it

## Checklist

- [x] Self-review completed
- [ ] CI checks passing (pending)

## Reviewer Checklist

- [ ] The pinned hash matches Maven Central's `freemarker-2.3.35.jar`

## Deployment Notes

Rebuild and redeploy the IAM image.

## Additional Notes

Separately, while testing I noticed that a browser login to the `baobab` realm is refused. Keycloak logs `auth-otp-form requires user to be set in the authentication context`, meaning the OTP step runs before any user is identified. This happens with either FreeMarker version, so it isn't caused by this PR, and I've reported it rather than widening this change.

author: frdomovic
body:
## The bug
Creating a workspace failed on the first real screen:

```
HTTP 400 Invalid JSON data: … upgradePolicy: unknown field `upgradePolicy`, expected one of `applicationId`, `name`, `appKey`, `bytecodeId`
```

core's `CreateNamespaceApiRequest` is `deny_unknown_fields`. mero-chat sent `{applicationId, upgradePolicy, alias, name}` and cast the body `as unknown as` the SDK type, so tsc never checked it.

## Same bug in three more bodies
| call | sent | core accepts |
|---|---|---|
| create namespace | `upgradePolicy`, `alias` | `applicationId`, `name`, `appKey` |
| reparent group | `new_parent_id` | `newParentId` |
| upgrade group | `migrateMethod` | `targetApplicationId`, `cascade`, `forceCodeOnly` |
| create invitation (type) | `requester`, `expirationBlockHeight` | `expirationTimestamp`, `recursive` |

All the body casts are gone, so the mero-js request types check these bodies now. The dead "Migration Method" input on the Upgrade tab is removed.

## Why every suite was green
- The unit tests **asserted the broken body verbatim** (`toHaveBeenCalledWith({… upgradePolicy …})`).
- Every Playwright mock answered **any** POST with a 200, and no test clicked **Create**.

Fix: `e2e/helpers/closed-bodies.ts` refuses unknown keys the way core does (key sets copied from core's `deny_unknown_fields` structs), and a new e2e test submits the create form and checks the body. **I re-added `upgradePolicy` and the test failed**, then it passed with the fix.

## Other apps
- `scripts/dev-node.sh` in mero-chat, mero-calendar, mero-design, mero-pixart and mero-stream, plus mero-chat's `setup-nodes.sh` and `permissions-testing.sh`, and mero-stream's `two-node-suite.mjs`, sent the same refused create body. They now send `{applicationId, name}`.
- The other apps' `createNamespace` calls in `src/` already send `{applicationId, name}` with no cast. mero-chat was the only app with the problem in its source.

## Verified locally
- `tsc -b` clean
- vitest: 62 files, 494 tests pass
- Playwright (mocked): 32/32 pass
- eslint: 0 errors
- `bash -n` / `node --check` on every edited script

author: diyaq
body:
## Summary

Enforce missing authorization checks and extract shared access-grant helper

## What was solved

### #851 — [clinical-guideline] create_reminder skips the provider-registry check every sibling function enforces

Add the missing provider-registry authorization check to create_reminder in the clinical-guideline contract so it matches the pattern enforced by every other mutating function (evaluate_guideline, calculate_drug_dosage, assess_risk_score, suggest_care_pathway, check_preventive_care). The fix inserts Self::is_provider_registered(&env, &provider_id) after require_auth() and rejects unregistered callers, plus adds a test exercising an unregistered caller.

Addressed:
- Changed: contracts/clinical-guideline/src/lib.rs, contracts/clinical-guideline/src/test.rs
- Add the same is_provider_registered check used by sibling mutating functions to create_reminder in contracts/clinical-guideline/src/lib.rs (around lines 348-385).
- Keep the existing provider_id.require_auth() call; only add the registry check and rejection path.
- Reject unregistered callers with the same error/panic pattern used by sibling functions (do not invent a new error type).

### #852 — [clinical-guideline] get_reminder has no authentication or access control

Add authentication and access control to the clinical-guideline contract's get_reminder function so that only the patient themselves or a registered provider can read a patient's care reminder, matching the pattern used elsewhere in the contract.

Addressed:
- Changed: contracts/clinical-guideline/src/lib.rs
- Add requester.require_auth() to get_reminder before returning the Reminder
- Add an access check allowing patient self-access (requester == patient_id) or a registered provider (is_provider_registered)
- Preserve existing get_reminder signature/return behavior for authorized callers

### #853 — [dental-records] Only authorization check in the contract is completely untested

Add a focused unit test to the dental-records contract test suite that exercises the sole explicit access-control check in document_procedure_performed: calling it with a dentist address different from plan.dentist_id and asserting Err(Error::Unauthorized). This closes the untested wrong-dentist authorization boundary without touching contract logic.

Addressed:
- Changed: contracts/dental-records/src/test.rs, contracts/dental-records/src/test.rs
- Add a test in contracts/dental-records/src/test.rs that calls document_procedure_performed with a dentist address different from plan.dentist_id and asserts Err(Error::Unauthorized).
- Ensure the test sets up a valid plan (initialized contract, registered/authorized dentist, created plan) so the failure is attributable to the wrong-dentist check rather than missing auth or missing plan.
- Do not modify the contract logic in contracts/dental-records/src/lib.rs; the check at lines 247-249 is correct and only needs coverage.

### #854 — [allergy-management/allergy-tracking] Access-grant logic duplicated instead of shared

Extract the duplicated patient/provider access-grant logic (grant/revoke/check plus GrantedProviders index maintenance and the patient-or-admin short-circuit) from allergy-management and allergy-tracking into a shared helper in contracts/shared, then have both contracts delegate to it. This removes drift (e.g. TTL extension present only in allergy-management) while preserving each contract's existing public API and behavior.

Addressed:
- Changed: contracts/shared/src/lib.rs
- Create a generic patient/provider access-grant helper in contracts/shared providing grant, revoke, and check operations plus GrantedProviders index maintenance and the 'patient or admin always has access' short-circuit.
- Refactor contracts/allergy-management/src/storage.rs (grant_access/revoke_access/check_access_permission, lines ~92-152) to use the shared helper instead of its local duplicated implementation.
- Refactor contracts/allergy-tracking/src/lib.rs (grant_access/revoke_access/check_access, lines ~563-601 and ~967-976) to use the same shared helper.

## Changes

- `contracts/clinical-guideline/src/lib.rs` (modify)
- `contracts/clinical-guideline/src/test.rs` (modify)
- `contracts/dental-records/src/test.rs` (modify)
- `contracts/shared/src/lib.rs` (modify)

## Approach

1. #851 — [clinical-guideline] create_reminder skips the provider-registry check every sibling function enforces (Changed: contracts/clinical-guideline/src/lib.rs, contracts/clinical-guideline/src/test.rs)
2. #852 — [clinical-guideline] get_reminder has no authentication or access control (Changed: contracts/clinical-guideline/src/lib.rs)
3. #853 — [dental-records] Only authorization check in the contract is completely untested (Changed: contracts/dental-records/src/test.rs, contracts/dental-records/src/test.rs)
4. #854 — [allergy-management/allergy-tracking] Access-grant logic duplicated instead of shared (Changed: contracts/shared/src/lib.rs)

## Issues

Closes #851
Closes #852
Closes #853
Closes #854

body:
Closes #3977

Prunes the tests in `src/lang/be` to `doc/language/test.md#test-policy`, with one commit per file or area. 559 tests become 380, so 179 are removed.

## Plan

- **Delete** tests that:
  - repeat another test or a link or corpus case. Each cited case was confirmed under `test/`, for example `3642-undefined-entry-debug-riscv32`, `3677-collected-function-debug-riscv32`, `macho-named-sections`, the `2800-pin-to-*` cases and `test/cases/call`.
  - check blatantly simple code: field copies, one-line clamps, membership scans, trivial constructors.
  - pin implementation detail rather than correctness: piece and move counts, allocator growth call counts, the 427-byte abbrev golden, cost ratios.
  - pin a problem that no longer exists, such as the `__1851` program pins and `rejects_unsupported_wide_op`, whose opcode now expands.
  - check only leaks or allocation-failure paths rather than behaviour: `dnit__frees_attributes`, `image_attributes__frees_intermediate_accumulators`, the ctwalk every-ordinal refusal walk, `encoder_output_dnit`.
  - decline on every host, like the off-win64 stack-probe geometry stub. The pinned win64 byte geometry went with it.
- **Fold** near-duplicates into one test per branch set:
  - per-target triples in `codegen.mach`
  - lane-width families in `legalize` and `vector_runtime`
  - the coalescing, rewrite and hole cases in `regalloc`
  - `extfold` shapes and `frame` limits
  - the linker overflow and symtab cases
- **Cut sweeps** to a representative set. mir/abi's tag and carrier sweeps keep one convention per classifier branch.
- **mir/abi transport sweeps** select each convention once from one registry instead of registering every target per cell, taking the module from about 4s to under 0.1s.
- **#2562:** the deleted linker test's one case, a loose object ahead of an archive satisfying the root so the member defining it stays out, is now an extra read in `read_objects__archive_members_resolve_in_input_order`. The check fails when `read_objects` stops noting loose definitions.
- **Keep** the only coverage of critical branches: regalloc invariants (verify_allocation, reserved registers, secret origin through spill and reload, fixed pairs, the shifted call-result pair), ABI classification on every convention, wide legalization with secret lanes and declassify barriers, the constant-time validator, DWARF tombstones, atom coalescing and archive resolution.
- **Rename** survivors into `subject__case`. No survivor pins an easy-to-reintroduce regression on its own, so none is named `regression__*`.
- **Helpers:**
  - Every test-only helper is marked `#[testing]`, including those in the runtime probes that only the `tests` library reaches.
  - Helpers nothing uses any more are deleted.
  - `doc/mach` and `doc/README.md` are regenerated, which drops only the now-testing `pub` helpers in `linker/common` and `linker/atoms`. The README reorder follows from the dropped `of.ar` import in `linker.mach`.
