body:
## Summary

`main` had fallen 41 commits behind `EuroHPC`, the branch where development actually happens. This PR merges `EuroHPC` into `main` (no conflicts; the merged tree is identical to `EuroHPC`) and adds four cleanup commits:

- **Drop unused dependencies.** `NK_Grid/requirements.txt` no longer pins matplotlib, seaborn or shap. Nothing imports them, and removing them cuts a fresh environment from 29 packages to 13 (numba and llvmlite are among those dropped).
  - The requirements hash is part of a launcher environment's recorded identity. An existing shared venv (BMRC `venv/aleatoric-<cpu>`, local `.venv-linux`) will be refused until it is recreated or refreshed with `--refresh-env` while no job is using it. Per-run Discoverer venvs are unaffected.
- **Correct `launch/DISCOVERER.md`.**
  - New runs start the shared single-model scheduler, the same one BMRC prepared-data runs use. The continuation protocol the guide describes now only resumes historical runs that have a `continuation.json`.
  - Removed the "BMRC keeps the old submitter" statement, which contradicted the other guides.
  - Lists the current algorithm versions: v10 for FFC, v11 for SMR.
- **Remove unreferenced files:**
  - `cutover_guard.py`
  - `NK_Grid/scheduler_profiles/ffc_gpa_local_bootstrap.json`
  - `NK_Grid/slurm/plan_production.sbatch` and `make_production_request.py`
  - `launch/fresh_gpa.py`

  None of these has an importer, caller or documentation reference. A run started with `fresh_gpa.py` should resume from its own frozen checkout.
- **Make `run.sh --update` branch-agnostic.** It used to require and pull `SMR&FFC`, which is stale here but may still be the tracked branch in upstream clones. It now fast-forwards whichever branch is checked out, keeps the clean-worktree check, and refuses a detached HEAD.

## Validation

- `pip install --dry-run` on the trimmed requirements resolves 13 packages, and none of the removed ones is pulled back in. No code imports any of the dropped packages.
- `bash -n run.sh` passes. In a temporary clone, `--update` fast-forwarded a non-`main` branch from its upstream and refused a detached HEAD.

Delete the stale branches:
- `SMR&FFC`
- `queue/batch-protocol`

- `claude/cost-calibration`
- `claude/mlp-cv-alpha`

All of their content is already in `main` or in this PR.

author: nihmar
body:
Closes #302.

**Today** `fullScan` loaded the whole library into memory before writing: every index row into one map, the disk walk into one list, the parsed text of every changed note into another map. `d30ae0b4` measured it at ~9 s and ~1 GB at a million notes — an OOM on a phone, on first open, explicit re-index *and* the periodic rescan.

## What this does

- **`DirWalker`** drives one long-lived background isolate that answers one directory listing per request, depth-first, parents first (one spawn per scan, not one per folder, and FUSE stats stay off the UI isolate).
- **`IndexReconciler`** mirrors the library folder by folder: load only that folder's rows, diff the listing, read/write its changed notes in bounded batches, move on. `indexTreeFirst` walks the same way; the one-time repairs are paged; the "notes without a content row" check is scoped to the directory.
- **Rename pairing across directories** goes through `scan_orphans`/`scan_gone` temp tables: gone notes stay in `notes` until the scan's end so a later folder can pair them, and a second pass pairs what a per-directory diff could not see (new home walked before the old one), deletes the fresh row and repoints the orphan. Ids, FTS, tags and title survive every move.
- **Link edges resolve after the walk**, from the durable `pending_links` queue. Inline per-directory resolution would miss a link to a note a later directory introduces, and would go ambiguous for a note moving into an earlier directory. Durable so a killed scan leaves its edges for the next one.

## AC

- ✅ Peak memory bounded by the largest directory/batch, not the library — measured below.
- ✅ An unchanged rescan holds no rows: 200 000-note rescan = 3.3 s, RSS delta 0 MB, no write (`onChanged` does not fire).
- ✅ Rename pairing keeps note ids across directories, both walk orders, plus folder moves; covered in `test/unit/index_reconcile_test.dart`.

## Measured

`NIMAN_FIXTURE_DIR=<tool/make_fixture.dart output> flutter test test/perf/index_scale_test.dart --plain-name "a full scan holds a directory"`:

| Notes | First scan | RSS delta | Unchanged rescan | Rescan RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 000 | 3.9 s | 7 MB | 91 ms | 0 MB |
| 50 000 | 47 s | 38 MB | 786 ms | 0 MB |
| 200 000 | 189 s | 45 MB | 3.3 s | −4 MB |

The delta the old implementation scaled linearly — a gigabyte at the million-note gate. Design record: `docs/records/index-reconcile.md`.

## Checks

- `./scripts/niman.sh check`: analyze clean, 5 494 tests passed.
- `./scripts/niman.sh integration`: app_boot passed, `sync_e2e` passed; `template_backlink` skips without the scratch library it documents.
- Beta builds: Linux bundle and Android APK both built.

body:
## Small MVP UX improvements

Closes #14.

### Conversation list
- Each row shows the last message (prefixed "Tu: " when mine), a time label (`14:32` today, `Ontem`, weekday, or date) and an unread badge
- Most recent conversation moves to the top; the web tab title shows the total unread count
- Backend: `other_users[].conversation_id` on login/session and `sender_user_id` on every `message` (taken from the connection), so the client can map conversation → user
- "Seen" is local state, separate from the read receipt

### Typing indicator
- New ephemeral `typing` WebSocket event, forwarded only to the conversation's connected devices — never queued or stored
- Sender: `true` on first keystroke, repeated at most every 3s; `false` after 3s idle, on send, on clearing the input or leaving the screen
- Receiver: three-dot bubble at the bottom of the chat and "a escrever…" in the list; expires on its own after 5s

### Editable display name
- `PATCH /users/me/display_name` (session token, trimmed, 1–80 chars); broadcasts `user_updated` to other connected devices
- New "O meu perfil" screen, opened from the settings button on the list

### Testing
- `pytest`: new `test_other_users.py`, `test_typing.py`, `test_display_name.py`
- `npm test`: new `conversationSummaries.test.ts`, `time.test.ts`, `typingSignal.test.ts`
- Manual, two tabs: unread badge and ordering, typing dots, renaming updates the other tab without refresh

---

## Pequenas melhorias de UX do MVP

Fecha a #14.

### Lista de conversas
- Cada linha mostra a última mensagem (com "Tu: " se for minha), a hora (`14:32` hoje, `Ontem`, dia da semana ou data) e o badge de não lidas
- A conversa mais recente sobe para o topo; na web, o título do separador mostra o total por ler
- Backend: `other_users[].conversation_id` no login/sessão e `sender_user_id` em cada `message` (tirado da ligação), para o cliente saber de quem é cada conversa
- "Vista" é estado local, separado do recibo de leitura

### Indicador "a escrever"
- Evento `typing` efémero no WebSocket, reencaminhado só aos devices ligados da conversa — nunca vai para a fila nem para a BD
- Quem escreve: `true` na primeira tecla, repetido no máximo a cada 3s; `false` após 3s sem teclas, ao enviar, ao apagar o texto ou ao sair do ecrã
- Quem recebe: bolha de três pontos no fundo da conversa e "a escrever…" na lista; expira sozinho ao fim de 5s

### Nome de exibição editável
- `PATCH /users/me/display_name` (token da sessão, trim, 1–80 caracteres); avisa os outros devices ligados com `user_updated`
- Ecrã novo "O meu perfil", aberto pelo botão de definições da lista

### Testes
- `pytest`: novos `test_other_users.py`, `test_typing.py`, `test_display_name.py`
- `npm test`: novos `conversationSummaries.test.ts`, `time.test.ts`, `typingSignal.test.ts`
- Manual, duas abas: badge e ordem, três pontos, mudar o nome atualiza a outra aba sem refresh

Seguinte Copilot, todo semestre do meu curso de ADS na UNIP temos que fazer um Projetor Integrado Multidisciplinar (PIM). O Projeto Integrado Multidisciplinar (PIM) é um recurso metodológico idealizado pela UNIP para promover o envolvimento de professores e estudantes na construção do trabalho em grupo e na busca da interdisciplinaridade. author: presidentaxel
body:
Décision de Louis du 2026-09-26 : pas de SMTP chez nous. Les notifications vivent dans l'app, et l'e-mail comme le SMS sont des intégrations que le gestionnaire branche lui-même.

**Notifications internes**
- `workflow/notifications.py` ne dépend plus d'un envoi : mêmes règles anti-harcèlement (un regroupement par dossier, 6 h mini, rappel à 7 jours), la notification est enregistrée et c'est tout. `workflow/emails.py` est supprimé, et les variables `SMTP_*`/`APP_BASE_URL` sortent de `.env.example`.
- Migration `e8c4f1a93b27` : colonne `lue_le`. Le rôle web peut lire la table et ne peut modifier que `lue_le` (testé en intégration, RLS comprise).
- API : `GET /dossiers/{id}/notifications` et `POST /dossiers/{id}/notifications/lues`, réservées à l'indiv.
- Frontend : une cloche dans l'en-tête de l'espace chauffeur, avec le nombre de non lues. L'ouvrir marque tout comme lu.

**Cron**
- `python -m axelcompta.taches` : pour chaque portefeuille, la synchro Digifactory (sautée si aucun dossier n'a de `contact_nr`) puis les notifications. Une synchro en échec n'empêche pas les notifications.
- `scripts/taches_planifiees.sh` : charge le `.env` s'il existe, `flock` contre les passages simultanés, écrit le journal dans `_demo_output/journaux/`. Sur le futur serveur, c'est le même script, lancé depuis un crontab ou un timer systemd.

**Vérifié**
- 419 tests unitaires, 40 tests d'intégration (Postgres local), ruff, mypy, lint-imports, eslint et tsc.
- La migration est appliquée sur la base Supabase de démo. Le cron tourne toutes les heures sur le poste de démo : un premier passage a créé la notification de Sophie, le second n'a pas créé de doublon.
- Les routes ont été testées en réel avec un compte Supabase jetable (liste, 403 sur un autre dossier, marquage lu), supprimé ensuite. La cloche n'a pas été vérifiée dans le navigateur.

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches auth/RLS sur `notifications_envoyees`, le parcours chauffeur et un job horaire qui appelle Digifactory ; le changement de canal est produit mais la surface API + cron augmente le risque opérationnel.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Les alertes « opérations à confirmer » passent de l'e-mail à la cloche in-app**, avec un cron qui enchaîne synchro Digifactory et notifications.
> 
> Le canal SMTP est retiré (`workflow/emails.py`, variables `SMTP_*` / `APP_BASE_URL`) : `notifier_a_trancher` **enregistre** une notification en base avec les mêmes garde-fous (regroupement par dossier, 6 h, rappel 7 jours), sans filtrer sur un compte activé ni envoyer de courriel. Migration **`lue_le`** + droits RLS pour que le rôle web ne modifie que l'état lu.
> 
> **API chauffeur** : `GET/POST …/notifications` (liste + marquer lues). **Front** : composant **Cloche** dans le layout chauffeur (badge, ouverture = lu).
> 
> **Planification** : nouveau `python -m axelcompta.taches` (tous les portefeuilles via `lister_tenants`, synchro sautée sans `contact_nr`, notifications même si synchro en échec) et `scripts/taches_planifiees.sh` (`flock`, logs). Refactors partagés : `synchroniser_portefeuille`, `notifier_depuis_base`.

## 요약

[#186](https://github.com/airmang/python-hwpx/pull/186) 리뷰에서 머지 전에 고쳐야 한다고 적은 문제와 제안을 고칩니다. #186은 이 수정보다 먼저 main에 머지되었습니다.

1. 번호를 다시 매길 때 구역마다 매니페스트를 처음부터 훑어서, `add_section`·`remove_section`의 시간이 구역 수의 제곱 이상으로 늘었습니다.
   - 이제 항목과 spine itemref의 표를 한 번 만들고, 항목과 itemref를 id가 아니라 요소로 짝짓습니다.
   - 구역 60개 문서에서 `add_section()` 59번이 이 환경에서 0.4초, `remove_section(0)` 10번이 0.1초입니다.
2. 구역 파트 이름에 번호가 없는 패키지(`Contents/section.xml`, id `section0`)에서 `add_section()`을 하면 새 구역도 id `section0`을 받았습니다. 그래서 저장한 순서가 뒤집혔습니다.
   - 이제 새 구역의 id와 파트 이름은 구역 파트나 매니페스트 항목이 쓰는 번호를 피합니다.
3. (제안) 문서를 저장할 때도 번호를 다시 매기고, id가 바뀔 때만 매니페스트를 저장합니다.
   - 그래서 id가 어긋난 채 저장된 파일(`section1`, `section2`)도 편집 없이 다시 저장하면 바로잡힙니다. 번호가 이미 맞으면 `content.hpf`는 그대로입니다.

- `src/hwpx/oxml/section_layout.py`: `number_section_ids`, `new_section_names`. `document_parts.py`가 줄 수 상한에 가까워서, `add_section`의 다른 도우미가 있는 이 모듈에 두었습니다. `module-ownership.json`의 설명도 고쳤습니다.
- `src/hwpx/oxml/document_parts.py`: `add_section`·`remove_section`·`serialize`가 위 도우미를 부릅니다. `_number_section_ids`는 지웠습니다.
- `tests/test_section_ids_order.py`: 번호 없는 파트 이름 패키지에 구역을 더해도 순서가 지켜지는지(`.hwp` 포함), 어긋난 id가 다시 저장하면 바로잡히는지, 맞는 id면 매니페스트가 그대로인지.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: #186 항목에 덧붙임.

## 검증

- 다섯 후속 PR(표 조작, 셀 필드, 메일 머지 글상자, 목록 라벨, 구역 id)을 main에 함께 얹은 트리에서 전체 테스트를 돌렸습니다: 3,727개 통과, 14개 건너뜀, xfail 1. 실패는 main에서도 이 개발 환경에서 똑같이 실패하는 테스트뿐입니다(심볼릭 링크, 배포 산출물 위생 검사, 줄끝(CRLF)에 기대는 문서 해시 검사, 콘솔 인코딩처럼 환경에 기대는 것).

author: paulmorrisdev
body:
Two changes that both came from running ClaudeGlass on real Claude Code 2.1.283 transcripts. They share the parser bump (`PARSER_VERSION` 26), so they land together.

## Fix: a session started with `/clear` was priced twice

After `/clear` in a web or mobile session, Claude Code writes the new session's lines to its own log, and **also** into the earlier session's log, keeping the new session's `sessionId` (same uuids, same message ids). The parser only removed repeats within one file, so every reply in the new session was priced in both logs.

- On one real pair this was 5.7% of total spend. After the fix, the earlier session comes within 0.5% of Claude Code's own `cost-state` total ($48.65 against $48.89), and every reply across the corpus is distinct.
- `parse.py`: a top-level transcript skips a line whose `sessionId` names another session **when that session's own `<id>.jsonl` sits beside it**. It counts those lines in `Diagnostics.copied_lines` ("Lines copied from another session" on Data quality).
- The guard matters: 11 of the 16 top-level fixtures carry a `sessionId` that isn't their file name, and a copy whose original is gone is the only record. Both cases are still counted. Ids outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` are never looked up, so there's no path traversal.
- **Known limitation:** the skip decision is cached with the digest. Claude Code's cleanup can delete the new session's own log while the earlier log lives on. If the earlier log then changes, it is re-read and the copy counted again, while the dashboard store still holds the deleted session. This needs both a deleted session and a later change to the copy-holder, so it's rare.

## Feature: what MCP tool search saves

Claude Code sends deferred tools by name only and loads a full definition when Claude calls `ToolSearch`. The transcripts record both: `deferred_tools_delta` (names added or removed) and `deferred_tools_record` (full definitions loaded).

- `parse.py` keeps `Turn.deferred_tools_by_server` (tools listed by name only when the reply was requested, by MCP server or `built-in`), `Turn.deferred_list_chars` and `TranscriptResult.tool_definition_chars` (the size of each loaded definition). It never keeps a description or schema, and drops names outside the API's tool-name alphabet (SECURITY.md updated).
- `tool_search.py`:
  - An unloaded tool is sized at its server's average loaded definition, or every server's average when none of its own was loaded.
  - It is priced at the reply's own front-of-prompt rate: cache read, or cache write on a full rebuild, else input.
  - The name list, and every reply that only called `ToolSearch`, are taken off.
  - Nothing is priced when no definition was loaded.
- Surfaces:
  - the `tool_search` section, on Agents & context › Context;
  - a new check, `claudeglass check tool-search`, which also appears in the Overview checklist;
  - `docs/tool-search.md`, and entries in the sections reference, ui, cli, api, README, savers and CHANGELOG.
- On the real sessions: up to 154 deferred tools (122 MCP), about **57,500 tokens kept out of each reply**, $6.77 saved, less $0.16 for the name list and $1.03 for 16 search-only replies, **$5.58 net**. By server: GitHub $2.20, Microsoft 365 $2.19, Claude Code's own tools $1.82, Google Drive $0.48, Claude Docs $0.08.

Third-party "saver" MCP servers (`savers.py`) are still switched off; that needs a with-and-without comparison, which is a separate change.

## Testing

- `pytest -q`: 10,715 passed, 7 skipped (was 10,588).
- New `tests/test_copied_sessions.py` (7 tests) and `tests/test_tool_search.py` (11 tests).
- Ran `check`, `check tool-search` and the dashboard (`serve`, headless Chromium at 1280px) against the real transcripts. The section, the Overview checklist row and the check page render, with no page errors.

author: sacrefizz
body:
Scenario files come from contributors, and `load_scenario` is the first code that reads them: any malformed input must be rejected with a clean `ValueError`.

**Fix (found by the fuzzer within seconds):** a check whose `step` or `type` is a list raised `TypeError` (unhashable). Step ids, tools and batch names must now be strings, as `docs/scenario-format.md` documents, and the name patterns are exact matches (`^…$` with `match()` accepted a trailing newline). All public scenarios and the self-test still validate.

**Fuzzing:**
- `fuzz/fuzz_load_scenario.py` (atheris): arbitrary bytes into `load_scenario`; only `ValueError` and `RecursionError` (raised by `json` on deep nesting) are accepted; seed corpus = the public scenarios; dictionary of JSON tokens and scenario keys.
- ClusterFuzzLite (`.clusterfuzzlite/`, workflow `fuzz`): 5 minutes on pull requests that touch the validator, 30 minutes every week; crashes go to code scanning. Build image pinned by digest (watched by Dependabot), actions pinned by SHA.
- Local run before this PR: 3 × 3 minutes, about 80 million inputs, no crash after the fix.

  - On phones it shows Prev / "Page 3 of 42" / Next.
  - With All, only the size picker shows, and each list keeps its "Load more" (History and Tracks) or shows its whole list (Playlists).

**Routes**
- Every list takes `?page=&size=`. The stored size (`rc:page-size:<list>`, default 20) applies when the URL has none.
- History and Tracks use either the infinite query or the paged query, depending on size. The loader fills whichever one is active.
- A page past the end is clamped with `replace`.
- Changing the size keeps the first visible row (`resizedPage`).
- Playlists and playlist detail page on the client, since those endpoints already return everything. The playlist sort moves into the URL.
- A new sort or filter goes back to page 1.

**Selection across pages**
- Picks are stored in a `Map` when toggled. Before, they were rebuilt from the rows on screen, so paging away dropped them.
- History still orders picked tracks newest first, and Tracks keeps them in list order.

**History extras**
- `olderPlayedAt` keeps gap markers across page edges.
- Now Playing shows on page 1 only.

**Tests**
- `ListPagination` stories: first and middle pages, one page, All, picking a size, phone.
- App stories: `TracksPages`, `TracksPageSize` (keeps the first row, remembers the size, All brings back "Load more"), `TracksPagesOnPhone`, `TracksSelectAcrossPages`, `HistoryPages` and `PlaylistPages`. `TracksLoadsMore` now runs at `?size=all`.
- MSW default handlers honour `limit`/`offset` through a `pageBy` helper.

## What does this PR do?

Implements roadmap item **#25 — Secure-field ask** (Phase 6, `apps/desktop/docs/agentic-desktop-roadmap.md`).

When the agent requests a secret mid-turn (the `secret` server request — e.g. a skill's required env var), the desktop now renders a **masked input row at the transcript tail**, parked on the session that raised it (same seam as the approval stack), instead of only a modal dialog. The value still only leaves via the request reply frame — the backend writes it to the profile's secrets/.env and it never enters the conversation context.

## Related Issue

Roadmap #25 (secure-field ask) — `apps/desktop/docs/agentic-desktop-roadmap.md`

- `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/tool/secret-request.tsx` (new): `PendingSecretCard` — session-scoped masked input row at the transcript tail. Reads the existing `sessionSecretRequest` keyed store; answers via `respondToServerRequest(requestId, { value })`; Skip sends `""`. No `autoFocus` — the card can land mid-typing and focus-steal is banned.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread/list.tsx`: mounts `PendingSecretCard` next to `PendingApprovalStack`.

author: wmurley
body:
## What this does

At the start of a new conversation, the workbench checks whether a connected program (The Lab, Workforce) or the template has something new, and the agent says so in one line. Until now that only happened in **Claude Code**. The template shipped the Claude wiring, and `aibl-update` said the Claude hook "does not establish a Codex session-start hook."

Codex supports the same thing: a project `SessionStart` hook in `.codex/hooks.json`, which takes the same output format the script already prints. So this adds **only the Codex wiring**. `update-check.mjs` is unchanged.

- `.codex/hooks.json`: runs `node .claude/hooks/update-check.mjs` at session start. It has no matcher, because the script itself keeps to new conversations (startup and clear, not resume or compaction).
- `aibl-update` step 3: `.codex/hooks.json` is handled like `.claude/settings.json`. The template copy is offered on a yes; an existing file is left alone except for a missing entry. It also tells the student that Codex asks them once to trust the hook, and never trusts it for them.
- README: the check runs in both apps, and Codex asks once.
- `tests/codex_hook.py` pins the wiring.

## Proven with a real Codex run (0.156.1, Windows, 09-26)

The test workbench was built from this branch and joined to the real `aibuild-lab/the-lab`, one edition behind.

1. **Interactive**, after a one-time trust, the first reply said: *"The Lab has a new edition with updated Orientation Day and GitHub Masterclass; aibl-update can show you the changes before merging them."*
2. **Headless** `codex exec` logged `hook: SessionStart` then `hook: SessionStart Completed`, and repeated: *"AIBL workbench update check, nothing was changed: The Lab has 1 new edition (what the team published: "The Lab: updated Orientation Day, GitHub Masterclass")."*
3. Simulated calls: the same conversation twice stays silent, a resume stays silent, and the PowerShell launch (how Codex runs hooks on Windows) works.

`transition.py`, `update-skill-choice.sh` and `codex_hook.py` pass.

## For members

- **New workbenches** get this automatically. Codex asks once to trust the hook.
- **Existing workbenches** get it offered through `aibl-update`.

author: jan-kubica
body:
Stacked on #3676.

## Summary

- Moves the certificate rules the signing picker uses (key type, validity, key usages, issuer) into a shared crate, so every platform filters the same way.
- Adds a Windows signer over the current user's certificate store. Listing opens keys silently and never prompts; signing lets the key's provider ask for a PIN, over the signing dialog.
- The dialog names the Windows certificate store in its wording, and the unsupported-platform message now names both platforms.

## Testing

- Shared rules and the macOS signer: existing tests, now run from the shared crate. There is also a new check that a converted ECDSA signature verifies with an independent verifier.
- Windows: CI installs throwaway certificates in the runner's store, one for each case: RSA, ECDSA, expired, login-only, and no private key. It checks that the listing offers exactly the signable ones and that each signature verifies against its certificate. A certificate with no key fails with a clear error. The certificates are removed afterwards.

## Known limit

Hardware tokens and smart cards are exercised through the operating system's certificate store, not on a physical card in CI.

author: timesselens
body:
## Summary

The reverse pass replays each loop from its limit, but the min-cut that decides what the forward pass keeps no longer seems to take that into account. Since #2089 it runs before any loop context exists, so the code that marks the values of the loop limits as needed (c5c13de6) sees no loops. When an inner loop's bounds are loaded from a stack slot that the outer loop rewrites, the forward pass caches only the exit branch, and differentiation fails with "Illegal replace ficticious phi". This PR proposes computing, for loops without a context, the values their limit will be expanded from, so that the min-cut keeps them.

## Before / after

Both bounds of an inner loop are loaded from a slot the outer loop rewrites, and the function is differentiated in split mode (`test/Enzyme/ReverseMode/looplimit-overwritten-slot.ll`, abridged):

```llvm
define void @kern(ptr %x, ptr %out, i64 %n) {
entry:
  %slot = alloca [2 x i64], align 8
  %hi.ptr = getelementptr inbounds i64, ptr %slot, i64 1
  %x0 = load double, ptr %x, align 8
  br label %outer
outer:
  %k = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %knext, %latch ]
  store i64 %k, ptr %slot, align 8
  %k2 = shl i64 %k, 1
  store i64 %k2, ptr %hi.ptr, align 8
  %lo = load i64, ptr %slot, align 8
  %hi = load i64, ptr %hi.ptr, align 8
  br label %inner
inner:                                   ; out[k] += x[0] * (hi - lo + 1)
  %j = phi i64 [ %lo, %outer ], [ %jnext, %inner ]
  ...
}
; @outer calls @kern(x + i, out, n) for i = 0, 1
```

```
$ opt -load-pass-plugin=LLVMEnzyme-16.dylib -passes=enzyme -enzyme-preopt=false -S looplimit-overwritten-slot.ll
main:    error: … Enzyme: Illegal replace ficticious phi for:
           %malloccall_replacementA = phi ptr  of  %malloccall = … @malloc(i64 16), !enzyme_fromstack
this PR: differentiates; the lli run prints dx0=6.000000 dx1=6.000000 dx2=0.000000 (1 + 2 + 3 inner iterations per call)
```

Julia code gets such a slot whenever a tuple is indexed at a run-time position inside a loop nest. This is reduced from the multigrid restriction of the CFD solver WaterLily.jl (Enzyme.jl 0.13.204):

```julia
using Enzyme
function f!(a, i, b)
    for I ∈ CartesianIndices(map(n -> 2:n-1, Base.front(size(a))))
        s = zero(eltype(b))
        for J ∈ CartesianIndices(ntuple(j -> j == i ? (2I.I[i]-2:2I.I[i]-2) : (I.I[j]:I.I[j]), 3))
            s += @inbounds b[J, i]
        end
        @inbounds a[I, i] = s
    end
end
g!(a, b) = (for i ∈ 1:3; f!(a, i, b); end; nothing)   # f! in a loop: split mode
a = zeros(6, 6, 6, 3); b = rand(12, 12, 12, 3); db = zero(b)
autodiff(Reverse, g!, Const, Duplicated(a, ones(size(a))), Duplicated(b, db))
# main: EnzymeInternalError … Illegal replace ficticious phi; this PR: sum(db) == 192
```

## Likely cause

- The reverse pass replays the inner loop `limit + 1` times. `CacheUtility::getContext` computes the limit with scalar evolution (`hi - lo` here) and expands it in the preheader, so the reverse function needs `lo` and `hi`.
- `computeMinCache` is meant to mark those values as needed (`NewLoopBoundReq`, from c5c13de6), but it takes them from `loopContexts`. Since #2089, `computeMinCache` runs before `forceAugmentedReturns` (because `getContext` may itself create caches), so `loopContexts` is empty at that point and no loop bound is ever required.
- The min-cut then sees only the exit branch as needed. `lo` and `hi` can't be recomputed (the slot is overwritten), so it caches the branch condition. In the reverse function nothing requires `lo` and `hi` any more, the slot is not rematerialized, and the expansion of the trip count reads a placeholder, which `eraseFictiousPHIs` reports.

## Proposed change

For each loop that has no context yet, `computeMinCache` computes the scalar evolution of its limit the way `getContext` will, and adds the values the expansion will use to the loop bound requirements:

```cpp
      for (Loop *L : LI.getLoopsInPreorder()) {
        if (loopContexts.count(L) || !L->getLoopPreheader())
          continue;
        const SCEV *Limit, *MaxIterations;
        computeLoopLimits(L, Limit, MaxIterations);
        if (Limit == SE.getCouldNotCompute())
          continue;
        // stop at an instruction that already computes (a part of) the limit where the expander would
        // reuse it (same criteria as SCEVExpander::FindValueInExprValueMap), else take the unknowns
        struct FindLimitValues { ... } Finder{*this, L->getLoopPreheader()->getTerminator(),
                                               LoopBoundRequirements};
        visitAll(Limit, Finder);
      }
```

The limit computation moves out of `getContext` into `CacheUtility::computeLoopLimits` unchanged, so both use the same code. The only textual difference is that it reads `L->getHeader()` where it read `loopContexts[L].header`, which `getContext` sets to `L->getHeader()` first. In this example the forward pass then tapes `lo` and `hi` (one value each per outer iteration) and recomputes the exit branch from them.

Alternatives tried:
- Requiring only the unknowns of the limit expression. That also handles the reproducers, but it changes what `krc_loop2.ll` and `loadisload.ll` cache (equivalent programs, different CHECK lines).
- Expanding the limit with a temporary `SCEVExpander` and removing it with `SCEVExpanderCleaner`. The cleanup leaves `SCEVUnknown`s of removed instructions in scalar evolution, and `usedinlastiter.ll` then allocates a cache of size `poison`.
- Creating the loop contexts before `computeMinCache`, which #2089 explains is not possible.

## Tests

New `test/Enzyme/ReverseMode/looplimit-overwritten-slot.ll` (opaque pointers, `%OPnewLoadEnzyme`, LLVM 15 and later): the function above, with a `main` that runs the gradient under `lli`. It fails on `main` with the error above.

```
llvm-lit -v build/test/Enzyme/ReverseMode/looplimit-overwritten-slot.ll
```

## Open questions

- The reuse check mirrors `SCEVExpander::FindValueInExprValueMap` (same type, dominates the preheader, not in a loop that excludes it) without its poison-flag check. If the expander declines such a value, it expands it from its operands, which the forward pass can recompute or has cached as the value's own inputs. Would that be acceptable, or would you prefer the exact check?
- Only the exact `Limit` is used; `MaxIterations` is only expanded under the hidden `-enzyme-max-cache` for dynamic loops. Should that path get the same treatment?

## Related

- #2089 moved `computeMinCache` before `forceAugmentedReturns` (its `krc_loop2.ll` still passes unchanged), and c5c13de6 added the loop bound requirements that this PR tries to make effective again.
- #3114 (open) makes unwrap lookups that fail rebuild uncacheable values, in the same lookup path. It does not seem to cover this case: with #3114 applied to `main` the new test still fails with the same error, and with both applied both tests pass. The two merge cleanly.
- #2925 (open, `legalRecompute` of a fictitious phi) and #3075 (open, a loopy reduction's start value) touch the same decisions; neither changes this reproducer's result, and both merge cleanly. #3214 (open) is #3075's sibling; #2827 (merged) and #3242 (merged) addressed other failures in the same area.
- Earlier Enzyme.jl reports of the same message, closed: EnzymeAD/Enzyme.jl#3065, EnzymeAD/Enzyme.jl#2580, EnzymeAD/Enzyme.jl#2369.

<details><summary>Verification</summary>

- lit (`check-enzyme`, `check-typeanalysis`, `check-activityanalysis`), macOS aarch64, LLVM from `LLVM_full_jll`, libEnzyme with assertions:

  | LLVM | `main` b85d5011 | this PR | this PR + #3114 (on dea2b4e6) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 15.0.7 | 1184 passed, 11 expectedly failed | 1185 passed, 11 expectedly failed | |
  | 16.0.6 | 1184 passed, 11 expectedly failed | 1185 passed, 11 expectedly failed | 1182 passed, 11 expectedly failed |

  No existing test changes its result. The new test also fails on `main` and passes with this PR on LLVM 18.1.7.

## What
Engine half of UP-4986 (D-14). Adds Vertex AI Agent Engine as a discovery connector on the D-13 framework, driven by a Discovery Source Config instead of engine environment variables. The Platform half (the `gcp_vertex` source type) is a separate change in the Platform repo.

**ml-engine**
- New `discovery/cloud/gcp_vertex/scanner.py`, registered as `SOURCE_SCANNERS["gcp_vertex"]`; lists agent engines via `vertexai.Client(...).agent_engines.list()` (google-cloud-aiplatform, already a dependency).
- Each record sets `external_id` **and** `service_names=[...]` to Google's `api_resource.name`, copied verbatim (Google returns the project-number form). The legacy poller mapped exactly that string as a SERVICE_NAME, so resolver rung 3 joins existing Vertex tasks instead of duplicating them. `name` = display name; `last_seen` = `update_time` (fallback `create_time`); `runs_on` = GCP; address = configured project id, region parsed from the name, engine id. `lookback_hours` is ignored (inventory).
- Credentials: only `service_account.Credentials.from_service_account_info` with the cloud-platform scope; non-`service_account` JSON types are rejected (external-account configs can point at local executables/files); parse errors never include key content. With no key, ADC is used only when `ARTHUR_ENGINE_GCP_VERTEX_ALLOW_ADC=true` (default off).

**genai-engine (legacy shim; nothing deleted)**
- `GENAI_ENGINE_LEGACY_GCP_DISCOVERY_ENABLED` (default true) disables only `_discover_gcp_agents`; trace fetching is untouched.
- Legacy discovery now skips engines whose resource name is already mapped (SERVICE_NAME or EXTERNAL_ID). This fixes a duplicate: `find_by_gcp_engine_id` could not see CLOUD-type tasks created by the connector, so running both paths would create a second task for each newly deployed agent.

## Tests
- `test_gcp_vertex_scanner.py`: 30 passed (including verbatim `external_id`/`service_names` with a project number that differs from the project id). Full ml-engine unit suite passed locally; mypy clean.
- genai-engine poller + resolver tests: 49 passed, including a test that builds a task exactly as the legacy poller does and then resolves a scanner-shaped record: the first scan joins by service name, a rescan by external_id, and the task count is unchanged.
- Verified locally against a real GCP project with two deployed agent engines: both emitted and passed the output-column check.

## Known gap before retiring the legacy path
Legacy trace fetch (`_poll_all_gcp_tasks`) only polls tasks whose creation source is `GCP`, in the `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` project/region. Connector-created tasks are `CLOUD`/`gcp_vertex`, so newly deployed agents found by the new path get no traces until trace fetch becomes source-driven. Follow-up proposed: retire legacy discovery and make GCP trace fetch source-driven.

## Open questions
1. Service-account key vs Workload Identity for customer data planes?
2. Which deployments run legacy Vertex discovery today, so the no-regression check uses their real data before the legacy path is disabled?
3. Ship the `gcp_vertex` source type as PREVIEW until the legacy path is removed?

body:
## Summary

**What changed** (1 commit, `74e2fe0`, never pushed; tree clean): both blocking findings named one pattern — the probe restore not guaranteeing branch-head-and-clean — with a single instance in the diff, the `finally` block in `target_fails` ([run.py](/home/dillonhoppe/.agentkit/wt/20260926-1625-agentkit-a-landing-check-that-fails-on-t/agentkit/run.py:4324)). Fixed there:

- Droppings are now dropped *before* the checkout back (`reset --hard`, then `clean` of paths new since the probe, then checkout branch/head), so a probe-created file the branch tracks can no longer refuse the checkout and strand the worktree detached at the tip.
- Each restore half runs even when the other stops: `Stopped` is caught per half and re-raised at the end, so a killed git no longer abandons the remaining steps, and the stop still ends the run after the best-effort restore.
- A `checkout --detach` that dies mid-apply now marks the worktree detached and restores instead of propagating with nothing put back.
- A worktree that still is not back on the head and clean after restore logs a `WARN` naming the commit, following `abort_stopped_integration`'s never-claim-clean precedent, instead of failing silently under `check=False`.
- Two regression tests in `tests/test_red_target.py` (now 6 tests): probe droppings colliding with a branch-tracked file still restore the branch exactly with the file intact; a `Stopped` mid-restore still attempts the checkout back, still raises, and leaves the branch back on its head clean. The non-blocking follow-ups were left as is.

**How verified:** the new collision test fails on the old restore order (HEAD left detached at the tip) and passes on the new one; all done-when commands exit 0 on the committed tree (compile, `def test_` count, `test_red_target` 6 OK, `test_deferred_checks` 4 OK + `test_repo_suite` 6 OK). Also re-ran green: `test_v5af` (7, exercises the real probe end-to-end), `test_merge_turn` (8), `test_merge_step` (17), `test_docs` (7). Smoke deferred to the loop by design.

**Open issues:** none new. The review's non-blocking follow-ups (skipped probe on dirty trees, unprobed `resume_review`/`fix_after_failed_review` re-checks, killed-command probes, live vs pinned tip, pre-existing untracked clobbering, `resolve_conflicts` probe coverage) remain as future work.

---

- verdict: PASS
- rounds: 2 of 3
- executor: spark, reviewer: mimo
- run: 20260926-1625-agentkit-a-landing-check-that-fails-on-t

## Follow-ups

- `agentkit/run.py:4302 - the probe is still skipped whenever the tree carries tracked changes - a landing check that failed on a red target alongside a tracked-regenerating command still spends its fixer rounds: the task's park is missed exactly then.`
- `agentkit/run.py:3794 - the integration re-check run inside resume_review (also run.py:3840 and fix_after_failed_review's at run.py:3599) is never probed - a red target there goes to a review and then fixer rounds with re-reviews each and can end handed back instead of parked: the same waste the task removes.`
- `agentkit/run.py:4328 - a probe killed by the silence window counts as "the target fails", and failing_checks counts [killed at the limit] and [not run: ...] records as failures - a command that hangs everywhere or the gate never ran parks with "<target> itself fails", waiting for a target move that cannot fix a hang.`
- `agentkit/run.py:4296 - the probe re-resolves upstream live while resolve_conflicts/integrate park on the pinned tip (run.py:3667-3669, 3827-3830) and their docstrings promise every check uses tip - a done-when command that fetches makes the probe judge and the park record different commits.`
- `agentkit/run.py:4340 - pre-existing untracked paths the probe deletes or overwrites are never restored (only paths new since the probe are dropped) - the probe can silently eat droppings the failing check left as evidence.`
- `agentkit/run.py:4314 - a checkout --detach that exits non-zero mid-apply (a fatal after partial application, e.g. an index write failure) is still read as "the tree is alone": detached stays False, nothing restores and no WARN names it - unlike the Stopped case just below it.`
- `agentkit/run.py:4288 - the docstring still promises a stop propagates "after the worktree is put back on the branch head, clean" while the code now deliberately promises only best-effort with a WARN (4334-4336) - one sentence whose truth the fix changed.`
- `tests/test_red_target.py:1 - no test covers the resolve_conflicts re-test probe (run.py:3667), the third call site - it can regress unnoticed.`
- `tests/test_red_target.py:28 - "for cwd in (owner,):" is a one-element loop left from a two-clone form - it reads like an editing mistake.`

body:
## Code submission

- Parameters: [[n, k, d]] = [[32,10,4]]
- Tracks: local-2d-bilayer / weight-6 (computed by the verifier from H and the layout: two qubits on each site of the 4x4 integer grid, layers 2, interaction radius 4.24, max check weight 6; the code also nests into the unrestricted and heavier-weight cells)
- Distance confidence: X: upper_bound, Z: upper_bound

Family tag: local-sat-css (a self-declared filter, never used for ranking).

### Checklist

- [x] One JSON file under `codes/`, conforming to `schema/code.schema.json`
- [x] Distance witness(es) included for each reported side
- [x] `python verify/qldpc_verify.py codes/32-10-4.json` passes locally
- [x] Construction and references filled in under `provenance`
- [x] If this may be equivalent to an existing entry, noted in `provenance.notes` (the validator's dedup found no exact or WL-equivalent board entry; the literature check has not been run)

### What frontier does this advance?

- local-2d-bilayer / weight <= 6: on the Pareto frontier against origin/main under the cell rule (n down, k up, d up, check weight down); `verify/validate_candidate.py` run against that tree reports passed, not refuted, no duplicate, and board_advancing true. The d >= 4 weight-6 entries of this cell at n <= 32 were [[30,8,4]] (one layer), [[25,7,4]], [[24,6,4]] (two layers), [[18,4,4]], and [[16,4,4]]; the best k at d = 4 was 8. This code raises it to 10 with every check of weight exactly 6.
- It does not change the cell's kd^2/n headline.

Score kd^2/n = 5.0, max check weight 6, locality class local-2d-bilayer (two qubits per site, measured interaction radius 4.24 within the 7.0 cap).

Distance evidence: d = 4 exactly. The CNF requires a nonzero syndrome for every Pauli error of weight at most 3, and the model passed the post-check for weight <= 3 stabilizers; an exhaustive enumeration after staging of every X-type and every Z-type error of weight at most 3 (5,488 supports per side, plain GF(2) arithmetic) found none with zero syndrome, so d >= 4 independently of the SAT encoding. The RIS search in `research/kit/submit.make_submission` at 20,000 trials per side found weight-4 logicals on both sides, which are the embedded witnesses, and the validator's refutation found nothing lighter in 3,780 trials. The file carries confidence upper_bound as the kit labels it.

Construction: bilayer 2D-local SAT search with `research/local_sat.py` build_local_cnf over a site list in which every point of the 4x4 grid appears twice (n = 32, layers = 2; the one-line `layers` extension of the single-layer encoder), G=11 checks per side, max_weight=6, t=3 detection, anchor radius 3.5 (check diameter at most 7.0), shared_t3 encoding, CaDiCaL 1.9.5 via python-sat, 20,000,000 conflicts per solve and a 6 h wall cap per solve; first model after 481.4 s and 529,455 conflicts, ten models in 1133.4 s, all [[32,10,4]]. Model 0 of the enumeration is the submitted code. The rung below, G=10 (k >= 12), exhausted its 20,000,000-conflict budget in 13,056 s with no model and no UNSAT proof; G=9 lies below the column-count bound. Check weights: X-rows eleven of weight 6; Z-rows eleven of weight 6. The per-instance driver and scheduler are not part of this repo; the note gives the equivalent `build_local_cnf` plus CaDiCaL call, and CaDiCaL is deterministic for a fixed clause order, so the first model reproduces.

Research note: `notes/32-10-4.md`

Related: the bilayer extension (Phase 2) of issue #2024, after its single-layer Phases 0 and 1 (#2115 to #2120, #2179, #2185, #2186, #2187, #2192, #2201) and beside #2209, #2210, #2211, and #2217.

author: tomconder
body:
The asset converter now gives glTF models the tangents that the glTF spec asks for. It reads the tangents stored in the file, and when a file has none, it computes MikkTSpace tangents with meshoptimizer. Before, it always replaced the stored tangents with its own per-vertex tangents, and those tangents don't match the space normal maps are usually baked in. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[glTF primitive] --> B{has TANGENT and NORMAL?} B -- yes --> C[use stored tangents] B -- no --> D["meshopt_generateTangents
(MikkTSpace mode)"] D --> E[one vertex per corner] C --> F[optimizeMesh welds vertices] E --> F ``` Changes: - `vcpkg.json`: move the baseline to the current registry, and raise the minimum versions of harfbuzz (14.5.0), meshoptimizer (1.3) and shader-slang (2026.18.2). - `gltfimport.cpp`: read the `TANGENT` attribute and transform it by the node matrix. Compute tangents only when the primitive has no tangents or no normals. - `tangents.cpp`: replace the Lengyel tangent code with `meshopt_generateTangents(..., meshopt_TangentCompatible)`. The function returns one tangent per triangle corner, so `computeTangents` unwelds the mesh, and `optimizeMesh` welds it again. - `objimport.cpp`: normalize OBJ normals, because the tangent generator needs unit normals. - `gltfimport.cpp`: print a warning when a primitive has no normals, because the generated normals are wrong on vertices that several triangles share. Effect on the shipped models: | Model | Tangents before | Tangents after | |---|---|---| | Sponza | computed, stored tangents ignored | stored tangents in 102 of 103 primitives | | DamagedHelmet | Lengyel, averaged per vertex | MikkTSpace | | Cube | Lengyel, averaged per vertex | MikkTSpace | Vertex counts don't change for the helmet or the cube. Sponza gains 17 vertices, where the stored tangents keep vertices apart that the weld used to merge. Known limits: - A node with a mirroring transform (negative scale) should flip the tangent sign. The importer doesn't flip it, and it doesn't flip the triangle winding either, so mirrored nodes were already wrong. No shipped model has one. - An OBJ normal of length zero becomes NaN after normalizing.

author: noctem-o
body:
## Summary
This change introduces support for "host facets" in the session worker architecture—trusted application-level facets that persist across plugin reloads and are never replaced by reloadable plugins. This enables the application to provide stable, privileged services (like inspection APIs) to the worker while maintaining a clear separation from reloadable plugin facets.

## Key Changes

- **Host facets concept**: Added `hostFacets` parameter to `createSessionWorkerServices()` and `SessionWorkerRuntime` to allow the application to provide trusted facets that:
  - Share the host lifetime and are never disposed during plugin reloads
  - Cannot be replaced or shadowed by reloadable plugins
  - Receive full capabilities (unlike plugins which get only Chord's facet API)

- **Plugin reload validation**: Enhanced the plugin reload mechanism to reject any reload attempt that would introduce a facet with an ID matching a host facet, throwing an error: "Session plugin reload cannot replace facet {id}"

- **Test coverage**: 
  - Added comprehensive tests in `experimental-plugin-reload.test.ts` validating host facet lifecycle and reload protection
  - Added new test file `session-host.test.ts` demonstrating the Endophasia Inspector as a host facet, including:
    - Verification that host facets persist across plugin reloads
    - Confirmation that plugins receive only Chord's facet API
    - Validation that the host provider continues serving the same instance after reloads

- **Refactoring**: Extracted a `fakeLane()` helper function to reduce duplication in plugin reload tests

## Implementation Details

The host facets are loaded into the facet host separately from plugin facets, ensuring they are established before any plugin loading occurs. During plugin reloads, the system validates that no plugin facet attempts to claim a host facet's ID, maintaining the integrity of the host-provided services.

body:
This resolves PR #206 against the current base branch without regressing the existing accountability hardening. It preserves the task-record expansion from the PR and adds a bounded, repository-controlled intelligence/value evaluation model with explicit provenance and evidence boundaries.

- **Merge resolution**
  - Forward-merged the founder task-record system onto the current base.
  - Preserved newer safeguards already on base:
    - protected accountability writes
    - strict `humanConfirmed` typing
    - separation of recorded outcome vs. current evidence-backed completion

- **Ledger model**
  - Added structured directive-level fields for:
    - `intelligenceEvaluation`
    - `valueAssessment`
  - `intelligenceEvaluation` now captures:
    - directive adherence / scope control
    - accuracy / truthfulness
    - verification quality
    - contribution value classification
    - decision-making quality
    - provenance / attribution integrity
  - `valueAssessment` now captures:
    - creator/claimant value
    - technical value
    - evaluated contribution value
    - estimated vs. validated value
    - decision / reasoning / recommendation quality
    - founder confirmation state
    - external review state

- **Truthfulness and evidence handling**
  - Kept `verified_success` dependent on explicit human confirmation plus already-verified evidence.
  - If supporting evidence later becomes disputed or no longer qualifies, the historical outcome remains recorded, while current projected status/evidence-backed completion downgrades accordingly.
  - Tightened same-day Task-ID generation to derive from the maximum existing daily sequence rather than event iteration order.

- **Attribution and provenance boundaries**

author: benmsanderson
body:
Three commits: region averaging that follows the AR6 Atlas, a record of the forty-model training run (including a draft issue for METEOR), and a fix for this PR's own first CI failure.

## 1. Land regions over land (`398cdb2`)
Until now every AR6 region was averaged over every grid box inside its polygon, land or sea, and each city was its nearest grid box. The AR6 WGI Atlas averages land regions over land: land fraction > 0.5, cos-latitude weights (`IPCC-WG1/Atlas`, `calculate_regional_means.R`).

**Does it matter?** Measured on six models' own ssp245 output, the difference in 2015–2034 to 2081–2100 warming has a median of 0.07 °C, but reaches 0.6 °C on coasts: NEU, RAR, northern and southern Australia.

**Decided:**
- **AR6 land regions:** land grid boxes only.
- **Ocean regions, and the mixed MED, CAR and SEA:** every grid box. Sea-only differs by at most 0.02 °C, and CAR is 3% land.
- **Cities:** the nearest grid box that's more than half land.
- **Drawn regions:** over land by default, with a *Land only* switch. Over open sea they fall back to every grid box and say so.

**How it works:**
- **No change to METEOR.** `scripts/landmask.py` applies it at export, by wrapping the two helpers every location reduction goes through: `_noise_weight_vector` and `_project_field`. So each location's noise, seasonal cycle, forced patterns and precipitation transform all share one mask.
- **Land fraction** is each model's own CMIP6 `sftlf`, or the Atlas's 1° land fraction for models that publish none.
- **Recorded:** each bundle records the convention and its land-fraction source.
- **For the browser:** a small `meteor_<model>_landfrac_v1.nc` (10–60 KB) ships beside the map data, for drawn regions.

**Checked** against CanESM5's own land-only warming: the new bundles are closer in 9 of 11 land regions, with the typical error down from about 0.3 °C to about 0.1 °C. The global mean and MED are unchanged, as designed.

## 2. The forty-model run (`77ffe39`)
`docs/05-training-run.md` records the run, from METEOR `integration/meteor-view` at `b02011b`, verified to be `base` plus #104, #102 and #101.

- **23 of 40 exported** and are on the `data-staging` branch, which won't be merged. All pass their golden fixtures, no bundle contains NaN, and 2081–2100 warming under ssp245 runs from 2.14 °C (MIROC6) to 4.06 °C (CanESM5), in the order the models' known sensitivities predict.
- **11 need a machine with about 32 GB:** the grids of about 1° and finer, killed by the out-of-memory killer at 15.7 GB. The doc gives the command. **NorESM2-MM, the site's default model, is among them.**
- **6 need METEOR fixes,** with a draft issue in the doc:
  - four runs whose time axes don't match what METEOR expects (checked against the archive's own time coordinates): ssp245 ending in 2099, historical running to 2016, and ssp245 running to 2500
  - two models whose archive data have no NaN at all, so the NaN that fails the fit must be introduced inside METEOR, most likely by the outer join across experiments of different lengths in `meteor.py:123`

`train-models.sh` gains `CLEAN_CACHE=1`, which deletes each model's downloads after a successful export.

## 3. CI fix (`fed25c7`)
- **The failure:** the first CI run failed because the land-only drawn-region tests read CanESM5's land-fraction file, which is on `data-staging`, not this branch. They had passed locally only because the training run left the file behind.
- **The fix:** they now use a synthetic land mask, since what they test is the weighting, not the data.
- **Also:** the golden-fixture test now skips a leftover fixture whose bundle is absent.

## Not in this PR: the data
The model data is on `data-staging`, as decided, so **merging this PR changes code only**:
- **The site keeps showing the same seven models, all still their earlier unmasked exports.** The land-masked versions of six of them, and 17 new models, are on `data-staging`.
- **Drawn regions on those seven:** their files have no land fraction, so a drawn box falls back to land and sea. Its chart title and status line say "land and sea" even with *Land only* ticked. This resolves itself once the data moves over.

## Testing
- **125 tests pass on a clean checkout,** with `data/` as committed, as CI sees it. New ones cover land-only drawn regions: a part-land box across the prime meridian differs, an all-land box is unchanged, and open sea falls back.
- **With the staged data present,** the golden fixtures of all 23 new exports also pass (198 tests).
- **In Chromium,** with a land-masked CanESM5 export, a coastal box over north-west Europe defaults to land only, switches to land and sea, and a South Pacific box falls back and says so.

author: nitinkumar004
body:
## Summary
Adds one background tick seam to `serve` for time-driven work (SCHED-0), and registers the alarm evaluators of all three clouds with it. In serve, a due CloudWatch alarm, Azure Monitor metric alert or GCP alert policy now changes state and fires its action with no read call, as on the real clouds.

- `config.Tickable` (`Tick(now time.Time) bool`) is the interface services implement.
- `server/serverkit/ticker.go` is a small scheduler. Each entry has an interval and a source that is resolved on every tick, so resets and lazily built AWS regions are picked up. A change marks persistence dirty.
- The Kubernetes progression ticker is now one entry, with the same flag, interval and gating as before.
- `Provider.Tickables()` on the AWS, Azure and GCP providers is where services register: CloudWatch (per AWS region), Azure Monitor and GCP Cloud Monitoring. SSM and CFN schedules can add themselves here later.
- Ticks use the providers' clock (real time unless `BaseOptions` sets one), so the `now` a mock sees matches its own clock.
- New `--tick-interval` flag (default `1s`, env `CLOUDEMU_TICK_INTERVAL`, `0` turns it off). A zero `serverkit.Config.TickInterval` means off, so direct `Config` users are unchanged. Library mode never ticks, so FakeClock tests stay deterministic.
- Shutdown now stops the ticks before the final persistence save. Before this change a Kubernetes tick could change state after that save.

The monitor mock packages are unchanged. They already had `Tick`.

## How verified
- Unit tests (`ticker_test.go`) check that registered Tickables are called, sources are re-resolved each tick, `stop` halts ticking, is idempotent and leaks no goroutines, disabled intervals are skipped, entry gating works, and every live region is covered (including after a reset).
- `ticker_shutdown_test.go`: with persist on and a Tickable that changes state every tick, no tick runs after shutdown and every change is in the final save. It fails when the old stop order is restored.
- `cloudwatch_tick_serve_test.go`: serve with a 100ms tick fires the alarm's SNS to SQS notification with no CloudWatch read. It fails with the tick off.
- `monitor_tick_serve_test.go`: serve on a fake clock with a 20ms tick delivers an Azure action-group webhook and a GCP webhook notification channel once time passes the next evaluation, with no monitor read. Both fail with the tick off.
- Provider tests check that each `Tickables()` returns that provider's monitor mock.
- serveflags tests cover the flag name set, the default, the env fallback and the mapping into Config.
- e2e: built the binary and ran `serve -providers aws -aws-port 62566 -k8s-port "" -tick-interval 500ms`. With the aws CLI I created an SNS topic and an SQS subscription, put a breaching datum dated 5s ahead, then created a period-10 alarm with an SNS action. Polling only SQS, the ALARM notification (`INSUFFICIENT_DATA` to `ALARM`) arrived 10s after the alarm was created. With `-tick-interval 0` no notification arrived in 40s. SIGTERM shut down cleanly (exit 0).
- Scoped gates, after merging origin/development: build, vet, `test -race -timeout 600s`, and `golangci-lint --new-from-rev=origin/development` (0 issues) on serverkit, serveflags, cmd/cloudemu, services/kubernetes, providers/aws, providers/azure, providers/gcp, config and persist. `contrib/server` builds and its flag tests pass.

author: wshallwshall
body:
BACKLOG #1711 -- batch 70 (observability), Manager optimistic-feistel-1f6a69 (acct-2).

**Own pull request, not batched:** it widens the shared PHI redactor.

| Source branch | Head SHA |
|---|---|
| `b70-1711-redactor-shapes` | `96fdc43d3c1c09b6ac84c4096d5a7740b192b7f6` (merge of main at the tip; the build commit is `5bbf0b8dd`) |

## What changed

Three label-anchored passes in `messagefoundry/redaction.py`. Each scrubs only the value, so keys, tags and element names stay. They run after the HL7 passes, so they only add redaction. `support/redact.py` picks them up by delegation (docstrings only there).

| Format | Scrubbed | Kept |
|---|---|---|
| JSON and Python dict/list repr | Values under `family`, `given`, `birthDate`, the DICOM JSON `001000xx` tags, and the `value` of an `identifier` or `telecom`; tuples, sets and calls such as `date(...)` are walked | `system`, `use`, `type`, every key |
| DICOM | `(0010,00xx)` tag values in dcmdump or pydicom dumps; values after `PatientName`, `PatientID`, `IssuerOfPatientID`, `PatientBirthDate`, `PatientBirthTime` in `=`, `:`, dict-key or `ds.X=` spelling | Tag and label |
| XML | Content and attributes of the same vocabulary, with or without a namespace prefix; inside `identifier`/`telecom`, only `<value>` | Tag names |

Unclosed regions run to the end of the text (fail closed at a clamp cut). An unclosed XML element counts as markup only on evidence, so prose placeholders such as `--email <address>` pass unchanged. `redact()` repeats to a fixed point (at most 8 rounds, then a flat pass) only when the structured passes changed the text; untouched text takes one round and is byte-identical to before.

**Deliberate narrowing, stated so it can be challenged:** in JSON, a plain string under `name` or `address` is kept; only a structure there is scrubbed. FHIR HumanName and Address are always objects or arrays, and a string there is usually a diagnostic (`{"name": "IB_ACME_ADT"}`, `{"address": "10.1.2.3"}`). Cost: a one-word patient name as a plain JSON string survives (a two-word name is still caught by the existing name pass). A test pins it.

**Why not `messagefoundry/anon/`:** it de-identifies whole HL7 v2 messages by field address into keyed surrogates and loads its denylist from `scripts/`; it has no FHIR, XML or DICOM vocabulary. `redaction.py` is already the central chokepoint and stdlib-only by design, so the passes sit there (CLAUDE.md section 9: centralise, do not inline).

## Red, then green (Builder)

`tests/test_redaction_structured_shapes.py` against the unmodified redactor: 51 failed, 52 passed (all 12 shapes across the redact, safe_text, bundle and control arms). At the head, it and `tests/test_redaction.py`: all pass. Each shape has a control that switches its own pass off and requires the values to leak. A seeded 20,000-input fixed-point fuzz is in the suite (200,000 run by hand: 0 failures, at most 3 rounds). Cost arms: growth under 24x for 8x the input and under 0.5 s per 64 KiB window.

**Cost:** a line with no structured shape pays a few microseconds more; a hostile 64 KiB window about 30 to 65 ms, up from about 5 ms.

## Checks

Builder, on the merged tree: ruff check and format clean (1475 files); engine mypy clean (302 files); `mypy --explicit-package-bases tests` clean (946 files); `test_redaction_structured_shapes`, `test_redaction`, `test_security_static`: 364 passed. Earlier, the redaction, logging, bundle and static-security set (19 files): 930 passed, 2 skipped. **Not run: the full suite** (stopped twice). CHANGELOG merge kept both sides: one entry added, none lost.

## Unread legs

Every required context, above all `test (ubuntu-latest, py3.14)` and the Windows legs, because the full suite never finished locally.

## Residuals, recorded in the module

JSON or XML escaped inside a JSON string; PHI used as object keys; object reprs other than calls; DICOM `(0010,1xxx)`/`(0010,2xxx)`; CDA/v3 vocabulary, FHIR `display` and the narrative `div`; XML text opening with whitespace or punctuation after a cut; per-line bundle redaction of pretty-printed multi-line JSON.

## Proposed new items (for the Lander)

1. Widen the DICOM pass to all of group 0010 (Other Patient IDs, Patient's Address, Telephone Numbers, Other/Birth/Mother's Birth Names).
2. Revisit the JSON `name`/`address` plain-string narrowing if a one-word-name leak matters more than diagnostic strings.
3. A bare `MRN <digits>` in prose leaks (measured in the row, outside its closing criteria).

## Landing order

None.

## Proposed ledger banner (for the Lander)

SHIPPED -- label-anchored FHIR JSON, DICOM and XML passes in the shared redactor; residuals recorded in redaction.py.

body:
## Summary

The SSRF deny-set unwraps IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible, NAT64 and 6to4 addresses and re-checks the embedded IPv4, but not Teredo (RFC 4380, `2001:0::/32`), which carries the Teredo server's IPv4 in bits 32..64 and the client's public IPv4, bit-inverted, in the last 32 bits. `[2001:0:4136:e378:8000:63bf:80fe:fefe]` embeds client `127.1.1.1` and passed every check. Defense in depth: reaching such an address needs a Teredo tunnel on the host, which Linux servers do not have by default, but it is a standards-defined IPv4 embedding and the deny-set's stated goal is that all of them agree.

Stacked on #1072, which moves `is_forbidden_ip` into the shared `obscura-ssrf` crate; only the last commit is new.

## Fix

Extract both embedded addresses and refuse the Teredo address if either is forbidden, the same shape as the NAT64 and 6to4 blocks above it.

## Test (RED before the fix)

`teredo_cannot_hide_a_forbidden_ipv4`: a loopback client, a private client and a private server are all refused; a public server with a public client is allowed.

## Verification

- `cargo nextest run --release -p obscura-net -p obscura-ssrf`: 105/105.
- `cargo nextest run --release --features render --no-fail-fast`: 1780/1780.
- Release build (`--features render`): clean.
- Obstacle course: 32/33; `observer-intersection` is the pre-existing failure on main.

author: thev1ndu
body:
## Purpose
Follow-up to #2033: adds a missing time-boxed dedup behavior, fixes the single largest RU-cost problem found in a review of Alert Core Service's Cosmos DB usage, and exposes the alert-ingestion webhook endpoint publicly for deployment.

## Goals
- Bound how long an incident keeps absorbing duplicate alerts, so a fingerprint that goes quiet and then recurs later opens a fresh incident instead of being folded into an arbitrarily old one forever.
- Eliminate `RetrySweep`'s unbounded full-table scan of `incidents_processed`, which re-scanned the service's entire incident history every 30 seconds and grew more expensive every day the service ran.
- Cut idle-time Cosmos reads from the poll loop's backstop ticker, which doesn't drive real-time alert pickup (that's `POST /alert`'s job) and was firing every 10 seconds regardless of alert volume.
- Make `/alert` and `/healthz` reachable from outside the project network for deployment, with authentication to be layered on separately via Choreo's own security configuration.

## Approach
- Added a fixed 5-minute dedup window (`engine.dedup_window` in `config.toml`), measured from an incident's `first_seen`: `model.Incident.IsOpen` now also reports closed once the window elapses, reusing the existing closed-incident "start a fresh generation" path in `store.IncidentRepo.Upsert` rather than adding a new code path.
- Replaced `ListPending`'s full scan with a maintained `incidents_pending` index table (`fingerprint` only): every write path that can change an incident's delivery-owed status (`Upsert`, `AppendWorkNote`, `RecordCSMIncident`, `RecordCSMAttemptFailure`, `ClearPendingNotes`) now keeps a single-row index entry in sync via a shared `isPending` predicate, so `RetrySweep` reads a small, bounded set of outstanding work instead of the whole table. Self-heals on read if an index entry is ever stale.
- Raised `poll.interval`'s default from 10s to 60s; `Wake()` (triggered by `POST /alert`) is what actually drives real-time pickup, so this only affects how long a missed wake call goes unnoticed.
- Set `networkVisibilities` to `Public` for the `alert` and `healthz` Choreo endpoints in `.choreo/component.yaml`.

## Release note
Add a fixed 5-minute incident dedup window, replace a full-table Cosmos scan in the retry sweep with a maintained pending-work index, widen the idle poll backstop interval, and expose the alert and healthz endpoints publicly.

## Documentation
Internal service component; no user-facing documentation impact.

## Migrations (if applicable)
This PR adds a new Cassandra table (`incidents_pending`, defined in `schema.cql`) that `store.IncidentRepo` writes to and reads from. It must be created in the target Cosmos DB Cassandra keyspace before deploying this build, or every incident write will fail against a table that doesn't exist yet.

## Security checks
 - Followed secure coding standards in http://wso2.com/technical-reports/wso2-secure-engineering-guidelines? yes
 - Ran FindSecurityBugs plugin and verified report? N/A (Go service)
 - Confirmed that this PR doesn't commit any keys, passwords, tokens, usernames, or other secrets? yes

## Automation tests
 - Unit tests
   > Added regression tests for the dedup window (duplicate-within-window folds, duplicate-past-window starts a fresh incident) and for the new pending-index predicate; `go test ./...` passes across the module

## Test environment
> Go 1.25, Cassandra (Cosmos DB Cassandra API), tested locally

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Duplicate alerts are grouped into the same incident within a configurable time window. Alerts received after that window can start a new incident, even if the previous incident remains open.
  * Pending incident work is tracked for more reliable retrieval, including incidents with queued work notes.
  * The alert and health-check endpoints are now publicly accessible.

* **Improvements**
  * The polling interval is now 60 seconds; real-time alert ingestion remains the primary pickup path.

author: ntatschner
body:
A project registered today has no memory, settings left at their defaults, and possibly agent files from before Loadout still in the repository, and nothing told its first session to do anything about that. This makes the first session onboard the project.

## What it does

**Registering queues it.** `ProjectService.AddAsync` declares the task `onboard-project` when it writes a fresh manifest, which covers `project add`, `project new`, `Ctrl+N` in the launcher and setup. A project whose manifest already exists was set up on another machine or by hand, so it isn't queued again, and `project clone` never queues. `loadout config set onboarding-run skip` records the task as dropped rather than leaving it out, so a skip can be told apart from something nobody thought of.

**The first session with no task of its own does it.** The launcher turns that launch into the onboarding:
- investigate mode unless another is asked for;
- `skill.project-onboarding` named explicitly, so it loads whatever the mode or the wording;
- "Onboard this project" sent as the first message, so the session starts working rather than waiting at an idle prompt.

A launch with a task of its own gets a reminder and is otherwise left alone. Team nodes are never touched. The launcher's launch-sheet preview uses the same rule, so it shows the session that will actually start.

**`loadout project onboard [--skip]`** starts it now in an ordinary session you watch, or records the skip.

**The agent proposes settings; a person applies them.** The settings choose what every later session is told, so an agent that could rewrite them would be choosing its own instructions unobserved.
- `loadout_project_settings` returns the current `project.yaml`.
- `loadout_propose_settings` stores a whole proposed file with its reasons.
- `loadout project proposal [--apply|--discard]` shows the proposal line by line and applies it or throws it away.
- A proposal may not change the identity, the repository, `environment` or `environments`. Those decide which credentials and sandbox a session gets.
- A proposal made before somebody edited the file is refused rather than applied over their edit.

**The skill** runs the launcher's own checks first: `instructions explain` and `audit`, `rules budget`, `memory list`, `project survey`, and `protect` and `migrate` in dry-run. It then follows the repository-review procedure, runs the build and the tests, records what stays true, and proposes settings. Anything that changes the repository or the workspace is reported for the person to run, not run.

It's recorded as a task rather than as memory. Memory holds what is true about the code; whether onboarding ran is what happened, and the task record already carries who, when and the state, is shared through the workspace, and is shown in the launcher.

## Smaller changes it needed

- **Opening prompt:** `LaunchRequest` and `AgentLaunchContext` carry an `OpeningPrompt`. Claude Code and Codex take it as their positional prompt, detected from the usage line, placed last behind a bare `--`, because Claude's `--add-dir` takes several values and would read the prompt as another directory. `claude -p --add-dir <dir> -- <prompt>` was checked by hand to answer the prompt. An agent described in `config.yaml`, or a build that doesn't advertise a prompt, starts without one, and the launch says what to type.
- **Launch history:** it recorded the typed task, so an onboarding session showed "(no task given)". It now records the task the session was given.
- **Task corroboration:** it no longer flags a finished onboarding for having no commit after it, since onboarding's work is all in the workspace.
- **`YamlStore`:** gains `Parse` and `Render` for YAML handed over as text.
- **Docs:** `docs/guides/adding-a-project.md` covers registering a project, onboarding, reviewing a proposal, and every `project.yaml` setting, including the ones nothing reads yet. The command reference, `onboarding-run` and the specialist counts are updated.

Two existing assertions were narrowed on purpose: registration tests that expected no tasks at all now expect no `setup-repository` task, because every new project now carries its onboarding.

## Evidence

- **Full suite:** 3,484 passed, 0 failed, 27 skipped.
- **Mutation checks:** every new test was checked by breaking what it covers, twelve mutations in all, and each one failed its tests. They covered queuing, skipping, the launcher turn and reminder, the preview, the guarded sections, the stale check, the opening prompt, the `--` guard, the history record, the corroboration exemption, and refusing unknown specialists.
- **End to end:** run against the built CLI with its app data moved to a sandbox. It covered registering, the onboarding and reminder dry runs, a proposal submitted through `mcp serve` over JSON-RPC, applying it, and skipping.
- **A real onboarding:** Claude Code onboarded a small single-script PowerShell repository.
  - It started on its own and ran the launcher's checks before reading any code.
  - It checked its findings by running the script against jar files it built for the test, and confirmed a real detection gap that way.
  - It recorded three memory topics, all specific and checked.
  - It read the settings and judged that no change was worth proposing, saying why.
  - It left `loadout protect` for the person, and closed the task with a note of what was left.
  
  That run is what found the idle-prompt, launch-history and corroboration problems fixed above.

- **A second real onboarding,** of a nine-project C# solution, run in print mode with the compiled context the launcher built for it and Loadout's MCP server.
  - It built the solution; all 165 tests passed.
  - It read all eight audit findings and judged them deliberate.
  - It recorded three checked memory topics.
  - It proposed excluding `framework.aspnet-core`, which had loaded only because an `appsettings.json` exists, and preferring `platform.windows`, with a reason for each.

  That run found two more problems, both fixed here:
  - **`is_empty` in every manifest:** it was written into every manifest and appeared as a changed line in the diff. It's now left out.
  - **An unchecked specialist id:** the agent named one without checking it. Such a proposal is now refused, and the skill tells the agent to confirm ids with `loadout_specialist`.

## Not covered

- Codex's opening prompt is covered by the adapter test against its usage line, not by a real Codex session.
- `loadout_remember`'s duplicate-topic guard refused two unrelated topics during the real run, and the agent had to resubmit them. That behaviour already existed and isn't changed here; it's tracked separately.

author: hannay001
body:
Follow-up to #5. It adds the biggest ranking gain yet, three ways to put Lockkeeper in front of agents, opt-in telemetry, and a README built to be found and understood.

## What changes

- **Routing reads what a skill's body is about** (`a0c498b`). At rebuild, every skill, agent and command gets up to 24 body keywords: its words ranked by tf-idf against every other body in the registry. They're matched like any other field (4 points per term), indexed by the lexical index, and kept out of search output. The registry format version is bumped, so existing registries rebuild themselves once on the next query.
- **`lockkeeper mcp`** (`dc5dddd`). Serves `route`, `search` and `audit` over MCP (stdio; protocol versions 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05) to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline and others.
  - The registry and lexical index stay loaded between calls and are re-validated at most every 30 s.
  - stdout carries protocol messages only. A test routes in a fresh home, where the registry rebuilds mid-session, to prove it.
- **`lockkeeper route-hook` and `lockkeeper hooks install claude`** (`4908e73`). A `UserPromptSubmit` hook routes each prompt and gives the agent the capabilities that fit, with the exact files to read.
  - It never blocks a prompt: it always exits 0, adds nothing for slash commands or short replies, never waits on a re-index, and skips the decision model.
  - The installer is idempotent, keeps all other settings, backs the file up, refuses to touch a settings file it can't parse, and adds the PreToolUse firewall only with `--firewall`.
- **Opt-in, anonymous telemetry** (`3b7627c`). Off by default. `DO_NOT_TRACK`, `LOCKKEEPER_TELEMETRY=0` and CI always force it off.
  - It collects one aggregate per day: a random install id, version, Python and OS, per-command counts with bucketed latency, runtimes, and registry size as a bucket. Never prompts, names or paths.
  - No endpoint ships (`DEFAULT_ENDPOINT` is empty), and it never sends during route, search or the hook.
  - Documented in `docs/TELEMETRY.md`; the ROADMAP non-goal is updated to match.
- **Benchmark page** (`80e02b2`). `docs/BENCHMARK.md` covers methods, before/after results at 26k and 79k skills, the per-change results, a comparison with the SkillRouter paper, and caveats.
- **README refactor** (`80e02b2`, `2ee6f05`). The README is now plain-language, scannable and written for search.
  - The order is: what it is, why it matters (with benchmark numbers), a 3-step quickstart, four ways to use it (automatic per-prompt routing, MCP, CLI, firewall), supported agents, benchmark, how it works, firewall, comparison, and an FAQ phrased as the questions people search for.
  - Reference detail moved to `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` and `docs/FIREWALL.md`; nothing was dropped.
  - Claims were checked against the code. For example, the per-prompt hook adds routing context but doesn't remove Claude Code's own skill list, and the FAQ says so.
  - The README used to be flagged hostile by Lockkeeper's own scanner, because it quoted attack syntax. It and the new pages now audit clean.
  - It also fixes a Claude Code hooks example that used a settings shape Claude Code doesn't accept and a millisecond timeout.
  - `pyproject.toml` gets a search-friendly description, keywords (claude-code, codex, cursor, mcp, model-context-protocol, agent-skills, context-window, …), the AI topic classifier, and Documentation/Benchmark links for the future PyPI page.

## Results (SkillRouter Eval Core, 75 tasks)

| | Before #5 | After #5 | This PR |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Hit@1, 26k skills | 0.347 | 0.507 | **0.653** |
| Bundle recall, 26k | 0.220 | 0.366 | **0.447** |
| Hit@1, 79,141 skills | 0.253 | – | **0.547** |
| Bundle recall, 79k | 0.206 | – | **0.417** |
| Route p50, 79k (warm) | 19.9 s | – | **2.5 s** |

At 79k, 0.547 falls between the SkillRouter paper's Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (0.533) and Gemini embedding (0.560) results, with no model loaded. Full tables and caveats are in `docs/BENCHMARK.md`.

**Cost:** rebuild at 79k goes from 42 s to 100 s (26k: 14 s to 29 s), and route p50 at 26k goes from 0.37 s to 0.69 s. Typical registries still rebuild in seconds.

## Testing

- Full suite passes: `HOME="$(mktemp -d)" python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -t .`
- New test files: `test_telemetry`, `test_mcp_server`, `test_route_hook`, plus body-keyword tests in `test_routing_scale`.
- CI's latency budget passes locally: `bench_route_latency.py --records 26000 --tasks 5 --max-p50 4.0` gives p50 1.87 s.
- Wheel built and installed into a clean venv. `lockkeeper telemetry`, `hooks show claude` and `mcp` (initialize, tools/list) work from the installed package, and the new metadata shows in the wheel.
- README and docs audit clean with `lockkeeper audit`.
- Not yet tried inside a live Claude Code or Cursor session. The hook and MCP server were tested with the exact messages those clients send.
