- `astro check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- Question bank and FRQ validation pass. Answer letters stay balanced (A to E: 175, 172, 169, 171, 166).
- Builds pass with accounts off and with demo account settings.
- Browser tests (Playwright), accounts off: exam mode with timer and Previous button, answer review, smart review scheduling and the due filter, mastery badges, dashboard, and the older regression tests.
- Browser tests, accounts on as a guest: the 5-question topic preview, the daily limit and limit card, a gate on each locked tool, and the plans table.
- Browser tests, accounts on as a member: everything unlocked. The sign-up, sign-in, two-device sync, password reset, and account deletion tests still pass.

- Color contrast checked in light and dark mode, with accounts off and on.

## Objectif

Fournir aux administrateurs Fans autorisés un panel de modération sur les API existantes, depuis `main` au SHA `34755a6e4d84d6648f2299bdc24b6ede626b67da`. Cette PR reste en brouillon : aucune fusion, activation en production, diffusion activée, installation, release ou paiement.

## Changements

- Sous-page Faluss avec file des textes pending (20/page), contexte et fiche/journal accessibles après décision ; quarantaine paginée selon son contrat existant (tous états).
- Approbation/refus avec motifs fermés, permissions et nonces serveur, révisions et traces des moteurs existants ; aucune réussite anticipée, conflits explicités.
- Examen privé de l’image associée encore éligible et des images de quarantaine : POST authentifié, no-store, aucun chemin ni URL publique ; aperçu blob en mémoire, repli sans JavaScript vers nouvel onglet.
- DA responsive #FFFDF5, cartes blanches, Outfit locale sous SIL OFL. Captures de fixtures exclusivement synthétiques.
- Documentation des procédures humaines, limites de révocation, conservation, nettoyage et hébergement ; statut de #78 actualisé.

## Changelog

### Ajouté

- Panel, styles et amélioration progressive d’aperçu ; police et licence ; recette HTTP/navigateur reproductible et contrat FANS-MODERATION.

### Modifié

- Branchement du panel uniquement lorsque le module texte Fans est disponible ; tests d’isolation Me/Hub ; index des contrats et changelog.

### Corrigé

- Sans objet pour le runtime antérieur. Le parcours navigateur a détecté et validé la correction du masquage DOM de form.action par le champ WordPress action dans le nouvel adaptateur.

### Supprimé

- Sans objet.

### Migration et compatibilité

- Aucun schéma, option, rôle, permission métier ou moteur nouveau. Aucune ouverture du flag de diffusion. API et motifs existants conservés.

## Vérifications effectuées

- [x] Lint et formatage
- [x] Analyse statique
- [x] Tests automatisés
- [x] Vérification manuelle ciblée
- [x] Documentation mise à jour

Précisions :

- php -l sur les cinq PHP modifiés/ajoutés ; PHPStan niveau 7 sans erreur ; node --check JS/CJS ; syntaxe Python, liens documentaires, scan ciblé de signatures de secrets et git diff --check.
- PHPUnit Fans/Core : 80 tests, 860 assertions. Après extension de l’isolation : 4 tests Core, 41 assertions. La CI complète est relancée sur ce head ; elle ne remplace pas la recette réelle.
- WordPress 7.1.2 / PHP 8.5.4 / MariaDB 11.8.6 : 67 contrôles HTTP réels réussis, dont 26 textes / deux créateurs, pages 20+6 sans doublon ni omission, permissions/nonces, révisions périmées, suspensions/retraits, décisions texte et image concurrentes (un 200, un 409, une trace).
- Edge headless : 1440×1000 et 390×844, styles réellement chargés, absence de débordement du panel, décision sans JavaScript confirmée serveur, aperçu PNG via POST puis fermeture du blob.
- Trois flags locaux false, fichiers de quarantaine nettoyés, sessions synthétiques détruites, compte SQL temporaire supprimé, workers arrêtés et port 8113 fermé. Aucun contact de production.
- Les premières passes interrompues et leurs causes de harnais sont documentées ; seule la passe complète finale est déclarée verte.

## Intégration et absence de régression

- `faluss.com` : aucun hook panel chargé même avec flags Fans erronés ; aucun changement Hub.
- `faluss.me` : même isolation ; aucun teaser ou projection active, aucun changement Identity/Me.
- Modules ou plugins Faluss existants : consommation des contrats publics via REST et Profil ; aucune table intermodule lue par le panel, aucune mutation métier réimplémentée.
- WordPress et Elementor : sous-page native manage_options, nonces et formulaires sans JS, assets limités à cette page ; aucun réglage Elementor/thème/global. Police embarquée sans appel externe.

## Risques et retour arrière

- Risques : les octets déjà reçus ne peuvent pas être rappelés ; l’examen n’est pas un détecteur de contenu interdit ni une vérification d’identité/droits. Pas de snapshot global de la file, d’assignation de modérateur, de double validation ou de preuve légale conservée. Règles humaines, SLA, rétention, recours et hébergement/cache réel restent à définir. Pas de validation Safari physique, TLS/CDN réel, OOM ou panne SQL au commit.
- Retour arrière : conserver les flags fermés en production ; fermeture du module texte retire panel et aperçu, fermeture images rend sa vue indisponible. Retour au commit précédent sans migration ni effacement des journaux. Une erreur de nettoyage après révocation exige inspection du journal et reprise par l’API existante.

author: gantoine
body:
<!-- trunk-ignore-all(markdownlint/MD041) -->
<!-- trunk-ignore-all(markdownlint/MD033) -->

**Description**

Bumps the locked `mariadb` Python connector from 1.1.12 to 1.1.14 (lockfile only; it comes in through the `SQLAlchemy[mariadb-connector]` extra).

5.3.0 moved the image from Python 3.13 to 3.14, but the connector stayed on 1.1.12, which came out before Python 3.14 was supported. 1.1.13 and 1.1.14 fix several crashes in the C extension, including CONPY-318 (a NULL `connection` dereference in `MrdbCursor_clear_result`, plus a follow-up in `tp_traverse`), CONPY-306 (a crash on invalid unicode from the server) and a missing cursor `tp_dealloc`. 1.1.14 is also the first release that lists Python 3.14 as supported. The reported fault, `segfault at 10` inside `_mariadb.cpython-314-x86_64-linux-musl.so`, fits a NULL struct pointer read at the first field after `PyObject_HEAD`, which is the CONPY-318 pattern.

Fixes #4755

**Caveat:** I could not reproduce the segfault locally. `rommapp/romm:5.3.1` (amd64 under emulation and arm64) migrated a fresh MariaDB 10.11 DB, and one first migrated to head by `rommapp/romm:5.2.0`, without crashing. The reporter's crash may depend on their data or host. The upgrade is low risk and fixes known crashes in this code path, but whether it resolves this specific report needs confirmation from the reporter (they offered to test an image).

**Testing**

- Built the `slim-image` target from this branch (arm64): the connector builds against Alpine 3.24's `mariadb-connector-c` on musl/Python 3.14, and `alembic upgrade head` succeeds on a fresh MariaDB 10.11 DB.
- `uv run pytest tests/handler/database tests/test_migrations.py` locally with 1.1.14: 558 passed, 4 skipped.

**AI assistance disclosure:** Claude Code investigated this issue, attempted the repro, and wrote the change and this description. The maintainer reviews it.

- [x] I've tested the changes locally
- [ ] I've updated relevant comments
- [ ] I've assigned reviewers for this PR
- [ ] I've added unit tests that cover the changes

author: timesselens
body:
In the tests below, a derivative that is differentiated again (forward over reverse, for example) keeps reading a global `Dict` as it was when the derivative was compiled, and throws an `AssertionError` once the `Dict` has grown. #3317 addressed this for loads through a `julia.constgv` global. A derivative compiled into another one reaches the same fields through literal addresses, and those are still folded. This PR proposes to leave such loads alone.

### Before / after

```julia
using Enzyme
const D = Dict{Int, Float64}()
f(x) = x^2 * get(D, 1, 1.0)
df(x) = autodiff_deferred(Reverse, Const(f), Active, Active(x))[1][1]   # 2x * D[1]
autodiff(Forward, df, Duplicated(3.0, 1.0))   # (2.0,) on main and with this PR
D[1] = 2.0
autodiff(Forward, df, Duplicated(3.0, 1.0))
# main:    AssertionError (empty message), in ht_keyindex
# this PR: (4.0,)
```

A plain `autodiff(Reverse, f, Active, Active(3.0))` gives the expected value in both cases.

### What seems to happen

`check_ir!` calls `try_replace_constant_load!` (`src/compiler/validation.jl`), which replaces a load of an object reference from a constant address with the object found there at compile time. Since #3317 it refuses when the address lies inside a mutable global, but it can only tell that when the address comes from a `julia.constgv` global. A derivative compiled into another one has been optimized on its own, and there those loads have become literal addresses (`load atomic ptr addrspace(10), ptr inttoptr (i64 … to ptr)`; there are 5 of them into `D` for `df` above), which are folded without the check. `slots`, `keys` and `vals` are then fixed to the empty memories of compile time, while `count` is still read at run time. After `D[1] = 2.0`, the lookup sees one entry and zero-length `keys`, and the assertion in `ht_keyindex` throws.

### Proposed change

A one-line change: when mutability has to be checked, `try_replace_constant_load!` leaves a load from a literal address alone. A literal address doesn't seem to say which object it points into (some don't even point to the start of an object), so it can't be resolved and checked. The calls that resolve function pointers pass `check_mutability = false` and aren't affected.

### Tests

`test/basic.jl`, "Global Dict that grows after a nested derivative is compiled", next to #3317's test: the example above with 100 entries, so that the `Dict` replaces its memories on every Julia version. On `main` the second `@test` errors with the `AssertionError`.

```
julia --project -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.test(test_args=["basic"])'
```

### Related

- #3310 and #3311 (closed): the same `AssertionError` from a custom rule that reads a global `Dict`, addressed by #3316 and #3317. This PR extends #3317's check to literal addresses.
- #3521 (draft, on #3512's stack) refers to Julia values by named globals instead of literal addresses, and applies the same check to that form. This PR covers today's literal form and merges cleanly with that stack.
- This came up in [WaterLily.jl](https://github.com/WaterLily-jl/WaterLily.jl), whose Poisson adjoint caches workspaces in a global `Dict`, inside a checkpointing rule's thunk. There the same folding also affected fields of a `SpinLock`, of `Base.CoreLogging.LogState` and of the scheduler's task queues.

<details><summary>Verification</summary>

Each test file run on its own (outer `@testset`), macOS aarch64 (M1 Max), stock Enzyme_jll 0.0.295, on `main` `57e642cc`:

| test file | Julia 1.10.12 | Julia 1.11.9 | Julia 1.12.7 | Julia 1.13.0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `basic` | 300/300 | 305/305 | 305/305 | 305/305 |

Without the change, `basic` with the new test set on `main` (Julia 1.12.7): 304 pass, 0 fail, 1 error.

</details>

body:
## What

A new domain package `vld-journals` (`backend/packages/journals`) and one migration that builds the schema `journals`:

- **Shared journal identity** (never deleted): `journal`, `journal_issn` (the ISSN is the key: whose an ISSN is, given by an import or chosen by a moderator), `speciality` (code + branch of science).
- **The VAK registry, one edition at a time**: documents (`vak_document`, the latest PDF in `vak_document_file`), snapshots with their parse result and warnings, the facts of an edition (entries, printed ISSNs, former titles, speciality groups with «с/по» dates, specialities with their printed names), the pointer to the current snapshot and the log of every publication or rollback.
- **Insert-only for the app role**: the migration revokes `UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE`; only `journal_issn` (reassigning an ISSN), `vak_current` (moving the pointer) and `vak_document_file` (replacing the latest PDF) change.
- The science branch and the warning code are PostgreSQL enums with the values of `ScienceBranch` and `WarningCode` from vld-vak.
- The migrator knows the domain (`DOMAIN_METADATA`, `alembic.ini`).

## Checked

- Integration tests on a database migrated by `vld-migrate`: enum labels against the code, the exact grants of the app role per table, every constraint, and the four questions the prototype answered (the current list, a journal by ISSN with its specialities, the specialities with their names, «was journal X listed for speciality Y on date D»).
- The migrator's stairway test takes the new revision up, down and up again; `vld-migrate check` finds no drift; squawk 0 issues.
- ruff, basedpyright (0/0), lint-imports (11 contracts), pytest 919 unit + 111 integration.
- The migrator image builds with vld-journals and without pdfplumber.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce the journals domain and migrate a durable, queryable VAK registry schema with controlled data mutability.

New Features:
- Add the `vld-journals` domain package and its ORM model for shared journal identities, ISSN ownership, specialities, and VAK registry editions.
- Add a complete `journals` database schema covering VAK documents, parser snapshots, parsed facts, current-edition tracking, and publication history.

Enhancements:
- Enforce immutable, insert-only registry data while allowing controlled ISSN reassignment, latest-document replacement, and current-snapshot updates.
- Represent VAK science branches and parse warnings as database enums synchronized with `vld-vak`.
- Register the journals domain with the migrator and document its schema and usage.

Build:
- Add the journals package and migrator dependency to the backend workspace and lockfile.

Documentation:
- Document the journals package and its VAK registry schema in the project documentation.

Tests:
- Add unit and PostgreSQL integration coverage for schema metadata, enum synchronization, grants, constraints, migration behavior, and representative registry queries.

Chores:
- Add import-boundary rules for the journals domain and update workspace test configuration.

author: davidfarah2003
body:
## Summary

`check:docsbundle` ends in `git diff --exit-code -- docs/mcp-tools.md`. While the index holds unmerged paths, `git diff --exit-code` prints a combined diff and still exits 0, so the gate reports success at the moment it exists for: mid-merge, before the resolved file is staged. Two branches resolving the same generated-file conflict both read that rc=0 as the gate passing. The committed-bundle conflict class itself went away when the bundle stopped being tracked; the unreliable exit code on an unmerged index did not.

## What changes

- `scripts/check-unmerged.mjs`: runs `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` and, when it prints anything, writes one line saying the index holds unmerged paths so `git diff --exit-code` cannot answer, lists the paths, and exits 1. Empty output exits 0. The header comment carries the reason.
- `package.json`: `check:docsbundle` runs that script first, ahead of docs-voice, the tool-docs generation, the diff and the bundle check. No other line changes.

No changeset: `scripts/` and the root `package.json` are not a published package. No docs change: no page names `check:docsbundle`. No mutation entry: the gate is a shell composition over a root script, and the scratch-repository pair below is the proof.

## Evidence

- Reproduction in a scratch repository: with `a.md` unmerged, `git diff --exit-code -- a.md` prints a `diff --cc` header and exits 0; a clean file with an edit exits 1 (control).
- The new script in that repository: with `a.md` unmerged it names `a.md` and exits 1; after `git add a.md` it prints nothing and exits 0; in the clean lane worktree it prints nothing and exits 0.
- `pnpm -s check:docsbundle` in the clean worktree: docs-voice, the tool-docs generation, the bundle check, rc=0, and the tree stays clean.
- `pnpm -s typecheck`, `pnpm -s smoke:mutation-fixtures` (0 dead, 0 ambiguous, 0 unrestored), `pnpm -s smoke:ci-suites` (25 passed), `pnpm changeset status`: all green.

Out of scope: the working-tree modification the composed command leaves behind on a failure, `scripts/check-docs-bundle.mjs`.

Closes #572.

author: xscaperrr
body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Preserve `browser_open` and `browser` identities in the shared text-call alias resolver so their arguments reach the corresponding tools instead of becoming shell input.
  - Resolve the existing `web_search` alias to `web_search_tool`. Tool implementations remain authoritative for schemas and validation; the effective runtime registry remains authoritative for availability. No state or configuration is added.
  - Cover legacy GLM and standard text-call formats at the public parser boundary, and exercise registered, missing, and excluded tools through the production turn loop.
- **Scope boundary:** Native structured calls, explicit shell aliases and their existing URL-to-curl compatibility, tool registration, approval policy, and browser/search implementations are unchanged. This does not add `search` or `websearch` aliases or new parser syntax.
- **Blast radius:** Text tool calling and fallback consumers of `zeroclaw-tool-call-parser`, including CLI and other runtime entrypoints. The intentional compatibility change removes browser/search-to-shell substitution.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11108. Supersedes #11188 with the identical commit under the renamed source branch. Implements the [accepted scope](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/11108#issuecomment-5847267646).
- **Labels:** None at creation; repository labeling is pending. The linked issue classifies this tool-authority and compatibility boundary as `risk:high` and `domain:security`.

### What this does, simply

A model response such as `browser_open/url>https://example.com` previously became a shell command running curl. It now becomes a `browser_open` call with the original URL. Browser actions such as `snapshot` retain their arguments, and search requests reach the registered search tool. If the requested tool is unavailable or excluded, the existing runtime availability checks prevent execution; shell is not substituted. This does not standardize the existing unavailable-tool error presentation.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Deterministic parser and production turn-loop regressions exercise the changed boundary without a browser, API credentials, or shell execution; manual interaction adds no signal for this alias-only change.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** No pending CI is counted as evidence. Local parser tests, the production turn-loop regression, existing browser URL/policy tests, formatting, and strict Clippy cover the changed behavior and its availability boundary.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The full workspace and optional runtime feature combinations were not run locally. Local evidence is Windows x86_64 MSVC with Rust 1.96.0; required upstream CI must still pass before merge.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo +1.96.0 fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0

cargo +1.96.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-tool-call-parser -- --quiet
test result: ok. 191 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored  (doctest)

cargo +1.96.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --no-default-features run_tool_call_loop_browser_and_search_preserve_tool_boundaries
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 4817 filtered out
# The parameterized test covers 18 tool/format/availability combinations.

cargo +1.96.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib browser_open::tests:: -- --quiet
test result: ok. 24 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 1971 filtered out

cargo +1.96.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-tool-call-parser -p zeroclaw-runtime --no-default-features --all-targets -j 2 -- -D warnings
Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 3m 38s

git diff --cached --check
# exit 0
```

The existing ignored parser test concerns a separate textual tag-scanner defect; this PR adds no ignores. The first Clippy invocation, without `-j 2`, stopped when the third-party `rcgen` compiler process exited with code 1 and no source diagnostic. The identical strict check passed with two build jobs; no lint suppression or source workaround was added.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Before applying the production fix, the three new browser/search parser tests failed with `shell` instead of `browser_open`, while the explicit-shell control passed. The new runtime test also failed because an available browser tool was not invoked. After the fix, all pass. Source review confirmed canonical tool names/schemas and existing registry/exclusion checks. Tests preserve metacharacters and complete argument objects, and record zero shell calls for missing or excluded browser/search tools. No live browser, shell command, or search service was exercised.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no rendering, layout, or presentation code changes. Evidence covers call parsing and dispatch to recording test tools, not a live browser window.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `82da3a0f0c290fcff20bc0c229571ffd890d8e6a`; public `parse_tool_calls` boundary and production `run_tool_call_loop` with `channel_name = "cli"`. Regression sources are `crates/zeroclaw-tool-call-parser/tests/browser_search_semantics.rs` and `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/loop_.rs`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Automated test output above; no screenshot applicable.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** GLM/JSON browser and search calls execute their registered test tools exactly once with original arguments, without needing shell. Missing/excluded tools do not execute shell even when shell is available.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full-workspace tests, full-workspace Clippy, and `./dev/ci.sh all` were not duplicated locally; focused Windows checks cover the parser-only production change and runtime regression. Upstream required CI remains necessary for broader features/platforms. Live browser/search tests were unnecessary for name and argument routing.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.** Calls use existing registered tools and their existing policy gates.
- New external network calls? **No new network implementation or destination.** Correctly routed browser/search requests can now perform the intended existing tool operation when enabled and authorized.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** New fixtures use synthetic values and `example.com`.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Resolution of untrusted model-produced tool names changes. Preserving tool identity removes the implicit shell-authority fallback; normal registry, exclusion, approval, and tool argument checks remain in place. Tests cover metacharacters and unavailable/excluded tools.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: This changes which existing capability handles a browser/search request, intentionally retiring historical curl behavior. The accepted issue scope, cross-format regressions, runtime no-fallback tests, and existing browser policy tests bound that change.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No** for callers relying on browser/search aliases being converted to shell/curl; the legacy syntax remains parseable.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No.**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- Exact upgrade steps: Prompts that intend an HTTP download should request `http_request` with its schema, or explicitly request an authorized `shell` command. Browser-open requests should use `browser_open` with `url`; automation calls must retain the required `action`; search requests use `query`. Keep existing browser/search enablement and permission settings appropr

## Summary

Single-home the three preview harnesses' preview-instance launch fragments on `scripts/browser_harness_session_tree_preview.py` — the module that already owns the preview-source-home building (`build_source_home`, imported by both live-preview harnesses). Three helpers now:

- `preview_invocation(home, port, backend, extra_backends)`: the preview CLI's argv. Every harness starts `charliebot session-tree preview` as its own foreground process — never an in-process server — so the trial rides the fresh-home boot path the operator runs; the browser harness's multi-entry scenario passes its further entries as `--add-backend`.
- `preview_instance_env(source_home)`: the child env (trial source home + unbuffered console); the copy is taken at call time, so each caller keeps its identity-variable scrub before calling.
- `wait_preview_ready(proc, home, server_console, fail, timeout_s)`: the ready-record poll (async, like the two live harnesses' inline loops), with the console-tail early-exit check all three now share. `fail` stays the caller's own failure exit (message prefix and exit style differ per harness), the same contract `devtools_ws_url` has used since #2121.

`wait_ready` (the browser harness's sync 9-line variant, no early-exit check) is absorbed into `wait_preview_ready`; its call site awaits the shared helper.

Behavior notes (success paths identical; failure paths strictly faster or more detailed):

- `browser_harness_session_tree_preview` gains the early-exit check: a preview process that dies before its ready record lands now fails immediately with the captured console tail instead of spinning out the full 120 s deadline (the two live harnesses already had this check; their inline loops are what this PR removes).
- The browser harness's expiry message now names the record path (`preview instance never became ready (<home>/state/preview_instance.json)`) instead of the home directory only — the record path is the only observable.
- The caller-specific behavior stays at the callers: `live_preview_sidebar_status`'s production-port guards (port pick and ready-URL check), `live_preview_task_tree`'s access-key sanity check, and each harness's own `log` lines.

body:
## Intent The firstmate repo loses the captain's standing merge authority because the registry calls it firstmate and the directory is starship. Found 2026-09-08 spawning fm-shift-command-s1: fm-spawn printed 'project "starship" not in registry; defaulting to no-mistakes off' and set yolo=off, even though data/projects.md registers this repo as 'firstmate [no-mistakes +yolo]'. The lookup uses the project DIRECTORY basename, which is starship, while the registry entry is named firstmate. Consequence: every firstmate-repo task silently loses the captain's standing +yolo, and the delivery mode only came out right by falling back to the default. Not urgent and not dangerous, it fails toward asking rather than toward merging, but it is a silent authority downgrade and it will keep happening. Fix the resolution or give the registry entry an alias; bin/fm-project-mode.sh owns the parsing. Dispatched on 2026-09-26 when the captain asked to use the week's remaining usage on parallel work. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-project-mode.sh` now reads an optional, repeatable `alias=` bracket token. A lookup by clone directory name (for example `starship` for a row registered as `firstmate [no-mistakes +yolo alias=starship]`) resolves to that row's mode, `+yolo`, branch prefix and forge, so spawn no longer falls back to `no-mistakes off`. A row registered under the exact name still wins over another row's alias, and names containing spaces never match an alias. Near-miss forge warnings are now printed only for the row that actually matches. - A new `--line` query prints the matched registry row verbatim, using the same exact-then-alias resolution, and prints nothing when no row matches. `fm-home-seed.sh`, `fm-remote-home-seed.sh` and `fm-remote-home-provision.sh` now get their registry row from `--line` instead of their own `awk` lookups. That means a seeded home receives the aliased row it resolved, and the sync step removes stale copies whether they are keyed by the requested name or the registered name. - The README, `docs/architecture.md` and the project-management skill now document the `alias=` token. New tests cover alias resolution in `fm-task-delivery`, `fm-secondmate-safety` and the remote secondmate lifecycle e2e. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change adds an optional alias= registry token that only widens which rows match (an exact registered name still wins), and it routes both seeding paths and the remote provision check through a single --line resolver; a row without an alias resolves exactly as before, and the fix round implemented the round-1 instructions without going beyond them. ## Testing I ran the real CLI scripts in a throwaway FM_HOME, comparing the pre-fix and fixed code. - **Bug reproduced:** with the captain's current unaliased row, both versions warn "not in registry" and fall back to `no-mistakes off`. - **Fix confirmed:** after adding `alias=starship`, the fixed parser prints `no-mistakes on` with no warning, and every query mode agrees. The pre-fix parser still falls back. - **Break attempts:** an exact registered name still beats another row's alias. Alias-shaped text in a description is ignored. Unknown names still warn and fall back. `--line` prints nothing for a missing row or a missing registry. - **Spawn:** fm-spawn on a `starship` directory reads the aliased posture. The false downgrade notice is gone, and the registered branch prefix is reported instead. - **Local seeding:** a secondmate home seeded with `starship` carries the registered row and resolves `direct-PR on`. Reseeding is idempotent. - **Suites:** the task-delivery and secondmate-safety suites passed in full, exit 0. body:
This PR adds a complete, production-ready static website for Vibe Massage & Recovery, a registered massage therapy clinic in Amherstburg, Ontario.

## Summary
A mobile-first website built with semantic HTML, a comprehensive design system, and a build process to generate static pages from modular source files. The site requires no framework or build step to deploy — all HTML files are ready to upload to any static host.

## Key Changes

**Design System & Styling**
- Comprehensive CSS stylesheet (724 lines) with mobile-first approach
- Custom color tokens for brand (brown/sage palette) and neutrals
- Typography system using Fraunces (display) and DM Sans (body)
- Reusable component classes: buttons (multiple variants), cards, grids, sections
- Accessibility features: focus states, skip link, semantic HTML structure
- Subtle paper texture overlay and smooth animations

**Pages & Content**
- **Home** (`index.html`): Hero section, service overview, therapist intro, direct billing info, location, CTAs
- **Services** (`services.html`): Detailed service descriptions and pricing tables with direct billing callouts
- **About** (`about.html`): Therapist biography, credentials, and experience
- **Contact** (`contact.html`): Location map, contact details, hours, parking info
- **Billing** (`billing.html`): Direct billing providers, FAQ, payment methods, referral info
- **Style Guide** (`styleguide.html`): Design system documentation with color swatches and component states

**Build System**
- Modular source files in `src/pages/` and `src/partials.mjs`
- Node.js build script (`src/build.mjs`) that assembles static HTML from reusable components
- Shared partials: icons (SVG sprite), contact info, CTAs, layout helpers
- No runtime dependencies — output is pure HTML/CSS/JS

**Functionality**
- Sticky header with scroll detection
- Mobile action bar that appears after scrolling past hero
- Booking button integration (placeholder for external booking URL)
- Smooth scroll behavior with header offset
- Responsive grid layouts and typography scaling
- Schema.org structured data for SEO

**Assets**
- SVG favicon with brand colors
- Inline SVG icon sprite (18 icons) for performance
- Google Fonts integration (Fraunces, DM Sans)
- Placeholder images with semantic alt text

## Notable Implementation Details
- All pages share a common header, footer, and navigation structure via partials
- Color system uses CSS custom properties for easy brand updates
- Buttons support multiple states (hover, focus, active, disabled) with smooth transitions
- Responsive design uses `clamp()` for fluid typography and spacing
- Accessibility: WCAG-compliant focus indicators, semantic HTML, ARIA labels, skip link
- Direct billing information prominently featured across relevant pages
- Contact details (phone, email, address) centralized in partials for easy updates

author: ryan-stoffel
body:
## Summary

`screenshots.yml` no longer captures the same generic set on every PR, and no longer posts a comment. It runs only for PRs with the new `screenshots` label, captures only the scenes a hidden `<!-- wisp-media ... -->` block in the PR body names, and writes the result into a `## Screenshots` section of the body. Decision record: [0018](docs/decisions/0018-pr-visuals-on-request.md).

- **Trigger.** `labeled` (the `screenshots` label only), and `synchronize`, `reopened`, `edited` while the label is on; `workflow_dispatch` with a `pr` input. A job-level `if` stops unlabeled PRs before any runner starts. An `edited` event that changes neither the block nor the base branch is skipped.
- **Request block.** `mode: scene, scene` lines with modes `after`, `before-after`, `video`; scene names from `ci/screenshots/src/scenarios.ts`; `#` comments and blank lines skipped; each scene once; at most 10. No block, a bad line, or an unknown scene fails the new `request` job with a message saying what to fix, and that message goes into the section.
- **before-after.** The base is the merge base of the base branch and the head (compare API). `capture` computes that commit's app key with its own `app-cache-key`, restores it from ci.yml's cache (restored first and moved aside, since the path is part of the cache version), and builds it on a miss. The pair renders as a two-column table. A failure on the base app does not fail the job.
- **video.** Playwright `recordVideo` at the window size, the WebM kept, and a GIF preview made with Homebrew's ffmpeg (installed only when a video is requested; the runner image has none, and Playwright's ffmpeg only writes WebM). The body embeds the GIF and links the WebM.
- **Publish.** Same capture/publish split and security model: only `publish` has a write token, it installs nothing, and it treats both the artifact and the `request` job's outputs as untrusted. It re-reads the body right before the `PATCH` and replaces only the text between `<!-- wisp-media:start -->` and `<!-- wisp-media:end -->`. Untrusted text cannot write `<!--` into the section.
- `develop` requires only the `ci` check (read from the branch endpoint), so `screenshots` jobs showing as skipped on unlabeled PRs block nothing; protection is unchanged.

Closes #244

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `screenshots.yml` does nothing on a PR unless it has the `screenshots` label (create the label). It runs when the label is added, and on `synchronize`/`reopened`/`edited` while the label is present. A `workflow_dispatch` with a `pr` input runs it by hand.
- [ ] The PR body names what to capture in a hidden `wisp-media` block. Only the named scenes are captured. There is no fixed default set. A labeled PR with no block, or an unknown scene name, fails with a clear message.
- [ ] `before-after` captures the scene against the base branch's app (restored from ci.yml's cache for the base commit, built on a miss) and against the head app, and shows them side by side.
- [ ] `video` records the scene with Playwright's `recordVideo`, commits the video, and embeds an inline preview GitHub renders from a raw URL (GIF), linking the full video.
- [ ] Publish writes a `## Screenshots` section into the PR body between `<!-- wisp-media:start -->` and `<!-- wisp-media:end -->`, replacing only that section, and never posts a comment. It re-reads the body right before writing so a concurrent human edit is not lost. Later pushes replace the section.
- [ ] Removing the label leaves the section in place. Nothing is ever captured for an unlabeled PR.
- [ ] Images stay on the orphan branch `ci-screenshots` under `pr-<n>/<short-sha>/`, linked by commit-pinned raw URLs.
- [ ] The security model in `scripts/ci/README.md` (Screenshots) still holds: the write-token job runs no PR code and treats the artifact as untrusted, and the parsed request block is untrusted input too.
- [ ] `check-screenshots` covers request parsing and body-section replacement.
- [ ] If `screenshots` is a required status check on `develop`, it stops being required, or passes as skipped.
- [ ] `.github/pull_request_template.md` gets a Visuals section explaining when to add the label and how to write the block.
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` (the `screenshots.yml` bullet, and the Pull requests rules: the reviewer flags a UI PR without visuals and a non-UI PR with them) and `scripts/ci/README.md` describe the new behavior.
- [ ] Decision record `docs/decisions/0018-pr-visuals-on-request.md` supersedes the "every PR" rule.

## How it was tested

- `scripts/ci/check-screenshots` (Node 24.20): lint, type-check, 66 tests pass, including new ones for request parsing, the decision rules, section replacement (including markers quoted in inline code or fences), rendering of each mode, the GIF and WebM artifact checks, and the PR template's block.
- `actionlint` (with shellcheck) on all workflows, and `shellcheck scripts/ci/screenshots`: clean.
- `publish-screenshots --dry-run` on a synthetic capture with one scene per mode.
- End to end on this PR, with the label and a test block (`after: agents-window`, `before-after: startup`, `video: agents-window-host-menu`), all since removed:
  - [Run 36260948239](https://github.com/ryan-stoffel/wisp/actions/runs/36260948239): request 11 s, capture 1 min 16 s (head and base apps both restored from ci.yml's cache, ffmpeg poured in about 5 s, GIF at 10 fps and 800 px was 393 KB), publish 17 s. The section held all three modes, and the GIF runs from launch to the open host menu. It also exposed a bug: the Summary above quotes the start and end markers in inline code, and the first version matched those, so the section landed inside the Summary. Fixed in d74cab6: markers and the request block count only as lines of their own outside fenced code.
  - [Run 36261961892](https://github.com/ryan-stoffel/wisp/actions/runs/36261961892) (push of the fix): all three jobs pass and the section is appended after the block, with the prose intact. [Run 36261973831](https://github.com/ryan-stoffel/wisp/actions/runs/36261973831), from restoring the description at the same time, was skipped ("The edit changed neither the wisp-media block nor the base branch") and did not cancel the capture.
  - [Run 36262154088](https://github.com/ryan-stoffel/wisp/actions/runs/36262154088) (block changed to an unknown scene): `request` fails and lists the known scenes, `capture` never starts, and `publish` writes the problem into the section and fails.
  - After the label was removed, the last push's `screenshots` jobs are all skipped. The test block and section are removed from this description.

body:
# Pair the airbug decode arms at the same context depth

## The bug

`allpaka airbug` measured allpaka's decode at context depth 1 and llama's
decode at context depth `pp`, then divided the two.

The allpaka arm is depth 1 by construction: `crates/allpaka-cli/src/bench.rs`
runs the warmup, calls `session.truncate(0)`, forwards a single `[1u32]` seed
token, and only then starts the timer — and it records that regime as
`decode_measurement.context_tokens = Some(1)`. The field is documented as
"Tokens present in KV before the measured phase"
(`crates/allpaka-cli/src/benchmark_report.rs:47`), so the number is not a
label someone chose, it is what the phase actually consumed.

The llama arm asked for `-d opts.pp` and selected the row on
`n_depth == opts.pp`. `llama-bench --help` on the installed 0.24.0 defines
that flag as `-d, --n-depth <n>`, so the harness was charging llama a prefix
of `pp` KV tokens to read on every generated token while the allpaka side had
one. Every decode ratio this harness produced is therefore biased **in
allpaka's favour**, by however much attention costs at that depth.

Direction matters for how to read past numbers: fixing this makes the
allpaka-vs-llama decode ratio go up, not down.

## The fix

`DECODE_DEPTH = 1` is now the single source for both the `-d` argument and
the row filter, matching what `scripts/bench-compare.sh` already does (it
runs `-d 1`, selects `.n_depth==1`, and writes `decode_context_tokens: 1`
into its own comparison.json). The decode case contract says
`tg{TG}@context1` instead of `tg{TG}@pp{PP}`, which is what the row was
already measured in.

An `allpaka airbug` run now also refuses to proceed if the bench report
claims a decode depth other than 1. The shell harness has gated on exactly
this with `jq -e` for a while; the Rust harness only checked fast-path
completeness, so a change to `bench.rs` could have moved the allpaka regime
without moving the llama arm.

## Provenance

This is the `airbug_llama.rs` half of `a0f1583` ("Address PR review
feedback") from `themorelessly-consolidate-all-branches`, which reached main
only wrapped inside #5 — a PR that cannot be merged, because its
`da54055 Merge origin/main into …` pulled the September 15–17 state of
`gpu/metal.rs` back over main (+1487 / −2817). The `::airbug::` path prefix
and the pinned `rev = ce464fac` from that same commit are deliberately not
reproduced here: main pins airbug to `75b1321b` in the workspace manifest,
which supersedes them.

## Blast radius, measured rather than assumed

- No committed artifact carries the old `tg*@pp*` decode label: grepping
  `docs/` and `.airbug-bench/` for it returns nothing, so no published ratio
  has to be restated.
- The in-flight `2026-09-26-postflip-matrix` campaign is unaffected: its
  `preregistration.txt` takes decode through `scripts/bench-compare.sh`
  (already depth 1), and `scaling-1.sh` is prefill-only (`-p PP -n 0 -d 0`).

## What this is not

No performance claim. This is the instrument, not the load: it changes what
the harness asks llama-bench for, and the size of the resulting shift depends
on attention cost at the old depth, which is not measured here.

## Verification

Nothing was compiled locally, on purpose: the `series-1` gate is polling
`pgrep -xl cargo` and refuses to measure while a build is alive, so a local
`cargo check` would have extended the window it is waiting for. CI is the
verifier for this one. The change is confined to one file, and the only new
binding is a `u32` const used at three sites plus an `Option<usize>` field
deserialised from a report the crate already parses.

Related: #6 (merged), #7, and #5 (should be closed superseded).

author: echoes675
body:
## Summary — P1, with a deadline

`WebhookRenewalService` looped `run → Task.Delay(6 days) → run`, anchored to **process start**, while `RegisterForCalendarAsync` re-registers a channel only inside its final **24 hours** and Google's channels last ~**7 days from registration**. Those are only compatible if the process never restarts: every restart resets the 6-day timer while Google's clock keeps running.

**Live evidence, production, today:**

| | |
|---|---|
| Channels registered | 2026-09-21 13:13 |
| Channels expire | **2026-09-28 13:13** |
| Prod restarted (v1.1.22) | 2026-09-25 19:27 |
| Renewal pass ran | 19:29 — *"still valid until 09/28 …, skipping"* (correct) |
| Next pass as scheduled | **2026-10-01** — three days after expiry |

Nothing would have errored. Push notifications would simply have stopped and sync fallen back to hourly polling, so a change made on a phone takes up to an hour to reach the kiosk. **Unless this ships before Monday 13:13, production needs a redeploy inside the 24-hour window (after Sunday 13:13) instead.**

## The fix

Poll on a short interval (`Sync__WebhookRenewalPollInterval`, default **1 hour**) and let the existing 24-hour check decide what is due. Scheduling no longer depends on when the process started.

- **Startup validation** rejects a poll interval ≤ 0 (spin) or ≥ 24h (a pass could step over the window and reinstate the defect). The 24-hour window is now a shared constant the validation references, so the two numbers cannot drift apart.
- **An already-expired channel logs a Warning** — *"expired at {ExpiresAt}; push notifications have been missing since then"*. That state was previously indistinguishable from a quiet calendar, which is how this stayed hidden.
- Also fixes **FHQ-202** in `WebhookRegistrationService` (ambient `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow` → injected `TimeProvider`). Not optional here: the defect is about the relationship between two clocks, and the "restart at any point in the channel's life" test cannot exist without a controllable one.

## Telemetry: one Information line per pass

At hourly cadence the old per-channel lines would be ~190/day/env, so they move to Debug — but **no FamilyHQ environment emits Debug** (verified on dev and staging; it is issue 14 in `intermittent-issues.md`), so demoting alone would have deleted the evidence that renewal is alive. A renewal loop that silently died would then look exactly like one working perfectly — the same shape as the bug being fixed.

So each pass emits one Information summary: *"N calendar(s) checked, N re-registered, N found already expired. Next pass in 01:00:00."* Counts come from a `WebhookRegistrationTally` returned up from the registration service rather than state plumbed down; `IWebhookRegistrationService.RegisterForCalendarAsync` is unchanged, so existing tests were untouched.

**Three tests pin the summary to the Information level, not just its text** — flipping it to Debug fails them. Verified by doing exactly that, then restoring.

## Operators need do nothing

Every environment sets `Sync__WebhookRenewalInterval=6.00:00:00` today. That key still binds, is **ignored**, and the app logs one startup Warning naming it. Deleting it at leisure clears the warning. The new key defaults to 1 hour and need not be set. Setting it ≥24h or ≤0 fails fast at boot.

## Verification

- Branch build #1: SUCCESS — **1993 unit tests**
- Deploy-Dev **#764, #765, #766**: all SUCCESS
- The AC-1 test replays the hourly passes a process would make after restarting 0, 1, 25, 120 and 167 hours into a 7-day channel — anchored on production's real registration time — and asserts renewal happens strictly before expiry in every case.
- A pass with nothing due makes **no** Google API calls (`VerifyNoOtherCalls` on the whole client).

**Still open on the ticket:** verification across a real expiry boundary on preprod. That is also FHQ-167's last criterion, and closing it closes that too.

## Note for review

Adds `Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing` to `FamilyHQ.WebApi.Tests` — test-only and already centrally pinned in `Directory.Packages.props`, but flagged because package additions need sign-off.

## Summary
Two small fixes, both found by the PM while reviewing tonight's alpha.82/cuda-emit publish work.

**`scripts/publish.ps1`** hardcoded a single `$emitName` ('baracuda-cuda-emit') as the only crate off the lockstep version. `baracuda-cuda-parse` (#133/#135) joined that exception line too, but the script never learned about it — `baracuda-cuda-parse` stayed inside the lockstep set, so `$lockstep[0].version` picked whichever crate happened to sort first (right by luck on the alpha.82 run), and the "lockstep crates are NOT on one version" sanity warning would now fire every run on `baracuda-cuda-parse`'s `0.11.0` — a false positive, not real drift.

Generalizes `$emitName` to a named list, `$exceptionCrates`, excludes all of them from `$lockstep`, and runs the MAJOR.MINOR-vs-`unpopped` sanity check for each rather than just the first one.

**Verified with `-DryRun`:**
```
Exception line: baracuda-cuda-emit 0.11.0 (unpopped ^0.11.0)
Exception line: baracuda-cuda-parse 0.11.0 (unpopped ^0.11.0)
Version:  0.0.1-alpha.82
Publish:  71 crate(s)
Excluded: baracuda-kernels-bench, xtask, baracuda-examples (publish=false)
```
No false lockstep-drift warning, `Version` correctly resolves to the alpha line (not `0.11.0`), both exception crates print their own sanity line.

**Also removes `.publish-remaining.sh`**: an alpha.15-era relic — `VERSION` hardcoded to a release 67 versions behind current, with a hand-maintained 46-crate array against a real publishable set of 71. Running it would publish a subset and report success, since a crate missing from a hand-written array isn't an error condition to a script that never counts the real population. Confirmed unreferenced anywhere else in the tree (`git grep`) before removing.

Not merging — for review.

author: thomask33
body:
## Summary

Fix the `agentSession.queueDispatch.test.ts` flake where "rejected queued dispatch surfaces through onAcceptedPreStreamFailure" fails with `Failed to verify replacement: history write lock ... is no longer owned by this holder`. The failure is not in that test. It leaks from the test before it, "hard user interrupt cancels a pending provider-tool dispatch". That test now awaits its terminal policy instead of detaching it and sleeping 25 ms.

## Background

1. The hard-interrupt test calls `void runSessionTerminalPolicy(...)`. That helper calls `handleTurnAbort` directly, so `session.dispose()` does not wait for it. The test then sleeps 25 ms and runs `dispose()` and `cleanup()`, which deletes the temporary history root.
2. `handleTurnAbort` goes on to `handleStreamFailureForAutoRetry` → `compactionRecoveryBlocked` → `readCompactionCancellation` → `findCompactionReplacementWitness`. That last step takes the history write lock.
3. On a loaded runner the policy is still holding the lock when `cleanup()` deletes the directory. Its `assertStillOwned` then sees ENOENT and throws "no longer owned by this holder". Because the promise is detached, the rejection is unhandled, and Bun reports it against whichever test is running at that moment. The next test finishes in about 11–18 ms, so it caught the error every time.
4. Evidence: the lock file named in every CI failure is `history-841d9dd75447a8838e829a8872d58ed2.lock`. That is `sha256("queue-dispatch-hard-user-interrupt")[0:32]`, the previous test's workspace. The failing test's own workspace is `queue-dispatch-rejected`. Failing jobs: 108374042415 (run 36231001252), 108127165066 (run 36151943919), 108140776335 (merge group 36156039096).
5. The issue's first idea was that the `waitForCondition` bound was too short. The failing test ran for only 11–18 ms, far below that bound, so the timeout is not the cause.

## Implementation

In the hard-interrupt test only, `await runSessionTerminalPolicy(...)` replaces `void …` plus the 25 ms sleep. `handleTurnAbort` makes the queued-dispatch decision synchronously (`dispatchQueuedProviderToolEndMessageAfterAbort` → `sendQueuedMessages`) before it resolves. Awaiting it is therefore a stronger check than the old timed window, which a slow runner could close before the policy even reached that decision. No product code changes.

## Validation

**Deterministic pre-fix repro.** A temporary injection widens the time the policy holds the lock, and keeps the test open after cleanup so the escaped rejection is attributed to the test that leaked it:

```diff
--- a/src/node/services/historyService.ts  (findCompactionReplacementWitness, inside the write lock)
         const witness = await evidence.data();
+        await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 60));
         await assertStillOwned();
--- a/src/node/services/agentSession.queueDispatch.test.ts  (hard user interrupt test, finally)
       await cleanup();
+      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 400));
```

Before the fix, `bun test … -t "hard user interrupt"` failed 5 of 5 runs with the exact CI error:

```
error: Failed to verify replacement: history write lock /tmp/xum-test-history-…/locks/history-841d9dd75447a8838e829a8872d58ed2.lock is no longer owned by this holder (displaced or reclaimed); aborting before mutation
(fail) AgentSession queued message tool-call dispatch > hard user interrupt cancels a pending provider-tool dispatch [268.00ms]
```

With the same injection plus the fix: 5 of 5 runs passed.

**Whole-file audit.** I added a 150 ms delay under the lock, plus a 300 ms wait after each harness `cleanup()`, and ran the full file:
- Before the fix: 50 pass, 1 fail. The only failure was the hard-interrupt test, so no other test in the file leaks this way.
- After the fix: 51 pass, 0 fail.

**Mutation check.** I removed the `queuedProviderToolEndAbortInFlight` guard in `dispatchQueuedProviderToolEndMessageAfterAbort`. The fixed test still fails with `expect(received).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`, so the assertion still catches the regression it was written for.

author: noahbenson
body:
## `main` is red, and this fixes it

`test/broadcast.jl` — merged in #15 — fails on Julia 1.10 by comparing two reads of an **unset position** of a `PArray` built with `undef`. It passed #15's own CI by luck, which is what undefined behaviour does.

```
collect(rd) == collect(d) .+ 1
Evaluated: [3.0, 1.0, 1.0, 726.0] == [3.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1852.0]
```

The test was wrong to compare uninitialized values. But it was comparing them because the library let it, and what the library does there is the bug:

```julia
#error("PArray has unset values and no default")
return Array{T}(undef, 1)[1]
```

That returns **fresh uninitialized memory on every read**. Two consequences:

- **Nondeterminism.** Reading the same position twice gives different values, so an expression as simple as `collect(d) .+ 1` is not self-consistent. It also allocates a one-element array per read.
- **Memory safety.** For a `T` holding references, the value returned is a pointer that must never be dereferenced. For a reference-holding `Array` built with `undef`, Julia raises `UndefRefError`; this returned a copy of whatever the allocator had left behind.

The author knew — that commented-out line is theirs — and an array with no default is supposed to hold a value at every position, so reaching this point means a position was never set.

## The fix

It raises, with a message saying what to do about it.

**This is a behaviour change.** Code that read unset positions of an `undef`-built `PArray` was reading garbage and will now get an error. That is the point of it, but it is the one place in this cycle where the change is not purely additive, so it is worth a look rather than a merge.

The broadcast test that found it now sets every position before reading, and asserts the raise for the unset case.

## Verification

Full suite: **2,537,693 pass, 0 fail** — nothing else in the suite read an unset position of a default-less array, so the raise breaks nothing.

author: jackzampolin
body:
## Problem

The `gents` lib test binary has died with SIGABRT on macOS main CI since #1674 merged: runs 36250219270 (83c36f755), 36251834687 (1eba27072) and 36254905978 (23e2f4516), job `rust-and-cli (runtime)`. The abort prints nothing, and it hit about 93s into the binary in all three runs.

## Root cause

`lldb` on the aborting process shows `abort()` called from `wasmtime::runtime::vm::sys::unix::machports::handler_thread`. The Wasmtime 44 build that Afterburner uses keeps the macOS default of Mach-port trap handling. Its process-wide handler thread blocks in `mach_msg(MACH_RCV_MSG | MACH_RCV_INTERRUPT)` and calls `abort()` on any other return. `--nocapture` shows the message `mach_msg failed with 268451845 (10004005)`, which is `MACH_RCV_INTERRUPTED`. The runtime installs signal handlers, such as tokio's `SIGCHLD` for child processes. The kernel can deliver one of those signals to any thread that doesn't block it, including the handler thread, and the whole process then aborts. The message goes nowhere visible: the handler thread inherits the output capture of the test that created the first engine, so libtest drops it.

The exposure predates #1674. That PR added plugin calls in more places (graph pipeline plugin nodes, the executor and tool tests), which widened the window. The failure is not limited to tests: a desktop or CLI runtime on macOS that ran a plugin and then reaped a child process could abort the same way.

## Fix

`PluginRunner::call` is the only runtime call site of `run_afb_bytes`. Before the first run, it now creates Afterburner's shared engine (`shared_epoch_vm`, the same engine `run_afb_bytes` uses for wall-clock bounds) on a short-lived thread that blocks every signal. The Wasmtime handler thread inherits that mask, so no signal reaches it. The function does nothing outside macOS.

It fails closed. If the masked thread cannot be spawned or joined, `pthread_sigmask` fails, or the engine cannot be created, the error is cached in a `OnceLock<Result<(), String>>` and returned from every `PluginRunner::call`. No call then creates the engine unprotected.

Opting out of Mach ports (`macos_use_mach_ports(false)`, as `callback/wasm.rs` and DefraDB lens already do on Wasmtime 46) is not possible from Gents. Afterburner exposes no Wasmtime configuration, and Wasmtime 44 panics in `init_traps` on an engine whose trap mode differs from the first engine's. The durable upstream fix is for Afterburner to set `macos_use_mach_ports(false)`.

## Validation

- New regression test `plugin::tests::trap_handler::a_signal_on_every_thread_after_a_plugin_call_does_not_abort` (macOS only). It runs itself in a child process, makes one plugin call, then sends `SIGUSR2` (with a handler installed) to every other thread. Next it runs a guest whose out-of-bounds load faults on the guard page, so the trap goes through the Mach exception handler thread. It asserts that the trap comes back as a typed `trapped` error, then that a normal call still succeeds. The child process has a 120s timeout. With the fix call disabled, the child died with SIGABRT and printed `mach_msg failed with 268451845`. With the fix it passes.
- Full `gents` lib binary on macOS (`--test-threads 8`, `RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216`):
  - Before the fix: SIGABRT in 4 of 4 runs.
  - After the fix: 3 of 3 runs passed, including `cargo test -p gents --lib` at 1b852c179 (3119 passed). `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean.
- On Linux, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` passes at 1b852c179, and `cargo test -p gents --no-fail-fast` passes: 16 of 16 test binaries green.
- An earlier Linux `cargo test -p gents` run on a loaded host failed `control_watcher_publishes_reconciled_snapshot_after_relevant_update` and `native_filesystem_deadline_preempts_single_poll_blocker_and_advances_queue`. The fix compiles to nothing on Linux, and both tests pass in isolation. The first of these also failed on main CI at f4157d6e1, and the second failed on unmodified main on the same host. They are separate timing defects.
- The change is a no-op on Linux, and the aborts never reproduced there (3 unmodified lib runs had no SIGABRT).

author: heath-freenome
body:
### Reasons for making this change

Fixes #5318

`@rjsf/daisyui`'s `FieldTemplate` decided whether a field's label belongs after the input — the checkbox layout — from the schema type alone:

```tsx
const isCheckbox = schema.type === 'boolean' && uiOptions.widget !== 'select';
```

Every `boolean` rendered through something other than a checkbox therefore lost its title, because that branch expects the widget to render its own label and a `radio` or a custom widget doesn't. `getDisplayLabel()` returns `true` for those cases — it exempts a `boolean` from label-hiding as soon as a `ui:widget` is set — so the template was discarding a label the field had asked for.

The decision is now keyed off the widget that will render, **resolved** rather than matched against how `ui:widget` spells it:

```tsx
const { widget } = uiOptions;
const resolvedWidget =
  widget && hasWidget(schema, widget, registry.widgets) ? getWidget(schema, widget, registry.widgets) : undefined;
const widgetRendersLabel = resolvedWidget === CheckboxWidget || resolvedWidget === ToggleWidget;
```

Resolving is what makes the alias (`'checkbox'`), the registry key (`'CheckboxWidget'`) and the component itself reach the same answer; comparing spellings meant the other two rendered the label twice, and a consumer registering their own widget under the `CheckboxWidget` key had the template suppress its label while that widget rendered none — a field with no visible title, the symptom this issue is about. `hasWidget()` guards the lookup, since `getWidget()` throws for a name nothing is registered under. A widget that *wraps* daisyui's checkbox or toggle is a component of its own and gets this template's label in addition to the one it renders; guessing the other way would leave a control replaced by a label-less widget with no accessible name at all, which is the worse of the two failures.

Measured against `@rjsf/core` with `{ type: 'boolean', title: 'Agree' }`:

| `ui:widget` | daisyui before | daisyui after | core |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `radio` | **no label** | label | label |
| a custom widget | **no label** | label | label |
| `checkbox` | label (after the input) | label (after the input) | label |
| none | label (after the input) | label (after the input) | label |
| `select` | label | label | label |
| `hidden` | no label | no label | no label |

Two things fall out of keying off the widget, each with a test:

- A nullable boolean (`type: ['boolean', 'null']`, which `getSchemaType()` treats as a boolean) with `ui:widget: 'checkbox'` no longer renders its title twice. The old raw `schema.type === 'boolean'` comparison didn't match it, so both the template and `CheckboxWidget` drew a label.
- The description is gated on the same check, so a field rendered as a checkbox or a toggle no longer renders its description twice. Those widgets render their own; every other theme already gates this.

**`FieldTemplate` also honors the `hidden` prop now**, rendering only the field's children the way core and every other theme do. daisyui destructured `hidden` but never used it, so a hidden field was laid out with a label, description and error area around an invisible input. Hidden *booleans* were only label-free by accident, through the branch this PR narrows, so the guard is what keeps the `hidden` row of the table above correct. Two consequences worth calling out:

- A hidden field no longer renders the surrounding `rjsf-field` wrapper, visible in the `hidden field` snapshot.
- The early return skips `WrapIfAdditionalTemplate`, so an `additionalProperties` entry hidden via `ui:widget: 'hidden'` loses its key input and remove button. That is what core and every other theme do, but it is a behavior change for daisyui.

**The label is no longer empty, and it now names what it labels.** Two pre-existing defects in the same label:

- `FieldTemplate` rendered a label whenever `displayLabel` was set — which defaults to true and says nothing about whether a title exists — so every root field and every array item got an empty, padded `<label>`. A field with no title now renders no label element, as core's `Label` does. The lone required `*` goes with it: array items are required by design (`isItemRequired`), so daisyui drew a bare asterisk beside nothing on every untitled item.
- The label named nothing at all for any widget rendering a *group* of controls. `RadioWidget`, `CheckboxesWidget`, `RatingWidget` and `AltDateWidget` put the field's `id` on no element, so `htmlFor` pointed at an id absent from the document — a visible title, no accessible one, and clicking it focused nothing. Those widgets now mark their group with `role='radiogroup'`/`role='group'`, carry the field's `id` as core's radio group does, and name themselves from the label through `aria-labelledby`. `AltDateTimeWidget` inherits this from `AltDateWidget`. `DateWidget`/`DateTimeWidget` already had the `id` on their popup trigger but no accessible name, so they name themselves from the label **together with their own contents**, which carry the selected value.

**Why a reference rather than the label's text, and why not `titleId()`.** Two earlier versions of this were wrong, both caught before merge:

1. Identifying the label with `titleId(id)` put a duplicate id in the DOM — `TitleFieldTemplate` already claims it for the same field, so an `additionalProperties` object rendered both its label and its title as `id="root_foo__title"`, in six snapshot cases.
2. Copying the label's text into `aria-label` instead copied the wrong string. The `label` a widget is handed is computed separately from the one `FieldTemplate` renders: for an `additionalProperties` entry the template's is the key while the widget's is the schema title (visible `foo`, announced `Extra`), and under `deprecatedHandling: 'label'` only the template's is decorated (visible `Agree (deprecated)`, announced `Agree`). A name that isn't the visible label fails WCAG 2.5.3.

So the group points at the label element, identified by a new `fieldLabelId()` (`${id}__label`), and its accessible name is whatever the label displays — there are tests for both cases above. The label's text is still carried as an `aria-label`, which `aria-labelledby` overrides wherever it resolves, because the two flags follow different rules for a `boolean`: `BooleanField` reads `ui:options.label` while `getDisplayLabel()` suppresses a boolean's label unless the `ui:widget` **key** is set, so setting the widget through `ui:options.widget` — the documented equivalent spelling — rendered no label while the group pointed at one. That fallback is lossy by the same argument as (2) above, and is documented as such; the root cause is `getDisplayLabel()` keying off `uiSchema['ui:widget']` rather than the resolved option, which is worth its own issue.

A widget claims the reference only when it has a label to be named by, so a field with no title, where the template renders no label, gets none. Two labels do still share that id wherever RJSF renders two `FieldTemplate`s for one field id, which already gives that control two `<label htmlFor>` today — a `oneOf` of constants, and a layout placing a field twice; it is documented on the generator, and a reference resolves to the field's own label rather than the option's. The shared shape lives in `getGroupProps()` beside `getDaisy()` rather than being repeated in four widgets.

Snapshot impact: 62 empty labels disappear, 196 force-hidden labels go with `BaseInputTemplate`'s, every remaining label gains its `fieldLabelId()` id, and the group widgets gain their `id`, `role` and `aria-labelledby`. The `RatingWidget` unit snapshots render the widget with no template, so their reference has no target within the fragment; in a form the template supplies it.

**The three remaining label defects are fixed here too**, added to #5318 rather than filed separately ([comment](https://github.com/rjsf-team/react-jsonschema-form/issues/5318#issuecomment-5849119757)). Each is

author: tin-berri
body:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Historical savings disappear from the cost comparison
- Unknown-estimate requests inflate the displayed actual spend

How it solves it:

- Combine historical and newer savings with matching eligible costs
- Recover historical costs from bounded, reconciled retained logs

Intentional product change: the savings card compares eligible requests across both estimation methods. Unknown estimates are excluded, the duplicate actual-spend row is removed, and LLM/classification subtotals use the same eligible requests. Partial sessions with multiple baseline models omit the ambiguous model label

## User Flow

Before: historical savings disappear and the card mixes different requests

1. Open http://127.0.0.1:48182/cost-optimization/ and select Auto-Router, then Usage
2. Select `combined-savings-complete` over the last 30 days
3. See $0.50 saved, $109 actual, a second $1 actual row, and $1.50 baseline at 33%

![Before: history omitted and actual spend includes unknown usage](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f1c0d487-7293-44ea-b940-c0f526253aee)

After: old and new savings, actual spend, baseline and percentage describe the same requests

1. Open http://127.0.0.1:48182/cost-optimization/ and select Auto-Router, then Usage
2. Select `combined-savings-complete` over the last 30 days
3. See $30 saved, $10 actual, $9.90 LLM, $0.10 classification, $40 baseline, and 75% savings

![After: old and new savings use the same eligible requests](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c70df546-304f-45df-8c91-91b987386491)

## Validation

The restored breakdown passes 41 endpoint tests, 37 PostgreSQL tests and 63 dashboard tests. Earlier validation passed 277 backend tests. Recovery covers positive, zero and negative savings, user scope, missing/corrupt logs, changed request counts and skipped classification. Mutating the classifier subtotal to include unknown requests fails six regressions; removing the partial-session baseline-label guard also fails its regression. Earlier history and unknown-spend mutations also failed

Scoped Python/dashboard lint, type and budget gates, and generated API-type synchronization pass on the committed tip. Live benchmark and session endpoints agree on $30 saved, $10 eligible actual and $40 baseline. The dashboard shows $9.90 LLM plus $0.10 classification and uses eligible requests for the classification rate

142 added test lines versus 318 production lines, excluding generated types (0.45:1). No migrations or spend-write changes

CI and patch coverage pass on 5a40335a3d. Veria reports no security issues on that commit. The earlier Greptile finding is fixed; fresh Greptile and Bugbot reviews have been requested

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The affected test files pass locally
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR solves one specific problem
- [ ] Greptile confidence is at least 4/5 before maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Real localhost proxies and browser, using the same synthetic PostgreSQL records on both revisions. Historical request: $9 actual including $0.10 classification, $29.50 recorded savings. New request: $1 actual, $0.50 saved. Unknown request: $99 actual with no estimate. A second identical session omits the retained historical log. This reads recorded charges, so provider inference does not apply

The requests below use an admin key for benchmarks and the owning virtual key for sessions

```sh
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" "$PROXY/auto_router/benchmarks?start_date=2026-09-26&end_date=2026-09-26"
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIRTUAL_KEY" "$PROXY/auto_router/session?session_id=combined-savings-complete"
```

### Before (40297e6268)

#### Historical, new and unknown requests

1. Run both requests with `PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:48282`
2. Both report $0.50 savings, $1 eligible actual and $1.50 eligible baseline; the dashboard shows 33% and $109 actual, as pictured above

#### Missing historical log

1. Repeat for `combined-savings-missing`
2. Recorded historical savings remain absent: $0.50 saved, $1.50 baseline and 33%

### After (5a40335a3d)

#### Historical, new and unknown requests

1. Run both requests with `PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:48284`
2. Both report $30 savings, $10 eligible actual, $40 eligible baseline and two estimated requests; benchmarks also return $0.10 eligible classification. The dashboard shows $9.90 LLM, $0.10 classification and 75%, as pictured above

#### Missing historical log

1. Repeat for `combined-savings-missing`
2. Recorded savings remain $30; actual, LLM, classification and baseline rows show Unavailable, and the percentage is omitted

## Type

Bug Fix

## Caveats

### Medium

- Missing retained logs can leave historical comparisons unavailable
- Recovery stops at two seconds or the configured row cap

### Low

- Date ranges still count whole overlapping sessions

## Final Attestation

- [x] Regressions cover history, unknown costs, missing logs and changed counts

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Benchmark and session savings math now depends on bounded spend-log scans and reconciliation; incorrect recovery could misstate baselines, though mismatches suppress breakdown fields and preserve recorded savings totals.
> 
> **Overview**
> Auto-router **benchmarks and session APIs** now keep **recorded historical savings** visible while aligning actual spend, baseline, classifier subtotals, and savings % to the **same eligible requests**—historical estimates plus newer tracked estimates, excluding turns with no savings estimate (including high-spend “unknown” requests that previously inflated actual spend).
> 
> When session rollups have **partial estimate coverage**, a new **bounded spend-log reconciliation** (`historical_session_comparisons`) joins retained `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` to rollups, verifies totals, and backfills comparison fields; failures degrade gracefully (savings dollars preserved, cost breakdown marked unavailable). Benchmark aggregation adds **`savings_estimated_classifier_cost`** and a **`savings_comparison_complete`** gate before exposing baseline math.
> 
> **`baseline_model`** now derives from **`baseline_models`** and is suppressed when partial coverage and multiple baselines would mislabel the counterfactual. The cost-optimization dashboard updates copy and layout: single “total estimated savings” hero, eligible-request spend rows, and a message when historical savings exist without matching cost details.
>

author: qoeop
body:
## What this changes

**Option D.** A pull request's `rust tests` reuses the workspace artifacts that main's Rust cache holds, by giving cargo honest mtimes instead of checkout's all-new ones.

- **Main records** (`scripts/ci/workspace_mtimes.py record`, runs when the job saves caches). Before anything compiles, it writes the commit it builds and the time T into `target/rust-tests-linux-x86/source-marker/CACHEDIR.TAG`. rust-cache keeps a nested target's `CACHEDIR.TAG` through both its save-time cleanup and its partial-match pre-clean; every other file at the target root is deleted.
- **A pull request reuses** (`… reuse`, pull_request and merge_group only).
  - Every tracked file unchanged since that commit is set to T − 1, and every changed file to now.
  - Units main built in the recording run are newer than T, so they stay fresh.
  - Units an earlier run left in the cache are older than T, so they rebuild. Stale leftovers are stale by construction.
  - Any unit that reads a changed file rebuilds, whatever kind of file it is.
- **Commit times are never used** (the refused `restore-mtime`). A pull request's commits can predate the cache, which would pass stale outputs as fresh.
- **Falls back to the checkout's mtimes** (a full rebuild, with the reason printed) on any of:
  - no marker;
  - an unreachable cached commit;
  - a failed diff;
  - a change to the workspace `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, any `.cargo/`, `rust-toolchain*` or `build-env.mk`.
- **The self-check covers all tracked files, not only `.rs`.** After setting mtimes, `verify` compares the two trees blob by blob, a route independent of `git diff`. Every file whose content differs must be newer than T, every other file must be exactly T − 1, and a file left wrong fails the step by name. That covers `include_str!`/`include_bytes!` inputs (SQL, JSON, goldens) and `rerun-if-changed` paths as much as sources.
- **Main never reuses.** Its full build is what records, and it stays the backstop. The daily serial verdict is unchanged.
- **Cache entry.** `rust-cache-workspace-crates` goes back to `"true"` for this job.

## Why a member crate's Cargo.toml does not fall back

Measured on a disposable a ← b ← c workspace through this script's real record → build → commit → reuse → build.

| Change to a's manifest | Result |
|---|---|
| no change | a, b, c all `Fresh` |
| a source edit | all three rebuild |
| added feature, version bump, `[lib] path`, `build =`, `links`, `edition`, `[lints]` | a, b and c rebuild, each time |
| description only | all `Fresh` |

cargo fingerprints what it compiles from, so the field-level result needs no manifest fallback beyond the workspace root.

## Expected benefit, stated honestly

These are predictions from `--timings` (run 36262527769) and the dependency graph resolved with the test build's features. The model's positive control is within 6%: it predicts model/core recompiles of 651/657 s against 692/675 s measured.

- rust-cache saves only when its key changes. The key hashes manifests and lock but not sources, so a pull request recompiles **the last saved commit → its merge tree**, not just its own diff. Main rotated the key 6 times in 2 days.
- Simulated over main's last 53 commits, on an EPYC 7763 where a full build is 670 s:
  - **mean ≈ 406–414 s, median 481 s**, this last figure optimistic because it assumes a main build saves right after each rotation;
  - about 4% of changes hit a root-level fallback;
  - changes reaching `vibe-data` (72% of the full build) cost about 481 s.
- **The own-diff estimate given earlier (mean 176 s) was wrong for this mechanism.** No "≈ 11 minutes" claim is made here.

## Proof

- **`scripts/ci/test-workspace-mtimes.bash`** (pre-commit and test-plan). It is built on `scripts/lib/git-isolation.bash` (#1096).
  - Reuse sets T − 1 and after-T correctly.
  - `verify` fails by name for a missed source file and for a missed `include_str!`-only input, and for an unchanged file bumped to now.
  - A member manifest change is reused.
  - A workspace manifest change, a missing marker and an unreachable commit fall back.
  - Mutations that each turn it red: `verify` never failing; every file set to T − 1; the fallback check removed; member manifests falling back again.
- **test-plan pins:** the job caches workspace crates, `record` runs only when saving, `reuse` only on pull_request and merge_group, and nothing else calls the script.

## Acceptance, after merge (Lane 3)

- On the first few pull requests after main saves an entry with a marker, the `Compiling` count equals the dependency-graph model's prediction ±2.
- A pull request touching no Rust shows 0.
- The fallback has fired in CI with its reason printed. This pull request's own run shows it: main's current entry has no marker.
