body:
## Summary

Plan 7, the last plan in the roadmap: Soundcheck gets a signed 1.0.0 release, its icon, the Manuscript look in the system UI, the staff and keyboard on the Warm-up screen, and hands-free Metronome control. It also fixes what the reviews and the phone check turned up.

- **Signed release:**
  - The release is signed from a gitignored `keystore.properties`, the same as the other apps. The key lives at `~/.android/soundcheck-release.jks`.
  - A release build without the file stops, with a clear message, before anything is packaged. Debug builds and `./gradlew test` never need it.
  - `-Psoundcheck.signWithDebugKey=true` makes a test release that prints a warning and is versioned `1.0.0-debugkey`.
  - Debug builds are `org.pashri.soundcheck.debug` ("Soundcheck debug"), so they install beside the release. The release is `org.pashri.soundcheck` 1.0.0.
- **Icon:** "Waveform on a staff", vermilion bars on a faint staff over paper, as an adaptive vector. It has a themed one-colour layer and a bars-only notification icon.
- **The Manuscript look everywhere:**
  - The launch window and splash are paper by day and ink at night.
  - Every Material colour slot and the type scale are mapped to the Manuscript palette and faces, so dialogs, menus and fields are no longer lavender or Roboto.
  - At the largest font and display sizes, buttons keep their padding, words never split (option rows wrap, and header notes move under the title), and ♭ ♮ ♯ are drawn the same size.
- **Warm-up playing screen:**
  - The Pattern is drawn on a staff at its real pitches. The clef comes from the Range: treble for Soprano and Alto, treble with an 8 below for Tenor, bass for Bass.
  - Notes are spelled from the key's letter, with courtesy naturals, ledger lines and beams. A vermilion note moves in time with the piano, and the staff keeps the same height through a Step.
  - Below the staff, a keyboard shows the Step's Range, the key and the top note. The key being sung looks pressed down, including when it is the key or the top note.
  - Only the moving note redraws each beat.
- **Hands-free Metronome:**
  - There is one app-level media session. The headphone button goes to whichever tool started last.
  - The Metronome keeps playing with the screen off or the app in the background, with a notification that has Pause/Play and Close. The headset toggles it.
  - Returning to its tab after an off-screen pause shows PAUSED.
  - It asks for notification permission on first Start. If notifications are off, a pause ends it.
  - There is no media session while mixing, not even before the settings load.
- **Smaller fixes:**
  - A pause you didn't make says why: a failed output, or another app using the sound.
  - The Tuner says when another app has the microphone.
  - Step menu moves go by Step, not by stale position.
  - A failed export deletes only a file it has just created and that was empty. It never deletes an existing backup.
  - Tuner tests fail instead of hanging.
- **README:** covers the icon, the staff, the Metronome button, night mode and the release build.

## Test plan

- [x] `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest`: 881 JVM tests, 0 failures. They cover:
  - clef choice and spelling in every key;
  - staff and keyboard layout, and the note-only redraw (`assertSame`);
  - theme slots and contrast;
  - icon geometry;
  - the signing configuration;
  - headphone routing and the session rules;
  - the Metronome lifecycle and notifications;
  - pause reasons, the Tuner's silenced state, Step moves and export cleanup.

  The key guards have recorded mutation checks.
- [x] `tools/run-native-tests.sh`: 32/32.
- [x] `./gradlew test` passes without `keystore.properties`. A keyless release build fails with the README message. The signed release verifies as CN=Patrick Linton.
- [x] A review after each task, a whole-branch review and one final fix wave, then reviews of each phone-check change.
- [x] On the emulator (Pixel 9, API 35), all 14 items:
  - the icon, including themed, and launch with no flash by day or night;
  - every screen and dialog in both themes;
  - the staff in all three clefs, with a courtesy natural;
  - the largest sizes (found and fixed), rotation, navigation and TalkBack labels;
  - media keys, with no session while mixing on a cold launch;
  - export and import;
  - the minified release.
- [x] On the Pixel, running the signed release:
  - the icon and themed icon;
  - piano and staff timing;
  - the Metronome on the Shokz, with the screen off, toggling;
  - hands-free Warm-up 1/2/3 presses and the lock screen;
  - the pressed key.
- [ ] Mic features on the emulator: not checked there, because the emulator hangs when the microphone is used. Recording was checked on the phone in Plan 6.
- [ ] The Tuner's "another app is using the microphone" message during a phone call: skipped on the phone. The app on screen always wins the mic from a recorder, so only a call can trigger the message.
- [ ] TalkBack swiping and double-tap recording: labels checked through uiautomator, but not with TalkBack itself.

author: cklxx
body:
## What

Fixes the residual first-use JIT stall left after #839/#840. The remaining
mixed-stream recompiles were **not** the linear GEMM M axis (an isolated
`T.const`→`T.dynamic` probe was elementwise-exact but measured **2× slower** on
sm70 — not pursued). Axis was named with a backend specialization-shape probe
on V100 (isolated cold cache, homogeneous vs frame-60 mixed traffic):

- S=1 plain decode Mb is constant (graph-captured).
- **S=2 spec verify in the host-eager path** grew its packed table width
  `Mb` with the selected-page ramp of a fresh sequence
  (6,9,13,17,20,23,27,31,129,193 pages). #839's cap applies only when the tick
  `has_prefill`; these rows are `decoding`, so they took their data width.
- `paged_attention_split` and `write_tokens_f32` specialize on `Mb`; each ramp
  value compiled a new cubin on the first mixed stream of a new process.

## Change

Host-eager **pure decode/verify** ticks round `Mb` up to a fixed **32-page
bucket**; padded columns are filled with a reserved **sentinel** pool block and
sit past every row's causal bound (`n = SeqLens-SeqQLens+tt+1` in the split
kernel; write_tokens only writes `t < SeqQLens`). Compile shape changes,
numerics do not.

- `SparseTracker.verify_mb_bucket=32`, `sentinel_page`.
- `PagedKvPool.reserve_sentinel()`: last block held out of the allocator,
  excluded from `used_blocks`.
- Eager packed attention table **and** eager `own_table` (write_tokens) both
  bucket; prefill ticks keep #839's cap; the graph/device captured path is
  untouched (its width is fixed per verify width).

`# ponytail: Mb rounds up to 32 pages, wastes <=31 table columns; finer buckets
if a profile shows them`

## Gates

CPU (this PR, green):
- solo S=1/S=2 verify and mixed prefill+decode ticks are **token-identical**
  with bucketing on (32) vs exact data width (`bucket=1`, no padded columns);
- eager verify width is one context-independent bucket multiple across 10-/16-
  page contexts (updated structural test).

Pending device run on V100 (will post numbers before merge/release):
1. sentinel block filled NaN → output bit-identical; then deliberately relax
   the OOB bound by one so the kernel reads a padded column — that control must
   go RED;
2. cold-cache fresh process, same mixed script twice: report first-pass new
   cubins, second pass must be 0;
3. concurrent 5.2k max frame gap < 1 s (old p99 5550 / max 9729 ms);
4. decode tok/s vs pre-change interleaved in one process, regression < 2%.

Does not touch `src/tilerl/static`.

author: ilkertskn
body:
…ropping it on SQL Server

On SQL Server 2022+ (compatibility level 160), TranslateTrimStartEnd accepts any single argument, but ProcessTrimStartEnd only handled SqlConstantExpression. A captured variable or parameter (`var c = 'S'; ... x.TrimStart(c)`) therefore fell through and the call was translated to the one-argument `LTRIM(x)`, silently trimming whitespace instead of the requested character and returning wrong rows.

A non-constant `char` argument is now passed to LTRIM/RTRIM as a parameter with the char type mapping, and a non-constant `char[]` argument makes the translation fail (as SQLite already does) instead of being dropped.

Adds parameterized TrimStart/TrimEnd tests to StringTranslationsTestBase with SQL Server, SQLite and Cosmos overrides.

author: lagop
body:
Three findings from trying to walk the sign-up flow as a customer would, plus one the accent guard uncovered on its way. ## `/register` answers 404 The middleware listed `/register` in both `publicPaths` and its matcher. That route does not exist. The sign-up page is `/signup`, which was not listed at all. Nothing changed for users — this middleware returns `NextResponse.next()` on every branch — but it was dead configuration pointing at a dead URL. ## The login page asked a question with no answer ```tsx

{t("login.no_account")}

``` Plain text. "¿No tienes cuenta?" and no link, no anchor, nothing. The sign-up page links *back* to the login form, so the path was one-way: anyone landing on `/login` without an account was at a dead end. ## The Spanish copy had almost no accents `messages/es.json`: **1695 strings, 47 of them containing an accent.** Including the entire sign-up form — the first thing a prospective Spanish salon reads: ``` signup.fields.salon: "Nombre del salon" signup.fields.phone: "Telefono" signup.fields.password: "Contrasena (min. 8 caracteres)" signup.languageEs: "Espanol" signup.terms: "Acepto los terminos y condiciones y la politica de privacidad." ``` For a product sold in Spain this is not a typographic preference. Copy without accents reads as unfinished, and the first screen is the worst place to suggest that. **327 strings corrected; 376 now carry an accent.** ### Method Diacritics only. Every replacement is the same word with its accent, applied as a whole word, so no wording, order or placeholder could change. A blind find-and-replace would have been wrong, so words that exist *both* ways were excluded from the automatic pass and read one occurrence at a time: | Word | Decision | |---|---| | `esta` | 22 occurrences: 6 were the verb (`está`), 16 the demonstrative — left alone | | `mas` | all 11 were the quantifier → `más` | | `estas` | all 7 were "¿Estás seguro…?" → `estás` | | `aun` | all 5 meant "todavía" → `aún` | | `publico` | 4 adjectives → `público`; `Publica tu widget` is the imperative, left alone | | `si` | only `saas.yes` was the affirmation → `Sí`; the rest are conditionals | | `salones` | left alone — the plural of *salón* drops the accent, the stress moves | | `solo` | left alone — the RAE has not required the accent since 2010 | ### Two replacements had to be reverted Caught by auditing every changed token for things that are not prose: ``` mi_salon_bot -> mi_salón_bot a Telegram username, which cannot contain an accent {salon} -> {salón} an interpolation key; the user would have seen the literal braces ``` The first slipped past my initial audit because the accent sat two letters away from the underscore rather than adjacent to it. The token-level check found it. **Verified:** 1696 keys before and after, none lost or added, and **zero interpolation placeholders altered**. ### The guard Two rules, both chosen so a correct string cannot trip them: 1. Singular `-ción` / `-sión` always carry the accent. The plural does not (*acción → acciones*), so the rule ignores a trailing `s`. 2. A curated list of words that do not exist in Spanish unaccented. The spec also asserts that no ambiguous word appears in that list, so the guard cannot start failing correct copy as the list grows. Wired into `npm test`. Verified non-vacuous: un-accenting two strings fails both rules. ## And one the guard found by itself `"session"` tripped the `-sión` rule — because an **untranslated English string was sitting in the Spanish file**. Following it led to six `alert()` / `confirm()` calls with hardcoded English, in files that use `t()` everywhere else (`payments/page.tsx` calls it 86 times): ```tsx alert("Failed to create checkout session"); if (!confirm("Are you sure you want to cancel your subscription?")) return; ``` So a salon owner in Spain hit English at exactly the moments that matter: a failed checkout, cancelling a subscription, a rejected deposit. All six now go through `t()`, with Spanish written for the situation rather than translated literally. Also drops a dead entry from both message files: someone had added `"Failed to create checkout session"` as a top-level key named after the English sentence, while the code passed the same literal to `alert()` and never looked it up. ## Verification - `npm test`: 125 assertions across four suites, all passing. - `tsc --noEmit`: clean — which also confirms every `t()` I introduced is in scope. ## Separately noted, not fixed here `rebooking.whatsapp.body` tells clients "Responde SÍ o usa este enlace". Nothing in the backend listens for that: `whatsapp.service.ts` matches only `stop`, `unsubscribe`, `cancelar` and `baja`. Replying does nothing. (Correcting the spelling was safe *because* no matcher exists.) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: bsletten
body:
Step 2 of the book review after core 0.1.72 (ledger [#521](http://localhost:1060/l/default/item/521)); closes the tracing half of [#167](http://localhost:1060/l/default/item/167).

**New chapter — "Tracing a resolution"**, in "Beyond one host" before "The machine client". `trace` was a command in two chapters and a subject in none. Now: the `TraceEvent` fields as a table; `set_tracer` versus `issue_traced` and why they are exclusive (a per-connection trace wants one destination; the global slot is the single-tenant path); and the three kernel-attached facts, each shown:

- **A denial** — Rust: `issue_traced` of a `Sink` on `counter` under a narrow capability returns `Denied` and records one event with `("denied", "urn:cap:tutorial:counter:write")`, `started`/`ended` `None`, `cache_hit` false. REPL: one line, `cap ✗ denied: …`, because `run_trace` renders the tree only on `Ok` — stated honestly; the event exists, the REPL does not draw it.
- **An alias hop** — REPL: `trace urn:fn:toUpper` through the CLI's own `urn:fn:` → `urn:iki:fn:` rule renders `alias=urn:fn:toUpper -> urn:iki:fn:toUpper` on the node, and the target is the canonical name.
- **A confined miss** — Rust: a `Confine`d endpoint's `Unresolved` is traced with `("scope", "urn:iki:tutorial:ctx:document severed")` and `("scope-unresolved", <title>)`, and no `denied` note.

Plus the wire (spans come back; a mount is stitched under its node) and a "What not to assume" list: tree only on success; no scope in the REPL; a successful `urn:kernel:*` op records no event, only its denial; installing a tracer to see denials builds an event per resolution.

**Also**
- `cli-vocabulary.txt`: `urn:kernel:aliases` and `urn:fn:toUpper` (the old spelling resolves through the CLI's table; the probe confirms it).
- `payoff.md`: the trace section points here.

Gates: `just gates` green; `test-books.sh` green first run; the `#[ignore]`d transcript replay against the installed `ikigai` 0.1.26 says `ok` for both new transcripts. The replay also surfaced a **pre-existing** MISS in `front-door/cli.md`: `urn:kernel:cache` now prints `entries 3 / 4096` and a `size … / 64.0 MB` line (the 0.1.70 LRU bound), and the description entry is 318 B — left for step 3, where the cache policy is taught.

_Requested by **Raynor** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_017As7C9uJ2DgNFVpoGeaNVe?thread=cmsg_017As7C9uJ2DgNFVpoGeaNVeWRwQCQXePPwYPoqzNNdMf4)_

Before: a store took orders whenever it was switched on and inside its working hours, whether or not anyone was there. When a customer tapped "I'm here", the kitchen board in the cabinet showed nothing (only a Telegram ping went to staff).

After: a store takes orders only while a shift is open. The kitchen board (including the PIN tablet) and each store card under "Точки" have "Начать работу" / "Закончить работу" buttons. While the shift is closed, the site, the Telegram mini app and the mobile app mark the store "Не работает", checkout is blocked, and the API refuses the order with `STORE_NOT_TAKING_ORDERS`. The customer can still browse the menu and build a cart. Tickets on the kitchen board show a green "Клиент на месте · N мин" badge, or "Клиент рядом".

**How**
- `StoreShift` table. A partial unique index allows only one open shift per store. The migration opens a shift at every store that isn't CLOSED, so nothing goes dark on deploy.
- `GET /stores` and `/stores/:id` return `acceptingOrders`, and `openNow` follows it. The mobile `Store.isOpen` accounts for it too, so the store picker from #143 greys out stores without a shift with no further changes.
- `GET /kds/shift` and `POST /kds/shift/open|close` are idempotent. Other screens update through the `kds.shiftChanged` event.
- Board rows carry `customerArrival` / `customerArrivedAt`, built from the existing `CUSTOMER_NEARBY` / `CUSTOMER_HERE` events.
- `libs/api-client-dart` model and codegen are updated. Codegen output matches the CI check (build_runner + format, no diff).

**Checks**
- API: 532 tests pass, including new ones for shifts and refused orders. The migration was applied to a local Postgres and `prisma migrate diff` shows no drift.
- admin, web and tma build. Tests pass for admin, web, tma and utils.

author: fas89
body:
## What was wrong

The build runner resolves `{{ env.NAME }}` placeholders in the whole contract before it writes (`build_runners/base.py::_resolve_env_placeholders`), and `fluid publish` resolves them too. The readers of a landed local file do not: `fluid verify` (`_verify_local_file`), `fluid diff`'s live local read and the local provider all go through `util/binding_paths.resolve_binding_path`, which anchored the raw template. Measured with a contract whose data lives under a shared directory named by a variable (`path: "{{ env.FLUID_DATA_DIR }}/customer_subscriptions/customer_subscriptions.parquet"`), running the generated pipeline's stage commands by hand from the contract's directory: stage 7 landed 10,172 rows at the resolved path; stage 9 reported `Output file not found: <contract dir>/{{ env.FLUID_DATA_DIR }}/...`; stage 5 reported the table `absent (to be created)` before and after it existed. In a CI job with one workspace per product this is the only way two products can share a landed file, so the pipeline failed at stage 9 and never published.

## What changes

- `resolve_binding_path` resolves `{{ env.NAME }}` before it anchors, exactly as the build runner resolves before it writes (an unset variable becomes the empty string on both sides), so writer and readers name the same file. `anchor_binding_paths` goes through it, so the local provider and `diff` follow.
- The placeholder pattern moves to `util/binding_paths.py` (stdlib only) and `build_runners/base.py` imports it, so there is one pattern for writers and readers.

## Validation

- New `tests/test_binding_path_env_templates.py` (8 tests): absolute and relative values, unset variable, a remote-URI value, readers equal to the build runner's resolution for each, `anchor_binding_paths`, and `_verify_local_file` finding a Parquet written under the resolved directory. All 8 fail on main (each reader returns the literal `{{ env.… }}` path) and pass here.
- ruff, black 24.10.0, `scripts/mypy_strict.py`, lint-imports, detect-secrets on the changed files; `tests/cli tests/build_runners tests/forge tests/iac` plus the quickstart e2e: 4,056 passed.

## Security

Only `location.path` strings are resolved, with the same pattern and the same environment as the build runner already uses when it writes; no new source of values. Secret-shaped names are not special-cased here because a path is not a credential, matching the writer.

author: matthargett
body:
Since the threads proposal landed, `with_memory!` takes a shared memory's lock inline and holds the guard until the access ends, and this actually dropped tinywasm's leaderboard placement in my WasmBench app on multiple devices. With the inline lock, load and store handler contain the `lock` and `unlock` calls, even though `core::hint::cold_path()` marks that branch cold. To keep values alive across those calls, each handler saves extra callee-saved registers on every access, whether or not the memory is shared.

This runs the shared-memory body in a `#[cold]`, `#[inline(never)]` helper that takes the lock. (There is a `core::hint::cold_path()` in there, but when I looked at the disassembled code for the Release build, it didn't affect codegen and Rust docs verify that its not necessarily meant to influence codegen.) The ordinary-memory path stays inline, which is seemingly more common in the wild, but if you have some specific workload you're optimizing for and need both paths to be equally fast, I can go back to the drawing board.

Everything measured with XCode 27's PMU template, the same approach I used for measuring and optimizing other projects (WAMR, wgpu-native, femtovg, BabylonNative, xmrsplayer, etc) on this set of hardware.

On aarch64 (iPhone XS A12 codegen, `nightly-tail-calls`):

| handler | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `I32Store` | 188 instructions, 5 saved register pairs, 17 calls | 137 instructions, 3 pairs, 8 calls |
| `I32Load` | 186 instructions, 5 pairs, 16 calls | 142 instructions, 3 pairs, 8 calls |

Three memory.copy / data-segment bodies used `?` inside the macro for a unit result. They now return the `Result` and apply `?` outside the macro, so a body means the same thing on both paths. 

**iPhone 12 (A14) efficiency cores.** Per-call medians of the kernel's retired-instruction and cycle counters, 5 interleaved runs of each build:

| row | instructions | cycles |
|---|---:|---:|
| byte-hash loop over one memory | −3.6% | −4.2% |
| convolution 256×256 (scalar) | −5.7% | −3.3% |
| sieve (scalar) | −4.2% | −7.8% |
| crc32 64 KB (scalar) | −4.0% | −6.3% |
| xmrsplayer | −2.7% | −1.1% |
| graphql-validation (AS) | −3.4% | −2.7% |
| shared memory: plain load/store | −4.2% | −4.1% |
| shared memory: atomic RMW | −6.3% | −10.7% |
| ordinary memory: plain load/store | −5.8% | −4.4% |
| fib(30), no memory ops | −0.1% | −0.0% |

**Apple Watch Series 10.**Per-call medians of the kernel's retired-instruction and cycle counters:

| row | instructions | cycles |
|---|---:|---:|
| byte-hash loop over one memory | −4.6% | −8.6% |
| convolution 256×256 (scalar) | −5.8% | −4.8% |
| sieve (scalar) | −4.2% | −8.3% |
| crc32 64 KB (scalar) | −4.0% | −6.2% |
| xmrsplayer | −2.9% | −3.6% |
| graphql-validation (AS) | −3.3% | −2.8% |
| fib(30), no memory ops | −0.2% | −0.0% |

author: moneycm
body:
## Qué hace
Módulo nuevo **Alertas Narrativas** (menú *Salida*). Cada lunes a las 07:00 y cada día 1 a las 07:00 (hora de Bogotá) genera un borrador de **máximo 6 líneas** para WhatsApp que combina:

1. Las **3 variaciones más significativas** del periodo frente al anterior, por delito, barrio/vereda y franja horaria (madrugada, mañana, tarde, noche).
2. El **estado de los compromisos** del Consejo de Seguridad: vencidos, próximos a vencer (15 días) y cumplidos recientes, y cuáles se relacionan con cada variación.
3. Una **acción sugerida**: pedir avance de compromisos vencidos relacionados, o llevar al Consejo un alza sin compromiso abierto.

Redacción con plantilla, **sin IA**: cada frase se rastrea a la evidencia guardada con el mensaje.

## Variación significativa (reglas 2026.09, publicadas en la página)
- Periodos anclados al **corte de la última sábana**, no a la fecha de hoy. Semanal: 7 días al corte frente a los 7 anteriores. Mensual: último mes completo frente al anterior.
- Prueba binomial condicional (dos conteos de Poisson), p < 5 %.
- Al menos 6 hechos entre ambos periodos y diferencia ≥ 3 (semanal) / ≥ 5 (mensual).
- Descarta rebotes: el cambio debe sostenerse frente al promedio de los 4 periodos anteriores.
- Alzas primero; máximo 2 de 3 en la misma dimensión; si hay menos de 3, el mensaje lo dice y no rellena.
- Porcentajes solo con base ≥ 30 hechos. Se informa cuántas variaciones se esperan por azar y cuáles pasan el umbral estricto (Bonferroni).

## Datos
- Reutiliza `hechos_seguridad` + `ingestion_runs` (un hecho por identidad, entrega más reciente), `council_commitments` + `council_commitment_updates`, `latest_covering_run` y las normalizaciones de `analitica`.
- Tablas nuevas: `narrative_alerts` (texto generado intacto, texto actual, estado, evidencia JSONB, versión, envío) y `narrative_alert_revisions` (historial con autor y fecha).
- Una entrega policial corregida del mismo periodo genera otra versión y marca los borradores anteriores como *reemplazados*; los enviados se conservan.

## Flujo de uso
Borrador → edición (valida 6 líneas / 1.200 caracteres, bloqueo optimista) → Copiar / Abrir en WhatsApp (`wa.me`) → Marcar como enviado (queda congelado) o Descartar con motivo. No hay envío automático: requeriría la API de WhatsApp Business.

## Pruebas
- `tests/test_narrative_alerts.py` (14) y `src/utils/narrativeAlerts.test.js` (4) pasan; `npm test` 65/65; `vite build` OK.
- Suite backend: mismas fallas preexistentes que `main`, ninguna nueva.
- Verificado en local: el programador generó los borradores semanal y mensual al arrancar; API (edición, límite de líneas, conflicto de versión, historial) y página revisadas en el navegador.

author: ralphkrauss
body:
## Scope

Identity hardening row 4 (and MANAGER §3 row 20): one identity system. The market-data plugin's ADR 0012 identity layer is removed, and market-data reads of a Pythia subject now go through core's bindings and source order (ADR 0037).

## What changed

**Core** (`runtime/managed/core`)
- `identity/page.py`: `answers()` (factored out of `compose`) and `price_sources()`. The second returns the ready quote/chart references for a subject: confirmed bindings plus addresses core derives, in core's order. A disabled, unconfigured or contradicted plugin contributes none, and so does one that still needs a resolve.
- `identity_ops.py`: `Identity.price_sources(subject_id)` returns `{asset_class, refs}` (local only). `_load` is shared with `_compose`. There is a module-level `price_sources()` through the registered core. `core/__init__` imports `identity_ops` so plugins can reach it.

**Market data** (`runtime/managed/plugins/market-data`)
- Removed `identity.py`, `identity_db.py`, `identity_matching.py`, `identity_overrides.py` and `identity_repair.py`, together with the actions `search`, `resolve_save`, `inspect_identity`, `inspect_subject`, `refresh_identity`, `inspect_repair`, `apply_override` and `revoke_override`. `details`, `series`, `read`, `read_many` and the preference actions remain.
- `backend.route()`: an explicit `provider_ref` reads only itself. A subject reads core's refs through `_platform.price_sources`. Saved preferences come first and core's order follows; the hard-coded default order is gone. The generation guard is gone too. The selected series stays in the cache key, and the delivery reuse scope now includes each subject's current refs.
- `preferences.py` now owns a private `preferences.sqlite3`. **One-time migration:** on first start it copies the source orders from the legacy `identity.sqlite3`. Scoped `subject_kind` rules become `asset_class` rules: crypto maps to crypto, and listing, instrument and company map to equity, with listing winning over instrument over company. It then renames the file `identity-retired.sqlite3`, keeps it and logs a warning with counts. Mappings are not migrated, because core derives or resolves addresses again.
- Tool description and `SKILL.md` updated. Subjects come from `pythia_identity_search`, and `unresolved_identity` points to `pythia_identity_subject` and `pythia_identity_resolve`.

**Wire types**
- `subject` is now `{kind: issuer|security|composite|listing, id: backbone subject id}`. The `mapping` kind and the `search` contribution operation are removed. `schema.json`, the examples and `packages/market-data/src/index.ts` are updated to match.

**Docs**
- ADR 0012 gets a retirement amendment and ADR 0037's consequence bullet is updated.
- `IDENTITY.md` is rewritten to cover how reads use core identity and what happens to retired state.
- `BACKEND.md`, the wire README, `docs/architecture/market-data.md`, `.agents/rules/financial-connectors.md` and the Yahoo README are updated.

**Unmigratable entries:** no Desk watchlist storage exists yet (the page is a placeholder), and instrument pages already use backbone ids. The only remaining references to retired subjects are old chat widget blocks and retained requests. They fail validation visibly as invalid requests; nothing is rewritten or dropped.

## How verified

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s runtime/test/python -p 'test_*.py'`: 257 tests OK (the one resident-RPC cancel failure seen in an earlier run also fails on the base branch and did not recur)
- `just check`: passed (exit 0)
- `packages/market-data`: `pnpm run test:unit` passed (21 tests). `check_wire.py` passed, and so did the `--json-schema` run via `uv run --with jsonschema==4.26.0`.
- `apps/desk`: `vitest run test/financial-data.test.ts` passed (4 tests).
- New tests:
  - core `price_sources`: order, and exclusion of unconfigured plugins and plugins that still need a resolve;
  - a subject core cannot route is `unresolved_identity` and makes no source call;
  - a retired subject kind is rejected;
  - legacy-file migration: copies, collapses scopes, keeps the retired file, warns, and runs only once.
- Lines: 715 added, 2223 removed. Runtime code: +342/−908. Tests: +150/−864.

## Gaps and follow-ups

- Wire leftovers that connectors still emit, kept to avoid touching five connectors: the `evidence` kind in `details`, `provenance.mapping_revision` (always null now) and the contribution `subject_kinds` (old coverage kinds). These are for the connector-adoption piece.
- A binding that changes during an in-flight read is no longer rejected. The next read routes through the new binding.
- `price_sources` re-reads the installed contracts on every subject read. That is fine at POC scale; cache it if reads get hot.
- No live stack run. The market-data → core path is covered by unit seams only.
- Test changes outside identity: `packages/market-data/test/widget*.test.ts`, `apps/desk/qualification/data-page.tsx` and `apps/desk/test/financial-data.test.ts` only swapped subject ids to backbone form. No widget binding code changed.

Nothing unmerged.

author: contactexepex
body:
## What changed and why

Four test files contained assertions that guarded against imagined future operator mistakes rather than validating the shipped artifact's own contract. This violates the operator-conformance principle codified in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (PR #165): reference templates/schemas/configs declare a contract; conformance is the operator's responsibility — the same model used by Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, and Azure DevOps. Tests validate that the *shipped artifact* conforms to its own contract; they do not pre-emptively guard against every way an operator could later break conformance.

**`render_tests/behaviors.py`**
- Removed hard-coded `required_mappings = {"anthropic": "claude-code-action", "openai": "codex"}` dict and the independent loop over it. The rationale was "iterating PROVIDER_TOOL directly would stop generating a case if an entry were dropped" — but that is a hypothetical future removal. The second loop already iterates `render.PROVIDER_TOOL.items()` and covers both entries today; if either were removed from PROVIDER_TOOL, the schema enum check in the same loop would still catch the inconsistency.
- Changed the default-provider inheritance loop to iterate `render.PROVIDER_TOOL.items()` for the same reason.

**`render_tests/auto_merge.py`**
- Removed three "closure regression fixture" checks that tested the `_closure_report` helper function itself (not the shipped artifact). A helper's internal logic is not part of the contract.
- Removed the RenderContext Mapping API block (six checks on indexing, `.get`, `.items`, `==`, etc.) with its Codex-authored comment directing future reviewers to preserve the API. That is documentation policy embedded in a test, not a behavioral assertion about the rendered workflow output.

**`render_tests/permissions.py`**
- Removed the job-level permissions pre-emption block. It asserted "no template sets job-level permissions today" as a guard against a future template that might add one. The EXPECTED coverage completeness check (kept) already ensures every new template must declare its top-level permissions — a new template that adds job-level permissions would trigger a security review at that point, not be pre-empted here.

**`render_tests/selection.py`**
- Changed LANES list equality to set equality. Emit order is an internal implementation detail, not a behavioral contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- All four hypothetical-future-state guards removed.
- All real behavioral assertions (injection matrix, P0 invariants, protected-paths, pipeline selection, least-privilege top-level permissions, EXPECTED coverage completeness) unchanged and passing.
- `python .github/scripts/validate_config.py` → all OK.
- `python .github/scripts/test_render.py` → all OK.

## Checks run

```
python .github/scripts/validate_config.py   → All contract validations passed.
python .github/scripts/test_render.py       → All M2 renderer/backend tests passed.
```

author: dmfenton
body:
## Why

The v1.41.3 release stopped twice in the gallery resave tests: an old thumbnail and old metadata could be accepted after the piece JSON was replaced because freshness relied on filesystem mtimes. The v1.41.2 attempt also built and scanned the backend image, then ECR rejected its push with `no basic auth credentials` despite a successful login step. The trusted runners share a home directory, so a job's ECR logout can remove another job's Docker login; that is a plausible explanation, not a confirmed incident trace.

## Changes

- Invalidate a piece's thumbnail and metadata sidecars under the existing gallery locks whenever its JSON is replaced. Readers rebuild from the new piece rather than comparing timestamps from different files.
- Give each release attempt a Docker config in its runner temp directory before ECR login, isolating login and logout from other jobs.
- Add a regression test with deliberately newer stale sidecar mtimes.

## Local verification

- Gallery thumbnail tests: 8 passed.
- Full server suite: 585 passed, 9 deselected.
- Web: 339 passed.
- MonetKit: passed (rerun with Swift cache access after the sandbox blocked its cache path).
- Ruff check and format, mypy on the changed workspace module, workflow `actionlint`, `git diff --check`, and commit hooks: passed.

Production remains on v1.41.0. The v1.41.1 run was canceled before deploy, v1.41.2 stopped before image push, and v1.41.3 stopped in tests.

author: jimutt
body:
Implements the decisions planned in #79. After this merges, `npm version 1.0.0-rc.3` on `v1` (DL-058).

| ID | Change |
|---|---|
| DL-055 | Claude Code gets the AGENTS.md rule block through a dld-kit `.claude/CLAUDE.md` holding `@../AGENTS.md`. This replaces the DL-054 note. `planRule` and `loadsRule` model what Claude Code reads: every CLAUDE file that exists, plus AGENTS.md when one of them imports it. A `CLAUDE.md` that already imports `@AGENTS.md` therefore no longer gets a second copy in `.claude/rules/`. |
| DL-056 | `dld --help` lists "Setup commands" (init, update, install-rule, session-context) apart from "Commands the skills run (internal; may change in minor releases)". An internal command's `--help` says so. The README and `docs/releasing.md` state the semver contract. |
| DL-057 | README section "Upgrading from 0.x", and a CLI test that upgrades a pre-1.0 fixture project. |
| DL-058 | `docs/releasing.md`: release candidates come from `v1` until 1.0.0, with the 1.0.0 steps listed and not done. |
| DL-059 | Every action in both workflows moves to its Node 24 major, pinned by SHA: checkout v7.0.1, setup-node v7.0.0, upload-artifact v7.0.1, download-artifact v8.0.1, github-script v9.0.0, setup-bun v2.2.0. I checked each breaking change against how the workflows use the action (details in DL-059). actionlint passes. |
| DL-060 | The annotation scan skips `.agents`, `.agent`, `.codex`, `.cursor`, `.opencode` and `.pi`, as it already skipped `.claude`. This fixes the 11 false annotations from `.agents/skills` in the rc.2 report. |

## Checks

- **Claude Code imports (DL-055).** Claude Code 2.1.283, headless, with a marker sentence in AGENTS.md. Three setups: `.claude/CLAUDE.md` alone; that file plus a `CLAUDE.md` and a `CLAUDE.local.md`; and a root `CLAUDE.md` holding `@AGENTS.md`. In each, the sentence was in context, and Claude reported seeing it once (that count is the model's own answer).
- **0.x upgrade (DL-057).** I built a project with `main`'s bash scripts: copied `.claude/skills`, a config, two records, an annotation, `INDEX.md`, audit and snapshot state, and the old CLAUDE.md section. Then I ran the built `dld update --agent claude,codex` on it:
  - It rewrote the 13 skills and removed their 22 `.sh` scripts.
  - The old CLAUDE.md section got a warning only.
  - `next-id` gave DL-003, and `regenerate-index` produced an identical INDEX.md.
  - `detect-snapshot-changes` printed the same output as the old script.
- **Test suite.** `npm test` passes (381 unit tests, 17 CLI tests), as do lint, typecheck, the coverage floor, `check:generated` and `check:installers`.

## Review subagent findings, fixed

- **Critical.** Reading instruction files as regular files only broke symlinks: with `CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md`, `session-context` would add the rule a second time. Files are now read through symlinks; ownership and writes still require regular files.
- A personal `CLAUDE.local.md` no longer blocks the import. Otherwise the committed result would give teammates without that file the rule twice. The DL-055 record's condition was changed to match.
- A symlinked `.claude` gets a warning and no import, rather than making `install-rule` fail.
- Code fences close only on a matching fence.
- The Biome line-length error in the new CLI test is fixed.

Each fix has a test that fails on the previous code.

## Open question: where a new rule block goes

The 0.x upgrade run turned up one more problem, left to a separate decision. Every 0.x project has a `CLAUDE.md`, because the old dld-init appended to it, and usually no `AGENTS.md`. Under DL-045, a new block then goes into `CLAUDE.md`, which Codex and Cursor don't read, so `update --agent claude,codex` warns.

For now, the README tells those users to create an empty `AGENTS.md` first. With it, the block goes to `AGENTS.md`, Claude Code gets `.claude/rules/dld-workflow.md`, and no other warning appears.

The better fix is to put a new block in `AGENTS.md` whenever an installed harness reads only `AGENTS.md`. That changes DL-045, so it needs its own decision.

author: ahzf
body:
`OnWebSocketFrameSent` is now raised through `InvokeAllAsync`, like the events next to it in `SendWebSocketFrame`. Every subscriber is called and waited for, one after another, and the ten-second bound it used to be given is gone.

### What was wrong

`SendOnWebSocketFrameSent` called the event itself and gave the task that came back ten seconds, with `WaitAsync(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10), CancellationToken)`. A multicast delegate that returns a `Task` returns the task of its **last** subscriber, and only that one:

- **Earlier subscribers were never waited for.** The send returned while they were still at work, and their work ran on alongside the next frame and its subscribers.
- **What they threw was never observed.** Only the last task was awaited, so nothing reached the log.
- **A subscriber that threw synchronously** (a non-`async` lambda) ended the call there, and **the subscribers behind it were never called at all**.
- **A slow subscriber outlived its caller's token.** `WaitAsync` stops waiting after ten seconds, or at once when the token is cancelled, but the subscriber keeps running. For a keep-alive ping that token is the connection loop's own, which is cancelled when the connection ends. That is exactly when the wait gave up.

### The fix

`SendOnWebSocketFrameSent` is now `OnWebSocketFrameSent.InvokeAllAsync(handler => handler(...), Logger)`. Its `protected` signature is unchanged for the servers built on this one.

**The ten-second bound is gone, and not kept per subscriber either.** The comment on the method gives the reasons:

- `WaitAsync` doesn't stop a subscriber; it only stops waiting for it. A bound per subscriber would leave the same stragglers behind, one subscriber at a time.
- The bound spared the sender little. `OnTextMessageSent` and `OnBinaryMessageSent` had the same ten seconds until 3524ffa54 (August 2024) moved them to a shared invoker without them. So a subscriber that hangs in any event raised after this one, from the same send, has held the send up all along.
- A slow subscriber now makes the send slow, which is where it shows. One that has to be quick has the token.

### Tests

Four in the new `WebSocketFrameSentEventTests`, each on a `WebSocketMirrorServer` with a client connected:

| Test | What it asks | On `master` |
|---|---|---|
| `TheSendWaitsForEverySubscriberNotOnlyTheLast` | a slow subscriber and a fast one behind it: the send returns after both, and the second is called once the first has finished | `first began, second, sent` |
| `ASubscriberThatThrowsAtOnceDoesNotSilenceTheOnesBehindIt` | a non-`async` subscriber throws, and the one behind it is still called | never called |
| `WhatASubscriberThrowsLaterIsReportedNotLost` | a subscriber that fails after its first `await` is in the server's log, and the one behind it is still called | empty log |
| `ASendWhoseTokenIsCancelledStillWaitsForItsSubscribers` | a send whose token is cancelled while a subscriber is at work returns only once that subscriber has finished | `began, returned` |

All **115** WebSocket tests pass, and so do `ConnectionLivenessTests` and `EventInvocationTests`. The four new tests passed eight repeated runs.

### What the tests catch

Checked by putting each alternative in place of the fix, one at a time, against these four:

| In place of the fix | Goes red |
|---|---|
| the old code (`master`) | all four |
| the event called directly and awaited, with no bound | the first three (the fourth has a single subscriber) |
| `InvokeAllAsync` with the bound put back per subscriber, `WaitAsync(10 s, token)` | `ASendWhoseTokenIsCancelledStillWaitsForItsSubscribers` |
| `InvokeAllAsync` with the bound put back around the whole round | `ASendWhoseTokenIsCancelledStillWaitsForItsSubscribers` |
| `InvokeAllAsync` with ten seconds per subscriber, without the token | **none**. Pinning that would take a test that waits the ten seconds out |

### Also checked

Nothing else in `Hermod/HTTP1/WebSocket` has this shape. `WebSocketClient` raises all of its events through `LogEvent`, which is `InvokeAllAsync`, and has no frame-sent event. The only other local event copies in the server belong to `OnValidateWebSocketConnection` and `OnValidateTCPConnection`. Those are validators, whose answers decide the connection. They deliberately don't use `InvokeAllAsync`, and their comments say why.

No file overlaps with #46, #47 or #48, and this merges cleanly with each of them.

author: sibtain2345
body:
Scope 6.6: the assistant "already knows what the user is studying, which section they are on, **and how the session is going**." The first two were true. The third was not — the assistant had no idea of the learner's state.

## What it does

The assistant is given a short, trusted style hint when the learner is `drifting`, `struggling` or `fatigued` — shorter and tied to the passage, one step at a time with a concrete example, brief and skimmable respectively. For `focused`, `recovered`, unknown or stale states the prompt gains **no section at all**, not an empty one that invites the model to comment on it.

## The state is read on the server, never from the request

`session_context` already exists on the request, but it comes from the browser and the prompt rightly treats it as untrusted. Engagement state steers how the model addresses the learner, so it has to come from where it was measured — the same reason Module 4 refuses to let the client report how badly it is struggling.

`app/engagement/latest_state.py` records the **final** state after the fatigue and recovery rules (`smoothing.py` only holds the model's smoothed class), keyed on the caller's own uid *and* session id, with a 60-second freshness limit, cleared on session end. Missing or stale changes nothing, which is the safe way to fail. The schema forbids unknown fields, so a forged `engagement_state` — top level or inside `session_context` — is refused with a `422 extra_forbidden`, and the service is never reached.

## The live call that changed the wording

I ran real Gemini against this instead of trusting the tests, and it found a real mistake in my first version of the rule.

The first version said *never mention a camera or tracking*. The learner asked "can you tell if I am confused?" and the model answered:

> "I don't have any way to see or track how you're feeling."

**That is false.** The camera is measuring engagement, and the pre-session screen says so. Forbidding the topic outright forced the model into a denial. So the rule is now about what to **volunteer**, and a direct question gets a true answer:

> "Yes, Adaptly uses numeric measurements from your camera to help adjust the level of support… No video is ever recorded or stored. These measurements are just rough signals… rather than actual knowledge of how you feel."

A second live call then said "I cannot see those measurements", which is also a denial — the assistant *does* receive a coarse state — so that is ruled out explicitly too. Both wordings are pinned by tests, including that the old "never mention a camera" text is gone. The guidance is deliberately soft ("may be finding this hard") because Struggling recall is about 10% on held-out data: an assistant that asserted the state would be confidently wrong most of the time.

## Something unrelated I tripped over

`ASSISTANT_MODE` defaults to **`mock`**, and it is in no `.env.example`. With it unset, every learner gets a fixed placeholder sentence — *"Mock assistant response for chunk 'ch1'…"* — **even when `GEMINI_API_KEY` is set**, and nothing says why. A fresh setup looks like a broken assistant. It is now documented in `.env.example`.

## Checks

```
603 backend passed, 3 skipped
26 new tests
```

Mutations, all caught: keying on session alone (leaks between learners), dropping the staleness check, dropping the disclosure rule, giving `focused` learners guidance, and reading the wrong uid.

**Noticed, not fixed here:** Module 5's Gemini call has **no retry on 503/429**, unlike Modules 4 and 8. Two of three live attempts in a row failed with "provider unavailable" before one went through. The panel shows a safe error with a retry button, so it is survivable, but it is worth its own small PR rather than folding into this one.

## Conflicts

Clean against develop, #93, #94, #79 and #64. It conflicts with #62, #80 and #89, but those conflict with develop on their own too (see the notes on each) — nothing here touches their files.

author: roryglenn
body:
Voice Studio previously required Apple Silicon for native inference, and the newer EPUB-to-audiobook workflow lived in private, book-specific scripts. This adds supported NVIDIA Ubuntu operation and reusable audiobook commands while preserving the Mac and historical edition paths.

## Changes

- Add a locked Ubuntu CUDA dependency profile, launcher, and runtime/model diagnostics. Preserve the selected model and precision; reject unavailable backends and incomplete assets.
- Coordinate Studio and book inference with a shared GPU lease. Release models and complete CUDA frees before handing the GPU to another process; preserve deterministic seeds and job state through failures.
- Add EPUB preparation, source-bound checkpoints, pause/resume, wording and pacing verification, scoped review/repair, and verified WAV/MP3/chaptered AAC-LC M4B exports with original cover artwork and the headphone strip.

- Bound long chapter filenames by UTF-8 byte length while preserving complete chapter metadata; use portable encoder lookup throughout packaging; include CUDA runtime/NVCC/CCCL versions in frozen job identities.

## Validation

The current head passed independent review and verification. Native speech and the complete pilot were exercised on the migration implementation; the final three review corrections were then tested on both operating systems, including real FFmpeg packaging and frozen-runtime rejection cases.

- Mac: 95 Python tests passed; Ubuntu: 93 passed, 2 intentional Mac-launcher skips.
- JavaScript: 16 tests passed on both platforms.
- Ruff lint and formatting, ten-source mypy, and Git whitespace checks passed.
- Real Ubuntu RTX 3060 Ti (8 GiB): all saved Natural voices and the Expressive audition engine generated and exported audio. A 100-word passage generated 31.84 seconds of audio in 8.47 seconds, excluding loading.
- A two-chapter, 10-passage native pilot completed preparation, pause/resume, recognition, a targeted synthetic-test rerender, and M4B packaging while Studio remained open. Full decode, waveform conservation, approved quiet intervals, chapter metadata, and cover preservation passed.
- Idle Studio GPU usage fell to 220–286 MiB after the CUDA cleanup fix. Independent review found no remaining actionable issues.
- Publication preflight confirmed all 44 indexed files match the validation manifest and the 20 changed files contain source, tests, and documentation only. Private voices, books, models, configuration, and runtime data are excluded.

Exact development gates:

```sh
uv run python -m unittest discover -p 'test_*.py'
node --test test_web.cjs
uvx ruff check .
uvx ruff format --check .
uvx mypy --python-executable .venv/bin/python studio.py voice_profiles.py project_paths.py run.py runtime.py doctor.py audiobook.py book_prepare.py book_pacing.py book_package.py
git diff --check
```

Ubuntu tests used the installed `.venv/bin/python` and Node executable; native setup used `uv sync --locked --extra ubuntu` followed by `python run.py doctor`.

## Limits

The generic book workflow uses Natural and supports unencrypted, well-formed XHTML EPUBs with supplied cover art. Multi-hour endurance and matched Mac/CUDA listening remain unverified. Held wording or unsafe timing blocks packaging. This does not resume or rewrite existing private book jobs.

Pilot for shortening the codebase's comments, on one module. **Comment- and docstring-only**: the parsed code is identical to `main` (AST compared with docstrings stripped), and no log string, name or behaviour changes.

## Before / after (`kalshi_betting/strategy.py`)

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Lines | 882 | 585 |
| Docstring lines | 428 | 227 |
| `#` comment lines | 156 | 60 |
| Prose share | 70% | 53% |
| Longest comment block | 27 lines | 6 lines |

The remaining prose is mostly the Args/Returns sections CLAUDE.md's docstring standard requires.

## What was removed
Bug history ("the old gate overstated EV…"), numbers from past runs, and reasoning repeated elsewhere in the file. CLAUDE.md already records all of it under the DR/TS IDs, which stay in the code as one-word pointers.

## What was kept at the code it protects
- Fee in Kelly's denominator, and `b` is not `profit_ratio` (DR-62)
- f* > 0 means positive EV only under the continuous fee approximation
- The post-shrink reachability backstop is not dead code (TS-08)
- `depth_levels` is read by type, not truthiness
- FoK caps come only from `scanner.v2_effective_cap`
- Reachability is gated to V2, and why
- `cost_with_fees_a/_b` are per market, not per side

## Comments that were false or overstated, now corrected
- `_kelly_p` cited `strategy.py:58` for the tradeable check; it is ~L617.
- `_solve_marginal_size` said the supported set is "very nearly" downward-closed. It is not; holes are possible.
- `_kelly_p_at` called the solver a "descent". It is a bisection.
- `_kelly_p` said the probability clamp is unreachable from the live pipeline. It can still fire on a crossed book or a stale fallback reference.
- The backstop comment said bisection always lands below any hole and that the cheapest level always fits. Neither is guaranteed.
- The header said only `time_series_profit_prob` is shared with the backtester/dashboard copies. They also share the fee helpers and constants, and the backtester's Pass 2 mirrors `select_portfolio`, which is now noted.

author: p00nsmasher
body:
Implements Step 3 of the learning plan: establish a methodologically clean learning baseline from Study Pilot sessions.

## Baseline cohort
- First 3 completed Study Pilot sessions only.
- 54 first-question exposures minimum.
- Baseline attempts are provisional until the full 18-question pilot completes.
- Abandoned/incomplete pilots are excluded from baseline evidence.

## No measurement contamination
- Adaptive difficulty is frozen during baseline pilot sessions.
- Skill accuracy, rubric evidence, response-time bands, and misconceptions are still recorded.
- Normal gameplay adaptation remains unchanged.
- Pilot adaptation can resume after the baseline cohort is complete.

## Frozen evidence
- Baseline-only counters are stored separately from later pilot/calibration data.
- Later pilot sessions cannot change the established baseline.
- Baseline session counts also live in the cross-version item metrics store, so future private publishes do not erase the benchmark.

## Reporting/privacy
- Live Open Cloud reader exposes baseline-only counters.
- Baseline report groups performance by skill, subject, domain, and difficulty.
- No usernames, user IDs, raw answers, or chat are included.

## QA
- Adds pilotBaselineIntegrity.test.js.
- Updates Steps 3-4 fixtures to the frozen baseline fields.
- Existing Step 4 calibration remains fail-closed and unchanged.

body:
Closes #15.

## From the #11 review
- README quickstart uses `sj.engines.load("jev")` instead of an undefined `engine`, and gets a short Engines section showing a Jev → LLM cascade. `snapjudge.engines` is exported as `sj.engines`.
- `Question.choice` / `score` raise `InvalidQuestionError` for non-list options (None, an int, or a bare string).
- `Decision.p` docstring: the renormalised distribution sums to 1 *within float rounding*.

## From the #12 review
- New `plain_context()` in `engine.py`: any Mapping becomes a plain dict, and nested values fall back to `str()`. Used by both the Jev and LLM adapters, so `MappingProxyType` and similar contexts work.
- SPEC §2 now matches v0: LLM probabilities are the model's own JSON estimate and are flagged `calibrated=False`. Logprobs are a later enhancement.

## From the #16 review
- Cascade `cost_usd` is None when any answering engine reported no cost, rather than a partial sum.
- `cascade.from_config(path)` loads the `[cascade]` table from `snapjudge.toml` (order, escalate_below, on_exhausted), moved here from #16 because it needed `snapjudge.engines`.

## Tests
76 passing (9 new).

<!-- mergesafe:start -->
## MergeSafe-generated description

### What changed
Exposed `snapjudge.engines`, added TOML-based cascade construction with engine order, escalation threshold, and exhaustion policy, and updated documentation with engine-loading examples. Context values are now normalized to JSON-safe values, cascade costs become unknown if any answering engine has an unknown cost, and choice/score inputs are restricted to lists or tuples.

### Impact
Users can load bundled engines and configure cascades from code or `snapjudge.toml`; context containing custom objects or non-finite floats can be sent as valid JSON. Cascade cost reporting avoids presenting partial costs as complete.

### Risk
Callers that previously passed generators or other `Sequence` types to choice/score APIs will now receive `InvalidQuestionError`. `from_config` uses `tomllib`, so it requires a Python version that provides that standard-library module (Python 3.11+).

author: jfrazx
body:
## What changed

Every WebSocket frame now runs as its connection's actor, with that actor's abilities primed, the way every HTTP request does. Before this, a client that sent a frame straight after connecting could reach the handler before its session lookup finished, because Nest does not await `handleConnection` (#427). And no frame had an ability context at all, so `@CheckPolicies` did nothing on a gateway and each handler resolved abilities by hand (#498). Implements `D-427-1` to `D-427-9` as locked on #427.

- **Handshake auth (`D-427-1`):** `AuthenticatedGateway.afterInit` registers namespace middleware, once per namespace. socket.io runs it before it accepts the connection, and a client cannot send a frame before that, so the window is gone rather than narrowed. `connectionStateRecovery.skipMiddlewares` is now `false`, or a socket recovered within 2 minutes would skip the check.
- **Per-frame actor scope (`D-427-2`):** a socket.io packet middleware opens the connection's CLS scope around each frame, through the new `WsActorScope`. socket.io dispatches after it in a `process.nextTick` that keeps the async context, so the scope covers the guards, the handler and `WsErrorFilter`. `WsActorInterceptor` is deleted: as an `APP_INTERCEPTOR` it never ran on a gateway message.
- **Abilities primed for each frame (`D-427-3`, `D-427-7`):** `WsFrameScopeGuard` primes them fresh, so a grant revoked mid-connection counts from the next frame. The base class's guards run `AuthGuard`, then `WsFrameScopeGuard`, then `PoliciesGuard`.
- **Policies on WS (`D-427-6`, `D-427-8`):** `PoliciesGuard` is bound on the base class. `search:start` carries `@CheckPolicies(read Game)`, like its REST twin, and its local half reads `getCurrentResourceConditions` instead of resolving the actor itself.
- **Backstops:** `handleConnection` closes, with a logged error, any connection that reaches it unauthenticated. Only a subclass that overrides `afterInit` without calling the base's gets there. The frame guard refuses a frame running as no actor with a logged 500.
- **The coordinator call now carries the socket's actor.** Before, no scope meant no `x-bge-actor` header, and the coordinator's inbound actor check refuses a call without one. So WS external search appears to have failed on every call. That comes from reading the code: the integration spec pins the header, but no e2e runs a coordinator.

## Contract change for WS clients

- **Connection refusals move from `auth:error` to `connect_error`,** with the same envelope as `err.data`. This covers no token, an invalid session, a refused actor, and a session lookup that fails outright (500). The client is never connected and does not retry on its own. This amends `D-426-1`.
- **`auth:error` now only means a live connection is closing,** on a frame whose session is gone.
- **`exception` is unchanged.**

## Also fixed: search frames never reached the client

This was found by the new e2e and predates the branch. The Redis streams adapter delivers a room broadcast, even to the local node, only after publishing it to Redis. `completeSearch` leaves the room in the same tick, so a search that finished quickly arrived empty in the shipped bundle. Search frames now go out with `.local`, since the socket is always on this node. No earlier e2e had run a successful WS search.

## Deviations from the locked plan

1. **`WsActorScope` lives in `actor-context-transport`, not `apps/api`.** The lint rule from #57 keeps `AuditContextInternalService` out of `apps/api`.
2. **Priming moved into a guard, after `AuthGuard` (review fix).** The lock had the packet middleware prime only events with a listener (`D-427-7`) and stash any failure for a backstop guard declared before `AuthGuard` to re-throw (`D-427-3`). A guard does both jobs with less: guards run only for frames some handler listens for, and a guard's error reaches the filter directly. Running after `AuthGuard` also fixes an ordering bug review found: a frame whose session had ended, and whose ability lookup also failed, got a 500 instead of its 401. The intent of both decisions is unchanged. The reconcile amendment on #427 will record the new mechanism.
3. **`AbilityService` stays injected in the search gateway.** `D-427-8` said to remove the injection but also to call `getCurrentResourceConditions`, which lives on `AbilityService`.
4. **The search gateway spec's two ability pins were rewritten, not deleted.** They now pin that the query reads the frame's primed conditions, and that nothing is queried when those cannot be read.

## Review points not taken

- **A `t()`-marker 403 reads "Forbidden Exception" off HTTP.** The `D-427-6` lock and the #180 amendment already name this, and #501 tracks it. Nobody can hit it today: every actor that can connect holds `read:game`.
- **Frames can overtake each other.** This predates the branch. Nest runs each event name as its own stream (`@nestjs/platform-socket.io` `io-adapter.js:42`), so `search:cancel` and `search:start` never had an order. Priming in a guard adds no new reordering point.
- **Priming on every handled frame.** HTTP primes every request too (`app.module.ts`, `AbilityContextMiddleware` on every route), and `D-427-7` chose fresh abilities per frame. WS throttling is #510.
- **`.local` gives the frames no recovery offset.** Connection-state recovery replays none of the search frames, and a search could not resume from them anyway: a disconnect cancels every search. The stale rooms a recovered socket gets back also predate the branch: socket.io saves them on `disconnecting`, before Nest's `disconnect` handler cancels the searches.
- **Handshake logs are attributed to whichever gateway registered first.** No namespace has two gateways, and every line carries the socket id.

## Worth a reviewer's attention

- **A recovered connection loses its searches silently.** This predates the branch. A disconnect cancels every search (`search.gateway.ts`, `handleDisconnect`), but recovery tells the client its state survived, and no `search:done` or error arrives.
- **A connection and its frames still read different credentials** (#511). The handshake reads `auth.token`, and `AuthGuard` reads each frame's `Authorization` header.
- **`apps/api-e2e/tsconfig.json` gains the `@bge/shared` reference** that `nx sync` reported missing. The suite has imported it since #426.
- **The branch is based on `b73c322`.** Master has since gained only #523, which touches no file here, and the branch merges cleanly.

## Verification

- **Red proof:** the new in-process integration spec runs a real socket.io server and client, with the session lookup held on a gate. On master it failed where it should: the early frame's search answered "Local search failed", and the filter saw no actor.
- **Integration spec:** 10 tests, green on 5 of 5 runs. It covers frames sent before the connection is accepted, two sockets not crossing, the coordinator call carrying the actor, a grant revoked mid-connection, the `@CheckPolicies` 403, a priming failure as a 500, an ended session refused with 401 before any ability lookup, and gateways that skip the base's hooks.
- **Revert-proofs, restored afterwards:** removing the scope, the priming, `PoliciesGuard`, the connection check or the frame's actor check, or priming before `AuthGuard`, each turns its tests red.
- **Unit tests:** `api` 141 passed, 1 skipped. `actor-context-transport`, `permissions`, `utils` and `shared` pass, 432 tests. Typecheck and lint are clean for `api` and `api-e2e`, apart from warnings already on master. Prettier is clean.
- **Full `api-e2e`:** 51 suites, 616 tests, all passing after the review fixes. It adds a search emitted before connect, and the WS mirror of #472's REST private-game search.

Closes #427
Closes #498
Refs #426 (connection refusals move to connect_error)
Refs #180 (the filter now runs inside the frame's scope)
Refs #501 (t() marker .message off HTTP)
Refs #510 (WS throttling)
Refs #511 (two credentia

author: ojardila
body:
## Problem (medium, anonymous amplification)

`GET /v1/farms/{slug}/provision-status` is public, with no rate limit. Each computation costs:

- a call to the farm's stack;
- an HTTPS probe;
- about 9 Kubernetes reads;
- while the farm is provisioning, **a GitHub API call using the dispatch token**.

The 4-second cache was written only *after* the computation finished (up to ~8 s), so concurrent requests all missed it.

Measured on master: **20 concurrent requests → 13 probes**. Looping that against a slug that's still provisioning uses up the token's hourly GitHub quota. After that, `kickTenantProvision` fails for real signups, and only a log line records it.

## Fix

- **Single-flight per slug.** Whoever arrives during a computation waits for it instead of starting another. The computation is detached from the first caller's connection (`context.WithoutCancel` plus a 30 s timeout), so a disconnect doesn't leave the others waiting on nothing.
- **A ready farm stays in cache for 60 s** instead of 4 s; there's nothing to watch closely.
- Errors (such as 404) are shared with the waiters and aren't cached.

## Tests

- New `TestProvisionStatusIsComputedOncePerSlugUnderLoad`: 20 concurrent requests make **1** probe. It **fails on master (13)** and passes here.
- Full `go test ./...` against PostGIS 17 passes; so do `go vet` and `gofmt`.

body:
Fixes #136

With `autoSelfCast` disabled, casting a helpful unit spell without a valid selected target refused locally with “You have no target” instead of entering unit-targeting mode.

**What this changes**

- Restores `autoSelfCast`’s 1.12.1 default of `"0"`.
- Sends a residual non-enemy unit target word to the hand cursor instead of refusing it locally.
- Allows the pending spell to be bound by clicking a world model or by `SpellTargetUnit`, including the player model and stock unit frames.
- Makes `SpellCanTargetUnit(unit)` answer for each resolved unit using the standing target word’s full unit checks.
- Uses the same unit-binding predicate for the initial selected target, world clicks, and UI-frame clicks.
- Rejects neutral units and friendly ambient NPCs that do not pass `CanAssist`, leaving the cursor armed.

**What 1.12.1 does, and how you know**

Observed in the 1.12.1 client:

- With `autoSelfCast` disabled, a helpful spell without a valid target enters the hand cursor.
- The spell can then be cast through the player model or a unit frame.
- Neutral creatures and friendly ambient NPCs such as critters, Joshua, Bo, and the Goldshire horses are not valid helpful-spell targets; clicking them leaves targeting armed.
- Ordinary harmful spells such as Smite still report “You have no target” rather than entering the hand cursor.

The client path agrees with those observations:

- `ArmCast` at `0x6e5250` seeds and resolves the target word.
- `autoSelfCast` is read at `0x6e53d7`, with a default CVar value of `"0"`.
- `BindTarget` at `0x6e5b40` applies the unit checks to the selected or clicked unit.
- `SpellCanTargetUnit` reaches the unit predicate at `0x6e6460`.
- The targeting predicates preserve the complete word: location at `0x6e6320` (`& 0x60`), item at `0x6e6330` (`& 0x4010`), and GameObject at `0x6e62d0` (`& 0x4800`).
- The enemy unit flag is `0x80`; a residual word carrying it follows the harmful-spell refusal path.
- `CanAssist` at `0x6066f0` requires a selectable target with a friendly reaction and, for a non-player-controlled NPC, `UNIT_FLAG_PVP` (`0x1000`) on the unit or its owner.
- The initial word comes from `Spell.dbc` `Targets` and the implicit-target fields.

**How you checked it**

Before:

1. Set `autoSelfCast` to `0`.
2. Clear the current target.
3. Cast a helpful unit spell.
4. Benilla reported “You have no target”.

After:

1. A helpful unit spell without a valid selected target enters the hand cursor.
2. Clicking the player model casts on the player.
3. Clicking the player or another valid unit frame casts through `SpellTargetUnit`.
4. Neutral creatures and friendly ambient NPCs remain invalid and leave the cursor armed.
5. Valid assistable units receive the spell.
6. Harmful spells such as Smite still report “You have no target”.

Checks run:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — passed.
- `cargo check -p benilla-app --lib` — passed.
- Focused `benilla-ui` tests for `SpellTargetUnit` and per-token `SpellCanTargetUnit` — passed.
- `scripts/check.sh` — formatting passed.

## Summary

This adds a test showing a pool slot that stays taken after its task moves on to a new launch attempt.

The owner keeps a reservation for each task that picks a pool member.

If the task is recreated while holding one, nothing frees it while the task stays queued.

With one slot in the pool, every other task on it is then deferred as "no member capacity" while nothing runs.

body:
Addresses #139.

Adds a new subsection **Required fields per packaging and role** (`{#requiredfields}`) directly after the Packaging table. It defines, for each `(packaging, role)` pair, which track-object fields MUST accompany the always-required set (`namespace`, `name`, `packaging`, `isLive`). The Packaging and Track role sections now cross-link to it.

Follows Will's proposal in the issue thread: field requirements are driven by the `packaging` value (not the role alone), so future packaging formats can extend the table in their own drafts.

Required-field set per pair:

| Packaging       | Role             | Also required                          |
|-----------------|------------------|----------------------------------------|
| loc             | audio            | codec, samplerate, channelConfig       |
| loc             | video            | codec, framerate                       |
| loc             | audiodescription | codec, samplerate, channelConfig, lang |
| loc             | signlanguage     | codec, framerate                       |
| eventtimeline   | eventtimeline    | eventType                              |
| mediatimeline   | mediatimeline    | -                                      |
| moqlog          | log              | -                                      |
| moqmetrics      | metrics          | -                                      |
| catalog         | any              | -                                      |

Deliberate deviations from Will's Aug proposal, called out for WG review:
- `bitrate` dropped from required (recent PRs made max/avg advisory).
- `width`/`height` dropped from `loc/video` required (they were made Optional in the merged width/height change).
- `lang` dropped from `loc/audio` required (excludes music/non-speech).
- `cmaf` row omitted (not a defined `packaging` value yet).

Not attempting the nested-object restructure Luke originally floated; WG thread converged on the flat + per-(packaging, role) table.

## Problem

The #1491 round-robin counted only `agent-fix`, `rebase` and `force-push` as attempts. An already-green PR logs `noop` / `already-green`, so it always looks never-attempted and sorts first.

On dogfood, #1460 and #1458 (both green) took both `max_concurrent_prs` slots every tick with instant no-ops. The red finalized PR #1483 has had no turn since 15:56, more than six hours.

`ATTEMPT_ACTIONS` now includes every action `PrFixer` records for a selected PR: `noop`, `give-up`, `pr-comment` and `label-apply`, as well as the three already counted. `skipped` and `list-prs` still don't count.

## Summary

Season-scoped Surprise Team Showdown, now through the data/schedule/Stats checkpoints. The season page's visual design has been reviewed; **the new historic chart and implementation changes are ready for review**. Kept draft pending that review; nothing merged or deployed to production.

### Completed checkpoints

1. `688b2ba` — reviewed Showdown UI and navigation, all 29 candidate seasons.
2. `0906a5d` — explicit home/away identities; verified backfill of **all 18,607 archived games**. Existing IDs, scores, dates and stored team order remain unchanged.
3. `7175348` — optional scoreless full schedule, preseason access, separate schedule KV cache, upcoming fixtures and next-matchup link. Completed results require NBA final status plus scores.
4. `00ba514` — bottom-row historic Stats chart: all **30 franchise groups**, archived seasons only, ranked by aggregate head-to-head win percentage, with W–L/PCT labels and keyboard tooltips.
5. `26d7595` — visual revision: larger matchup @ symbols, alternating red/thicker chart bars, overlaid `W–L | PCT` labels, and removal of the supplemental accordion/table.

## Preview / review paths

- [2025 Showdown](https://feature-showdown-ba16e25edf49-nba-surprise-teams.zemccartney.workers.dev/2025/showdown/)
- [New historic chart](https://feature-showdown-ba16e25edf49-nba-surprise-teams.zemccartney.workers.dev/stats/#showdown-history)

The homepage currently shows the 2026 countdown and deliberately has no Showdown link until candidate standings appear. No fake candidate odds are committed/deployed.

## Code review guide

- `src/data/showdown*.ts`: candidate-only selection, standings, calendar merge/deduplication, archived franchise aggregation.
- `src/components/showdown/` and `src/pages/[seasonId]/showdown.astro`: shared historical/live presentation, existing popover and deferred-island behavior.
- `src/loaders/live/` and `src/actions/index.ts`: optional schedule, final-only results, home/away normalization, cache versioning and isolated `<seasonId>:schedule` key. Existing results-only callers retain `<seasonId>` and empty preseason results.
- `data/migrations/003-game-venues.sql`, `data/node/backfill-venues.ts`, archive importer and CLI: separate venue enrichment table, exact archive/score identity checks, transactional backfill.

- `src/components/charts/showdown-standings.*`, `src/pages/stats.astro`: existing TanStack renderer/theme/tooltips, ranked horizontal bars, overlaid records and keyboard-accessible descriptions.
- The Git-fixture isolation fix from the initial checkpoint was independently adopted on `main`; latest `main` (`626171e`) is merged here, so that fix is no longer an extra PR diff. Hooks were never bypassed.

### Source anomaly handled explicitly

NBA's 2024-11-02 game log labels both MIA and WAS as away for Mexico City game `0022400147`. The official NBA box score identifies MIA away / WAS home with matching 118–98 scores. Paired venue conflicts now require independent box-score verification of provider identity, both teams and both scores; no hardcoded correction or guessed home/away order.

- Commit hooks passed, including working/staged SQL-dump parity checks.

- Browser at 1440px/390px: no horizontal overflow; all 99 2025 matchup pairs align; standard popover behavior verified.
- Historic chart: all 30 groups, keyboard navigation follows rank (Home selects HOU), working tooltip, no runtime exceptions. All 30 pipe-separated overlay labels fit at 390px/1440px; no supplemental table.
- Upcoming UI: actual deferred islands tested with temporary local-only candidates and a local cache normalized from the real 2026–27 NBA feed. Both head-to-heads render Eastern times, no scores, zero records and next-matchup link. Temporary odds/cache removed and DB/dump parity rechecked.

## Operational follow-up (not hidden)

Direct NBA requests from **local workerd return HTTP 403**; Node feed fetching works. Local error UI was verified and schedule UI/cache tested via the local seed described above, not misrepresented as a successful local upstream refresh. Hosted NBA access was verified during production cutover, but active-season end-to-end schedule/result transitions should be rechecked after real candidates are published. Conservative status-3 finality still has the existing preseason observation task in `MAINTENANCE.md`.

author: edbertchan
body:
## Summary

A pool slot held by a stale reservation is now freed once its task has moved on to a new launch attempt.

Each reservation now records which launch attempt made it. The periodic reclaim frees a reservation whose task now has a different attempt, even while that task is still queued.

This stops one leftover reservation from blocking every task on a one-slot pool until the owner restarts.

## Review Claim

Approve freeing a pool reservation when its task's current launch attempt differs from the attempt that made the reservation.

## Review Lane

behavior

## Review Unit

routing

## Safety Invariant

A pool reservation is freed early only when its task has moved on to a different launch attempt; a reservation made by the task's current attempt, or with no recorded attempt, is kept exactly as before, and terminal/deleted-task reclaim is unchanged.

## Slice Rationale

One rule added to the existing stale-reservation reclaim, plus flipping the proof case from the previous slice to a normal passing test.

## Non-goals

- No reconciler that compares in-memory load against persisted running tasks.
- No change to the missing-workspace startup path in the dispatcher.
- No change to how running executions are reclaimed.

## Test Plan

- [x] `cd packages/execution-engine && pnpm test -- src/__tests__/pool-capacity-pending-selection-leak.test.ts`: `7 passed (7)`, including the case that failed before this change
