author: cybercyclone
body:
## What changed

- **"Local models" is now "Host models"** wherever a person reads it (screen, settings row, server messages, `/host-models`). Code, API paths, testIDs and error codes keep `local`.
- **Pinning.** A *Keep loaded* switch per model. A pinned model loads straight away, again after every restart or preset reload, and is never unloaded to make room. Only an enabled model can be pinned; disabling unpins.
- **Loxaic decides what is unloaded, by memory.** The router runs with `--models-max 0`. Before loading a model, `llama/room.ts` unloads unpinned models, least recently used first, re-measuring free memory after each; a model with a request in flight is never unloaded.
- **No-room modal.** When pinned models are what leave no room, the send is refused before anything is written, and chat, agent and routine chats show a modal naming them (admins get a *Host models* button, everyone gets *Choose a loaded model*). The unsent message goes back in the box.
- **Honest multi-GPU fit.** The fit already added both GPUs, but used the free memory listed when the router started — on .13, LM Studio held ~26 GB of one V620, so "both GPUs" was ~34 GB while the rows showed 30 GB each. Free memory is now re-measured, our unpinned models count as reclaimable, and the estimate says what other programs hold. GPU rows are **switches** showing "X free of Y".
- **Loaded badges in the model picker**, loaded host models first in their group.

Found and fixed on the way:
- **Every web modal whose content arrived after it opened stayed the size of its loading spinner** — reanimated pins a custom (`withInitialValues`) entering animation to its measured size. That was the tiny quant list. `Modal` and `Menu` use a built-in animation on the web.
- **A runtime restart asked for during another was dropped**: CPU → Automatic in quick succession left the CPU running with Automatic selected. Found by the Electron lane.
- A downloaded quant's fit in the HuggingFace sheet now counts its own memory.
- The picker's load badge was pushed off the row on phones (Android only).
- **A model card's HTML showed as tags** in the HuggingFace sheet. It is converted to the markdown it means (`components/markdown/html.ts`); images are not fetched (a badge becomes its link) and only http(s)/mailto links open.
- **Markdown text on the web ignored its paragraph's colour and size** (react-native-web's 14px black defaults), so headings were body-sized and chat replies dim — app-wide, not only the card.
- A bare `<Spinner />` raised the red "styleq: tailwind typeof undefined" toast in dev builds.

## Verified

- Server: 1,155 tests pass. New: `room.test.ts` (every unload/refuse branch), `memory.test.ts`, `pinning.test.ts` (fake router with a memory budget: eviction, refusal at send and request time, pin load, reload after restart, queued restart).
- e2e `local-models.spec.ts`: **15/15 on web and on Electron**. New cases for the GPU switches, sheet height, loaded badges, pin → no-room (admin and user), unpin → eviction, pin → load → restart.
- Red first: the sheet-height case fails against the old modal (the list is unreachable); the queued-restart unit test fails against the old `ensureRuntime`.
- iOS simulator and Android emulator, by hand: picker badges, no-room modal and *Choose a loaded model*, text restored, pin and GPU switches, quant sheet.
- Full web lane: 43/44 spec files. `providers.spec.ts` fails on the local dev database, not this branch: a provider row "Acme Production" (created 2026-09-25) hides the *add first provider* button the spec waits for.

- Model cards: 15 unit tests over real cards' HTML; the e2e card case goes red without the conversion. Checked by hand on web (dev build), and on iOS and Android against the real unsloth Qwen3-Coder card.

Not verified: real Vulkan GPUs (everything ran against the fake router), and attach mode, whose free-memory figure is only as fresh as the sidecar's start.

## Screenshots

From `apps/e2e/artifacts/` (not committed):

| file | shows |
|---|---|
| `web/2026-09-26T11-38-52-842Z/02-local-models-gpu-switches.png` | GPU switch, "23.4 GB free of 24.0 GB" |
| `web/2026-09-27T04-06-16-186Z/04-local-models-details-card.png` | model card: HTML drawn as bold text, links and a badge link, heading at heading size |
| `web/…/04-local-models-details-fit-labels.png` | quant sheet at full height, content loaded a second after opening |
| `web/…/16-local-models-picker-loaded.png` | picker: Loaded badge, loaded first, hint |
| `web/…/17-local-models-pinned.png` | Keep loaded switch and Pinned pill |
| `web/…/18-local-models-no-room-admin.png` | no-room modal for an admin |
| `web/…/19-local-models-no-room-user.png` | no-room modal for an ordinary user |
| `web/…/20-local-models-evicted-for-second.png` | unpinned, the second model answers after the first is unloaded |
| `electron/2026-09-26T11-49-25-398Z/…` | the same run in Electron |
| `android/2026-09-26-manual/01…05` | Android: badges, no-room modal, pinned row, GPU switch, quant sheet |

## What you need to do

1. Merge this PR once CI is green.
2. Cut a beta afterwards (`scripts/release.sh`) and have it deployed to .13. Pinning and the new free-memory figures have only run against the fake router; on the real V620s the GPU rows should show ~3.7 GB free on Vulkan0 while LM Studio holds it, and a pinned model should come back after Restart.
3. Decide about the "Acme Production" provider in your local dev database (`http://192.168.1.13:1234/v1`, created 2026-09-25). Recommended: delete it under Settings → Model providers if it was a test; while it exists, `providers.spec.ts` fails on this machine.

2. **Details: the focused part sits in the middle of the screen.** The version picker, season picker and each episode scroll to the centre when they get focus, instead of staying at the very bottom. This uses the bubbling `onFocus` of a wrapping view plus `measureLayout` against the panel.
3. **Entering an episode lands on Play.** Each episode row is a focus guide with `autoFocus`: moving down from the season picker (or between episodes) lands on **Play** instead of the nearest button (the external-player icon). The episode's version picker now comes after its buttons, so Play is first in the row.

author: ctoth
body:
Conformance: MongooseMoo/moo-conformance-tests#109 (`builtins/set_thread_mode_activation_scope.yaml`)

## Divergence
Toast keeps thread mode on each activation. `get_thread_mode`/`set_thread_mode` read and write `RUN_ACTIV.threaded`. `call_verb2` receives `DEFAULT_THREAD_MODE` (true) for verb calls and `pass()`, and eval activations and forked tasks reset to the default. Barn kept a single per-task `ctx.ThreadMode`, so `set_thread_mode(0)` in one verb leaked into the verbs it called and back into its caller.

## Fix
- `ctx.ThreadMode` is still the read API. It now means the running activation's mode.
- Verb calls, `pass()`, `eval()`, and builtin-driven verb calls (`CallVerbInContext`) set it to true on push.
- The caller's mode is kept in the new `StackFrame.SavedThreadMode` and restored at the four return/unwind sites, the same way the other saved context fields are restored.
- `#0:bf_<name>` protected wrappers inherit the caller's mode, as in Toast (`functions.cc` `call_verb2(..., get_thread_mode())`).
- Checkpoints: `VMFrameSnapshot.ThreadMode` records each activation's own mode.
  - The Toast activation `threaded` slot now carries the real value instead of a constant 0.
  - Barn frame metadata carries it as well. Barn frames written before this change don't have the flag and load as enabled.
  - Restore rebuilds each frame's `SavedThreadMode` and the context's mode from the snapshot.

## Evidence
- Stock WSL Toast oracle (sha256 `72fb1cf9…2bde`, Test.db `1a3f23eb…408e`): the new file passes 9/9, including `capability_admission`.
- Barn at master `5028895`: 6 of the 8 new tests fail. At this branch (linux build sha256 `1dff6f76…736d`) all 9 pass.
- Thread, SQLite, and background selection: Barn 30 passed; Toast 27 passed, 3 skipped.
- Full managed conformance suite on Barn: 12620 passed, 440 skipped, 0 failed.
- `gofmt`, `go vet ./...`, `staticcheck ./...`, `go build ./...`, `go test ./... -count=1`, and `git diff --check` are all clean.
- New `vm/persistence_thread_mode_test.go` covers a checkpoint round trip of a task suspended inside `eval()` under a disabled outer activation. I mutation-checked the restore derivation and the reader flag against it.

Replaces the emoji and wave art with ten GPT Image 2.5 Flare paintings: one per goal, plus the landing night lake and its session-complete sunrise over the same lake. Live layers are pinned to each painting's own coordinates: glow, water glints and ripples, light shafts, mist, stars, meteor, aurora, and particles.

## Mobile performance

All motion is `transform`/`opacity` on plain HTML elements, so the compositor runs it without main-thread paint. No SVG repaint, blend modes, filters, backdrop blur, or fixed-background repaint. Pointer parallax, tilt, and glare are mouse-only; animations pause offscreen, while a session is paused, and behind dialogs.

Measured on a 390 px phone viewport with 4x CPU throttle, against the previous preview:

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Landing, main thread idle (per 4 s) | 3772 ms | 173 ms |
| Sessions, main thread idle (per 4 s) | 3898 ms | 109 ms |
| Scroll, main thread | 2883 ms | 1202 ms |
| Scroll FPS | 87 | 144 |
| Estimated GPU texture | ~1.2 GB | ~245 MB |

## Also

- `vercel.json` pins the Vite build and `dist/` output, so every deployment serves the built app regardless of the project's framework preset.
- Card paintings (~220 KB) are precached for offline use; large ones are cached on first view.

author: matheuzindev
body:
@
Primeira peça da camada de adaptadores. **Nenhum adaptador real de marketplace** entra aqui, e isso é intencional.

## Por que sem adaptador real

A credencial da Open API da Shopee foi solicitada e ainda não chegou, e a documentação oficial (`affiliate.shopee.com.br/open_api`) exige login e não pôde ser lida. A `affiliateshopee.com.br/documentacao` **se declara não oficial** no próprio topo da página, então não serve como contrato.

Escrever o adaptador agora significaria inventar nomes de campo e formato de resposta — exatamente o risco que o `docs/requisitos.md` registra: *"Detalhes da API da Shopee vêm de ferramentas de terceiros | Contrato da API pode diferir | Confirmar na documentação oficial antes de codificar"*.

A interface, por outro lado, se desenha pelo lado do **domínio**: o que a coleta e o motor de regras precisam consumir (RF10). Traduzir o formato de cada marketplace é trabalho do adaptador concreto. Se a interface fosse moldada pela resposta da Shopee, o RNF16 morreria no segundo marketplace.

## O que entra

**RF04 — contrato comum** (`adapters/base.py`, `adapters/dto.py`)
- `Protocol` com `marketplace`, `nome` e `consultar(item_id) -> Resultado`
- DTO de domínio normalizando o que o RF10 exige: preço à vista, parcelado (total e nº de parcelas), frete, estoque, vendedor, cupom aplicável
- Dinheiro em `Decimal` com `max_digits=12, decimal_places=2`, compatível com `NUMERIC(12,2)`, e um validador que **rejeita `float`** em vez de apenas tipar
- `origem` e `coletado_em` obrigatórios, com fuso exigido (RNF09)
- Vendedor guardado como payload **cru**; o núcleo não normaliza para nota nem tier

**RF06 — registro de permissões** (`adapters/permissoes.py`)
- Lugar único onde as permissões são declaradas: guardar histórico, alertar preço, canais permitidos, avisos exigidos
- Consultado pelo núcleo; o adaptador não decide durante a execução
- **Padrão nega tudo** e o mapa por marketplace está **vazio**, com o motivo no código: valores só entram depois de os termos serem lidos

**RNF07 — falha isolada** (`adapters/nucleo.py`)
- `Resultado = Leitura | Falha`: falha é valor, não exceção
- `consultar_isolado` converte exceção inesperada em `Falha`; `coletar` não para no primeiro erro
- `TipoFalha.DESATUALIZADO` para o dado velho que o RNF09 manda marcar

**RNF10 — adaptador falso** (`adapters/fake.py`)
- Lê respostas gravadas de fixtures, sem rede, e implementa o contrato inteiro

Fora de escopo por decisão: RF05 (precisa de credencial), RF07 (limites de chamada reais), RF29 (configuração sem código). Nenhum endpoint criado; `main.py`, `models.py`, `alembic/` e `catalog/` não foram tocados.

## Consequência operacional

Com o padrão negando tudo e o mapa vazio, **nada coleta nem alerta** até a entrada da Shopee ser preenchida. Isso é o comportamento correto — permissão não deve nascer permissiva — mas torna "preencher as permissões da Shopee" uma task obrigatória assim que os termos da API forem lidos.

## Validação

`pytest` **77 passed** (66 existentes + 11 novos) · `alembic upgrade head` limpo · `ruff` limpo · `mypy src` limpo (17 arquivos).

O worker reportou honestamente que não conseguiu rodar os 66 testes existentes por o PostgreSQL estar parado no ambiente dele, e pediu que o coordenador rodasse a suíte completa. Foi feito, com o banco no ar, e os 77 passam.

Verificação independente do coordenador, além da suíte:

- `preco_vista=199.90` (float) é rejeitado; `Decimal` e string passam; três casas decimais e valor negativo também rejeitados
- `coletado_em` sem fuso é rejeitado
- payload de vendedor volta idêntico, e o DTO não expõe nenhum atributo `reputacao`, `score`, `tier` ou `nota`
- um adaptador que **levanta exceção** vira `Falha` sem propagar
- coleta com três adaptadores, dois explodindo, devolve três resultados e não para no primeiro erro
- **RNF16 provado por fora**: um adaptador de Mercado Livre escrito do zero, sem herdar nada, satisfaz o contrato e lê permissões sem nenhuma mudança no núcleo

author: madkoding
body:
Implements phase 5 of `docs/self-improvement-design.md`, which was designed and never built: the library of procedures now has a window, a maintenance pass, and commands to drive it.

Eight commits, one per phase, each with its own tests and each at 100% coverage of its package.

## What it does

**The library is served.** Eight endpoints (`/v1/skills*`, `/v1/curator*`), process-wide rather than per-session because the library is one directory, behind two new interfaces in `Options` so the 17 existing `fakeService` tests were not touched. The index carries no body on purpose, and an unreadable library answers `500` rather than an empty list - a browser that drew "no skills" over a broken directory would send the user looking for documents they still have.

**It has a window.** The browser interface's Skill library placeholder is now a real browser: the index with lifecycle badges, a filter that runs in memory, the document rendered, and the archive with a way back. Pin lives in the detail view, not on the row, because an exemption flipped off a list is how somebody pins the wrong document.

**It keeps itself tidy.** A curator marks documents stale after 14 days unused and archives them after 30, with no model involved - the pass runs a week apart and only when nobody has been talking for two hours. It never deletes: a document that ages out is *moved* to `.archive/` and restorable. It only ages documents the agent wrote; one written by hand is skipped. `pinned` is the user's veto over every automatic transition.

**`motita curator status|run|pin|unpin|restore|list-archived`**, positional like `gateway`, with the scan that restarts after every word it removes so one line can carry both subcommands. None of these need an API key - tidying a shelf is filesystem work. `--consolidate` is the deliberate exception.

## Verification

- `make check` (fmt-check, vet, full suite) passes.
- The CI coverage gate is **green at 100% per package** - including the five packages that were below it on `main` (`procedures`, `usage`, `webui`, `updater`, and `review` which had no tests at all).
- Driven in a real browser over CDP (this box has no Chromium default, so a raw driver was used): the modal opens, rows render, the filter narrows, a document opens with its markdown rendered, Pin flips to Unpin and the server confirms `pinned:true`, and a curator-archived document appears under Archived where Restore puts it back - with `GET /v1/skills/archived` returning `[]` afterwards. No console errors.
- The CLI was exercised end to end with the real binary, exit codes included.

## Known, not introduced here

`make test-matrix` fails to build `internal/app` for `windows/386` (`cmd.SysProcAttr.Setsid` in `gatewayseams_test.go:101`). Verified pre-existing on `main`; CI does not run that target.

author: paulbratslavsky
body:
## Why

`@tanstack/ai-anthropic` was an optional peer at `^0.18.0`, while the plugin depended on `@tanstack/ai@^0.52.0`. The adapter's own peer requirement on the SDK moved independently:

| adapter | needs `@tanstack/ai` |
|---|---|
| `ai-anthropic@0.18.3` | `^0.52.0` |
| `ai-anthropic@0.18.10` | `^0.58.0` |
| `ai-anthropic@0.18.13` | `^0.59.0` |

So `npm install strapi-plugin-tanstack-ai @tanstack/ai-anthropic` picked the newest in range, and the install **succeeded** with two SDK copies:

```
0.52.3  node_modules/strapi-plugin-tanstack-ai/node_modules/@tanstack/ai
0.59.0  node_modules/@tanstack/ai
```

The plugin built its adapter against one version and called `chat()` from the other. That is a silent mismatch, not an error. Anthropic is the default provider, so this was the common path.

## What changed

- All four `@tanstack` packages (`ai`, `ai-react`, `ai-anthropic`, `ai-ollama`) are now dependencies at **exact** versions. The plugin owns one set that is known to agree, so the graph cannot split. No `@tanstack/*` peer dependencies remain.
- Install is one package: `npm install strapi-plugin-tanstack-ai`. Picking a provider is config only.
- The seam is unchanged. Everything is still reached through a dynamic `import()` behind `chat.enabled`, only the configured provider's adapter is ever imported, and `check:seam` still asserts that no static require survives the build.
- The loader's error text now describes a load failure as a broken install, not a missing step.
- README, `docs/configuration.md` and `docs/development.md` are updated. The clean-install check is now `npm ls @tanstack/ai`, expecting exactly one version, which is the check that catches this class of bug.

The cost is about 11 MB of adapters on every install, including the one you don't use. That buys a dependency graph that cannot split.

## Verification

- `npm run verify` passes: package check, eslint, seam, 197 tests.
- A clean project with only the packed 1.6.0 installed yields exactly one `@tanstack/ai` (0.52.3), with both adapters present.
- A real Strapi app declaring only this plugin boots with `chat ENABLED` and `registered 3/3 MCP tool(s)`.

body:
Final README and documentation sync before the v1.3.0 release. **Documentation only — no application behaviour changes.** No tag, no release.

## What was wrong on `main`

- The READMEs still listed **Row-Template 1.3.0** under *Roadmap*.
- PasarGuard's supported version (**5.x**) was only on the compatibility page. The READMEs, Installation, Getting started and Overview did not name it.
- The **`RT_PANEL` requirement** was vague ("in a script, reads `RT_PANEL`"). In the code (`rt_panel_choose`), a non-interactive fresh install on a server with several panels **stops before changing anything** unless `RT_PANEL` is set, `RT_PANEL` must name an installed panel, and an existing install keeps its panel.
- The README rollback text did not say that a rollback restores the page and the recorded version, **not the manager**, or that **only the two newest backups** are kept. The docs site already said this.
- "Updating from 1.1.0 or **1.2.x**" and troubleshooting's "Since **1.2.1**": 1.2.1 was never released and shipped in 1.3.0.
- `docs/design/README.md` still called PasarGuard and Rebecca "research targets".
- Dead anchors: Getting started linked to `installation/#activate-it`, and the fa/ar pages to similar anchors, none of which exist.
- `docs/README.md` pointed at `src/content/docs/en/`, which does not exist.
- The bug-report form asked only for a "3X-UI (panel) version".

## Changes

**READMEs (en, fa, ar, ru, zh-CN), kept structurally identical**
- Panel table: PasarGuard **5.x**. Rebecca's 0.0.x Docker image is marked **Not supported** (refused, nothing changed). The table still has one row per panel, as `tests/panel-support.test.mjs` requires.
- New **Limitations in 1.3.0** list: live refresh is 3X-UI only, Rebecca Docker is refused, some cases need a setting entered by hand, some panel settings take precedence, no `subTitle`/Clash templates, and one panel per server.
- `RT_PANEL` requirement for scripted multi-panel fresh installs, stated explicitly.
- Requirements now name PasarGuard 5.x and Rebecca 1.x (binary install).
- All 17 `RT_TEMPLATE` ids are listed: `row`, `editorial`, `canvas`, `prism`, `terminal`, `pulse`, `brutal`, `arcade`, `sketch`, `signature`, `saffron`, `pulsenova`, `prismnova`, `terminalnova`, `arcadenova`, `meter`, `notebook`.
- Rollback limits, and upgrade from 1.1.0 or 1.2.0. PasarGuard and Rebecca users run the installer.
- Removed the 1.3.0 roadmap line. The diagram now labels live status as 3X-UI.
- The Rebecca edition note now comes after the Rebecca activation steps.

**Docs site (en, fa, ar)**
- Installation: PasarGuard 5.x, the Rebecca Docker refusal, the `RT_PANEL` requirement, three more install error messages (`RT_PANEL=…, but … was not detected`, `installed for …; uninstall it before installing for …`, and the Rebecca 0.0.x refusal), and a new **Upgrading** section.
- Compatibility: the `RT_PANEL` requirement and one panel per server.
- Getting started and Overview: panel versions.
- Configuration: 1.2.x → 1.2.0. Troubleshooting (en, fa): "since 1.2.1" → 1.3.0.
- Fixed the dead anchors. The Arabic stub pages now link to the matching English page instead of the site root.

## Checked, already correct

- `VERSION` = 1.3.0. The template registry, `docs/src/data/templates.json` and the preview set (34 images + manifest) all hold the same 17 ids. The 3×17 panel shells are unaffected.
- No README or docs page calls PasarGuard or Rebecca *Research*. The compatibility matrices (en, fa, ar) mark all three panels ✅ in all 10 columns.
- The docs site rollback text (page + recorded version, two newest backups) matches the code (`rt_backups_prune 2`).

## Validation

- `cd docs && npm run build`: 37 pages, no errors. The only warnings are Vite's `MODULE_LEVEL_DIRECTIVE` notices, emitted for every page including untouched ones.
- Internal link check over `docs/dist`: **2126 links, all resolve**, including `#fragment`s. The relative and docs-site links in the READMEs, `docs/*.md`, CHANGELOG, PROVENANCE, CONTRIBUTING and SECURITY: **237 checked, all resolve**.
- README sync check: the five READMEs have identical fenced blocks, inline-code multiset, link targets, image sources, section/table/list skeleton and version numbers. Every in-page anchor resolves.
- `npm run verify`: all checks passed.
- `node --test tests/panel-support.test.mjs tests/release.test.mjs`: 21/21.
- `npm test` on a clean clone of this branch (Windows): **761 tests, 754 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped** (the usual Windows platform skips).

## Pre-existing issue on `main` (not in this PR)

In a long-lived working tree, `tests/preview-determinism.test.mjs` › *an all-template build produces seventeen fresh artifacts* can fail after a checkout or pull. `tools/write-if-changed.mjs` (3d89bff) leaves build outputs whose bytes are unchanged untouched, so their mtimes stay older than a source that git just rewrote. The same check makes `docs/scripts/capture-previews.mjs` refuse to run. ## Summary

Python suggested verify commands interpolated the test path raw. A file named `tests/foo$(id).py` became `pytest tests/foo$(id).py::test_ok`, which a POSIX shell expands. TypeScript already single-quotes that class of path. Python now uses the same character class for pytest and unittest command text.

Plain paths such as `tests/test_checkout.py` stay unquoted, so existing commands and goldens are unchanged. `suggested_test_file` and `suggested_test_node_id` stay the raw spelling.

## Swarm / Source Boundary

This PR targets `EffortlessMetrics/ripr-swarm`, the normal development trunk for trusted same-repo `ripr` work. Confirm the change belongs here:

- [x] ordinary feature, analyzer, editor, docs, spec, fixture, badge, dependency, or repo-ops development for `ripr-swarm`
- [ ] repair or follow-up for a same-repo swarm PR
- [ ] swarm-only CI, runner, routing, source-of-truth, or agent-operating surface
- [ ] other swarm-scoped work:

Proposal:
Spec:
ADR:
Plan item:
Governing issue or accepted claim: #4211
Acceptance delta (one sentence): A Python verify command single-quotes a non-plain test path, and a plain relative path is unchanged.

## Candidate Relationships

Candidate branch (GitHub PR head is authoritative after publication): `fix/python-verify-quote`
Exact candidate SHA: `280e77cae016d9a5f35a459bbbecbdbc9d840d05`
Stack parent or prerequisite PR (if any):
Proposed replacement of PR (if any; not yet accepted):
Accepted winner and losing candidate disposition (when decided):

## Scope

Quote the path token inside Python pytest and unittest verify command text.

## Scope Classification

This PR is scoped by:

- [x] One production behavior
- [ ] One public contract
- [ ] One architectural seam
- [ ] Docs/spec/test-only evidence package
- [ ] Other:

Production delta:

`verify_command_for_test` is the only command builder. Repair placement copies that string. The quote rule matches `shell_quote_file_arg` in the TypeScript package verifier: non-empty ASCII alphanumeric plus `.` `_` `/` `-` stays raw; anything else is single-quoted with `'\''` for an embedded quote.

Evidence/support delta:

Unit coverage for `$()`, a space, an embedded quote, a plain path that must stay raw, and both the pytest and unittest repair commands. The stored node id is asserted raw.

Single acceptance criterion:

`pytest 'tests/foo$(id).py'::test_ok` is the command, `tests/foo$(id).py::test_ok` is the stored node id, and `pytest tests/test_checkout.py::test_ok` is still unquoted.

Non-goals:

- Executing the command, or claiming a shell was exploited.
- PowerShell quoting.
- Quoting a leading `-` (the TypeScript quoter also treats `-` as safe).
- Tier promotion or 0.11 publication.

## Support-tier Impact

- [x] none
- [ ] updates `docs/status/SUPPORT_TIERS.md`
- [ ] changes a README, release, docs, CLI, JSON, editor, CI, or package claim

No support-tier text changes. Plain-path fixture commands are unchanged, so goldens were not blessed.

- [ ] doc artifacts
- [ ] CI lane
- [ ] package boundary
- [ ] lint / Clippy
- [ ] no-panic
- [ ] file policy
- [ ] generated artifact
- [ ] dependency
- [ ] process/network

Ledger or exception notes:

No new process. No allowlist change.

## Proof

`cargo check -p ripr --offline --jobs 1 --lib --tests` and `cargo clippy -p ripr --offline --jobs 1 --lib --tests -- -D warnings` completed on this host. `cargo test -p ripr --lib` was not linked here (the test binary is killed by the memory limit). The new assertions are in `verify_command_quotes_shell_metacharacters_and_leaves_plain_paths_raw`.

Not run: a live shell paste of the hostile command. The oracle is the rendered string.

## Claim Boundary

What may be claimed after this PR? The rendered pytest and unittest command text quotes a non-plain path the same way TypeScript quotes a file argument, and plain paths are unchanged. What must not be claimed yet? That ripr executes the command, that PowerShell is covered, or that a leading `-` is quoted.

Revert this PR. Command text goes back to raw interpolation. Stored paths were never quoted.

author: dichovsky
body:
Part of #22 (second R01 PR, after #61).

## The gap this closes

R01 requires "packed executable protocol checks pass for both eras and stdout is clean". Before this PR:

- `npm run test:package` ran only `--help`, `-h`, `--version` and `-v` against the installed tarball.
- `tests/transport/lifecycle.test.ts` runs the repo-built `dist/cli.js`, in the legacy era only, with an `initialize`, a malformed line, a ping and an unknown method. It never lists tools or calls one.
- `docs/transport.md` nonetheless said the lifecycle test drove "the packaged executable".

## What changes

`scripts/package-protocol.mjs` is called from `verify-package.mjs` after the tarball is installed into a clean directory. It runs three MCP sessions against the installed `dist/cli.js`. Each session gets its own TestRail stand-in on `127.0.0.1` (`TESTRAIL_ALLOW_INSECURE`/`TESTRAIL_ALLOW_PRIVATE_HOSTS`), and the server runs with Node's warnings silenced (`NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1`, no `NODE_OPTIONS`).

| Session | Transport | Must negotiate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| legacy | recording stdio transport | legacy (`initialize`) |
| pinned `2026-07-28` | recording stdio transport | modern |
| `auto` | the SDK's own `StdioClientTransport`, which probes a sibling process | modern |

**Every session** must pass these checks:

| Check | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| Era | read from the connection right after connect |
| Discovery | exactly the 133 inventory names; a second listing byte-identical; the client cache bypassed; **0** TestRail requests |
| `testrail_get_project {project_id: 7}` | success; `data` is the stand-in's body; text equals `structuredContent`; **1** request, `GET /index.php?/api/v2/get_project/7`, correct Basic auth |
| `project_id: "7"` | `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, still 1 request |
| Unknown tool | `ProtocolError` `InvalidParams` (-32602), then a full listing still served |
| stderr | every line a JSON event object, `server_started` present; no API key, Basic credential, email or TestRail address |

The **two recorded sessions** must additionally pass these:

| Check | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| stdout | every line, a final unterminated one included, is JSON-RPC and carries none of those values |
| Shutdown | `server_stopped` on stderr; exit `{ code: 0, signal: null }` within 10 s of stdin closing. The harness then SIGKILLs, and a kill fails the check. |

A failure names the session and the step and ends with the server's stderr. The recorded sessions also report the exit status. For example: `legacy session failed at testrail_get_project: Connection closed; the server exited with 3; its stderr ended: …`.

`docs/transport.md` now says what each suite actually drives. `docs/issues/R01.md` records the progress.

## Verification

- `npm run check` passes: 4837 tests across 30 files, registry 133/133, and a package smoke line reading `MCP over stdio (legacy: 133 tools, 2026-07-28: 133 tools, auto: 133 tools)`.
- The sessions add about 3 s to the package step.
- Mutations applied to the source (or to the script's timeout) and run against the built executable. Each fails unless marked:

| Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| A stray stdout line, with or without a final newline | fails |
| Diagnostics routed to stdout | fails |
| One tool dropped | fails |
| Diagnostics written as Node warnings | fails: no `server_started` diagnostic |
| API key, Basic credential or TestRail address in a diagnostic | fails |
| A non-event JSON value on stderr | fails |
| An unknown tool that is never answered | fails: not the invalid-params error |
| A server that exits during a call | fails with session, step, exit status and stderr tail |
| A server that ignores stdin closure | fails in 11 s instead of hanging |
| A cached tool list plus a server that stops serving after an unknown tool | fails even in the pinned session run alone |
| An era mismatch | fails at the `negotiation` step |
| A correct server emitting a startup deprecation warning, or run with `NODE_OPTIONS=--trace-warnings` | **passes**, as it should |

## Review

- [Pass one, adversarial panel](https://github.com/dichovsky/testrail-mcp/pull/65#issuecomment-5850659102): 16 confirmed, 1 split, 0 refuted, as eight distinct problems. All fixed in 8467dab.
- Pass two, fresh reviewer: 5 findings, all reproduced and fixed in bbe406e. Summary in the latest comment.

`main` was merged in (0299a1b) so CI also runs against the current base.

## Still to do under #22

1. Result contract and paging through registered tools.
2. Runtime lifetime through registered tools. A parallel session is working on this on `claude/r01-runtime-lifetime`.
3. Coverage and fixture-evidence reports as CI artifacts.

body:
When a task consumes an upstream that only ran remotely, vx-reapi grafts that upstream's execution record into the task's input root by reference. The graft included the record's files and directories but skipped its symlinks. So the action ran without an input it had declared, and its result was cached under a key that claims the input was present.

The record's `output_symlinks` now go into the input tree as symlinks.

A new row in `executor-sweep.test.ts`, "a record graft keeps the upstream's symlinks", fails without the fix. The gate passed on this commit before the rebase, and the vx-reapi suite passes after it. STATUS item 920 is updated. This closes the vx-reapi review.

author: hartra344
body:
The macOS app freezes at launch on main: the main thread sits at 100% CPU and the app has to be force quit.

**Cause:** `sample` shows SwiftUI stuck in an app graph update loop (`AppDelegate.appGraphDidChange → makeMainMenu` and `AppMenuBarExtrasController.updateMenuBarExtras`). Bisecting found the regression between 8847547 (fine) and c0be0c0 (freezes), which covers the menu bar item (#104) and Gateway Health dismissals (#105). Taking the `PincerMenuBar` scene out fixes it. The app then sits idle in the event loop.

**Changes**
- Take `PincerMenuBar(app:)` out of `PincerScene` and hide the Settings → General → Menu Bar section until the item is fixed. The code is left in place.
- Make the `ReplyToLast` and `SearchMessagesAction` focused values `Equatable`, so they don't invalidate the main menu on every render. This hardening doesn't fix the freeze by itself.
- Docs: README, the menu bar guide (caution note) and try-the-demo now say the menu bar item is temporarily disabled.

**Follow-up (#119):** fix the loop in `PincerMenuBar`/`MenuBarInbox` (it builds the inbox with `Date()` and lazily creates `gateway.health` inside `body`), then turn the scene back on.

body:
## Intent

Firstmate repo, bin/. Filed 2026-09-05 as a follow-up from the fm-chrome-bridge-sweep review: extend the chrome-bridge sweep shutdown confirmation to the Orca, Zellij, and cmux backends. Today the cleanup path skips the sweep with a visible line on those runtimes, so a browser bridge started by a worker on one of them is never retired at cleanup.

## What Changed
- Added strict shutdown confirmation for Orca, Zellij, and cmux endpoints before signaling browser bridges.
- Preserved bridges when inventories are malformed, unreadable, or otherwise fail to prove endpoint absence.
- Added teardown coverage and updated backend verification documentation.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is narrowly scoped to strict post-close endpoint confirmation and bridge cleanup, with conservative failure handling and behavioral regression coverage.

## Testing

Fixture-based teardown tests exercised confirmed and malformed shutdown inventories for Orca, Zellij, and cmux; live backend runs were unavailable.

- Live validation: ⚠️ inconclusive - 0 of 4 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Orca cleanup confirms typed terminal absence and retires the browser bridge | ⏸️ untested | no | The orca CLI/runtime is not installed or running; provide a live Orca runtime and terminal endpoint. |
